“真是太难了，”坐在我对面的那位男子说。“我们结婚快五十年了，但我从没想到会发生这样的事。”

“发生了什么事？”我同情地问艾尔。

“是丽莎，”他说。“你知道她的记忆已经有一阵子在退步了。嗯，我们按照你的建议去看了神经科医生，他们做了一大堆检查，还有一种大脑扫描。然后，他们告诉她她得了痴呆症。”

“我就觉得可能是这样的，”我回答。

“我知道你曾告诉我们那样，”艾尔说。“有时她认不出我。她看着我一脸茫然，好像在想是什么疯狂的陌生人闯进了她的家。”

“那一定很难受，”我说。

“我发现唯一能把她带回现实的方法就是出去到外面，然后打她的手机。我告诉她出来到车库，我有东西要给她看。不知怎么的，当我那样做时，她就能回到当下，认出我——至少能持续一会儿。”

我们接着谈了别的事，但我能感觉到艾尔的心在破碎。他48年的妻子外表看起来和以前一样，然而她却成了一个完全不同的人。

我想探讨一下应对痴呆症的一些挑战。

《圣经》中的痴呆

传道书 12:1-7 对衰老过程给出了一幅有些阴郁的图景。“Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them; While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low; Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

在这段经文中，这种诗性的描述似乎谈到牙齿脱落、听力丧失、步伐不稳以及整体的虚弱。很难说这些意象中是否有任何直接指向记忆丧失。可以确定的是，这段经文以一个命令开始：“要记念！”

这并不是《圣经》中唯一命令人们要记念的地方。我们一再被告知要记念神。我们应当确保把关于祂的教导传给我们的儿女。“And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (申命记 6:7)。

当我们不能再记得的时候，时机也许会到来。在思考痴呆这一课题时，最重要的事是记念那位创造我们的主，并以全心跟随祂。

什么是痴呆

痴呆是任何导致记忆、推理和社会功能丧失的疾病。大多数人主要想到的是记忆丧失。我想这是因为在疾病早期，其他人会注意到如找词困难和频繁重复故事之类的现象。

社会功能通常会维持到疾病较晚期。如果你问一个轻度痴呆的人今天的日期，他们很可能回答：“哦，你知道，自从我退休后我就不怎么注意这些事情了。”

最常见的痴呆病因是阿尔茨海默氏症痴呆——至少有70%的渐进性记忆丧失患者患有阿尔茨海默氏症。阿尔茨海默氏症似乎与一种叫淀粉样蛋白的蛋白质有关，这些蛋白在大脑中沉积，阻止神经细胞相互通讯。

其他病因包括血管性痴呆，脑血管阻塞导致神经细胞死亡。路易体痴呆是一种与帕金森病相关的记忆丧失类型。约80%的帕金森病患者最终会出现痴呆。

痴呆的诊断

如果家人怀疑有人出现记忆衰退，最好的办法是带他去看初级保健医生做评估。除了体格检查外，医生通常会让患者画一个时钟，并做一个简短的精神状态检查，问很多简单的问题并测试一些短期记忆回忆。

还会做包括甲状腺和维生素B12水平在内的血液检查。可能还会做大脑扫描或颈部动脉超声检查。

目标是识别可以治疗的方面并处理它们。

停用药物

许多药物会增加记忆问题的风险。随着年龄增长，尽量避免这些药物有助于预防痴呆的发展。

抗胆碱能药物可能是我遇到的最大罪魁祸首。这类药物中最常见的是较老的抗组胺药，如苯海拉明（既可作为助眠药也可作为抗过敏药）和多塞拉敏（作为助眠药使用）。一项研究显示，服用抗胆碱能药物累计相当于三年的患者，其痴呆风险显著高于服用此类药物不到三个月的患者。1较老的抗抑郁药也可能属于这一类别。

抗焦虑药，也就是苯二氮卓类药物，也与记忆问题有关。研究表明，服用这些药物的患者比不服用者更有发展为痴呆的风险。2

抗癫痫药物也可能使思维能力变差。患有癫痫似乎会增加痴呆的风险，但某些较老的药物如丙戊酸和加巴喷丁似乎使老年人的思维更不清晰，若可能的话，应为老年人改用风险较低的抗癫痫药物。

有时某人确实需要服药，但随着年龄增长，重要的是要考虑这些药物的风险。对于65岁以上患者，有一份最应避免的药物清单，称为比尔斯（Beers）清单。建议用副作用较少的类似药物替代或使用更低剂量。3

药物治疗

处理痴呆的第一条规则是确保所有代谢方面尽可能得到良好控制。因此，如果有人有糖尿病，最好确保他们的血糖尽可能控制好。如果有人有高血压，要确保血压得到良好调节（如果是血管性痴呆，这一点尤其重要）。

目前有几类药物获批用于治疗痴呆。其中一类是胆碱酯酶抑制剂。这些药物可以提高大脑和周围神经系统中一种叫乙酰胆碱的化学物质的水平。这些药物当然不是灵丹妙药，充其量似乎只能减缓记忆丧失的进程，而不能真正恢复先前的大脑功能。

另一种药物叫美金刚（memantine）。它通过作用于大脑中的谷氨酸受体来发挥作用。和胆碱酯酶抑制剂一样，美金刚的效果也并不显著，最终结果只是减缓记忆丧失的速度。

这两类药物均为通用名药，尝试使用并观察患者反应是合理的。

最后要提到的一种药物叫利卡奈单抗（lecanemab）。它是一种静脉注射的输液药，针对淀粉样蛋白，这种蛋白会在阿尔茨海默氏症患者的大脑中形成。该药在清除患者大脑中的淀粉样蛋白方面效果相当好。该药价格非常昂贵（每年26,500美元），并且已与中风风险增加有关。在研究中，与安慰剂相比，痴呆症状仅被约30%地减缓。

目前没有其他药物获批用于治疗痴呆。

非药物疗法

有几件事可以帮助减缓痴呆的进展。这些对有强烈家族史并希望预防发病的人可能有帮助。

心血管锻炼非常重要。医生在几乎所有慢性疾病方面都会提到锻炼，因为事实证明它有效。在痴呆方面，规律锻炼的人患病风险下降约30%。定期锻炼似乎也能减缓痴呆的进展。4

做需动脑的益智游戏，如数独或填字游戏，似乎有助于减缓记忆丧失的进程，也可能降低发展为痴呆的几率。

最后，学习新事物很有帮助。学习新技能或专注于学习一门新语言的人，记忆力会有很大帮助。一项研究比较了学习新技能的老年人与参加社交活动的人。

要点似乎是我们的脑需要被推动去建立新的路径，否则它们会趋于退化。5

照护痴呆患者

照护痴呆患者在许多方面都是有挑战性的。常常很难判断应给予患者多少独立性。关于这一主题已有很多书籍，但有几件事值得一提。

重要的是要避免危险的事情。对记忆有缺陷的人来说，最危险的两件事是开车和做饭。这两件事看似平常，患者表面上看起来也许还能应付，但却能非常迅速地变成问题。

开车的危险有两个方面。首先，有些人在某些环节会突然僵住，记不起如何执行某项技能。这不仅对他们自己构成问题，也可能对路上的其他人造成危险。

第二，老年人可能出发去附近的商店或餐馆，结果在途中迷路。我有病人曾在开车回家的路上困惑不已，最终在城里兜了好几个小时才找到回家的路。

至于做饭，当然归结为是否记得要设定计时器并在适当时间把东西从炉子或烤箱上取下来。

很多时候，痴呆患者并不意识到自己的能力下降了多少，并会抗拒放弃车钥匙的想法。也许这仅仅归结为对独立性的失去，但面对自己不再能安全驾驶的事实是很难的。

尽量在房间和家中保持事物不变。即使是家具摆放的微小变化也可能足以扰乱局面。把某人从他们的家中带走——例如把他们送进医院——通常会使情况变得更糟。原本看似轻微的困惑会突然变得非常严重。

如果有圣灵的果子中有一项对处理痴呆患者尤为关键，那就是耐心。我们没有人拥有足够的耐心，而痴呆会把耐心消耗得非常薄弱。

痴呆患者常常像长途旅行中的小孩一样反复发问。他们一遍又一遍地问什么时候回家。他们会记不得死去的亲人在哪里，或为什么孩子们还没回家。无论你怎么解释都无济于事，因为在他们问问题后一两分钟，他们就会忘记答案，又会再次提问。

他们的技能常常时好时坏。一天他们还能扣好衬衫，第二天那项技能似乎就消失了。很容易相信他们在“没尽力”，如果他们多努力一点就能做得更多。

不幸的是，某人昨天能做某事并不意味着他们今天还能记得如何做。对他们生气只会让情况更糟，因为这会给已经缺乏执行某项技能记忆的人增加焦虑。

尽可能温柔地回答他们，即使这是你第五十三次回答同样的问题。也要使用分散注意力的方法。如果有他们仍能做的活动，比如缝纫或拼图（即使是带很大块的儿童拼图），让他们去做。疾病晚期，让他们看有漂亮图片的书，或有时给他们一个婴儿娃娃抱着，可以帮助安抚他们并把注意力从当下的焦虑中转移开。

寻求他人帮助

很容易感到沮丧。试图独自提供所有照护并不是长期之计。照顾痴呆症患者是场马拉松，不是短跑。许多人在确诊后还会存活很多年，即便他们的身体相对强壮，却需要越来越多的照护。

拥有家庭关系和教会团体的祝福之一是我们能够获得提供帮助的人。

让家人或朋友介入，给你一些喘息时间，是避免严重倦怠甚至对你所关心的人生气的关键。在你精神耗尽之前定期抽出一些时间离开是最好的。你可能认为自己做得相当好，但如果从不休息，我们都会在行善中疲惫不堪。

结论

我希望对痴呆有更多的医学解决方案。或许以后会有更多。但就目前而言，可用的药物非常有限。

关键是把圣灵的果子付诸实践。“But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (加拉太书 5:22-23)。

即便在最令人沮丧的日子里，应对严重记忆丧失的人仍需要家人的爱、温柔和耐心。唯有靠着圣灵的能力，我们才能为那些身体强壮但已不再认得你的人，提供所需的照护。

“Adrianna, what’s the temperature outside?” asked Asher. He and Adrianna were sitting at the table doing school with their siblings Emily and Kianna.

“Probably about 50.” Adrianna glanced lazily at the thermometer. “Hey, it’s 65 degrees! Mom, may we eat lunch outside?”

Mom looked up from the sink. “If you do a good job with your school until then, you may,” she told them. “And if you get your school done before lunch, you may play outside for a while this afternoon.”

Asher let out a whoop and started writing fast. The girls grinned at each other and picked up their pencils.

Everyone worked diligently until lunchtime. Then Adrianna made sandwiches while Asher put cookies in bags, Emily collected bags of chips, and Kianna ran down to the basement to grab a few apples. They each packed their lunch in a shopping bag and went out to their picnic spot, a big, flat rock in a clearing in the woods.

They ate quickly, then Adrianna suggested, “Let’s go kayak on the pond!”

“I guess we could,” said Asher slowly. “But didn’t Mom say that Emily and Kianna are too small to handle the kayaks?”

“Oh, yes, I guess she did. Well, they can play on the swings or something,” she shrugged

“I think we should play something everyone can help with,” said Asher. He turned to Emily and Kianna. “What do you want to do?”

“Let’s make a playhouse!” suggested Kianna.

“Yes, let’s!” Emily agreed. “You could hunt for us,” she told Asher.

“And Adrianna could be the mom!” said Kianna.

Adrianna stood with a scowl on her face. Playhouse indeed! She was way too old for that! “I’m going kayaking,” she announced. “You can just have your playhouse.” She picked up her shopping bag and put her sandwich and cookie bags into it. She threw her apple core to the dogs and started for the house.

“Adrianna, can you please take ours too?” begged Emily. “You're going to the house anyway.”

“You can take care of your own stuff,” Adrianna called back, crossly. She dropped her shopping bag on the counter, hoping to slip out of the house before Mom saw her.

She heard her mom’s voice. “Wait, Adrianna, what’s wrong? Your face looks like a thunderstorm!”

Adrianna sighed. She hadn’t been fast enough. “I wanted to go kayaking, but Asher doesn’t want to,” she grumbled.

“Well,” said Mom slowly, “I think Asher is remembering that the other girls can't handle kayaks yet. What are they doing?”

“They’re building a playhouse. I'm way too old for that!” Adrianna burst out.

Mom smiled, “What makes you think that?”

“I'm sure none of the girls my age do stuff like that with their little siblings.”

“Are you sure you're not being selfish?” Mom asked. “Sometimes, we need to give up what we want so that others can be happy.”

Adrianna shrugged and went out to the shed to get a kayak. She lifted her blue kayak off the rack and hauled it down to the pond. She snapped the paddle together, hopped into the seat, and pushed the kayak onto the smooth surface of the water. She sighed with pleasure. This was way better than building a playhouse in the woods! She took a few loops around the pond before her paddle began to slow. Somehow it wasn’t as fun this time. She heard Asher and the girls laughing and shouting as they played. Maybe Mom was right, she thought. Maybe I would be happier if I gave up what I want so that we can all play together. Slowly she paddled to the edge of the pond. She stepped out of the kayak, pulled it out of the water, and flipped it over to dry. Resolutely, she walked out of the pasture to find Asher and the girls.

“Hey! Here comes Adrianna!” called Emily happily as Adrianna walked up.

Adrianna grinned, “It looks like you have your house about set up,” she said encouragingly. “What do you need to finish it?”

“We still need a stove, and something for a countertop,” said Kianna.

“I can help you find something,” Adrianna told them. Together they hunted in the woods and the shed for boards and logs to finish the house. When suppertime came and they went in for supper, Adrianna was very happy. Mom was right, she thought. It is more fun to give up my way and do what everyone else wants to.

Asher laat ’n gejuig hoor en begin vinnig skryf. Die meisies glimlag na mekaar en vat hul potlode op.

Almal werk ywerig tot middagete. Toe maak Adrianna toebroodjies, terwyl Asher koekies in sakke sit, Emily sakke skyfies bymekaarskraap, en Kianna afhardloop na die kelder om ’n paar appelteë te kry. Hulle pak elk hul middagete in ’n sak en gaan na hul piekniekplek, ’n groot, plat rots in ’n oop plek in die bos.

Hulle eet vinnig, toe stel Adrianna voor: “Kom ons gaan kajak op die dam!”

“Dalk kan ons,” sê Asher stadig. “Maar het Ma nie gesê Emily en Kianna is te klein om die kajakke te hanteer nie?”

“O, ja, ek dink sy het. Wel, hulle kan op die swaaie speel of iets anders,” skouerhaal sy.

“Ek dink ons moet iets speel waaraan almal kan help,” sê Asher. Hy draai na Emily en Kianna. “Wat wil julle doen?”

“Kom ons bou ’n speelhuis!” stel Kianna voor.

“Ja, kom ons doen!” stem Emily in. “Jy kan jag vir ons,” sê sy vir Asher.

“En Adrianna kan die ma wees!” sê Kianna.

Adrianna staan met ’n frons op haar gesig. ’n Speelhuis! Sy is baie te oud daarvoor! “Ek gaan kajak,” kondig sy aan. “Julle kan maar julle speelhuis hê.” Sy vat haar sak en sit haar toebroodjie- en koekiesakke daarin. Sy gooi haar appelkern vir die honde en begin na die huis toe stap.

“Adrianna, kan jy asseblief onsne ook neem?” vra Emily. “Jy gaan tog na die huis.”

“Julle kan jul eie goed versorg,” roep Adrianna terug, ontsteld. Sy laat haar inkopiesak op die toonbank val en hoop om uit die huis te glip voordat Ma haar sien.

Sy hoor haar ma se stem. “Wag, Adrianna, wat is fout? Jou gesig lyk soos ’n donderstorm!”

Adrianna sug. Sy was nie vinnig genoeg nie. “Ek wou gaan kajak, maar Asher wil nie,” brom sy.

“Wel,” sê Ma stadig, “ek dink Asher onthou dat die ander meisies nog nie kajakke kan hanteer nie. Wat doen hulle?”

“Hulle bou ’n speelhuis. Ek is veel te oud vir so iets!” blêr Adrianna uit.

Ma glimlag, “Wat laat jou dink so?”

“Ek is seker geen meisies van my ouderdom doen sulke dinge saam met hul kleiner susters nie.”

“Is jy seker jy is nie selfsugtig nie?” vra Ma. “Soms moet ons prysgee wat ons wil hê sodat ander gelukkig kan wees.”

Adrianna skouerhaal en gaan uit na die skuur om ’n kajak te haal. Sy lig haar blou kajak van die rak af en sleep dit na die dam. Sy klik die roer bymekaar, spring in die sitplek en stoot die kajak op die gladde water. Sy sug van plesier. Dit is baie beter as om ’n speelhuis in die bos te bou! Sy maak ’n paar rondtes om die dam voordat haar roeiver traag begin raak. Op een of ander manier is dit hierdie keer nie so pret nie. Sy hoor Asher en die meisies lag en skreeu terwyl hulle speel. Miskien het Ma reg, dink sy. Miskien sal ek gelukkiger wees as ek prysgee wat ek wil hê sodat ons almal saam kan speel. Stadig roei sy na die oewer. Sy stap uit die kajak, trek dit uit die water en draai dit om om te droog. Vasbeslote stap sy uit die veld op soek na Asher en die meisies.

“Kyk! Hier kom Adrianna!” roep Emily vrolik toe Adrianna aangestap kom.

Adrianna glimlag, “Dit lyk of julle huis al byna klaar is,” sê sy aanmoedigend. “Wat benodig julle om dit te voltooi?”

“Ons het nog ’n stoof nodig, en iets vir ’n toonbank,” sê Kianna.

“Ek kan help om iets te kry,” sê Adrianna vir hulle. Saam soek hulle in die bos en die skuur vir planke en takkies om die huis klaar te maak. Toe dit aandete-tyd raak en hulle inkom vir aandete, is Adrianna baie gelukkig. Ma het reg gehad, dink sy. Dit is meer pret om my eie manier prys te gee en te doen wat almal anders wil hê.”

Spring is my favorite time of the year. Everything is new. Hyacinths are trying their noble best to poke their buds through the cold constraint of the winter-bound earth. Migrating waterfowl bring new sounds as they honk and quack their way to their final nesting places. This year the spring peepers in our area were “winter peepers” as they feebly squeaked their greetings to the arriving spring in mid-February. Tree buds are swelling, waiting to burst forth in full glory.

Oh, the magnificence of God’s nature joining forces to proclaim the glory of new life. Surely it must have been during this exuberant time of the year when the Psalmist wrote, “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9). This display of new life springing from the earth is a beautiful representation of new life found in Christ Jesus. The wonders of the newness of life springing from the deadness of sin cannot be fully displayed by even the best show of God’s creation. It can only be experienced within the soul.

As I write this, I am flying 35,000 feet over the sub-Saharan desert land of Chad and Niger. The stark contrast between the landscape described in the previous paragraphs and the parched desert land hurrying by six miles below me is nearly beyond my comprehension. The dry earth begs for rain as livestock scrounge for anything green to fulfill their appetite. The vast dryness loudly proclaims a reminder of the millions of parched souls who have never heard of the “well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14). Millions who never experienced Christ the fountain as described in the Hymn History article in this issue:

Oh! Christ He is the foutain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above:
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

At times a yearning stirs in my heart to live the relaxed, relational lifestyle experienced in these impoverished tribal communities. Family and friends are more important than calendars and commitments. As we read in the Sister to Sister article, commitments and busyness can bring us to the overload point when we feel we cannot handle anything more. Read more to learn how to take practical steps to avoid that breaking point.

Most people in this area are Muslims. As I write this, Muslims are in the middle of Ramadan, a month-long season of fasting. They fast from food and water every day from dawn to dusk, even though daytime temperatures exceed 110 degrees. Their rigorous fasting, along with stopping their work to pray many times a day, is driven by a fervent desire to seek forgiveness of sins and obtain enough merit to enter heaven. If they only knew that true grace and mercy comes from God through the salvation of his Son, Jesus Christ. Our works can never bring us into right standing with God. The writer of the article “How to Increase Your Faith” clearly points this out “Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety.”

As we plant our gardens and watch the trees burst forth in bloom, let us be reminded of the words of the prophet Isaiah, “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” (Isaiah 61:11).

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

האביב הוא עונה אהובה עלי. הכל מתחדש. רקפות מנסות במאמצן האצילי לדחוף את הניצנים שלהן דרך הקרקע הקפואה של החורף. עופות מים נודדים מביאים קולות חדשים כשהם מנקרקים ומקרקרים בדרכם למקומות הקינון הסופיים שלהם. השנה ה"פיפרים" של האביב אצלנו היו "פיפרי חורף" כשהם זמזמו בחוסר כוח את ברכותיהם לבוא האביב באמצע פברואר. ניצני העצים מתנפחים, מצפים לפרוח ולהתמלא תפארת.

או, הגדול של טבע האלוהים המתגייס להכריז על תפארת החיים החדשים. ללא ספק זה היה בעונה השופעת הזאת בשנה כאשר המזמור אמר, “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9). המחזה של חיים חדשים המתפרצים מן האדמה הוא ייצוג יפה של החיים החדשים הנמצאים במשיח ישוע. נפלאות חידוש החיים המתעוררים מתוך חרפת החטא אינן יכולות להיות מוצגות במלואן אפילו על ידי המופע הטוב ביותר של בריאת האל. הן יכולות להיחוות רק בתוך הנפש.

כשאני כותב זאת, אני טס בגובה של כ־35,000 רגל מעל אדמות המדבר הדרום־סהרוויות של צ'אד וניג'ר. הניגוד החריף בין הנוף המתואר בפסקאות שלמעלה ובין אדמת המדבר היבשה הממהרת מתחתיי, במרחק של כ־שישה מייל, כמעט מעבר להכילתי. האדמה היבשה זועקת לגשם בעוד הבקר מחפש כל ירוק כדי לספק את תאבונו. היובש העצום מכריז בקול על מיליוני נשמות צמאי־נפש שמעולם לא שמעו על ה"well of water springing up into everlasting life" (John 4:14). מיליונים שמעולם לא חוו את ישוע כמעיין המתואר במאמר ה"Hymn History" בגיליון זה:

או! המשיח הוא המעיין,
באר העמוקה והמתוקה של האהבה!
הנחלים שעל האדמה שטעמתי,
עמוק יותר אשקה מעלה:
שם, עד למלואו של אוקיינוס,
רחמיו מתרחבים,
ותהילה — תהילה שורה
בארץ עמנואל.

לפעמים מתעורר בליבי כמיהה לחיות את אורח החיים המרגיע והקשרי שמתקיים בקהילות השבטיות העניות האלה. משפחה וחברים חשובים יותר מלוחות זמנים ומחויבויות. כפי שאנו קוראים במאמר "Sister to Sister", מחויבויות ועסוקיות עלולות להביא אותנו לנקודת עומס בה נדמה שאיננו יכולים להתמודד עם דבר נוסף. קראו עוד כדי ללמוד כיצד לנקוט צעדים מעשיים כדי להימנע מנקודת השבירה הזו.

מרבית האנשים באזור זה מוסלמים. כשאני כותב זאת, המוסלמים באמצע הרמדאן, חודש של צום. הם צמים מאוכל וממים כל יום משחר עד שקיעה, אף על פי שהטמפרטורות במהלך היום עולות על 110 מעלות. הצום הקשוח שלהם, יחד עם הפסקת עבודתם כדי להתפלל פעמים רבות ביום, מונע על ידי כמיהה לְחפש סליחה על החטאים ולקבל מספיק זכות מעשית כדי להיכנס לגן־עדן. אם רק ידעו שהחסד והרחמים האמיתיים באים מאלוהים באמצעות ישוע המשיח בנו. מעשינו לעולם אינם יכולים להכניסנו למצב של תקינות מול אלוהים. מחבר המאמר "How to Increase Your Faith" מציין זאת בבירור: "Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety."

כשאנחנו שותלים את הגנים שלנו וצופים בעצים פורחים, נזכור את דברי הנביא ישעיהו, "For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations" (Isaiah 61:11).

מברכות לכל,

אדוארד מרטין

Part 1

For Alice, life is exasperating. Each day feels like an endless grind. She loves her family, but in her heart, she questions if what she is working so hard to accomplish makes any difference at all. She didn’t always feel bogged down, and she wondered what changed to make her feel overwhelmed so much of the time.

Sometimes busyness increases so gradually that we barely recognize the change. Busyness, given the chance, will overload us with more obligations than we can realistically get done in one day, or one week, or even one lifetime. Then, without warning, we reach the overload point when we feel as though we cannot possibly handle any more. Relentless overload can cause physical and mental exhaustion to the point where we feel deprived of enthusiasm, energy, and purpose. Some women seem to have a built-in indicator of where the overload line is. Others, like myself, struggle to find that balance. Constantly. There are so many good, interesting, and exciting options right at our fingertips; without much thought, we fill our days.

Concepts that contribute to overload

Playing multiple roles can be stressful. Overloading yourself with responsibilities and commitments can make you forget what is most important. It is easy to equate busyness with self-worth. By default, we start believing that:

  • Homemakers are capable of handling everything.
  • Homemakers, especially godly homemakers, are never frustrated.
  • A homemaker should anticipate all her family’s needs.

If we are honest, we know that these statements are unrealistic. Homemakers cannot do everything. All homemakers experience frustration occasionally. A mother cannot consistently be one step ahead of her family’s needs.

Rethinking the busy life

Household duties and caring for our families fill our days. Sometimes those tasks alone make us extremely busy. But what about the extra-circular activities or the high standard we hold ourselves to? We may need to think differently so we can break free from habits that threaten to control us.

Accept your limits

Maybe you can go to a Tupperware party, attend a Bible study, and repaint the bathroom all in one week. But should you? Good homemakers allow themselves to simplify even if they prefer doing it another way. That means if you are an avid bread maker, it’s all right to toss a few loaves of bread into your shopping cart.

Evaluate what causes frustrations

Artificial smiles can hide inner frustrations, but it doesn’t cure them. It works best to admit that there is a problem and then seek a solution. I’ve had to learn this repeatedly. All my family members know that we eat dinner at 5:30. But a late arrival habit is trending, and it bothers me.

When I told my husband about the frustration, he simply said, “Why don’t you explain the issue and quit being so uptight about it?” Good point. Proactively seeking solutions works for many problem areas.

Imperfect women make good homemakers

Quit worrying about perfection and make decisions based on what is best for today. Fun-loving, happy, homemakers might have a few dust bunnies under the furniture, but they radiate an aura that draws people to their hearts and homes.

Everyone differs when it comes to how much we can handle. On the other hand, everyone is the same; we all have limits. In future installments, we will discuss how to deal with common points of overload.

Part 2

Many homemakers find themselves stretched thin among commitments that go with home, family, and other activities. As busy as we are, why do we continue to fill our schedules fuller?

It is easy for me to commit to a new project and then realize, halfway into the task, that I have overstepped my limits. Too often, I overestimate the amount of time I must have to complete a project and underestimate the amount of time a task will take.

Commitment overload happens by default. When we play multiple roles and add more responsibilities, we can easily become slaves to the promises we have made. Overload tends to drain our energy, dull our senses, and deaden our joy.

Recognizing Overload

Sometimes multiple activities take place in rapid sequence. Normally, we can flow with short-term spurts of busyness. But if the flow of activities is never-ending and we keep adding more obligations, we develop a pattern that becomes a way of life.

Too many commitments beyond normal duties make us candidates for depression and burnout. Personally, when I experience insomnia, apathy, or irritability, it is time to examine my schedule. If adjustments aren’t made, someone or something will suffer.

No one can overextend themselves indefinitely. Sometimes we suffer consequences for keeping a pace that is beyond our resources. Symptoms of overload can include lack of sleep, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure, and a susceptible immune system.

Breaking Free of Overload

Identifying overload takes an honest evaluation of yourself. How can you know if this is just a busy season or if busyness is the new normal? Are you declining a request because life is too full, or is it an excuse? Do you have to say “yes” on the spot? With practice, you can learn how to pull back before reaching the overload point.

Let an idea or request gel before committing

This has saved me a great deal of stress. There are so many good things to be involved in, and new inspirations come daily. Sometimes tasks can be incorporated into my/our schedule. Other times I must simply let them go and stay focused on what is most important. Consider waiting a few hours before incorporating new ideas and requests.

Seek advice, especially your husband’s

A renowned doughnut maker was asked to have a stand at an auction. She asked her husband what he thought about it. He said, “As long as you don’t complain and stress about it like you did last year, I don’t care.” Was her husband saying “yes” or “no”? This lady should take the cue that doughnut making was somehow adding stress. Either she should not do it, or together they must seek a workable solution.

Evaluate your schedule regularly

Keep a detailed calendar to have a picture of past, present, and future events. If your family had the flu last week and you plan to take an out-of-state trip next week, should you add more? What is the emotional health of your family? Is your husband stressed at work? Sometimes it is better to have a time slot of nothing so it can be filled with what is important now. You can’t do a good job at anything if you are spread too thin. Too many obligations make it hard to be personally refreshed and congenial. Choosing commitments wisely will help you invest your energy where it is most valuable for today.

Μέρος 1

Για την Άλις, η ζωή είναι εξαντλητική. Κάθε μέρα μοιάζει με ατελείωτο μόχθο. Αγαπά την οικογένειά της, αλλά μέσα της αμφιβάλλει αν ό,τι προσπαθεί τόσο σκληρά να πετύχει έχει πραγματικά κάποια σημασία. Δεν ένιωθε πάντα καταβεβλημένη, και αναρωτιόταν τι άλλαξε ώστε να νιώθει τόσο συχνά υπερφορτωμένη.

Μερικές φορές η πολυασχόληση αυξάνεται τόσο βαθμιαία που σχεδόν δεν αντιλαμβανόμαστε την αλλαγή. Η πολυασχόληση, αν της δοθεί η ευκαιρία, θα μας υπερφορτώσει με περισσότερες υποχρεώσεις απ’ όσες πραγματικά μπορούμε να φέρουμε εις πέρας σε μία μέρα, ή μία εβδομάδα, ή ακόμα και σε μια ζωή. Έπειτα, χωρίς προειδοποίηση, φτάνουμε στο σημείο υπερφόρτωσης όπου νιώθουμε πως δεν μπορούμε να αντεπεξέλθουμε σε τίποτα περισσότερο. Η διαρκής υπερφόρτωση μπορεί να προκαλέσει σωματική και πνευματική εξάντληση έως ότου χάσουμε τον ενθουσιασμό, την ενέργεια και το σκοπό μας. Κάποιες γυναίκες μοιάζει να έχουν έναν έμφυτο δείκτη για το που βρίσκεται η γραμμή υπερφόρτωσης. Άλλες, όπως εγώ, δυσκολεύονται συνεχώς να βρουν εκείνη την ισορροπία. Υπάρχουν τόσες πολλές καλές, ενδιαφέρουσες και συναρπαστικές επιλογές μπροστά μας· χωρίς πολλή σκέψη, γεμίζουμε τις μέρες μας.

Έννοιες που συμβάλλουν στην υπερφόρτωση

Η ανάληψη πολλών ρόλων μπορεί να είναι στρεσογόνα. Η υπερφόρτωση με ευθύνες και δεσμεύσεις μπορεί να σε κάνει να ξεχάσεις τι είναι το πιο σημαντικό. Είναι εύκολο να ταυτίσουμε την πολυασχόληση με την αυτοαξία. Από προεπιλογή, αρχίζουμε να πιστεύουμε ότι:

  • Οι νοικοκυρές είναι ικανές να τα κάνουν όλα.
  • Οι νοικοκυρές, ειδικά οι ευσεβείς νοικοκυρές, δεν απογοητεύονται ποτέ.
  • Μια νοικοκυρά πρέπει να προβλέπει όλες τις ανάγκες της οικογένειάς της.

Αν είμαστε ειλικρινείς, ξέρουμε ότι αυτές οι δηλώσεις είναι μη ρεαλιστικές. Οι νοικοκυρές δεν μπορούν να κάνουν τα πάντα. Όλες οι νοικοκυρές βιώνουν περιστασιακά απογοήτευση. Μια μητέρα δεν μπορεί διαρκώς να βρίσκεται ένα βήμα μπροστά από τις ανάγκες της οικογένειάς της.

Επαναπροσδιορίζοντας τη γεμάτη ζωή

Οι οικιακές δουλειές και η φροντίδα των οικογενειών μας γεμίζουν τις μέρες μας. Μερικές φορές αυτές οι εργασίες από μόνες τους μας κάνουν εξαιρετικά πολυάσχολες. Αλλά τι γίνεται με τις εξωσχολικές δραστηριότητες ή το υψηλό πρότυπο που θέτουμε για τον εαυτό μας; Μπορεί να χρειαστεί να σκεφτούμε διαφορετικά ώστε να απελευθερωθούμε από συνήθειες που απειλούν να μας ελέγξουν.

Αποδέξου τα όριά σου

Ίσως μπορείς να πας σε ένα πάρτι Tupperware, να παρακολουθήσεις μια μελέτη Βίβλου και να ξαναβάψεις το μπάνιο μέσα στην ίδια εβδομάδα. Αλλά πρέπει; Οι καλές νοικοκυρές επιτρέπουν στον εαυτό τους να απλοποιήσει ακόμη και αν προτιμούν να το κάνουν με διαφορετικό τρόπο. Αυτό σημαίνει πως αν είσαι ενθουσιώδης αρτοπαρασκευάστρια, είναι εντάξει να βάλεις μερικές φρατζόλες στον καλάθι των αγορών σου.

Αξιολόγησε τι προκαλεί απογοητεύσεις

Τα τεχνητά χαμόγελα μπορούν να κρύψουν εσωτερικές απογοητεύσεις, αλλά δεν τις θεραπεύουν. Είναι καλύτερο να παραδεχτείς ότι υπάρχει πρόβλημα και μετά να αναζητήσεις λύση. Έχω χρειαστεί να μάθω αυτό ξανά και ξανά. Όλη μου η οικογένεια ξέρει ότι τρώμε δείπνο στις 5:30. Αλλά η συνήθεια των αργοποριών γίνεται μόδα, και αυτό με ενοχλεί.

Όταν μίλησα στον άντρα μου για την απογοήτευση, απλώς είπε, «Γιατί δεν εξηγείς το ζήτημα και δεν είσαι τόσο αγχωμένη γι’ αυτό;» Καλό σημείο. Η προληπτική αναζήτηση λύσεων λειτουργεί σε πολλούς τομείς προβλημάτων.

Ατελείς γυναίκες γίνονται καλές νοικοκυρές

Σταμάτησε να ανησυχείς για την τελειότητα και πάρε αποφάσεις βάσει του τι είναι καλύτερο για σήμερα. Οι αστειογνώστριες, χαρούμενες νοικοκυρές μπορεί να έχουν λίγη σκόνη κάτω από τα έπιπλα, αλλά εκπέμπουν μια αύρα που προσελκύει τους ανθρώπους στις καρδιές και τα σπίτια τους.

Όλοι διαφέρουμε στο πόσα μπορούμε να αντέξουμε. Από την άλλη πλευρά, όλοι είμαστε ίδιοι· έχουμε όρια. Σε μελλοντικά μέρη θα συζητήσουμε πώς να αντιμετωπίζουμε κοινά σημεία υπερφόρτωσης.

Μέρος 2

Πολλές νοικοκυρές νιώθουν πως τεντώνονται πέρα ως πέρα ανάμεσα σε υποχρεώσεις που συνοδεύουν το σπίτι, την οικογένεια και άλλες δραστηριότητες. Όσο πολυάσχολες κι αν είμαστε, γιατί συνεχίζουμε να γεμίζουμε ακόμη περισσότερο το πρόγραμμά μας;

Μου είναι εύκολο να δεσμευτώ σε ένα νέο πρότζεκτ και μετά να συνειδητοποιήσω, στη μέση της δουλειάς, ότι ξεπέρασα τα όριά μου. Πολύ συχνά υπερεκτιμώ τον χρόνο που θα χρειαστώ για να ολοκληρώσω ένα έργο και υποτιμώ τον χρόνο που θα πάρει μια εργασία.

Η υπερφόρτωση δεσμεύσεων συμβαίνει από προεπιλογή. Όταν παίζουμε πολλούς ρόλους και προσθέτουμε περισσότερες ευθύνες, μπορούμε εύκολα να γίνουμε σκλάβοι των υποσχέσεων που έχουμε δώσει. Η υπερφόρτωση τείνει να μας αποστραγγίζει την ενέργεια, να μουντάρει τις αισθήσεις μας και να αμβλύνει τη χαρά μας.

Αναγνωρίζοντας την υπερφόρτωση

Μερικές φορές πολλές δραστηριότητες συμβαίνουν σε γρήγορη αλληλουχία. Κανονικά, μπορούμε να ρέουμε με τις βραχυπρόθεσμες εξάρσεις πολυασχόλησης. Αλλά αν η ροή των δραστηριοτήτων δεν τελειώνει ποτέ και συνεχίζουμε να προσθέτουμε περισσότερες υποχρεώσεις, αναπτύσσουμε ένα μοτίβο που γίνεται τρόπος ζωής.

Πολύ πολλές δεσμεύσεις πέρα από τα κανονικά καθήκοντα μας κάνουν υποψήφιες για κατάθλιψη και εξουθένωση. Προσωπικά, όταν βιώνω αϋπνία, απάθεια ή ευερεθιστότητα, είναι καιρός να εξετάσω το πρόγραμμα μου. Αν δεν γίνουν προσαρμογές, κάτι ή κάποιος θα υποφέρει.

Κανείς δεν μπορεί να υπερεκτείνεται επ’ αόριστον. Μερικές φορές υφιστάμεθα συνέπειες επειδή διατηρούμε έναν ρυθμό που υπερβαίνει τους πόρους μας. Τα συμπτώματα της υπερφόρτωσης μπορούν να περιλαμβάνουν έλλειψη ύπνου, επιβαρυμένες σχέσεις, αναβλητικότητα, φόβο αποτυχίας και ευαισθησία του ανοσοποιητικού συστήματος.

Απελευθέρωση από την υπερφόρτωση

Η αναγνώριση της υπερφόρτωσης απαιτεί ειλικρινή αυτοαξιολόγηση. Πώς μπορείς να ξέρεις αν αυτό είναι απλώς μια πολυάσχολη περίοδος ή αν η πολυασχόληση είναι ο νέος κανόνας; Αρνείσαι ένα αίτημα επειδή η ζωή σου είναι υπερβολικά γεμάτη, ή είναι μια δικαιολογία; Πρέπει να λες «ναι» στην ίδια στιγμή; Με άσκηση, μπορείς να μάθεις πώς να υποχωρείς πριν φτάσεις στο σημείο υπερφόρτωσης.

Άφησε μια ιδέα ή ένα αίτημα να ωριμάσει πριν δεσμευτείς

Αυτό μου έχει γλιτώσει από μεγάλο στρες. Υπάρχουν τόσα πολλά καλά πράγματα για να συμμετάσχεις, και νέες έμπνευσεις έρχονται καθημερινά. Μερικές φορές εργασίες μπορούν να ενταχθούν στο πρόγραμμά μου/μας. Άλλες φορές πρέπει απλώς να τις αφήσω να φύγουν και να παραμείνω επικεντρωμένη σε ό,τι είναι πιο σημαντικό. Σκέψου να περιμένεις μερικές ώρες πριν εντάξεις νέες ιδέες και αιτήματα.

Ζήτησε συμβουλή, ειδικά από τον άντρα σου

Μια γνωστή παρασκευάστρια ντόνατς της προτάθηκε να έχει πάγκο σε μια δημοπρασία. Ρώτησε τον άντρα της τι νομίζει. Εκείνος είπε, «Εφόσον δεν παραπονιέσαι και δεν αγχώνεσαι όπως έκανες πέρυσι, δεν με νοιάζει.» Έλεγε ο άντρας της «ναι» ή «όχι»; Αυτή η κυρία θα πρέπει να πάρει το μήνυμα ότι η παρασκευή ντόνατς πρόσθετε κάποιο άγχος. Είτε να μην το κάνει, είτε μαζί να βρουν μια ρεαλιστική λύση.

Αξιολόγησε το πρόγραμμα σου τακτικά

Κράτησε ένα λεπτομερές ημερολόγιο για να έχεις μια εικόνα παρελθόντων, παρόντων και μελλοντικών γεγονότων. Αν η οικογένειά σου είχε γρίπη την προηγούμενη εβδομάδα και σκοπεύεις να κάνεις ένα ταξίδι εκτός πολιτείας την επόμενη, πρέπει να προσθέσεις κι άλλα; Ποια είναι η συναισθηματική υγεία της οικογένειάς σου; Ο άντρας σου είναι πιεσμένος στη δουλειά; Μερικές φορές είναι καλύτερα να έχεις ένα κενό χρονικό σημείο ώστε να μπορεί να γεμίσει με ό,τι είναι σημαντικό τώρα. Δεν μπορείς να κάνεις κάτι καλά αν είσαι απλωμένη υπερβολικά. Πάρα πολλές υποχρεώσεις δυσκολεύουν το να είσαι προσωπικά ανανεωμένη και προσιτή. Η σοφή επιλογή δεσμεύσεων θα σε βοηθήσει να επενδύσεις την ενέργειά σου εκεί που είναι πιο πολύτιμη για σήμερα.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

Morals have to do with right and wrong behavior. Purity is being free from moral fault or guilt, marked by chastity, which is personal integrity. Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

מוסר קשור להתנהגות הנכונה והשגויה. טוהר הוא היעדר פגם מוסרי או אשמה, מסומן בכנות מינית ובשלמות אישית. טוהר אינו מכיל דבר שאינו שייך שם כהלכה. כפי שהכותרת מרמזת, מאמר זה יתמקד בעשיית הראוי ובהיותנו חפים מפגם מוסרי ואשמה, בחיי שלמות ובהבטחת שכל מה שבפנים ובחוץ יהיה נקי מדברים שאינם שייכים.

שימו לב למה שהתנ"ך אומר על היותנו טהורים. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

להיות טהור מבחינה מוסרית לא יקרה בלי נחישות ודיסיפלינה חזקה. זה תמיד היה כך, אך אפילו יותר כיום עם עליית הטכנולוגיה וזמינות הרע בקצות אצבעותינו.

חטאים מיניים אינם זרים לכנסייה. למעשה, הם אינם זרים לאף עם ולאף גזע. איננו יכולים להירגע ולהוריד את המשמר ולסבור שילדינו יהיו בטוחים מפני רעי החברה והאדם. עלינו להראות בדוגמה וללמד את ילדינו ונוערנו אם אנו מצפים שהם יישארו טהורים בחברה מושחתת זו. איננו יכולים להניח שאם אדם מתלבש בצורה מסוימת — הכול תקין בפנים. הסיפור אינו מסופר במלואו רק על ידי המראה החיצוני. הפרושים גרמו לחיצוניות להיראות טובה, בעוד שהפנים היו מלאים בשחיתות. ישוע אמר, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). גם אנו צריכים לתת תשומת לב עיקרית לנושאי הלב. כשהלב נקי, גם החיצוניות תוכל להיות מטוהרת.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

מסר זה נועד להיות מסר של תקווה, לא ייאוש. אם יש לך נקודה חשוכה סודית, התוודה עליה והיפטר ממנה. אתה יכול להשתחרר! אפשר להשתחרר מאחיזתו של השטן ולחיות חיים פתוחים ושקופים עם שמחה בנפש. אינך צריך לעבור את החיים מנסה להסתיר את חשכת הרע. ישוע רוצה לסלוח ולרפא.

השטן אכזר. ב־John 10:10 ישוע אמר, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

חטא מוסרי כל כך מביש וקשה להודות בו. הדבר הטבעי הוא לנסות להסתיר כשעוברים על החוק. ילדים הלומדים להסתיר מעשים רעים בגיל צעיר מפתחים באופן טבעי לנוער שמסתיר דברים מהורים, ממורים ומשרתי כנסייה. אדם כזה יצטרך ללמוד להיות פתוח ושקוף, או שיגיע הזמן שבו יתחיל להסתיר דברים גם ממלווהו. ההסתרה גורמת לחיים כפולים ומובילה ליותר עבדות ולמערכות יחסים שבורות. אנשים שיש להם דלתות סגורות בפינות מסוימות של חייהם יהיו קנאים לגבי הטלפונים שלהם ולא יסכימו לשתף סיסמאות עם בן/בת זוג מהימן. נדמה שאנו שוכחים בקלות כמה חסר תועלת להסתיר מאלוהים. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” כיצד נוכל להיות כה תמימים וטפשים לחשוב שנוכל להסתיר משהו מאלוהים? או לקחת צעד נוסף: למה היינו רוצים להסתיר משהו ממנו? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” אלוהים אוהב אותך יותר מדי כדי לא לאפשר לך להמשיך להסתיר מה שצריך להיחשף ולהיות מסולח.

חטאים מיניים גם הם מטעות ביותר. בדרך כלל זה קורה כפי ש־James תיאר בפרק הראשון. אנו מתפתים, נמשכים הצידה, נמשך כמו מגנט ממוקד, מרגישים גל של תשוקה, מוודאים שאיש אינו מסתכל, מכסים את עקבותינו, מתקרבים צעד קרוב יותר לאסור, מרגישים עוד תשוקה, ומתחילים מהר לאבד שיקול דעת ומחשבה שפויה, לא מסוגלים לחשב תוצאות בדומה לאדם שכר, ואז James 1:15 קורה: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James יאמר לנו שלא להשתוקק לדברים שאינם שלנו, אפילו לא כהרף עין. התנ"ך מצווה אותנו לברוח משלושה דברים. אחד מהם הוא זנון, שניתן להרחיבו לכל החטאים המיניים. אל תתעסקו עם זה; אל תביטו שוב; התרחקו ממנו! החליפו את המחשבות הללו במחשבות בונות על אלוהים ודרכו. שירו המנון ישן; תודה לאל שאיננו יכולים לחשוב על שני דברים בו־זמנית. לא משנה מה צריך, ברח מהתשוקה הזו. היא תקח אותך רחוק יותר ממה שתרצה ותעלה לך יותר ממה שתהיה מוכן לשלם. רוץ את הסרט עד הסוף ושאל את עצמך, אם אלך אחרי מה שמתפתים אליו, האם אקבל את מה שאני רוצה? השטן תמיד מבטיח עונג, אך מספק כאב. זכרו, השטן מעולם לא המציא הנאה; הוא רק לוקח מה שאלוהים עשה טהור וטוב, מקלקל אותו, ומציע אותו חזרה בצורה מעוותת. זכרו, חרב השטן שלופה כדי להרוג בנקודה זו. ברחו מהרצונות הרעים!

אל תלכו אחרי התשוקה שלכם. פורנוגרפיה ממכרת מאוד ושיתקה רבים. Promise Keepers אמרו שסקר שלהם מצא כי 65% מהגברים התמכרו. התמכרות לפורנו דומה להתמכרות לאלכוהול או לסמים. הם אומרים לנו שהמוח דורש שאנדורפינים יוזרמו אליו, בין אם מהתמכרות לאלכוהול, לסמים או לפורנו. אני מדגיש שוב שהגברים והנשים שיעלו לניצחון יהיו אלה ש, כמו דניאל בימי קדם, יתחייבו בלבם לא להתנכר.

נושא זה גם מיועד לאחיותינו, וכמה שאלות נראות הולמות. מה בחייך הפנימיים מסודר ומוסתר היטב? האם אכזבות החיים יצרו ריק שמוביל לנטילת ׳טיילנול רגשי׳ שגורם לך להרגיש טוב לזמן קצר? האם הקשר הרגשי שלך בטוח במקום שאלוהים תכנן שיהיה?

נערות צעירות צריכות ללמוד לפתח שמירת מרחק בריאה מול גברים. לא בגישה מתנשאת ולעולם לא ללא חיוך, אך גם לא בחופשיות יתר בקשר לנערים. החברה שלנו מכוונת בדיוק להפך, ומגן ילדים מבית הספר היסודי והלאה מציקים לבנים ולבנות לגבי חברות מיוחדות. כתוצאה מכך, ילדים גדלים עם מעט או בלי שמירת מרחק. יש להימנע מהתכתבות חברתית בין המינים מחוץ ליחסים משפחתיים. זה יפתח אצל הנוער הרגל שיום אחד יצטרך להישבר אם הם מצפים לחיות חיים פתוחים ושקופים עם בן/בת זוג. חשבו על זה כך: האם היית רוצה שבן/בת זוגך תתכתב חברתית עם המין השני ברשתות החברתיות?

אחיות, היזהרו מספרי קריאה שאתם קוראות. רומנים רומנטיים מקהים את התאווה לתורת האלוהים ויוצרים ציפיות בלתי מציאותיות מחיי נישואין. ספרים אלה מעבירים את הרעיון שהאיש הנכון אי שם יהיה המפתח למימוש ואושר בחיים. רק ישוע יכול למלא את החור שהחטא גרם לכל אדם היום. אף גבר או אישה לא יוכלו אי פעם לתת את הביטחון והשקט של הנפש שכולנו כל כך כוונים אליו. הכאב הזה בלב לעולם לא ישותה על ידי פלסטרים או משככי כאבים. הם עוזרים רק לרגע, וכאשר הם פגתים, הצעקה של הלב חזקה אף יותר. ספרים בלתי בריאים מקהים את הטעם לדברים של אלוהים, ובמקומם יוצרים תאווה למזון מהיר ונכסים מרגיעי כאב.

דאגה נוספת לאחיות היא כמות הזמן שאתן מבלות ברשת. אין גבול להאכיל את התאווה ליופי, ייחודיות, חן ומראה. אל תתנו לדברים אלה להניע את חייכן כי הם לעולם לא יאמרו 'די' ולא ימלאו את הנפש ולא יכוונו את ילדיכן בדרך הנכונה. שקלו את כמות הזמן שאתן משקיעות באירוח מסיבות. במהלך השנים ראיתי שמות של הזדמנויות עסקיות ומוצרים שבמשך תקופה צריך היה להחזיק — אך לצערי, אחרי כמה שנים איננו זוכרים אפילו את השמות האלה ובינתיים הילדים גדלו וכעת הם בוגרים. שקלו את הצרכים האמיתיים בחייכן ואת אחריותכן, ואז החליטו מה יביא השקעה נצחית. נשים עם ילדים צריכות להגביל תחביבים שנהנות מהם מאוד כיוון שלרגע זה, הן מבורכות בילדים בעלי נשמות נצחיות וזמן איתם הוא השקעה נצחית. זכרו שבעליכן וילדיכן ראויים בהרבה לזמנכן מאשר בילוי שעות במסיבה נוספת.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

אלוהים יצר אותנו כך שכאשר אנו אוהבים את הדברים שאלוהים אוהב, ללבנו עדיין יש מקום לאהוב עוד. לא חשוב כמה ילדים, נכדים או ידידים קדושים יש לנו, ללבנו עדיין יש מקום לאהבה נוספת. אך ברגע שאנו מתחילים לאהוב את מה שאלוהים אסר, זה מתחיל להחליף ולהשמיד כל אהבה אחרת, ממלא את לבנו בריק, בכאב ובבדידות, מה שמוביל לסוף מר.

רבים מהגברים חזרו להכרה וראו את הטיפשות המוחלטת של הדרך שבה הלכו. חלקם ניסו להסתיר התנהגות טמאה והצליחו עד מאוחר בחייהם. אחרים שמרו זאת בסתר עד שאחרי מותם נחשף הדבר. שאלה למחשבה: האם זה שווה את זה? כמובן שהתשובה היא לא מוחלטת!

כמה נפלא לחיות חיים פתוחים חסרי אשמה ולקבל שלום עם אלוהים וביטחון במחיקת החטאים, כדי שיום אחד ניוצא מהעולם הרע הזה ונכניס לנוכחות אלוהינו הקדוש.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

A wonderful thing about being a Christian is anticipating the day when we feast our eyes on the magnificent beauty of our God. Quite likely, we have all created mental pictures of what we think God might look like, although we know that our wildest imaginations will be exceeded. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). The Bible is full of descriptive word pictures attempting to give us a brief glimpse into the realms of the heavenly. The landscape on the hills of glory, the wonderful creatures that dwell there, and most of all, the Supreme Being on the throne, all defy our human attempt to grasp and understand the beauty and glory of our God.

At times we admire beauty in a song, a work of art, a story, or even another person, but David describes the delight of gazing at the beauty of God. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). God is beautiful because His excellence is attractive— His character is flawless. David experienced the pleasure that comes from knowing and experiencing God in all His fullness. How does God express His Beauty?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). In the awfulness of the Passion of Christ, we find a profound and sober beauty— the beauty of a sacrifice made by a sinless Savior for undeserving humanity. Sometimes the most stirring kind of beauty is found in things we cannot fully comprehend.

There is beauty in weeping of Mary and the disciples around the cross that held the lifeless body of their beloved Master. But when dawn broke on resurrection morning, despair turned into hope and grief into joy.

We see a beautiful scene at the Mount of Olives forty days later as the same disciples wistfully gazed into the sky, watching as their risen Lord disappeared into the heavens. With great joy, they returned to Jerusalem, with the promise of His return burning in their hearts, to wait for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

Today we expectantly wait for the Son of God to appear from heaven with power and great glory to complete the work of salvation. Then will we look upon Him in all His splendor and beauty. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

How should we, as God's image-bearers, reflect His beauty through the Gospel? God is an uncreated eternal being, and man was created in His image to reflect His glory and beauty. However, this beauty has been marred by sin and is no longer a worthy representation of God's character. But, there is redemption! Very little surpasses the beauty of a life that was once bruised and broken by sin but is now restored, redeemed, and made whole by the Gospel. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Atheists challenge the existence of God, scientists argue against Biblical creation, scholars question the inerrancy of scripture, but nobody can dispute the testimony of a redeemed life.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). All beauty in the created world comes from God. A beautiful sunset, a lovely rose, a towering redwood, a majestic mountain peak, all testify of the beauty of God illustrated in creation. As road signs along the highway guide us to our destination, likewise, creation directs mankind to God himself. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). These gifts of creation are given to give us a brief glimpse of the One who created them.

How should we, as part of God's creation, reflect His creative beauty? Although we cannot make something out of nothing, God has designed us to be creative, using the resources of His creation and our intellectual abilities to make life practical. The fulfilling sense of accomplishment derived from a job well done has its origin in creation, where God regarded His work and declared it to be good. In our attempt to live non-extravagant lives we sometimes fail to take joy in the beautiful things in life. It is right and good and in harmony with how we were created to find pleasure in things of beauty. Ungodly men have used this gift of creativity many times for evil means. So much the more, let us glorify God by using His creation in ways that reflect His character.

A warning for all who love nature and creation (natural and man-made): let us be careful to not elevate earthly beauty above the Creator, which leads to idolatry. Sunsets fade, redwoods tumble, roses wilt, the human body turns to dust again, but God remains. Life and all of its beauty begins and ends with God.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) According to the book of Revelation, God's throne is surrounded by sound: thundering and lightning; praises flowing from the angels, the four beasts and twenty elders, and the great multitude which no man can number; and the new song by the one hundred and forty four thousand.

God created the beauty of sound to glorify Himself in ways that mere words cannot. The intricacy of His creativity is powerfully displayed in the way various sound frequencies come together to create a beautiful and heavenly harmony. It is honoring to God for mankind to take pleasure in the beauty of sounds He has created for His glory. The person who loves God will be drawn to Him whenever He is serenaded by pleasing sounds: the people of God singing the songs of Zion, the prayers of the saints, the wind whispering through the treetops, the songbird praising its Maker, the rumble of thunder, or the simple patter of rain on the roof.

How should we, as instruments of sound, reflect God's beauty through sound? We should always seek to listen to and resemble the sounds and harmonies of heaven. Although we will never be able to completely accomplish this on earth, it should be a lifelong endeavor. The questions have been asked,” Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” and “when have we reached ‘good enough’?” We will never be able to attain heavenly perfection, so the question should rather be asked, “Are we giving God the best we have?” Some people have more singing capabilities than others, but the question remains. “Are we giving our best or are we satisfied with an inferior sacrifice?” Let us be producers of God-honoring sounds that bring joy to the heart of the Creator!

Through the Church:

The Bible speaks extensively about the beauty of God's people. “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” and“The Church” are synonymous expressions woven throughout scripture referring to the habitation of God's people on the earth. It is God's desire that His beauty would be reflected in the lives of His people. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Nothing is dearer to the heart of God than His church. When the children of Israel journeyed through the wilderness, they built the tabernacle as a place for God to dwell among them. When Solomon dedicated the temple as God's dwelling place, God was very pleased and 2 Chronicles 7:1 says the glory of the Lord filled the temple. The temple was considered the House of the Lord–Jesus himself referred to it numerous times as God's house and was very passionate that it should be kept holy.

Today, neither the tabernacle nor the temple hosts the presence of God but rather His divine passion is concentrated on the church of Jesus Christ. Here are the people who truly love Him and are willing to lay down their lives for Him. Here are the people who are willing to give up their rights as individuals and surrender themselves to a greater cause. Here is where many a saint has given His very life's blood for the Gospel. And here is where one day our Savior will return as He has promised, and will transport His bride, the church, to her eternal habitation. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

How should we, as God's people, reflect His beauty in the church? By dwelling together in unity and harmony with love for all men, especially the household of God. The church should be a place where the world can get a glimpse of what goes on in heaven. It should be a place where Christ is always elevated as the victorious conqueror of sin, death, and hell.

Sadly, many people have become disoriented with the church's failures and have walked away from the true apostolic faith. In spite of our disappointments, let us “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) and let us press on. We will never have a higher calling, and never a more noble warfare to wage.

Lastly, how should we reflect His beauty in our lives? By delighting in Him. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). The greatest fulfillment in life comes from finding pleasure in bringing joy to the heart of God by delighting in what He delights in and loving what He loves. Let us never lose the wonder of the beauty of our Salvation!
