Morals have to do with right and wrong behavior. Purity is being free from moral fault or guilt, marked by chastity, which is personal integrity. Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

La moral tiene que ver con el comportamiento correcto e incorrecto. La pureza es estar libre de culpa o falta moral, marcada por la castidad, que es integridad personal. La pureza no contiene nada que no pertenezca debidamente allí. Como sugiere el título, este artículo tratará de obrar correctamente y estar libre de culpa o falta moral, de vivir una vida de integridad y de mantener nuestro interior y exterior libres de todo aquello que no pertenece debidamente.

Fíjate en lo que dice la Escritura sobre ser puro. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” En otras palabras, son las personas que están limpias por dentro y por fuera las que verán a Dios y entrarán en Su presencia.

Ser moralmente puro no ocurrirá sin una fuerte determinación y disciplina. Siempre ha sido así, pero hoy más aún con el auge de la tecnología y la disponibilidad del mal al alcance de nuestros dedos.

Los pecados sexuales no son extraños a la iglesia. De hecho, no son extraños a ningún pueblo de ninguna raza. No podemos relajarnos y bajar la guardia pensando que nuestros hijos estarán a salvo de los males de la sociedad y de nuestra humanidad. Debemos predicar con el ejemplo y enseñar a nuestros hijos y jóvenes si esperamos que permanezcan limpios en esta sociedad corrupta. No podemos suponer que si una persona se viste de cierta manera, todo esté bien por dentro. La historia no se cuenta completamente por el exterior. Los fariseos hacían que lo exterior pareciera bien, mientras que el interior estaba lleno de corrupción. Jesús dijo: “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). Nosotros también debemos prestar atención primordial a los asuntos del corazón. Cuando el corazón está limpio, entonces el exterior también podrá limpiarse.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” La oscuridad interna destruirá siempre la comunión y matará las relaciones—siempre.

Esto pretende ser un mensaje de esperanza, no de desaliento. Si tienes un punto oscuro oculto, confésalo y deshazte de él. ¡Puedes ser libre! Es posible librarse de las garras de Satanás y vivir una vida abierta y transparente con gozo en el alma. No necesitas pasar la vida intentando ocultar la oscuridad del mal. Jesús quiere perdonar y sanar.

Satanás es cruel. En John 10:10, Jesús dijo, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” todas las relaciones piadosas. Su interés es romper tu hogar, destruir tu respeto y enviarte al infierno. Todo el tiempo, él te está seduciendo por la lujuria de tu carne, con su espada desenvainada para atarte y matarte.

El pecado moral es tan vergonzoso y difícil de admitir. Lo natural es intentar esconderse cuando obramos mal. Los niños que aprenden a ocultar las malas acciones tempranamente en la vida naturalmente se convierten en jóvenes que ocultan cosas a los padres, a los maestros y a los ministros. Esta persona necesitará aprender a ser abierta y transparente, o llegará un momento en que estará ocultando cosas a su compañero. Ocultar resulta en una doble vida y conduce a más esclavitud y relaciones rotas. Las personas que tienen puertas cerradas en algunos rincones de su vida serán posesivas con sus teléfonos y no querrán compartir sus contraseñas con una pareja de confianza. Parece que olvidamos con facilidad lo inútil que es esconderse de Dios. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” ¿Cómo podemos ser tan ingenuos y necios de pensar que podemos ocultarle algo a Dios? O yendo un paso más allá: ¿Por qué querríamos ocultarle algo a Él? Numbers 32:23 sigue siendo muy verdadero al decir, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” Dios te ama demasiado como para dejar que sigas escondiendo lo que necesita salir a la luz y ser perdonado.

Los pecados sexuales también son extremadamente engañosos. Generalmente suceden como lo describió Santiago en el capítulo uno. Somos atraídos, apartados, jalados como un imán fuera de centro, sentimos un oleada de deseo, nos aseguramos de que nadie esté mirando y cubrimos nuestras huellas, damos un paso más hacia lo prohibido, sentimos más deseo y comenzamos muy rápidamente a perder el razonamiento y el pensamiento sano, incapaces de calcular las consecuencias muy parecido a una persona intoxicada; entonces ocurre James 1:15: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” El versículo 16 dice, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

Santiago nos diría que no codiciemos lo que no es nuestro, ni siquiera una insinuación. La Biblia nos manda huir de tres cosas. Una de ellas es la fornicación, que puede ampliarse a todos los pecados sexuales. No juegues con ello; no mires dos veces; aléjate. Sustituye esos pensamientos por pensamientos edificantes de Dios y Su camino. Canta un himno antiguo; por fortuna no podemos pensar en dos cosas a la vez. Hagas lo que hagas, huye de ese deseo lujurioso. Te llevará más lejos de lo que quieres ir y te costará más de lo que quieres pagar. Visualiza la cinta hasta el final y pregúntate: si sigo lo que estoy siendo tentado a hacer, ¿tendré lo que quiero? Satanás siempre promete placer, pero luego entrega dolor. Recuerda, Satanás nunca ha inventado un placer; solo toma lo que Dios hizo puro y bueno, lo pervierte y lo ofrece de vuelta en su forma pervertida. Recuerda, la espada de Satanás está desenvainada para matar en este punto. ¡Huye de los deseos malos!

No sigas tu lujuria. La pornografía es extremadamente adictiva y ha atrapado a muchas personas. Promise Keepers dijo que el 65% de los hombres en su encuesta eran adictos. La adicción a la pornografía es como el alcohol o las drogas. Nos dicen que el cerebro está pidiendo que se le viertan endorfinas, ya sea por adicción al alcohol, a las drogas o a la pornografía. Enfatizo nuevamente que los hombres y mujeres que lleguen a la victoria serán aquellos que, como Daniel de antaño, se propongan en su corazón no contaminarse.

Este tema también va dirigido a nuestras hermanas, y parecen apropiadas algunas preguntas. ¿Qué hay dentro de tu vida que está cuidadosamente guardado y oculto? ¿Las decepciones de la vida han causado un vacío que te hace tomar un «Tylenol emocional» que te hace sentir mejor por un corto tiempo? ¿Está tu conexión emocional segura en el lugar donde Dios la ha planeado?

Se debe enseñar a las jóvenes a desarrollar una reserva sana con los hombres. No con una actitud altiva y sin sonreír jamás, pero tampoco siendo demasiado sueltas al relacionarse con jóvenes varones. Nuestra sociedad va exactamente en sentido opuesto, y desde el jardín de infancia en adelante, niños y niñas son provocados sobre amistades especiales. Como resultado, los niños crecen con poca o ninguna reserva. Se debe evitar socializar mediante mensajes entre los géneros fuera de las relaciones familiares. Esto desarrollará un hábito en los jóvenes que algún día tendrá que romperse si esperan vivir una vida abierta y transparente con un cónyuge. Piénsalo así: ¿querrías que tu cónyuge socializara con el género opuesto en las redes sociales?

Hermanas, tengan cuidado con los libros que leen. Las novelas románticas adormecen el deseo por la Palabra de Dios y dan expectativas poco realistas de la vida conyugal. Estos libros transmiten la idea de que el hombre adecuado en algún lugar sería la llave para la plenitud y la felicidad en la vida. Solo Jesús puede llenar el hueco que el pecado ha traído a todo ser humano hoy. Ningún hombre ni mujer podrá jamás dar la seguridad y la tranquilidad del alma que todos anhelamos tanto. Este dolor en el corazón nunca se apagará con curitas ni analgésicos. Ayudan solo por un momento, y cuando se acaban, el clamor del corazón es aún más fuerte. Los libros insalubres adormecen el gusto por las cosas de Dios y, en cambio, crean un anhelo por comida chatarra y analgésicos.

Otra preocupación para las hermanas es la cantidad de tiempo que pasan en línea. No hay fin en alimentar el anhelo de lo refinado, lo único, el encanto y la belleza. No permitas que estas cosas sean el motor de tu vida, porque nunca dirán «basta» y no harán nada para satisfacer el alma ni para señalar a tus hijos en la dirección correcta. Considera la cantidad de tiempo que dedicas a organizar fiestas. A lo largo de los años, he visto nombres de oportunidades de negocio y productos que hay que tener venir y desaparecer. Pero, ay, en unos años ni siquiera recordamos esos nombres y mientras tanto los niños crecían y ahora son adultos. Considera las necesidades reales en tu vida y tus responsabilidades, y decide cuáles traerán inversiones eternas. Las mujeres con hijos necesitan limitar los pasatiempos que tanto disfrutan porque, en este momento, están bendecidas con hijos que tienen almas eternas y el tiempo con ellos es una inversión eterna. Recuerda que tu esposo y tus hijos merecen mucho más tu tiempo que pasar horas en otra fiesta.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” Se necesita humildad y quebrantamiento para reconocer nuestras necesidades, pero el quebrantamiento es la clave de la victoria. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. Una de las definiciones más comprensivas de gracia es la asistencia divina no merecida dada a los humanos para la regeneración y la santificación. La regeneración es la «gracia redentora», y la santificación es la «gracia transformadora». La verdad de esto es que Dios da «gracia transformadora» a los humildes. Esta gracia nos cambia de adentro hacia afuera haciéndonos santos. Este aspecto de la gracia debe ser deseado y buscado tanto como lo fue la gracia redentora cuando Dios nos salvó. Probablemente este sea el paso más importante para superar adicciones de cualquier tipo. Sé lo bastante humilde para convertirlo en una oración diaria a Dios por Su gracia transformadora. Jesús enseñó en Matthew 23:26, donde dijo: "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examina tus pensamientos, acciones, tentaciones, las cosas con las que luchas: ira, lujuria, orgullo, amargura, etc. ¿Eres tan espiritual como aparentas ser por fuera? Elimina el barniz y admite la necesidad de ayuda.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. Somos tan necios al pensar que podemos ocultar el mal. Podemos ocultarnos por un tiempo, pero algún día nuestras acciones estarán desnudas delante de un Dios omnisciente. ¿Por qué intentaríamos ocultar algo ahora? Esas cosas ocultas pueden ser llevadas delante del juicio, y una vida libre de culpa puede ser hoy una realidad. Sé transparente; debe ser una meta en acción.

Tell yourself the truth. Cuando eres tentado, considera el final de tu deseo lujurioso. ¿Obtendrás lo que quieres? ¿Se satisfará este ansia, o solo querrá más? Si vieras a tu hermano haciendo lo que persigues, ¿cómo se vería? ¿Cómo se verá dentro de treinta años si sigues tu deseo malo? ¿Traerá gozo o tristeza? ¿Será de ayuda para alguien, o asustará a otra persona? Dite la verdad antes de volverte intoxicado e incapaz de hacer juicios racionales.

Teach your eyes to bounce. No puedes controlar lo que miras la primera vez, pero sí puedes controlar lo que miras por segunda vez. Haz la práctica hasta que se vuelva hábito de desviar la mirada en otra dirección cada vez que veas algo que conduzca a pensamientos impuros.

Teaching our children. Esto debe pesar en nuestro corazón desde la primera infancia. Si no enseñamos a nuestros hijos que Dios nos hizo a Su imagen, la cual debe mantenerse pura, alguien más les enseñará a ser secretivos y a sentirse impuros. Mantente cerca de tus hijos y enséñales conforme maduran.

Keep your emotions. Esto es una salvaguarda en nuestra sociedad corrupta. Cuanto más te apartes de esto, más vulnerable serás a la corrupción. Mantén a tu cónyuge en primer lugar en la vida, a aquel con quien compartes y con quien estás ligado emocionalmente.

Flee lust and fornication. ¡Huye de ello! Estos antojos son adicciones que deben romperse. Recuerda, lo que alimentas crece, y lo que dejas morirá. Estas adicciones pueden romperse, pero necesitarás alimentar las relaciones que Dios te ha dado y dejar morir las perjudiciales.

Dios nos ha creado de tal manera que cuando amamos las cosas que Él ama, nuestro corazón aún tiene espacio para amar más. No importa cuántos hijos, nietos o amigos piadosos tengamos, nuestro corazón aún tiene espacio para amar más. Pero en el momento en que empezamos a amar lo que Dios ha prohibido, comienza a reemplazar y destruir todo otro amor, llenando nuestros corazones de vacío, dolor y soledad, lo que conduce a un final amargo.

Muchos hombres han vuelto en sí y han visto la absoluta necedad del camino que tomaron. Algunos intentaron ocultar conductas impuras y tuvieron éxito hasta muy tarde en la vida. Otros lo mantuvieron oculto hasta después de haber partido. Una pregunta para reflexionar: ¿vale la pena? Por supuesto, la respuesta es un rotundo ¡NO!

Qué maravilloso es vivir una vida abierta libre de culpa y tener paz con Dios y la certeza de los pecados perdonados, de modo que un día seamos sacados de este mundo malo y conducidos a la presencia de nuestro Santo Dios.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

A wonderful thing about being a Christian is anticipating the day when we feast our eyes on the magnificent beauty of our God. Quite likely, we have all created mental pictures of what we think God might look like, although we know that our wildest imaginations will be exceeded. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). The Bible is full of descriptive word pictures attempting to give us a brief glimpse into the realms of the heavenly. The landscape on the hills of glory, the wonderful creatures that dwell there, and most of all, the Supreme Being on the throne, all defy our human attempt to grasp and understand the beauty and glory of our God.

At times we admire beauty in a song, a work of art, a story, or even another person, but David describes the delight of gazing at the beauty of God. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). God is beautiful because His excellence is attractive— His character is flawless. David experienced the pleasure that comes from knowing and experiencing God in all His fullness. How does God express His Beauty?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). In the awfulness of the Passion of Christ, we find a profound and sober beauty— the beauty of a sacrifice made by a sinless Savior for undeserving humanity. Sometimes the most stirring kind of beauty is found in things we cannot fully comprehend.

There is beauty in weeping of Mary and the disciples around the cross that held the lifeless body of their beloved Master. But when dawn broke on resurrection morning, despair turned into hope and grief into joy.

We see a beautiful scene at the Mount of Olives forty days later as the same disciples wistfully gazed into the sky, watching as their risen Lord disappeared into the heavens. With great joy, they returned to Jerusalem, with the promise of His return burning in their hearts, to wait for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

Today we expectantly wait for the Son of God to appear from heaven with power and great glory to complete the work of salvation. Then will we look upon Him in all His splendor and beauty. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

How should we, as God's image-bearers, reflect His beauty through the Gospel? God is an uncreated eternal being, and man was created in His image to reflect His glory and beauty. However, this beauty has been marred by sin and is no longer a worthy representation of God's character. But, there is redemption! Very little surpasses the beauty of a life that was once bruised and broken by sin but is now restored, redeemed, and made whole by the Gospel. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Atheists challenge the existence of God, scientists argue against Biblical creation, scholars question the inerrancy of scripture, but nobody can dispute the testimony of a redeemed life.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). All beauty in the created world comes from God. A beautiful sunset, a lovely rose, a towering redwood, a majestic mountain peak, all testify of the beauty of God illustrated in creation. As road signs along the highway guide us to our destination, likewise, creation directs mankind to God himself. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). These gifts of creation are given to give us a brief glimpse of the One who created them.

How should we, as part of God's creation, reflect His creative beauty? Although we cannot make something out of nothing, God has designed us to be creative, using the resources of His creation and our intellectual abilities to make life practical. The fulfilling sense of accomplishment derived from a job well done has its origin in creation, where God regarded His work and declared it to be good. In our attempt to live non-extravagant lives we sometimes fail to take joy in the beautiful things in life. It is right and good and in harmony with how we were created to find pleasure in things of beauty. Ungodly men have used this gift of creativity many times for evil means. So much the more, let us glorify God by using His creation in ways that reflect His character.

A warning for all who love nature and creation (natural and man-made): let us be careful to not elevate earthly beauty above the Creator, which leads to idolatry. Sunsets fade, redwoods tumble, roses wilt, the human body turns to dust again, but God remains. Life and all of its beauty begins and ends with God.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) According to the book of Revelation, God's throne is surrounded by sound: thundering and lightning; praises flowing from the angels, the four beasts and twenty elders, and the great multitude which no man can number; and the new song by the one hundred and forty four thousand.

God created the beauty of sound to glorify Himself in ways that mere words cannot. The intricacy of His creativity is powerfully displayed in the way various sound frequencies come together to create a beautiful and heavenly harmony. It is honoring to God for mankind to take pleasure in the beauty of sounds He has created for His glory. The person who loves God will be drawn to Him whenever He is serenaded by pleasing sounds: the people of God singing the songs of Zion, the prayers of the saints, the wind whispering through the treetops, the songbird praising its Maker, the rumble of thunder, or the simple patter of rain on the roof.

How should we, as instruments of sound, reflect God's beauty through sound? We should always seek to listen to and resemble the sounds and harmonies of heaven. Although we will never be able to completely accomplish this on earth, it should be a lifelong endeavor. The questions have been asked,” Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” and “when have we reached ‘good enough’?” We will never be able to attain heavenly perfection, so the question should rather be asked, “Are we giving God the best we have?” Some people have more singing capabilities than others, but the question remains. “Are we giving our best or are we satisfied with an inferior sacrifice?” Let us be producers of God-honoring sounds that bring joy to the heart of the Creator!

Through the Church:

The Bible speaks extensively about the beauty of God's people. “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” and“The Church” are synonymous expressions woven throughout scripture referring to the habitation of God's people on the earth. It is God's desire that His beauty would be reflected in the lives of His people. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Nothing is dearer to the heart of God than His church. When the children of Israel journeyed through the wilderness, they built the tabernacle as a place for God to dwell among them. When Solomon dedicated the temple as God's dwelling place, God was very pleased and 2 Chronicles 7:1 says the glory of the Lord filled the temple. The temple was considered the House of the Lord–Jesus himself referred to it numerous times as God's house and was very passionate that it should be kept holy.

Today, neither the tabernacle nor the temple hosts the presence of God but rather His divine passion is concentrated on the church of Jesus Christ. Here are the people who truly love Him and are willing to lay down their lives for Him. Here are the people who are willing to give up their rights as individuals and surrender themselves to a greater cause. Here is where many a saint has given His very life's blood for the Gospel. And here is where one day our Savior will return as He has promised, and will transport His bride, the church, to her eternal habitation. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

How should we, as God's people, reflect His beauty in the church? By dwelling together in unity and harmony with love for all men, especially the household of God. The church should be a place where the world can get a glimpse of what goes on in heaven. It should be a place where Christ is always elevated as the victorious conqueror of sin, death, and hell.

Sadly, many people have become disoriented with the church's failures and have walked away from the true apostolic faith. In spite of our disappointments, let us “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) and let us press on. We will never have a higher calling, and never a more noble warfare to wage.

Lastly, how should we reflect His beauty in our lives? By delighting in Him. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). The greatest fulfillment in life comes from finding pleasure in bringing joy to the heart of God by delighting in what He delights in and loving what He loves. Let us never lose the wonder of the beauty of our Salvation!

Una cosa maravillosa de ser cristiano es anticipar el día en que contemplaremos la magnífica belleza de nuestro Dios. Muy probablemente todos hemos creado imágenes mentales de cómo pensamos que podría lucir Dios, aunque sabemos que nuestras más atrevidas imaginaciones serán superadas. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). La Biblia está llena de imágenes descriptivas que intentan darnos un breve vistazo a los reinos celestiales. El paisaje en las colinas de la gloria, las maravillosas criaturas que habitan allí y, sobre todo, el Ser Supremo en el trono, desafían cualquier intento humano por captar y comprender la belleza y la gloria de nuestro Dios.

A veces admiramos la belleza en una canción, una obra de arte, una historia o incluso en otra persona, pero David describe el deleite de contemplar la belleza de Dios. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). Dios es bello porque Su excelencia resulta atractiva: Su carácter es impecable. David experimentó el placer que proviene de conocer y experimentar a Dios en toda su plenitud. ¿Cómo expresa Dios Su Belleza?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). En lo estremecedor de la Pasión de Cristo hallamos una belleza profunda y sobria: la belleza de un sacrificio hecho por un Salvador sin pecado por una humanidad que no lo merece. A veces la clase de belleza que más conmueve se encuentra en cosas que no podemos comprender por completo.

Hay belleza en el llanto de María y de los discípulos junto a la cruz que sostenía el cuerpo inerte de su amado Maestro. Pero cuando amaneció la mañana de la resurrección, la desesperación se convirtió en esperanza y el dolor en alegría.

Vemos una escena hermosa en el Monte de los Olivos cuarenta días después, cuando los mismos discípulos miraban con añoranza al cielo, viendo cómo su Señor resucitado desaparecía en los cielos. Con gran gozo, regresaron a Jerusalén, con la promesa de Su venida ardiendo en sus corazones, para esperar la venida del Espíritu Santo.

Hoy aguardamos expectantes que el Hijo de Dios aparezca desde el cielo con poder y gran gloria para completar la obra de la salvación. Entonces le contemplaremos en todo su esplendor y belleza. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

¿Cómo deberíamos, como portadores de la imagen de Dios, reflejar Su belleza mediante el Evangelio? Dios es un ser eterno no creado, y el hombre fue creado a Su imagen para reflejar Su gloria y belleza. Sin embargo, esta belleza ha sido mancillada por el pecado y ya no es una representación digna del carácter de Dios. ¡Pero hay redención! Muy pocas cosas superan la belleza de una vida que fue una vez magullada y quebrantada por el pecado, pero ahora es restaurada, redimida y hecha completa por el Evangelio. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Los ateos desafían la existencia de Dios, los científicos discuten contra la creación bíblica, los eruditos cuestionan la inerrancia de las Escrituras, pero nadie puede disputar el testimonio de una vida redimida.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). Toda la belleza del mundo creado proviene de Dios. Un atardecer hermoso, una rosa encantadora, una secuoya imponente, una cumbre montañosa majestuosa, todo testifica la belleza de Dios ilustrada en la creación. Así como las señales en la carretera nos guían hacia nuestro destino, asimismo la creación dirige a la humanidad hacia Dios mismo. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). Estos dones de la creación se nos dan para darnos un breve vistazo del que los creó.

¿Cómo deberíamos, como parte de la creación de Dios, reflejar Su belleza creativa? Aunque no podemos crear algo de la nada, Dios nos diseñó para ser creativos, usando los recursos de Su creación y nuestras capacidades intelectuales para hacer la vida práctica. El sentido de realización que proviene de un trabajo bien hecho tiene su origen en la creación, donde Dios miró Su obra y la declaró buena. En nuestro intento de vivir vidas no extravagantes, a veces fallamos en gozar de las cosas bellas de la vida. Es correcto y bueno y está en armonía con cómo fuimos creados encontrar placer en las cosas de belleza. Los hombres impíos han usado este don de creatividad muchas veces con fines malvados. Con mayor razón, glorifiquemos a Dios usando Su creación de maneras que reflejen Su carácter.

Una advertencia para todos los que aman la naturaleza y la creación (natural y hecha por el hombre): tengamos cuidado de no elevar la belleza terrenal por encima del Creador, lo que conduce a la idolatría. Los atardeceres se desvanecen, las secuoyas caen, las rosas se marchitan, el cuerpo humano vuelve al polvo otra vez, pero Dios permanece. La vida y toda su belleza comienzan y terminan con Dios.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) Según el libro de Apocalipsis, el trono de Dios está rodeado de sonido: truenos y relámpagos; alabanzas que fluyen de los ángeles, las cuatro criaturas y los veinticuatro ancianos, y la gran multitud que nadie puede contar; y el nuevo cántico de los ciento cuarenta y cuatro mil.

Dios creó la belleza del sonido para glorificarse de maneras que las simples palabras no pueden. La complejidad de Su creatividad se muestra poderosamente en la forma en que distintas frecuencias sonoras se combinan para crear una armonía bella y celestial. Es un honor para Dios que la humanidad encuentre placer en la belleza de los sonidos que Él ha creado para Su gloria. La persona que ama a Dios será atraída hacia Él siempre que sea serenateada por sonidos agradables: el pueblo de Dios cantando los cánticos de Sion, las oraciones de los santos, el viento susurrando entre las copas de los árboles, el pajarillo alabando a su Creador, el retumbar del trueno o el simple golpeteo de la lluvia sobre el techo.

¿Cómo deberíamos, como instrumentos sonoros, reflejar la belleza de Dios mediante el sonido? Siempre deberíamos procurar escuchar y asemejarnos a los sonidos y armonías del cielo. Aunque nunca podremos lograr esto completamente en la tierra, debe ser un esfuerzo de toda la vida. Se han planteado las preguntas: “Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” y “when have we reached ‘good enough’?” Nunca podremos alcanzar la perfección celestial, así que la pregunta debería ser más bien, “Are we giving God the best we have?” Algunas personas tienen más capacidad para cantar que otras, pero la pregunta sigue siendo la misma. “Are we giving our best or are we satisfied with an inferior sacrifice?” Seamos productores de sonidos que honren a Dios y traigan gozo al corazón del Creador.

Through the Church:

La Biblia habla extensamente sobre la belleza del pueblo de Dios. “Zion”, “The Temple”, “The Mountain of God”, “Jerusalem” y “The Church” son expresiones sinónimas entretejidas a lo largo de las Escrituras que se refieren a la morada del pueblo de Dios en la tierra. Es el deseo de Dios que Su belleza se refleje en las vidas de Su pueblo. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

No hay nada más querido para el corazón de Dios que Su iglesia. Cuando los hijos de Israel peregrinaron por el desierto, construyeron el tabernáculo como un lugar para que Dios habitara entre ellos. Cuando Salomón dedicó el templo como morada de Dios, Dios quedó muy complacido y 2 Chronicles 7:1 dice que la gloria del Señor llenó el templo. El templo fue considerado la Casa del Señor: Jesús mismo se refirió a él numerosas veces como la casa de Dios y fue muy apasionado en que debía mantenerse santo.

Hoy, ni el tabernáculo ni el templo hospedan la presencia de Dios, sino que Su pasión divina está concentrada en la iglesia de Jesucristo. Aquí están las personas que verdaderamente lo aman y están dispuestas a dar su vida por Él. Aquí están los que están dispuestos a renunciar a sus derechos como individuos y entregarse a una causa mayor. Aquí es donde muchos santos han derramado la sangre de sus vidas por el Evangelio. Y aquí es donde un día nuestro Salvador volverá como ha prometido, y transportará a su novia, la iglesia, a su morada eterna. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

¿Cómo deberíamos, como pueblo de Dios, reflejar Su belleza en la iglesia? Viviendo juntos en unidad y armonía con amor hacia todos los hombres, especialmente hacia la familia de Dios. La iglesia debe ser un lugar donde el mundo pueda vislumbrar lo que sucede en el cielo. Debe ser un lugar donde Cristo siempre sea exaltado como el victorioso conquistador del pecado, la muerte y el infierno.

Tristemente, muchas personas se han desorientado por los fracasos de la iglesia y se han alejado de la verdadera fe apostólica. A pesar de nuestras desilusiones, levantemos “the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) y sigamos adelante. Nunca tendremos un llamamiento más alto, ni una guerra más noble que librar.

Por último, ¿cómo debemos reflejar Su belleza en nuestras vidas? Gozo en Él. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). El mayor cumplimiento en la vida proviene de encontrar placer en traer gozo al corazón de Dios complaciéndolo en lo que Él se deleita y amando lo que Él ama. No perdamos jamás el asombro por la belleza de nuestra Salvación.

The glory of the spring, how sweet!
The newborn life, how glad!
What joy the happy earth to greet
In new, bright raiment clad!

Divine Redeemer, Thee I bless;
I greet Thy going forth;
I love Thee in the loveliness
Of Thy renewed earth.

But O these wonders of Thy grace,
These nobler works of Thine,
These marvels sweeter far to trace,
These new births more divine:

This new-born glow of faith so strong,
This bloom of love so fair,
This new-born ecstasy of song,
And fragrancy of prayer!

Creator Spirit, work in me
These wonders sweet of Thine;
Divine Redeemer, graciously
Renew this heart of mine.

Still, let new life and strength upspring,
Still, let new joy be given;
And grant the glad new song to ring
Through the new earth and Heaven.

Hili furaha jipya la wimbo lililozaliwa,
Na harufu tamu ya sala!

Mwokozi wa Muumba, nifanyie kazi
Maajabu haya tamu yaako;
Mkombozi wa Mungu, kwa neema
Rudisha moyo huu wangu.

Baki, na ulete uzima mpya na nguvu ijenguke,
Baki, na ulete furaha mpya itolewe;
Na utupatie wimbo wa shangwe mpya uwe ukienea
Kupitia dunia mpya na Mbingu.

“Adrianna, what’s the temperature outside?” asked Asher. He and Adrianna were sitting at the table doing school with their siblings Emily and Kianna.

“Probably about 50.” Adrianna glanced lazily at the thermometer. “Hey, it’s 65 degrees! Mom, may we eat lunch outside?”

Mom looked up from the sink. “If you do a good job with your school until then, you may,” she told them. “And if you get your school done before lunch, you may play outside for a while this afternoon.”

Asher let out a whoop and started writing fast. The girls grinned at each other and picked up their pencils.

Everyone worked diligently until lunchtime. Then Adrianna made sandwiches while Asher put cookies in bags, Emily collected bags of chips, and Kianna ran down to the basement to grab a few apples. They each packed their lunch in a shopping bag and went out to their picnic spot, a big, flat rock in a clearing in the woods.

They ate quickly, then Adrianna suggested, “Let’s go kayak on the pond!”

“I guess we could,” said Asher slowly. “But didn’t Mom say that Emily and Kianna are too small to handle the kayaks?”

“Oh, yes, I guess she did. Well, they can play on the swings or something,” she shrugged

“I think we should play something everyone can help with,” said Asher. He turned to Emily and Kianna. “What do you want to do?”

“Let’s make a playhouse!” suggested Kianna.

“Yes, let’s!” Emily agreed. “You could hunt for us,” she told Asher.

“And Adrianna could be the mom!” said Kianna.

Adrianna stood with a scowl on her face. Playhouse indeed! She was way too old for that! “I’m going kayaking,” she announced. “You can just have your playhouse.” She picked up her shopping bag and put her sandwich and cookie bags into it. She threw her apple core to the dogs and started for the house.

“Adrianna, can you please take ours too?” begged Emily. “You're going to the house anyway.”

“You can take care of your own stuff,” Adrianna called back, crossly. She dropped her shopping bag on the counter, hoping to slip out of the house before Mom saw her.

She heard her mom’s voice. “Wait, Adrianna, what’s wrong? Your face looks like a thunderstorm!”

Adrianna sighed. She hadn’t been fast enough. “I wanted to go kayaking, but Asher doesn’t want to,” she grumbled.

“Well,” said Mom slowly, “I think Asher is remembering that the other girls can't handle kayaks yet. What are they doing?”

“They’re building a playhouse. I'm way too old for that!” Adrianna burst out.

Mom smiled, “What makes you think that?”

“I'm sure none of the girls my age do stuff like that with their little siblings.”

“Are you sure you're not being selfish?” Mom asked. “Sometimes, we need to give up what we want so that others can be happy.”

Adrianna shrugged and went out to the shed to get a kayak. She lifted her blue kayak off the rack and hauled it down to the pond. She snapped the paddle together, hopped into the seat, and pushed the kayak onto the smooth surface of the water. She sighed with pleasure. This was way better than building a playhouse in the woods! She took a few loops around the pond before her paddle began to slow. Somehow it wasn’t as fun this time. She heard Asher and the girls laughing and shouting as they played. Maybe Mom was right, she thought. Maybe I would be happier if I gave up what I want so that we can all play together. Slowly she paddled to the edge of the pond. She stepped out of the kayak, pulled it out of the water, and flipped it over to dry. Resolutely, she walked out of the pasture to find Asher and the girls.

“Hey! Here comes Adrianna!” called Emily happily as Adrianna walked up.

Adrianna grinned, “It looks like you have your house about set up,” she said encouragingly. “What do you need to finish it?”

“We still need a stove, and something for a countertop,” said Kianna.

“I can help you find something,” Adrianna told them. Together they hunted in the woods and the shed for boards and logs to finish the house. When suppertime came and they went in for supper, Adrianna was very happy. Mom was right, she thought. It is more fun to give up my way and do what everyone else wants to.

« Adrianna, quelle est la température dehors ? » demanda Asher. Lui et Adrianna étaient assis à la table en train de faire l’école avec leurs frères et sœurs Emily et Kianna.

« Probablement environ 10 degrés. » Adrianna jeta un coup d’œil paresseux au thermomètre. « Hé, il fait 18 degrés ! Maman, on peut déjeuner dehors ? »

Maman leva les yeux de l’évier. « Si vous faites bien votre travail d’école jusque-là, vous pouvez, » leur dit-elle. « Et si vous avez fini votre travail d’école avant le déjeuner, vous pourrez jouer dehors un moment cet après‑midi. »

Asher poussa un cri de joie et se mit à écrire vite. Les filles se sourirent et prirent leurs crayons.

Tous travaillèrent assidûment jusqu’à l’heure du déjeuner. Puis Adrianna prépara des sandwichs pendant qu’Asher mettait des biscuits dans des sachets, Emily ramassait des sachets de chips et Kianna descendait au sous‑sol pour attraper quelques pommes. Chacun rangea son déjeuner dans un sac de course et alla à leur lieu de pique‑nique, un gros rocher plat dans une clairière du bois.

Ils mangèrent rapidement, puis Adrianna suggéra : « Allons faire du kayak sur l’étang ! »

« Je suppose que nous pourrions, » dit Asher lentement. « Mais maman n’a‑t‑elle pas dit qu’Emily et Kianna sont trop petites pour manier les kayaks ? »

« Oh oui, je crois qu’elle l’a dit. Bon, elles peuvent jouer sur les balançoires ou quelque chose, » haussa‑t‑elle les épaules.

« Je pense qu’on devrait jouer à quelque chose où tout le monde peut aider, » dit Asher. Il se tourna vers Emily et Kianna. « Qu’est‑ce que vous voulez faire ? »

« Construisons une cabane ! » proposa Kianna.

« Oui, faisons ça ! » approuva Emily. « Toi tu pourrais nous chercher des choses, » dit‑elle à Asher.

« Et Adrianna pourrait être la maman ! » dit Kianna.

Adrianna se tint là, fronçant les sourcils. Une cabane, vraiment ! Elle était beaucoup trop âgée pour ça ! « Je vais faire du kayak, » annonça‑t‑elle. « Vous pouvez garder votre cabane. » Elle prit son sac de course et y mit son sandwich et ses sachets de biscuits. Elle jeta son trognon de pomme aux chiens et se dirigea vers la maison.

« Adrianna, peux‑tu aussi prendre nos trucs ? » supplia Emily. « Tu vas de toute façon à la maison. »

« Occupez‑vous de vos affaires, » cria Adrianna en colère. Elle laissa tomber son sac de course sur le comptoir, espérant sortir de la maison avant que maman ne la voie.

Elle entendit la voix de sa mère. « Attends, Adrianna, que se passe‑t‑il ? Ton visage ressemble à un orage ! »

Adrianna soupira. Elle n’avait pas été assez rapide. « Je voulais faire du kayak, mais Asher ne veut pas, » grogna‑t‑elle.

« Eh bien, » dit maman lentement, « je pense qu’Asher se souvient que les autres filles ne peuvent pas encore gérer les kayaks. Que font‑elles ? »

« Elles construisent une cabane. Je suis beaucoup trop vieille pour ça ! » s’exclama Adrianna.

Maman sourit, « Qu’est‑ce qui te fait penser ça ? »

« Je suis sûre qu’aucune des filles de mon âge ne fait ce genre de choses avec ses petits frères et sœurs. »

« Es‑tu sûre de ne pas être égoïste ? » demanda maman. « Parfois, nous devons renoncer à ce que nous voulons pour que les autres puissent être heureux. »

Adrianna haussa les épaules et sortit à la remise pour prendre un kayak. Elle souleva son kayak bleu du support et le traîna jusqu’à l’étang. Elle emboîta la pagaie, sauta dans le siège et poussa le kayak sur la surface lisse de l’eau. Elle soupira de plaisir. C’était bien mieux que de construire une cabane dans les bois ! Elle fit quelques tours autour de l’étang avant que sa pagaie ne commence à ralentir. D’une certaine façon, ce n’était pas aussi amusant cette fois. Elle entendit Asher et les filles rire et crier pendant qu’ils jouaient. Peut‑être que maman avait raison, pensa‑t‑elle. Peut‑être que je serais plus heureuse si je renonçais à ce que je veux pour que nous puissions tous jouer ensemble. Lentement, elle pagaia jusqu’au bord de l’étang. Elle sortit du kayak, le tira hors de l’eau et le retourna pour le faire sécher. Résolument, elle traversa le pâturage pour retrouver Asher et les filles.

« Hé ! Voilà Adrianna ! » cria joyeusement Emily quand Adrianna arriva.

Adrianna sourit, « On dirait que votre maison est presque prête, » dit‑elle en les encourageant. « De quoi avez‑vous besoin pour la finir ? »

« Il nous faut encore une cuisinière et quelque chose pour un plan de travail, » dit Kianna.

« Je peux vous aider à trouver quelque chose, » leur dit Adrianna. Ensemble, ils cherchèrent dans les bois et la remise des planches et des bûches pour finir la maison. Quand arriva l’heure du souper et qu’ils rentrèrent pour dîner, Adrianna était très heureuse. Maman avait eu raison, pensa‑t‑elle. C’est plus amusant de renoncer à ma façon et de faire ce que tout le monde veut.

“It is so hard,” the man sitting across from me said. “We’ve been married for nearly fifty years, but I never expected anything like this.”

“What is going on?” I asked Al, sympathetically.

“It’s Lisa,” he said. “You know her memory has been slipping for a little while. Well, we went to the neurologist like you told us to, and they ordered a whole bunch of tests and a brain scan of some sort. Then, they told her she had dementia.”

“I thought that was what was going on,” I replied.

“I know you told us that,” Al said. “Well, there are times she doesn’t recognize me. She looks at me blankly like she is wondering what crazy stranger has gotten into her house.”

“That’s got to be hard,” I said.

“The only thing I’ve found that brings her back to herself is to go outside and call her on her cell phone. I tell her to come out to the garage, I’ve got something to show her. Somehow when I do that, it brings her back to the present and lets her know who I am – for a little bit, anyway.”

We moved on to talking about other things, but I could tell that Al’s heart was breaking. His wife of 48 years looked the same as ever on the outside and yet, she was a completely different person.

I’d like to explore some of the challenges in dealing with dementia.

Dementia in the Bible

Ecclesiastes 12:1-7 gives a somewhat dismal view of the aging process. “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them; While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low; Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

In this passage, the poetic description seems to speak of loss of teeth, loss of hearing, unsteady gait, and general frailty. It is hard to say if any of these images speak of memory loss. What is certain is that the passage begins with a command: “Remember!”

This is not the only place in Scripture where humans are commanded to remember. Over and over, we are told to remember God. We are to make certain that we instruct our children about Him. “And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (Deuteronomy 6:7).

The time may come when we are not able to remember anymore. The most important thing – even as we think about the subject of dementia is that we remember the One who made us and follow Him with all our hearts.

What Dementia is

Dementia is any illness that causes a loss of memory, reasoning, and social functioning. Most people think mostly of the loss of memory. I suppose this is because early in the illness other people notice things like difficulty finding words and frequent repetition of stories.

Social functioning is often maintained until late in the illness. If you ask someone with mild dementia if they know today’s date, they will likely answer, “Oh, you know, I stopped paying attention to things like that when I retired.”

The most common cause of dementia is Alzheimer’s dementia – at least 70 percent of people who have progressive memory loss have Alzheimer’s dementia. Alzheimer’s seems to be related to proteins called amyloid, which get deposited in the brain and prevent nerve cells from communicating with each other.

Other causes are vascular dementia, where blockages in the blood vessels in the brain cause the death of nerve cells. Lewy Body Dementia is a sort of memory loss that is associated with Parkinson’s Disease. Approximately eighty percent of people with Parkinson’s Disease will eventually develop dementia.

Diagnosing Dementia

If family members suspect someone is developing memory loss, the best thing is to bring them to their primary care provider for an evaluation. Along with doing a physical exam, the doctor will typically do things like have the patient draw a clock and do a mini mental status exam, which asks the patient to answer a lot of simple questions and do some short-term recall of items.

Blood tests including a thyroid and Vitamin B12 level would be done. A brain scan or ultrasound of the neck arteries might be done as well.

The goal is to identify areas that can be treated and take care of those.

Eliminate Medications

Many medications increase the risk of memory issues. As people get older, trying to avoid these medications is helpful to prevent the development of dementia.

Anticholinergic medications are probably the biggest culprit that I encounter. The most common of these medications are older antihistamines like diphenhydramine (used as either a sleep aid or allergy pill) and doxylamine (used as a sleep aid). In one study, patients who took an anticholinergic medication for the equivalent of three years had a significantly higher risk of dementia than patients who took these sorts of medications for less than three months.1 Older depression medications can also fall into this category.

Anxiety medications, called benzodiazepines, have also been associated with memory issues. Studies indicate that patients who take these medications have a higher risk of developing dementia than patients who do not take them.2

Seizure medications may make thinking ability worse as well. Having a seizure disorder seems to increase the risk of dementia, but certain older medications like valproate and gabapentin seem to make it harder for older people to think clearly, and shifting to lower-risk seizure medications is in order (if possible) for older people.

There are times when someone needs to take medication, but as patients get older, it is important to think about the risks of those medications. There is a list of medications that are wisest to avoid for patients over 65 years of age, called the Beers List. Substituting similar medications with fewer side effects or using lower doses is recommended.3

Medical Treatments

The first rule when dealing with dementia is to make certain that all of the metabolic things are in as good control as possible. So, if someone has diabetes, it is best to make certain that their sugar is in as good control as possible. If someone has high blood pressure, make certain that it is well-regulated (this is particularly true if someone has vascular dementia).

There are several different classes of medications that are approved for treating dementia. One group is the cholinesterase inhibitors. These medications raise the level of a chemical called acetylcholine in the brain and peripheral nervous system. These medications are certainly not miracle drugs and at best they seem to slow the progression of memory loss and do not really restore previous brain function.

The other medication is called memantine. It works by targeting the glutamate receptor in the brain. Just as with the cholinesterase inhibitors, the effects are not huge and the end result only slows the memory loss.

Both of these medications are generic, and it is reasonable to try them and see how someone responds to them.

One last medication to mention is called lecanemab. It is an IV infusion that targets amyloid, a kind of protein that develops in the brain of people with Alzheimer’s dementia. The medication seems to work quite well at clearing amyloid from patient’s brains. This medication is very expensive ($26,500 per year)and it has been linked to an increase in strokes. In the studies, dementia symptoms were only slowed by about 30 percent compared with a placebo.

There are no other medications currently approved to treat dementia.

Non-medication Therapies

There are several things that people can do to help slow the progression of dementia. These can be helpful for people who have a strong family history of dementia and want to prevent its onset.

Cardiovascular exercise is very important. Doctors mention exercise in relation to nearly every chronic illness because it has been shown to work. In the case of dementia, people who exercise regularly have about 30 percent decreased risk of developing the disease. Regular exercise seems to slow the progression of dementia.4

Doing puzzles that require mental activity, like Sudoku or crossword puzzles seems to help slow the progression of memory loss and may also reduce the chance of developing dementia.

Lastly, it is helpful to learn something new. People who learn a new skill or focus on learning a new language help their memories quite a bit. A study compared older people who learned a new skill with people who went to social events.

The point seems to be that our brains need to be pushed to create new pathways or they will tend to break down.5

Caring For Someone with Dementia

Caring for someone with dementia is challenging in a number of ways. It is often difficult to know how much independence to allow the person. There have been many books written on this subject, but there are a few things that are worth mentioning.

It is important to avoid dangerous things. The two most dangerous things for someone with faulty memory are driving and cooking. Both of these seem commonplace, and the person may seem to be doing fine, but they can become a problem very quickly.

The danger of driving a car or a buggy is twofold. First, some people freeze at certain points, not remembering how to do a particular skill. This can be a problem, not only for them but also for others on the road.

Second, older people can start off on short journeys to a local store or restaurant and end up getting lost. I have had patients who ended up driving around for hours trying to find their way home when they got confused driving to town.

Cooking, of course, really comes down to a question of remembering to set timers and take things off the stove or out of the oven at the appropriate time.

Many times, people who have dementia do not realize how much their abilities have slipped and resist the idea that they need to give up the car keys. Maybe it simply comes down to a loss of independence, but it is hard to face the fact that you are no longer safe behind the wheel.

Try to keep things the same within the room and the home. Even small changes in room arrangement can be enough to upset the situation. Taking someone out of their home – for instance, admitting them to the hospital often makes things a lot worse. Suddenly, confusion that only seemed mild before is now extremely high.

If there is a fruit of the spirit that is key for dealing with someone with dementia, it is patience. None of us has as much patience as we need, as dementia spreads that patience awfully thin.

People with dementia often act like children on a long trip. They ask over and over when they are going home. They wonder where dead relatives are or why the children aren’t home yet. No amount of explanation helps, because only a minute or two after they ask the question, they have forgotten the answer and are asking again.

Their skills often wax and wane. One day, they can button their shirt, and the next day, that skill seems to have flown out the window. It is easy to believe that they aren’t “trying hard” and that they could do more if they would only make the effort.

Unfortunately, the fact that someone with dementia could do something yesterday doesn’t mean that they can remember how to do it today. Getting upset with them only makes these things worse as it adds anxiety to a person who already lacks the memory of how to do a skill.

As much as possible, answer the person gently even if it is the fifty-third time that you have answered the same question. Use distractions as well. If there is an activity that they can still do, such as sewing or jigsaw puzzles (even children’s puzzles with really big pieces), get them to do it. Late in the illness, letting them look at books with pretty pictures or sometimes even giving them a baby doll to hold can help settle them and distract them from their anxieties of the moment.

Get Others to Help

It is easy to become frustrated. Trying to provide all of the care needed by yourself is not a long-term solution. Dementia care is a marathon and not a sprint. Many people live for years after the diagnosis, and even though their physical body remains relatively strong, they require more and more care.

One of the blessings of having family connections and church communities is that we have people who are available to provide assistance.

Having family members or friends step in to give you some respite is key to not becoming seriously burned out or even angry with someone that you care about. It is best to take some time away periodically before you are mentally depleted. You may think you are doing fairly well, but all of us have a tendency to get weary in well doing if we never get a break.

Conclusion

I wish there were more medical solutions for dementia. Perhaps more will come later. For now, medications are quite limited.

The key is to put the fruit of the Spirit into practice. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (Galatians 5:22-23).

Even on the most frustrating days, people who are dealing with severe memory loss need love, gentleness, and patience from their family members. It is only through the Holy Spirit’s power that we can provide the care that is needed for someone whose body is strong, but who no longer even recognizes you.
