“정말 힘들다.” 내 맞은편에 앉아 있던 남자가 말했다. “우리는 결혼한 지 거의 50년이 되었는데, 이런 일이 생길 줄은 전혀 몰랐어.”

“무슨 일이 일어나고 있나요?” 나는 알에게 공감하며 물었다.

“리사야.” 그가 말했다. “기억력이 조금씩 흐려지는 건 네가 알다시피 있었지. 네가 말한 대로 신경과에 데려갔더니 이것저것 검사하고 뇌 스캔 같은 것도 했대. 그리고 나서 그녀에게 치매가 있다고 말하더군.”

“그게 무슨 일인가 싶었어요.” 나는 대답했다.

“네가 그렇게 말했단 걸 알아.” 알이 말했다. “어떤 때는 그녀가 나를 알아보지 못할 때가 있어. 그녀는 마치 집에 들어와 있는 낯선 사람이 누구냐고 빈 표정으로 바라봐.”

“그건 참 힘들겠네요.” 나는 말했다.

“그녀를 지금의 상태로 되돌리는 유일한 방법은 밖으로 나가서 휴대전화로 그녀를 부르는 거야. 차고로 나오라고 하고 보여줄 게 있다고 하지. 이상하게도 그렇게 하면 잠깐 동안 현재로 돌아오고 누군지 알아보더군—어쨌든 잠깐 동안은 말이야.”

우리는 다른 이야기들로 화제를 옮겼지만, 알의 마음이 무너지고 있다는 것을 알 수 있었다. 48년간의 아내는 겉모습은 여전했지만 완전히 다른 사람이 되어 있었다.

치매를 다루는 데 있어 몇 가지 어려움을 살펴보고자 한다.

Dementia in the Bible

Ecclesiastes 12:1-7 gives a somewhat dismal view of the aging process. “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them; While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low; Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

이 구절에서의 시적 묘사는 이빨의 상실, 청력 상실, 불안정한 보행, 전반적인 허약함을 말하는 것처럼 보인다. 이러한 이미지들 중 어느 것이 기억력 상실을 가리키는지는 단정하기 어렵다. 확실한 것은 이 구절이 명령으로 시작한다는 점이다: “기억하라!”

성경에서 하나님을 기억하라는 명령은 이곳만이 아니다. 우리는 계속해서 하나님을 기억하라는 지시를 받는다. 자녀들에게 그분에 대해 반드시 가르쳐야 한다. “And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (Deuteronomy 6:7).

기억하지 못하는 때가 올 수 있다. 치매라는 주제를 생각할 때에도 가장 중요한 것은 우리를 지으신 분을 기억하고 온 마음을 다해 그분을 따르는 것이다.

What Dementia is

치매는 기억력, 추론 능력, 사회적 기능의 상실을 초래하는 모든 질병을 말한다. 대부분의 사람들은 주로 기억력 상실을 떠올린다. 아마도 병의 초기에는 말 찾기 어려움이나 이야기의 잦은 반복 같은 것들을 다른 사람들이 먼저 알아차리기 때문일 것이다.

사회적 기능은 종종 병의 말기까지 유지된다. 가벼운 치매가 있는 사람에게 오늘 날짜를 아느냐고 물으면, 그들은 대개 “아, 저는 은퇴하고 나서 그런 건 신경 쓰지 않게 되었어요.”라고 대답할 것이다.

치매의 가장 흔한 원인은 알츠하이머성 치매다—진행성 기억 상실이 있는 사람들 중 적어도 70퍼센트가 알츠하이머성 치매를 앓는다. 알츠하이머는 아마도 아밀로이드라는 단백질과 관련이 있어, 이 단백질이 뇌에 침착되어 신경세포들이 서로 소통하지 못하게 한다.

다른 원인으로는 뇌의 혈관 폐색이 신경세포의 사멸을 일으키는 혈관성 치매가 있다. 루이소체 치매는 파킨슨병과 연관된 일종의 기억 상실이다. 파킨슨병 환자의 약 80퍼센트는 결국 치매를 발병하게 된다.

Diagnosing Dementia

가족들이 누군가가 기억력 저하를 보인다고 의심하면, 최선의 방법은 일차 진료의에게 평가를 받게 하는 것이다. 신체검사와 함께 의사는 환자에게 시계를 그리게 하거나, 간이 정신상태 검사(Mini Mental Status Exam) 같은 것을 시행해 간단한 질문에 답하게 하고 단기 기억을 검사하는 항목을 요구할 것이다.

갑상선 기능과 비타민 B12 수치를 포함한 혈액검사가 이루어질 것이다. 뇌 스캔이나 경동맥 초음파 검사가 시행될 수도 있다.

목표는 치료 가능한 부분을 찾아 그것을 관리하는 것이다.

Eliminate Medications

많은 약물이 기억 문제의 위험을 증가시킨다. 사람들이 나이가 들수록 이러한 약물을 피하려고 하는 것이 치매 발병을 예방하는 데 도움이 된다.

내가 접하는 가장 큰 범인은 아마도 항콜린성 약물이다. 이 계열의 가장 흔한 약물은 디펜히드라민(수면제나 알레르기 약으로 사용)과 독실아민(수면제로 사용) 같은 오래된 항히스타민제다. 한 연구에서는 항콜린성 약물을 3년 상당 기간 복용한 환자는 이러한 약물을 3개월 미만 복용한 환자보다 치매 위험이 유의하게 높았다.1 예전의 일부 우울증 치료제들도 이 범주에 속할 수 있다.

불안장애 치료제인 벤조디아제핀 계열 약물도 기억 문제와 관련이 있다. 연구들은 이러한 약을 복용하는 환자가 복용하지 않는 환자에 비해 치매 발병 위험이 더 높다고 보고한다.2

발작 약물도 사고력을 악화시킬 수 있다. 발작장애 자체가 치매 위험을 높이는 경향이 있지만, 발프로에이트나 가바펜틴 같은 일부 오래된 약물은 노인의 사고력을 흐리게 하는 경향이 있어 가능하면 위험도가 낮은 발작 약물로 바꾸는 것이 필요하다.

어떤 경우에는 약을 복용해야 할 때가 있지만, 환자가 나이가 들수록 약물의 위험성을 생각하는 것이 중요하다. 65세 이상의 환자가 피하는 것이 좋다고 권고되는 약물 목록이 있는데, 이를 비어스 리스트(Beers List)라고 한다. 부작용이 적은 유사 약물로 대체하거나 용량을 낮추는 것이 권장된다.3

Medical Treatments

치매를 다룰 때의 첫 번째 원칙은 모든 대사적 요인들이 가능한 한 잘 조절되도록 하는 것이다. 따라서 누군가 당뇨병이 있다면 혈당을 가능한 한 잘 관리하는 것이 최선이다. 고혈압이 있다면 잘 조절되었는지 확인하라(이는 특히 혈관성 치매 환자에게 중요하다).

치매 치료에 승인된 여러 약물 계열이 있다. 한 그룹은 콜린에스터라제 억제제다. 이 약물들은 뇌와 말초 신경계에서 아세틸콜린이라는 화학물질의 수준을 높인다. 이 약들이 기적적인 약물은 아니며, 최선의 경우 기억력 저하의 진행을 늦출 뿐 이전의 뇌 기능을 복원하지는 못하는 것으로 보인다.

다른 약물은 메만틴이라고 불린다. 이것은 뇌의 글루탐산 수용체를 표적으로 작용한다. 콜린에스터라제 억제제와 마찬가지로 그 효과는 크지 않으며 최종적으로는 기억력 저하를 늦출 뿐이다.

이들 약물은 모두 제네릭으로 되어 있으며, 시도해보고 환자가 어떻게 반응하는지 보는 것이 합리적이다.

언급할 마지막 약물은 레카네맙(lecanemab)이다. 이는 알츠하이머성 치매 환자의 뇌에 생기는 일종의 단백질인 아밀로이드를 표적으로 하는 정맥주사(IV) 제제다. 이 약물은 환자의 뇌에서 아밀로이드를 제거하는 데 꽤 효과적인 것으로 보인다. 이 약은 매우 비싸며(연간 $26,500) 뇌졸중 증가와 연관되어 있다. 연구에서 치매 증상은 위약과 비교했을 때 약 30퍼센트 정도만 늦춰졌다.

현재 치매를 치료하도록 승인된 다른 약물은 없다.

Non-medication Therapies

치매 진행을 늦추는 데 도움이 될 수 있는 여러 가지 방법이 있다. 강한 가족력 때문에 치매를 예방하고자 하는 사람들에게도 도움이 될 수 있다.

심혈관계 운동은 매우 중요하다. 의사들은 거의 모든 만성 질환과 관련하여 운동을 권하는데, 그 효과가 입증되었기 때문이다. 치매의 경우, 규칙적으로 운동하는 사람들은 질병을 발병할 위험이 약 30퍼센트 감소한다. 규칙적인 운동은 치매의 진행을 늦추는 것으로 보인다.4

스도쿠나 십자말풀이처럼 정신적 활동을 요구하는 퍼즐을 하는 것은 기억력 저하의 진행을 늦추는 데 도움이 되며 치매 발병 가능성을 줄일 수도 있다.

마지막으로 새로운 것을 배우는 것이 도움이 된다. 새로운 기술을 배우거나 새로운 언어 학습에 집중하는 사람들은 기억력이 상당히 좋아진다. 한 연구는 새로운 기술을 배운 노인들과 사교 모임에 참석한 사람들을 비교했다.

요지는 우리 뇌가 새로운 경로를 만들도록 자극받아야 하지 않으면 경로들이 쇠락하는 경향이 있다는 것이다.5

Caring For Someone with Dementia

치매 환자를 돌보는 일은 여러 면에서 도전적이다. 그 사람에게 어느 정도의 독립성을 허용할지 판단하기가 종종 어렵다. 이 주제에 관해 쓰인 책들이 많지만, 몇 가지 언급할 가치가 있는 점들이 있다.

위험한 것들을 피하는 것이 중요하다. 기억이 흐려진 사람에게 가장 위험한 두 가지는 운전과 요리이다. 둘 다 일상적인 일이기에 그 사람이 잘하는 것처럼 보일 수 있지만, 아주 빠르게 문제가 될 수 있다.

자동차나 마차를 운전하는 위험은 두 가지면에서 생긴다. 첫째, 어떤 사람들은 특정 상황에서 얼어붙어 어떤 기술을 어떻게 해야 할지 기억하지 못한다. 이는 그들 자신뿐만 아니라 도로 위의 다른 사람들에게도 문제가 될 수 있다.

둘째, 노인들은 근처 상점이나 식당에 잠깐 운전해서 가려다가 길을 잃기 시작할 수 있다. 나는 헷갈려서 집으로 돌아가는 길을 찾으려 몇 시간씩 운전한 환자들을 본 적이 있다.

요리는 적절한 시간에 타이머를 맞추고 스토브나 오븐에서 음식을 꺼내는 것을 기억해야 한다는 점에서 문제다.

많은 경우, 치매가 있는 사람들은 자신의 능력이 얼마나 떨어졌는지 깨닫지 못하고 자동차 열쇠를 포기해야 한다는 생각을 거부한다. 아마도 단순히 독립성의 상실 때문일 것이다. 그러나 더 이상 운전대 뒤에 서 있는 것이 안전하지 않다는 사실을 인정하기는 어렵다.

방과 집 안의 환경을 가능한 한 같게 유지하려고 해라. 방의 배치에 작은 변화만 있어도 상황을 악화시킬 수 있다. 예를 들어, 병원에 입원시키기 위해 집에서 떠나게 하는 것은 상황을 훨씬 더 악화시키는 경우가 많다. 갑자기 이전에는 경미해 보였던 혼란이 매우 심해진다.

치매 환자를 대할 때 성령의 열매 중 핵심적인 것은 인내다. 우리 중 누구도 필요한 만큼의 인내를 항상 가진 것은 아니며, 치매가 퍼질수록 그 인내는 얼마나 얇아지는지 모른다.

치매 환자들은 종종 긴 여행 중인 아이들처럼 행동한다. 그들은 언제 집에 가느냐고 반복해서 묻는다. 돌아가신 친척들이 어디에 있는지, 왜 아이들이 아직 집에 오지 않았는지 궁금해한다. 아무리 설명해도 소용이 없다. 그들이 질문을 한 지 1~2분 후면 이미 대답을 잊어버리고 다시 묻기 때문이다.

그들의 기능은 종종 오르내린다. 어떤 날은 셔츠 단추를 채울 수 있는데 다음 날에는 그 기술이 사라진 것처럼 보인다. 우리는 그들이 ‘노력하지 않는다’고, 더 노력하면 더 할 수 있을 것이라고 생각하기 쉽다.

불행히도 어제 할 수 있었던 일이 오늘도 기억해서 할 수 있다는 보장은 없다. 그들에게 화를 내는 것은 상황을 악화시킬 뿐이며 이미 어떻게 하는지 기억하지 못하는 사람에게 불안을 더할 뿐이다.

가능한 한 부드럽게 답해라, 비록 같은 질문에 쉰세 번째 대답을 하는 중일지라도. 주의를 돌리는 방법도 사용하라. 그들이 아직 할 수 있는 활동—바느질이나 직소 퍼즐(아주 큰 조각이 있는 어린이용 퍼즐도 좋다)—같은 것이 있다면 시키라. 병의 말기에는 예쁜 그림이 있는 책을 보여주거나 때로는 아기 인형을 쥐어주는 것이 그들을 안정시키고 순간의 불안을 잊게 하는 데 도움이 될 수 있다.

Get Others to Help

좌절감을 느끼기 쉽다. 모든 돌봄을 혼자 제공하려고 하는 것은 장기적인 해결책이 되지 못한다. 치매 관리는 단거리 경주가 아니라 마라톤이다. 많은 사람들이 진단 후 수년을 살며, 신체는 상대적으로 강하게 남아 있어도 점점 더 많은 돌봄을 필요로 한다.

가족 연결과 교회 공동체가 주는 축복 중 하나는 도움을 제공할 수 있는 사람들이 있다는 것이다.

가족 구성원이나 친구들이 교대해 가며 휴식을 줄 수 있도록 하는 것은 심하게 탈진하거나 사랑하는 사람에게 화를 내는 것을 피하는 데 핵심이다. 정신적으로 소진되기 전에 정기적으로 시간을 내어 쉬는 것이 가장 좋다. 자신이 꽤 잘해내고 있다고 생각할지 모르지만, 우리는 모두 쉬지 못하면 선한 일에도 지치기 마련이다.

Conclusion

치매에 대한 의학적 해결책이 더 많았으면 좋겠다. 아마도 이후에 더 많은 것이 나올지도 모른다. 현재로서는 약물이 매우 제한적이다.

핵심은 성령의 열매를 실천하는 것이다. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (Galatians 5:22-23).

가장 답답한 날에도 심한 기억 상실을 겪는 사람들에게는 가족의 사랑, 다정함, 인내가 필요하다. 온전한 돌봄을 제공할 수 있는 것은 오직 성령의 능력뿐이다. 신체는 강하지만 더 이상 당신을 알아보지 못하는 사람을 돌보는 데 필요한 것은 성령의 능력이다.

“It is so hard,” the man sitting across from me said. “We’ve been married for nearly fifty years, but I never expected anything like this.”

“What is going on?” I asked Al, sympathetically.

“It’s Lisa,” he said. “You know her memory has been slipping for a little while. Well, we went to the neurologist like you told us to, and they ordered a whole bunch of tests and a brain scan of some sort. Then, they told her she had dementia.”

“I thought that was what was going on,” I replied.

“I know you told us that,” Al said. “Well, there are times she doesn’t recognize me. She looks at me blankly like she is wondering what crazy stranger has gotten into her house.”

“That’s got to be hard,” I said.

“The only thing I’ve found that brings her back to herself is to go outside and call her on her cell phone. I tell her to come out to the garage, I’ve got something to show her. Somehow when I do that, it brings her back to the present and lets her know who I am – for a little bit, anyway.”

We moved on to talking about other things, but I could tell that Al’s heart was breaking. His wife of 48 years looked the same as ever on the outside and yet, she was a completely different person.

I’d like to explore some of the challenges in dealing with dementia.

Dementia in the Bible

Ecclesiastes 12:1-7 gives a somewhat dismal view of the aging process. “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them; While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low; Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

In this passage, the poetic description seems to speak of loss of teeth, loss of hearing, unsteady gait, and general frailty. It is hard to say if any of these images speak of memory loss. What is certain is that the passage begins with a command: “Remember!”

This is not the only place in Scripture where humans are commanded to remember. Over and over, we are told to remember God. We are to make certain that we instruct our children about Him. “And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (Deuteronomy 6:7).

The time may come when we are not able to remember anymore. The most important thing – even as we think about the subject of dementia is that we remember the One who made us and follow Him with all our hearts.

What Dementia is

Dementia is any illness that causes a loss of memory, reasoning, and social functioning. Most people think mostly of the loss of memory. I suppose this is because early in the illness other people notice things like difficulty finding words and frequent repetition of stories.

Social functioning is often maintained until late in the illness. If you ask someone with mild dementia if they know today’s date, they will likely answer, “Oh, you know, I stopped paying attention to things like that when I retired.”

The most common cause of dementia is Alzheimer’s dementia – at least 70 percent of people who have progressive memory loss have Alzheimer’s dementia. Alzheimer’s seems to be related to proteins called amyloid, which get deposited in the brain and prevent nerve cells from communicating with each other.

Other causes are vascular dementia, where blockages in the blood vessels in the brain cause the death of nerve cells. Lewy Body Dementia is a sort of memory loss that is associated with Parkinson’s Disease. Approximately eighty percent of people with Parkinson’s Disease will eventually develop dementia.

Diagnosing Dementia

If family members suspect someone is developing memory loss, the best thing is to bring them to their primary care provider for an evaluation. Along with doing a physical exam, the doctor will typically do things like have the patient draw a clock and do a mini mental status exam, which asks the patient to answer a lot of simple questions and do some short-term recall of items.

Blood tests including a thyroid and Vitamin B12 level would be done. A brain scan or ultrasound of the neck arteries might be done as well.

The goal is to identify areas that can be treated and take care of those.

Eliminate Medications

Many medications increase the risk of memory issues. As people get older, trying to avoid these medications is helpful to prevent the development of dementia.

Anticholinergic medications are probably the biggest culprit that I encounter. The most common of these medications are older antihistamines like diphenhydramine (used as either a sleep aid or allergy pill) and doxylamine (used as a sleep aid). In one study, patients who took an anticholinergic medication for the equivalent of three years had a significantly higher risk of dementia than patients who took these sorts of medications for less than three months.1 Older depression medications can also fall into this category.

Anxiety medications, called benzodiazepines, have also been associated with memory issues. Studies indicate that patients who take these medications have a higher risk of developing dementia than patients who do not take them.2

Seizure medications may make thinking ability worse as well. Having a seizure disorder seems to increase the risk of dementia, but certain older medications like valproate and gabapentin seem to make it harder for older people to think clearly, and shifting to lower-risk seizure medications is in order (if possible) for older people.

There are times when someone needs to take medication, but as patients get older, it is important to think about the risks of those medications. There is a list of medications that are wisest to avoid for patients over 65 years of age, called the Beers List. Substituting similar medications with fewer side effects or using lower doses is recommended.3

Medical Treatments

The first rule when dealing with dementia is to make certain that all of the metabolic things are in as good control as possible. So, if someone has diabetes, it is best to make certain that their sugar is in as good control as possible. If someone has high blood pressure, make certain that it is well-regulated (this is particularly true if someone has vascular dementia).

There are several different classes of medications that are approved for treating dementia. One group is the cholinesterase inhibitors. These medications raise the level of a chemical called acetylcholine in the brain and peripheral nervous system. These medications are certainly not miracle drugs and at best they seem to slow the progression of memory loss and do not really restore previous brain function.

The other medication is called memantine. It works by targeting the glutamate receptor in the brain. Just as with the cholinesterase inhibitors, the effects are not huge and the end result only slows the memory loss.

Both of these medications are generic, and it is reasonable to try them and see how someone responds to them.

One last medication to mention is called lecanemab. It is an IV infusion that targets amyloid, a kind of protein that develops in the brain of people with Alzheimer’s dementia. The medication seems to work quite well at clearing amyloid from patient’s brains. This medication is very expensive ($26,500 per year)and it has been linked to an increase in strokes. In the studies, dementia symptoms were only slowed by about 30 percent compared with a placebo.

There are no other medications currently approved to treat dementia.

Non-medication Therapies

There are several things that people can do to help slow the progression of dementia. These can be helpful for people who have a strong family history of dementia and want to prevent its onset.

Cardiovascular exercise is very important. Doctors mention exercise in relation to nearly every chronic illness because it has been shown to work. In the case of dementia, people who exercise regularly have about 30 percent decreased risk of developing the disease. Regular exercise seems to slow the progression of dementia.4

Doing puzzles that require mental activity, like Sudoku or crossword puzzles seems to help slow the progression of memory loss and may also reduce the chance of developing dementia.

Lastly, it is helpful to learn something new. People who learn a new skill or focus on learning a new language help their memories quite a bit. A study compared older people who learned a new skill with people who went to social events.

The point seems to be that our brains need to be pushed to create new pathways or they will tend to break down.5

Caring For Someone with Dementia

Caring for someone with dementia is challenging in a number of ways. It is often difficult to know how much independence to allow the person. There have been many books written on this subject, but there are a few things that are worth mentioning.

It is important to avoid dangerous things. The two most dangerous things for someone with faulty memory are driving and cooking. Both of these seem commonplace, and the person may seem to be doing fine, but they can become a problem very quickly.

The danger of driving a car or a buggy is twofold. First, some people freeze at certain points, not remembering how to do a particular skill. This can be a problem, not only for them but also for others on the road.

Second, older people can start off on short journeys to a local store or restaurant and end up getting lost. I have had patients who ended up driving around for hours trying to find their way home when they got confused driving to town.

Cooking, of course, really comes down to a question of remembering to set timers and take things off the stove or out of the oven at the appropriate time.

Many times, people who have dementia do not realize how much their abilities have slipped and resist the idea that they need to give up the car keys. Maybe it simply comes down to a loss of independence, but it is hard to face the fact that you are no longer safe behind the wheel.

Try to keep things the same within the room and the home. Even small changes in room arrangement can be enough to upset the situation. Taking someone out of their home – for instance, admitting them to the hospital often makes things a lot worse. Suddenly, confusion that only seemed mild before is now extremely high.

If there is a fruit of the spirit that is key for dealing with someone with dementia, it is patience. None of us has as much patience as we need, as dementia spreads that patience awfully thin.

People with dementia often act like children on a long trip. They ask over and over when they are going home. They wonder where dead relatives are or why the children aren’t home yet. No amount of explanation helps, because only a minute or two after they ask the question, they have forgotten the answer and are asking again.

Their skills often wax and wane. One day, they can button their shirt, and the next day, that skill seems to have flown out the window. It is easy to believe that they aren’t “trying hard” and that they could do more if they would only make the effort.

Unfortunately, the fact that someone with dementia could do something yesterday doesn’t mean that they can remember how to do it today. Getting upset with them only makes these things worse as it adds anxiety to a person who already lacks the memory of how to do a skill.

As much as possible, answer the person gently even if it is the fifty-third time that you have answered the same question. Use distractions as well. If there is an activity that they can still do, such as sewing or jigsaw puzzles (even children’s puzzles with really big pieces), get them to do it. Late in the illness, letting them look at books with pretty pictures or sometimes even giving them a baby doll to hold can help settle them and distract them from their anxieties of the moment.

Get Others to Help

It is easy to become frustrated. Trying to provide all of the care needed by yourself is not a long-term solution. Dementia care is a marathon and not a sprint. Many people live for years after the diagnosis, and even though their physical body remains relatively strong, they require more and more care.

One of the blessings of having family connections and church communities is that we have people who are available to provide assistance.

Having family members or friends step in to give you some respite is key to not becoming seriously burned out or even angry with someone that you care about. It is best to take some time away periodically before you are mentally depleted. You may think you are doing fairly well, but all of us have a tendency to get weary in well doing if we never get a break.

Conclusion

I wish there were more medical solutions for dementia. Perhaps more will come later. For now, medications are quite limited.

The key is to put the fruit of the Spirit into practice. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (Galatians 5:22-23).

Even on the most frustrating days, people who are dealing with severe memory loss need love, gentleness, and patience from their family members. It is only through the Holy Spirit’s power that we can provide the care that is needed for someone whose body is strong, but who no longer even recognizes you.

“Es tan difícil”, dijo el hombre sentado frente a mí. “Llevamos casados casi cincuenta años, pero nunca esperé algo así”.

“¿Qué está pasando?” pregunté a Al, con simpatía.

“Es Lisa”, dijo él. “Sabes que su memoria ha ido fallando desde hace un tiempo. Pues fuimos al neurólogo como nos dijiste, y le mandaron un montón de pruebas y algún tipo de escáner cerebral. Entonces le dijeron que tenía demencia”.

“Pensé que eso era lo que pasaba”, respondí.

“Sé que nos lo dijiste”, dijo Al. “Bueno, hay veces en que no me reconoce. Me mira con la cara en blanco como preguntándose qué extraño loco ha entrado en su casa”.

“Debe de ser duro”, dije.

“Lo único que he encontrado que la devuelve a sí misma es salir y llamarla al móvil. Le digo que salga al garaje, que tengo algo que mostrarle. De alguna manera, cuando hago eso, la trae de vuelta al presente y le hace saber quién soy —por un rato, al menos—”.

Pasamos a hablar de otras cosas, pero pude notar que el corazón de Al estaba destrozándose. Su esposa de 48 años parecía igual que siempre por fuera y, sin embargo, era una persona completamente diferente.

Me gustaría explorar algunos de los desafíos al tratar la demencia.

Dementia in the Bible

Ecclesiastes 12:1-7 gives a somewhat dismal view of the aging process. “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them; While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low; Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

En este pasaje, la descripción poética parece hablar de la pérdida de dientes, de la pérdida de audición, de un andar inestable y de una fragilidad general. Es difícil decir si alguna de estas imágenes se refiere a la pérdida de memoria. Lo que es seguro es que el pasaje comienza con un mandato: “¡Recuerda!”

Este no es el único lugar en las Escrituras donde se manda a los humanos recordar. Una y otra vez se nos dice que recordemos a Dios. Debemos asegurarnos de instruir a nuestros hijos acerca de Él. “And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (Deuteronomy 6:7).

Puede llegar un tiempo en que ya no seamos capaces de recordar. Lo más importante —incluso cuando pensamos en el tema de la demencia— es que recordemos al que nos hizo y le sigamos con todo nuestro corazón.

What Dementia is

La demencia es cualquier enfermedad que cause pérdida de memoria, razonamiento y funcionamiento social. La mayoría de la gente piensa principalmente en la pérdida de memoria. Supongo que es porque al inicio de la enfermedad otras personas notan cosas como la dificultad para encontrar palabras y la repetición frecuente de historias.

El funcionamiento social suele mantenerse hasta etapas avanzadas de la enfermedad. Si le preguntas a alguien con demencia leve si sabe la fecha de hoy, probablemente responderá: “Oh, ya sabes, dejé de prestar atención a cosas así cuando me jubilé”.

La causa más común de demencia es la demencia por Alzheimer: al menos el 70 por ciento de las personas que tienen pérdida progresiva de memoria padecen demencia por Alzheimer. El Alzheimer parece estar relacionado con unas proteínas llamadas amiloide, que se depositan en el cerebro e impiden que las células nerviosas se comuniquen entre sí.

Otras causas son la demencia vascular, donde bloqueos en los vasos sanguíneos del cerebro causan la muerte de células nerviosas. La demencia por cuerpos de Lewy es una especie de pérdida de memoria asociada con la enfermedad de Parkinson. Aproximadamente el ochenta por ciento de las personas con Parkinson acabarán desarrollando demencia.

Diagnosing Dementia

Si los familiares sospechan que alguien está desarrollando pérdida de memoria, lo mejor es llevarlo a su médico de atención primaria para una evaluación. Además de hacer un examen físico, el médico normalmente hará cosas como pedir al paciente que dibuje un reloj y realizar un mini examen del estado mental, que pide al paciente responder muchas preguntas sencillas y recordar a corto plazo algunos elementos.

Se harían análisis de sangre que incluyan la tiroides y el nivel de vitamina B12. También podría realizarse un escáner cerebral o una ecografía de las arterias del cuello.

El objetivo es identificar aspectos que se puedan tratar y ocuparse de ellos.

Eliminate Medications

Muchos medicamentos aumentan el riesgo de problemas de memoria. A medida que las personas envejecen, evitar estos medicamentos ayuda a prevenir el desarrollo de la demencia.

Los medicamentos anticolinérgicos son probablemente los principales culpables que encuentro. Los más comunes de estos medicamentos son los antihistamínicos antiguos como la difenhidramina (usada como ayuda para dormir o como pastilla para la alergia) y la doxilamina (usada como ayuda para dormir). En un estudio, los pacientes que tomaron un medicamento anticolinérgico durante el equivalente a tres años tuvieron un riesgo significativamente mayor de demencia que los pacientes que tomaron este tipo de medicamentos durante menos de tres meses.1 Los antidepresivos antiguos también pueden entrar en esta categoría.

Los medicamentos para la ansiedad, llamados benzodiacepinas, también se han asociado con problemas de memoria. Los estudios indican que los pacientes que toman estos medicamentos tienen un mayor riesgo de desarrollar demencia que los pacientes que no los toman.2

Los medicamentos para las convulsiones pueden empeorar la capacidad de pensar también. Tener un trastorno convulsivo parece aumentar el riesgo de demencia, pero ciertos medicamentos antiguos como el valproato y la gabapentina parecen dificultar que las personas mayores piensen con claridad, y conviene cambiar a medicamentos anticonvulsivos de menor riesgo (si es posible) para las personas mayores.

Hay ocasiones en que alguien necesita tomar medicación, pero a medida que los pacientes envejecen, es importante pensar en los riesgos de esos fármacos. Existe una lista de medicamentos que es más sabio evitar en pacientes mayores de 65 años, llamada la Lista de Beers. Se recomienda sustituir por medicamentos similares con menos efectos secundarios o usar dosis más bajas.3

Medical Treatments

La primera regla al tratar la demencia es asegurarse de que todas las cuestiones metabólicas estén lo mejor controladas posible. Así que, si alguien tiene diabetes, es mejor asegurarse de que su azúcar esté lo mejor controlada posible. Si alguien tiene presión arterial alta, hay que asegurarse de que esté bien regulada (esto es particularmente cierto si alguien tiene demencia vascular).

Hay varias clases de medicamentos aprobados para tratar la demencia. Un grupo son los inhibidores de la colinesterasa. Estos medicamentos aumentan el nivel de una sustancia química llamada acetilcolina en el cerebro y en el sistema nervioso periférico. Estos medicamentos ciertamente no son milagrosos y, en el mejor de los casos, parecen ralentizar la progresión de la pérdida de memoria y no restauran realmente la función cerebral previa.

El otro medicamento se llama memantina. Actúa sobre el receptor de glutamato en el cerebro. Al igual que con los inhibidores de la colinesterasa, los efectos no son enormes y el resultado final solo ralentiza la pérdida de memoria.

Ambos medicamentos son genéricos, y es razonable probarlos y ver cómo responde alguien a ellos.

Un último medicamento para mencionar se llama lecanemab. Es una infusión intravenosa que apunta a la amiloide, un tipo de proteína que se desarrolla en el cerebro de las personas con demencia de Alzheimer. El medicamento parece funcionar bastante bien para eliminar la amiloide del cerebro de los pacientes. Este medicamento es muy caro (26.500 dólares al año) y se ha relacionado con un aumento de los accidentes cerebrovasculares. En los estudios, los síntomas de la demencia solo se ralentizaron en aproximadamente un 30 por ciento en comparación con un placebo.

No hay otros medicamentos actualmente aprobados para tratar la demencia.

Non-medication Therapies

Hay varias cosas que las personas pueden hacer para ayudar a ralentizar la progresión de la demencia. Pueden ser útiles para personas que tienen una fuerte historia familiar de demencia y quieren prevenir su aparición.

El ejercicio cardiovascular es muy importante. Los médicos mencionan el ejercicio en relación con casi todas las enfermedades crónicas porque se ha demostrado que funciona. En el caso de la demencia, las personas que hacen ejercicio regularmente tienen alrededor de un 30 por ciento menos de riesgo de desarrollar la enfermedad. El ejercicio regular parece ralentizar la progresión de la demencia.4

Hacer rompecabezas que requieren actividad mental, como Sudoku o crucigramas, parece ayudar a ralentizar la progresión de la pérdida de memoria y también puede reducir la probabilidad de desarrollar demencia.

Por último, es útil aprender algo nuevo. Las personas que aprenden una nueva habilidad o se centran en aprender un nuevo idioma mejoran mucho su memoria. Un estudio comparó a personas mayores que aprendieron una nueva habilidad con personas que asistieron a eventos sociales.

La idea parece ser que nuestros cerebros necesitan ser estimulados para crear nuevas vías o tenderán a deteriorarse.5

Caring For Someone with Dementia

Cuidar a alguien con demencia presenta retos en varios sentidos. A menudo es difícil saber cuánta independencia permitir a la persona. Se han escrito muchos libros sobre este tema, pero hay algunas cosas que vale la pena mencionar.

Es importante evitar cosas peligrosas. Las dos cosas más peligrosas para alguien con memoria defectuosa son conducir y cocinar. Ambas parecen cotidianas, y la persona puede parecer que está bien, pero pueden convertirse en un problema muy rápidamente.

El peligro de conducir un automóvil o un carro es doble. Primero, algunas personas se bloquean en ciertos momentos, sin recordar cómo realizar una habilidad en particular. Esto puede ser un problema, no solo para ellos sino también para otros en la carretera.

Segundo, las personas mayores pueden salir en viajes cortos a una tienda o restaurante y acabar desorientadas. He tenido pacientes que terminaron conduciendo durante horas tratando de encontrar el camino a casa cuando se confundieron al ir a la ciudad.

La cocina, por supuesto, se reduce a recordar poner temporizadores y sacar cosas de la estufa o del horno en el momento adecuado.

Muchas veces, las personas con demencia no se dan cuenta de cuánto han empeorado sus capacidades y se resisten a la idea de entregar las llaves del coche. Tal vez simplemente se reduce a la pérdida de independencia, pero es difícil enfrentar el hecho de que ya no eres seguro al volante.

Procura mantener las cosas igual dentro de la habitación y del hogar. Incluso pequeños cambios en la disposición de la habitación pueden ser suficientes para alterar la situación. Sacar a alguien de su casa —por ejemplo, ingresarlo en el hospital—a menudo empeora mucho las cosas. De repente, una confusión que antes parecía leve ahora es extremadamente intensa.

Si hay un fruto del Espíritu que es clave para tratar a alguien con demencia, es la paciencia. Ninguno de nosotros tiene tanta paciencia como necesita; a medida que la demencia se extiende, esa paciencia se vuelve extremadamente escasa.

Las personas con demencia a menudo actúan como niños en un viaje largo. Preguntan una y otra vez cuándo se van a casa. Se preguntan dónde están los parientes fallecidos o por qué los hijos no han llegado todavía. Ninguna cantidad de explicación ayuda, porque solo uno o dos minutos después de hacer la pregunta han olvidado la respuesta y vuelven a preguntar.

Sus habilidades a menudo fluctúan. Un día pueden abrocharse la camisa y al siguiente esa habilidad parece haber desaparecido. Es fácil creer que no están “intentando lo suficiente” y que podrían hacer más si se esforzaran.

Desafortunadamente, el hecho de que alguien con demencia pudiera hacer algo ayer no significa que recuerde cómo hacerlo hoy. Enfadarse con ellos solo empeora estas cosas, ya que añade ansiedad a una persona que ya carece de la memoria de cómo realizar una habilidad.

En la medida de lo posible, responde a la persona con dulzura incluso si es la quincuagésima tercera vez que contestas la misma pregunta. Usa también distracciones. Si hay una actividad que todavía pueden hacer, como coser o puzzles de encaje (incluso puzzles infantiles con piezas realmente grandes), anímales a hacerlo. En etapas avanzadas de la enfermedad, dejarles mirar libros con imágenes bonitas o, a veces, darles una muñeca para que la abracen puede ayudar a calmarlos y distraerlos de sus ansiedades del momento.

Get Others to Help

Es fácil frustrarse. Intentar proporcionar todo el cuidado por ti mismo no es una solución a largo plazo. El cuidado de la demencia es una maratón y no un sprint. Muchas personas viven años después del diagnóstico y, aunque su cuerpo físico se mantenga relativamente fuerte, requieren cada vez más cuidado.

Una de las bendiciones de tener conexiones familiares y comunidades de iglesia es que tenemos personas disponibles para brindar ayuda.

Que familiares o amigos intervengan para darte un respiro es clave para no agotarte gravemente o incluso enfadarte con alguien a quien cuidas. Es mejor tomarse un tiempo fuera periódicamente antes de quedar mentalmente exhausto. Puedes pensar que lo estás haciendo bastante bien, pero todos tenemos tendencia a cansarnos de hacer el bien si nunca tenemos un descanso.

Conclusion

Ojalá hubiera más soluciones médicas para la demencia. Tal vez vengan más después. Por ahora, los medicamentos son bastante limitados.

La clave es poner en práctica el fruto del Espíritu. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (Galatians 5:22-23).

Incluso en los días más frustrantes, las personas que lidian con una pérdida de memoria severa necesitan amor, gentileza y paciencia de sus familiares. Solo mediante el poder del Espíritu Santo podemos brindar el cuidado necesario a alguien cuyo cuerpo está fuerte, pero que ya ni siquiera te reconoce.

It's incredible to me to see how God uses His people throughout history to bring glory to His name. He uses the weak things to confound the wise; the base things to bring to nothing the wisdom of earthly wise men. God uses physical weakness, hardship, loss, grief, toil, and pain to increase our spiritual treasures and build His Kingdom here on the earth!

This hymn became precious to my family and me several years ago as we awaited the birth of our fourth genetically challenged baby. We knew she couldn't stay with us very long. She passed away at just three days old. After researching this hymn, I was amazed to find out that the man whose story had inspired this hymn had lost eight out of his nine children.

The story of this man is a notable one. His 61 years on earth were marked by grief and loss, persecution and imprisonment. Yet, his dedication to Christ was outstanding, and his fire for God and zeal for preaching the gospel never waned until his last day.

Samuel Rutherford, son of a prosperous farmer, was born in the year 1600. His life began in the small village of Nisbet, Scotland. As we glimpse into his life, we notice the hand of God at work in Samuel’s early years. At only three years old, he was playing with his friends when he fell into the town well. His sister and friends ran to get help. When they returned, they found a very wet Samuel sitting on the grass beside the well. They asked him how he got out, and his reply was, "A bonny white man came and drew me out of the well." His family believed that God sent an angel to rescue him that day.

From what we know about Samuel Rutherford, he had two brothers and one sister. He was sent to school when he was young, and he became a very diligent scholar. He learned Latin and Greek so well that he eventually became a professor. He married Eupham Hamilton around 1624, soon after he began teaching at Edinburgh University. At this time, Samuel was yet unconverted and cared only for pursuing his academic goals.

In 1626, at the age of 26, Samuel came to a clear and saving faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. He said, "O but Christ hath a saving eye. When He first looked on me I was saved. It cost Him but a look to make hell quit to me." From that moment he was filled with a passion to preach and to speak about his Saviour. This change of life caused such a stir in the university that Rutherford ended up resigning his professorship.

In 1627, Samuel took his wife and two young children to Galloway, Scotland, where he began pastoring the small church of Anwoth. As he commenced his calling there he said, "I have received the commission from the royal and princely Master, my Lord Jesus, to preach Christ to the people." His passion was for the conversion of the people, and it is said that he seemed to be always praying, always preaching, always visiting the sick, always teaching and instructing, always writing or studying. The zeal with which he preached and his concern for the welfare of his congregation had a great effect on them. Not only them, but folks came from the surrounding towns and villages to hear his preaching. A friend once reported, "Many times I thought he would have flown out of the pulpit when he came to speak of Jesus Christ."

Samuel was not estranged from grief and sorrow. In 1631, only four short years after he began his work as a pastor, his wife passed away. His two children also became ill and left this world. In 1636, after nine years of preaching, he was banished to Aberdeen, where he was forbidden to preach the gospel. This was a very difficult time for him as he greatly missed his wife and children as well as his congregation, the Church at Anwoth. This time in his life is indeed one reason he is so well remembered, for he began writing letters back to his church people and friends. Out of the 365 letters he wrote, 220 of them were written during these 22 months of banishment.

The government eventually changed hands, which gave more liberty to the non-conformist Covenanters. Thereupon Rutherford quickly returned to his beloved flock at Anwoth. About a year later, in the fall of 1639, he again reluctantly left Anwoth but this time to fulfill an appointment to become Professor of Divinity at St Mary's College in St. Andrews. This change was difficult for him, as he again greatly missed his congregation. He writes, "My removal from my flock is so heavy to me, that it maketh my life a burden to me, I had never such a longing for death. The Lord help and hold up this sad clay."

After five months in his new position and having been alone for nearly ten years, the 40-year-old Samuel married Jean McMath. Together they had seven children. Sadly, six of them died in infancy and early childhood. Only a daughter named Agnes survived to adulthood.

Rutherford continued to be an influential leader in the non-conformist movement in Scotland for the next 20 years until 1660. With the death of Cromwell, the rule of the commonwealth came to an end, and Charles II was restored to power. Once again, the wrath of the monarchy fell on Samuel. He was summoned to appear before the judge and charged with high treason against the government for preaching the truth. He was put in prison to await execution. However, before the king could put him to death, Samuel became quite sick. He said, "I have a summons already from a superior Judge, and I behoove to answer my first summons and when your day arrives I shall be where few Kings and great folks come."

Late in the afternoon of the last day of his life in answer to the question, "What think ye now of Christ?" answered thusly, "Oh, that all my brethren in the land may know what a Master I have served, and what peace I have this day! I shall sleep in Christ, and when I awake, I shall be satisfied with His likeness. This night shall close the door, and put my anchor within the veil, and I shall go away in a sleep by five of the clock in the morning. Glory! glory to my Creator and my Redeemer forever! I Shall live and adore Him. Oh, for arms to embrace Him! Oh, for a well-tuned harp! Glory! glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land!" These words were heard by his wife, daughter and friends, and he was indeed with his Lord by five in the morning.

Nearly two centuries later, Annie Ross Cousin, a Scottish poet and hymn writer and the wife of a minister, was inspired by the life and writings of Samuel Rutherford. She summarized his life in a biographical hymn,"The Sands of Time are Sinking". This hymn was first published in 1857 in the Christian Treasury. Out of the nineteen original verses, only four are used in our hymn books. (in bold copy)

The sands of time are sinking,
The dawn of heaven breaks,
The summer morn I’ve sighed for,
The fair, sweet morn awakes:
Dark, dark hath been the midnight,
But dayspring is at hand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

2. Oh! well it is forever,
Oh! well forevermore
My nest hung in no forest
Of all this death-doomed shore!
Yea, let the vain world vanish,
As from the ship the stand,
While glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

3. There the Red Rose of Sharon
Unfolds its heart-most bloom.
And fills the air of Heaven
With ravishing perfume;
Oh, to behold its blossom,
While by its fragrance fann’d
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

4. The King there in His beauty,
Without a veil is seen:
It were a well-spent journey
Though seven deaths lay between:
The Lamb with His fair army,
Doth on Mount Zion stand;
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

5. Oh! Christ He is the fountain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above;
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

6. E’en Anwoth was not heaven—
E’en preaching was not Christ;
And in my sea-beat prison
My Lord and I held tryst:
And aye my murkiest storm-cloud
Was by a rainbow spann’d,
Caught from the glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land.

7. But that He built a heaven
Of His surpassing love,
A little New Jerus’lem,
Like to the one above,—
“Lord, take me o’er the water,”
Had been my loud demand,
“Take me to love’s own country,
Unto Immanuel’s land.”

8. But flowers need night’s cool darkness,
The moonlight and the dew;
So Christ, from one who loved it,
His shining oft withdrew;
And then, for cause of absence,
My troubled soul I scann’d—
But glory, shadeless, shineth
In Immanuel’s land.

9. The little birds of Anwoth,
used to count them blest,—
Now, beside happier alters,
go to built my nest:
O’er these there broods no silence,
No graves around them stand,
For glory, deathless, dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

10. Fair Anwoth by the Solway,
To me thou still art dear!
E’en from the verge of Heaven
I drop for thee a tear.
Oh! if one soul from Anwoth
Meet me at God’s right hand,
My Heaven will be two Heavens,
In Immanuel’s land!

11. I’ve wrestled on towards Heaven,
‘Ganst storm, and wind, and tide;—
Now, like a weary traveler,
That leaneth on his guide,
Amid the shades of evening,
While sinks life’s ling’ring sand,
I hail the glory dawning
From Immanuel’s land.

12. Deep waters cross’d life’s pathway,
The hedge of thorns was sharp;
Now these lie all behind me,—
Oh, for a well-tuned harp!
Oh, to join Hallelujah
With yon triumphant band,
Who sing where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land!

13. With mercy and with judgment
My web of time He wove,
And aye the dews of sorrow
Were lustered with His love!
I’ll bless the hand that guided,
I’ll bless the heart that plann’d,
When throned where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

14. Soon shall the cup of glory
Wash down earth’s bitterest woes,
Soon shall the desert brier
Break into Eden’s rose:
The curse shall change to blessing–
The name on earth that’s bann’d,
Be graven on the white stone
In Immanuel’s land.

15. Oh! I am my Beloved’s,
And my Beloved’s mine!
He brings a poor vile sinner
Into His “house of wine:”
I stand upon His merit,
I know no other stand,
Not e’en where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

16. I shall sleep sound in Jesus,
Fill’d with His likeness rise,
To live and to adore Him,
To see Him with these eyes:
‘Tween me and resurrection
But Paradise doth stand;
Then—then for glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land!

17. The bride eyes not her garment,
But her dear Bridegroom’s face;
I will not gaze at glory,
But on my King of Grace—
Not at the crown He giveth,
But on His pierced hand:
The Lamb is all the glory
Of Immanuel’s land.

18. I have borne scorn and hatred,
I have borne wrong and shame,
Earth’s proud ones have reproach’d me,
For Christ’s thrice blessed name:
Where God His seal set fairest
They’ve stamp’d their foulest brand;
But judgment shines like noonday
In Immanuel’s land.

19. They’ve summoned me before them,
But there I may not come,—
My Lord says, “Come up hither,”
My Lord says, “Welcome home!
My King now at His white throne,
My presence doth command,
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

The fine complementary tune for this text was composed in the early 1800s by a French musician, Chretien D`Urhan. It is well fitted to the words of the hymn—its solemn tempo matches the solemnity of the words. The rising melodic line of the last phrase perfectly matches the anticipated joy expressed by the refrain—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

As we conclude this hymn history, let us continue to marvel at the providence of God in the lives of those who have gone before us. May we follow Christ with all our hearts and be vessels ready for the Master's use! One last quote by Samuel Rutherford to take with us. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."

The information for this article was sourced from 101 Hymn Stories, A Treasury of Hymns, Crichbaptist.org.

Inanivutia kuona jinsi Mungu anavyotumia watu Wake katika historia kuleta utukufu kwa Jina Lake. Anatumia vitu dhaifu kuwachanganya wenye hekima; vitu vya chini kuufanya uzingo wa wana watu wenye hekima wa dunia kutokuwa na thamani. Mungu anatumia udhaifu wa mwili, taabu, upotevu, majonzi, bidii, na maumivu kuongeza hazina zetu za kiroho na kujenga Ufalme Wake hapa duniani!

Wimbo huu ukawa wa thamani kwa familia yangu na mimi miaka michache iliyopita tuliposubiri kuzaliwa kwa mtoto wetu wa nne mwenye matatizo ya kijenetiki. Tulijua hangeweza kubaki kwa muda mrefu pamoja nasi. Alikufa akiwa na siku tatu tu. Baada ya kutafiti kuhusu wimbo huu, nilishangaa kugundua kwamba mtu aliyekuwa na hadithi iliyomhamasisha mwimbaji alimtangaza alipoteza watoto nane kati ya tisa wake.

Hadithi ya mtu huyu ni ya kutambulika. Miaka yake 61 duniani yamewekwa alama na majonzi na upotevu, mateso na kifungo. Hata hivyo, kujitolea kwake kwa Kristo kulikuwa kwa kiwango cha juu, na moto wake kwa Mungu na hamu yake ya kuhubiri injili hakukosekana hadi siku yake ya mwisho.

Samuel Rutherford, mwana wa mwanamkulima mwenye mali, alizaliwa mwaka 1600. Maisha yake yalianza katika kijiji kidogo cha Nisbet, Scotland. Tunapoangalia maisha yake, tunagundua mkono wa Mungu ukifanya kazi katika miaka ya mapema ya Samuel. Alipokuwa na miaka mitatu tu, alikuwa akicheza na marafiki zake alipokuwa anakumbwa na kuangukia kisima cha mji. Dada yake na marafiki wakakimbia kupata msaada. Waliporudi, walimpata Samuel akiwa amebeba maji karibu na kisima. Wakamwuliza alivyotoka, na aliposema, "Mtu mweupe mzuri alikuja akaninogoa kutoka kwenye kisima." Familia yake waliamini kwamba Mungu alimpeleka malaika kumwokoa siku hiyo.

Kulingana na tunachojua kuhusu Samuel Rutherford, alikuwa na ndugu wawili na dada mmoja. Alitumwa shule akiwa mdogo, na akawa mwanafunzi mwenye bidii sana. Alijifunza Kilatini na Kigiriki vizuri sana hadi hatimaye akawa profesa. Alioa Eupham Hamilton karibu mwaka 1624, hivi karibuni baada ya kuanza kufundisha katika Chuo Kikuu cha Edinburgh. Wakati huo, Samuel hakuwa bado ameongoka na alizingatia tu kufuatilia malengo yake ya kitaaluma.

Mwaka 1626, akiwa na umri wa miaka 26, Samuel alipata imani wazi na ya kuokolewa kwa Bwana Yesu Kristo. Alisema, "Ee lakini Kristo ana jicho la kuokoa. Alipolitania kwangu mara ya kwanza nilikuokoka. Ilimgharimu tu kuangalia kufanya kuzimu kuninyooshea." Tangu wakati huo alijazwa na shauku ya kuhubiri na kuzungumza kuhusu Mwokozi wake. Mabadiliko haya ya maisha yalisababisha vurugu katika chuo kiasi kwamba Rutherford alimaliza kujiuzulu nafasi yake ya uprofesa.

Mwaka 1627, Samuel alichukua mkewe na watoto wawili wadogo kwenda Galloway, Scotland, ambapo alianza kuwa mchungaji wa kanisa dogo la Anwoth. Alipoanza wito wake pale alisema, "Nimepokea mamlaka kutoka kwa Mwalimu wa kifalme na wa kijinga, Bwana wangu Yesu, kuhubiri Kristo kwa watu." Shauku yake ilikuwa kwa wokovu wa watu, na inasemekana kwamba alionekana kuwa daima anasali, daima anahubiri, daima akitembelea wagonjwa, daima akifundisha na kuelimisha, daima akiandika au akisoma. Waliopaa sana alivyohubiri na hamu yake kwa ustawi wa makanisa yao ilikuwa na athari kubwa kwao. Si wao tu, bali watu waliokuja kutoka miji na vijiji vinavyozunguka kumtukuzwa. Rafiki mmoja aliwahi kuripoti, "Mara nyingi nilifikiria angeweza kuruka kutoka kanisani alipokuwa anazungumzia Yesu Kristo."

Samuel hakuachwa na majonzi na huzuni. Mwaka 1631, miaka minne tu baada ya kuanza kazi yake kama mchungaji, mkewe alifariki. Watoto wake wawili pia wakaugua na kuondoka katika dunia hii. Mwaka 1636, baada ya miaka tisa ya kuhubiri, alitetewa hadi Aberdeen, ambapo aliamriwa kususia kuhubiri injili. Hii ilikuwa wakati mgumu kwake kwani alikosa sana mkewe na watoto pamoja na makanisa yake, Kanisa la Anwoth. Kipindi hiki maishani mwake ni mojawapo ya sababu anavyokumbukwa sana, kwa sababu alianza kuandika barua kwa watu wa kanisa lake na marafiki. Kutoka kwa barua 365 alizoandika, 220 kati yao ziliandikwa katika miezi 22 ya uhamisho huyo.

Serikali hatimaye ilibadilika mikononi, jambo ambalo lilileta uhuru zaidi kwa Wakili wa Agano waliositishwa. Hivyo Rutherford alirudi kwa haraka kwa kundi lake mpendwa Anwoth. Karibu mwaka mmoja baadaye, msimu wa vuli wa 1639, aliondoka tena Anwoth kwa kukasirika lakini wakati huu ili kutimiza uteuzi wa kuwa Profesa wa Ustaarabu katika St Mary's College huko St. Andrews. Mabadiliko haya yalikuwa magumu kwake, kwani tena alikosa sana makanisa yake. Anaandika, "Kuondoka kwangu kutoka kundi langu ni mzito sana kwangu, kiasi kwamba kunawafanya maisha yangu kuwa mzigo, sikuwahi kuwa na hamu kama hiyo ya kifo. Bwana anisaidie na kuimarisha mchanga huyu wa huzuni."

Baada ya miezi mitano katika nafasi yake mpya na akiwa peke yake kwa karibu miongo miwili, Samuel mwenye umri wa miaka 40 alioa Jean McMath. Pamoja walizaa watoto saba. Kwa masikitiko, sita kati yao walikufa utotoni na enzi za utoto. Ni binti mmoja aliyeitwa Agnes aliyebaki hadi ukuaji.

Rutherford aliendelea kuwa kiongozi mwenye ushawishi katika harakati za wasiobadilika nchini Scotland kwa miaka 20 iliyofuata hadi 1660. Kwa kifo cha Cromwell, utawala wa taifa lilikuja mwisho, na Charles II akarudishwa madarakani. Mara nyingine tena, hasira za kifalme zilimpata Samuel. Alitumwa kuonekana mbele ya jaji na kumshtaki kwa uhaini dhidi ya serikali kwa kuhubiri kweli. Alitumwa gerezani kusubiri kutekelezwa adhabu. Hata hivyo, kabla mfalme angeweza kumtii, Samuel aliuma sana. Alisema, "Nina wito tayari kutoka Jaji wa juu, na ni lazima nijibu wito wangu wa kwanza na wakati siku yako itafika nitakuwa mahali ambapo wafalme wachache na watu wakubwa huja."

Aliproga saa za jioni za siku yake ya mwisho, akijibu swali, "Mnadhani sasa nini kuhusu Kristo?" akajibu hivi, "Ee, wajua ndugu zangu wote katika nchi ni Mwanafunzi aliemwongoza nani nimehudumu kwake, na amani gani nina leo! Nitalala katika Kristo, na nitakapomwake nitafurahishwa kwa sura Yake. Usiku huu utaifunga mlango, na kuiweka nanga yangu ndani ya pazia, nami nitaondoka kwa usingizi saa tano asubuhi. Utukufu! utukufu kwa Muumba wangu na Mwokozi wangu milele! Nitaishi na kumwabudu. Ee, kwa mikono ya kumkumbatia! Ee, kwa kibao kilichopangwa vizuri! Utukufu! utukufu unaishi katika nchi ya Immanuel!" Maneno haya yaliwasikika na mkewe, binti na marafiki, na alikuwa pamoja na Mwanaweza kwake saa tano asubuhi.

Karibu karne mbili baadaye, Annie Ross Cousin, mshairi wa Scotland na mwandishi wa nyimbo na mke wa mchungaji, alihamasishwa na maisha na maandishi ya Samuel Rutherford. Aliandika muhtasari wa maisha yake katika wimbo wa kumbukumbu, "The Sands of Time are Sinking". Wimbo huu ulitolewa mara ya kwanza mwaka 1857 katika Christian Treasury. Kutoka kwa vifungu asilia kumi na tisa, vinne tu vinatumika katika vitabu vya nyimbo zetu. (kwa nakala iliyo kwa herufi nzito)

Wash down earth’s bitterest woes,
Soon shall the desert brier
Break into Eden’s rose:
The curse shall change to blessing–
The name on earth that’s bann’d,
Be graven on the white stone
In Immanuel’s land.

15. Oh! I am my Beloved’s,
And my Beloved’s mine!
He brings a poor vile sinner
Into His “house of wine:”
I stand upon His merit,
I know no other stand,
Not e’en where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

16. I shall sleep sound in Jesus,
Fill’d with His likeness rise,
To live and to adore Him,
To see Him with these eyes:
‘Tween me and resurrection
But Paradise doth stand;
Then—then for glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land!

17. The bride eyes not her garment,
But her dear Bridegroom’s face;
I will not gaze at glory,
But on my King of Grace—
Not at the crown He giveth,
But on His pierced hand:
The Lamb is all the glory
Of Immanuel’s land.

18. I have borne scorn and hatred,
I have borne wrong and shame,
Earth’s proud ones have reproach’d me,
For Christ’s thrice blessed name:
Where God His seal set fairest
They’ve stamp’d their foulest brand;
But judgment shines like noonday
In Immanuel’s land.

19. They’ve summoned me before them,
But there I may not come,—
My Lord says, “Come up hither,”
My Lord says, “Welcome home!
My King now at His white throne,
My presence doth command,
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

Tune nzuri inayolingana vizuri na maandishi haya ilitengenezwa mwanzoni mwa 1800 na mwanamuziki Mfaransa, Chretien D`Urhan. Inafaa vizuri kwa maneno ya wimbo—tembo yake ya hamsini inalingana na uzito wa maneno. Mstari wa melodi unaopanda katika kifungu cha mwisho unalingana kikamilifu na furaha inayotarajiwa iliyoonyeshwa na kifungu cha kurudia—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

Tunapo maliza historia ya wimbo huu, tuendelee kushangazwa na uenyeuzi wa Mungu katika maisha ya wale walio mbele yetu. Tufuate Kristo kwa mioyo yetu yote na tuwe vyombo vinavyotayarika kwa matumizi ya Mwalimu! Nukuu moja ya mwisho kutoka kwa Samuel Rutherford tuichukue pamoja nasi. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."

Taarifa kwa ajili ya makala hii ilichukuliwa kutoka 101 Hymn Stories, A Treasury of Hymns, Crichbaptist.org.

A wonderful thing about being a Christian is anticipating the day when we feast our eyes on the magnificent beauty of our God. Quite likely, we have all created mental pictures of what we think God might look like, although we know that our wildest imaginations will be exceeded. “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). The Bible is full of descriptive word pictures attempting to give us a brief glimpse into the realms of the heavenly. The landscape on the hills of glory, the wonderful creatures that dwell there, and most of all, the Supreme Being on the throne, all defy our human attempt to grasp and understand the beauty and glory of our God.

At times we admire beauty in a song, a work of art, a story, or even another person, but David describes the delight of gazing at the beauty of God. “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). God is beautiful because His excellence is attractive— His character is flawless. David experienced the pleasure that comes from knowing and experiencing God in all His fullness. How does God express His Beauty?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). In the awfulness of the Passion of Christ, we find a profound and sober beauty— the beauty of a sacrifice made by a sinless Savior for undeserving humanity. Sometimes the most stirring kind of beauty is found in things we cannot fully comprehend.

There is beauty in weeping of Mary and the disciples around the cross that held the lifeless body of their beloved Master. But when dawn broke on resurrection morning, despair turned into hope and grief into joy.

We see a beautiful scene at the Mount of Olives forty days later as the same disciples wistfully gazed into the sky, watching as their risen Lord disappeared into the heavens. With great joy, they returned to Jerusalem, with the promise of His return burning in their hearts, to wait for the coming of the Holy Spirit.

Today we expectantly wait for the Son of God to appear from heaven with power and great glory to complete the work of salvation. Then will we look upon Him in all His splendor and beauty. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

How should we, as God's image-bearers, reflect His beauty through the Gospel? God is an uncreated eternal being, and man was created in His image to reflect His glory and beauty. However, this beauty has been marred by sin and is no longer a worthy representation of God's character. But, there is redemption! Very little surpasses the beauty of a life that was once bruised and broken by sin but is now restored, redeemed, and made whole by the Gospel. “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). Atheists challenge the existence of God, scientists argue against Biblical creation, scholars question the inerrancy of scripture, but nobody can dispute the testimony of a redeemed life.

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). All beauty in the created world comes from God. A beautiful sunset, a lovely rose, a towering redwood, a majestic mountain peak, all testify of the beauty of God illustrated in creation. As road signs along the highway guide us to our destination, likewise, creation directs mankind to God himself. “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). These gifts of creation are given to give us a brief glimpse of the One who created them.

How should we, as part of God's creation, reflect His creative beauty? Although we cannot make something out of nothing, God has designed us to be creative, using the resources of His creation and our intellectual abilities to make life practical. The fulfilling sense of accomplishment derived from a job well done has its origin in creation, where God regarded His work and declared it to be good. In our attempt to live non-extravagant lives we sometimes fail to take joy in the beautiful things in life. It is right and good and in harmony with how we were created to find pleasure in things of beauty. Ungodly men have used this gift of creativity many times for evil means. So much the more, let us glorify God by using His creation in ways that reflect His character.

A warning for all who love nature and creation (natural and man-made): let us be careful to not elevate earthly beauty above the Creator, which leads to idolatry. Sunsets fade, redwoods tumble, roses wilt, the human body turns to dust again, but God remains. Life and all of its beauty begins and ends with God.

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) According to the book of Revelation, God's throne is surrounded by sound: thundering and lightning; praises flowing from the angels, the four beasts and twenty elders, and the great multitude which no man can number; and the new song by the one hundred and forty four thousand.

God created the beauty of sound to glorify Himself in ways that mere words cannot. The intricacy of His creativity is powerfully displayed in the way various sound frequencies come together to create a beautiful and heavenly harmony. It is honoring to God for mankind to take pleasure in the beauty of sounds He has created for His glory. The person who loves God will be drawn to Him whenever He is serenaded by pleasing sounds: the people of God singing the songs of Zion, the prayers of the saints, the wind whispering through the treetops, the songbird praising its Maker, the rumble of thunder, or the simple patter of rain on the roof.

How should we, as instruments of sound, reflect God's beauty through sound? We should always seek to listen to and resemble the sounds and harmonies of heaven. Although we will never be able to completely accomplish this on earth, it should be a lifelong endeavor. The questions have been asked,” Should we always be trying to improve our music making?” and “when have we reached ‘good enough’?” We will never be able to attain heavenly perfection, so the question should rather be asked, “Are we giving God the best we have?” Some people have more singing capabilities than others, but the question remains. “Are we giving our best or are we satisfied with an inferior sacrifice?” Let us be producers of God-honoring sounds that bring joy to the heart of the Creator!

Through the Church:

The Bible speaks extensively about the beauty of God's people. “Zion,” “The Temple,” “The Mountain of God,” “Jerusalem,” and“The Church” are synonymous expressions woven throughout scripture referring to the habitation of God's people on the earth. It is God's desire that His beauty would be reflected in the lives of His people. “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

Nothing is dearer to the heart of God than His church. When the children of Israel journeyed through the wilderness, they built the tabernacle as a place for God to dwell among them. When Solomon dedicated the temple as God's dwelling place, God was very pleased and 2 Chronicles 7:1 says the glory of the Lord filled the temple. The temple was considered the House of the Lord–Jesus himself referred to it numerous times as God's house and was very passionate that it should be kept holy.

Today, neither the tabernacle nor the temple hosts the presence of God but rather His divine passion is concentrated on the church of Jesus Christ. Here are the people who truly love Him and are willing to lay down their lives for Him. Here are the people who are willing to give up their rights as individuals and surrender themselves to a greater cause. Here is where many a saint has given His very life's blood for the Gospel. And here is where one day our Savior will return as He has promised, and will transport His bride, the church, to her eternal habitation. “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

How should we, as God's people, reflect His beauty in the church? By dwelling together in unity and harmony with love for all men, especially the household of God. The church should be a place where the world can get a glimpse of what goes on in heaven. It should be a place where Christ is always elevated as the victorious conqueror of sin, death, and hell.

Sadly, many people have become disoriented with the church's failures and have walked away from the true apostolic faith. In spite of our disappointments, let us “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) and let us press on. We will never have a higher calling, and never a more noble warfare to wage.

Lastly, how should we reflect His beauty in our lives? By delighting in Him. “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). The greatest fulfillment in life comes from finding pleasure in bringing joy to the heart of God by delighting in what He delights in and loving what He loves. Let us never lose the wonder of the beauty of our Salvation!

একজন খ্রিস্টান হওয়ার এক অনবদ্য বিষয় হল সেই দিনের প্রত্যাশা—যখন আমরা আমাদের ঈশ্বরের চমৎকার সৌন্দর্যকে নিজের চোখে দেখব। খুব সম্ভবত, আমরা সবাই মননে এমন ছবি তৈরির চেষ্টা করেছি যে ঈশ্বর কেমন দেখতে হতে পারে, যদিও আমরা জানি আমাদের সর্বাধিক কল্পনাও বিচ্ছিন্ন হবে। “Thine eyes shall see the king in his beauty: they shall behold the land that is very far off” (Isaiah 33:17). বাইবেল পূর্ণবিচিত্র বর্ণনামূলক দৃশ্যকল্পে, স্বর্গীয় রাজ্যের এক ক্ষুদ্র ঝলক দেওয়ার চেষ্টা করে। জয়ের পাহাড়ের ভুবন, সেখানে বাস করা আশ্চর্যপ্রাণীসমূহ, এবং সর্বোপরি, সিংহাসনে অধিষ্ঠিত সর্বশক্তিমান—এসবই আমাদের মানব-চেষ্টাকে ছাপিয়ে যায় যখন আমরা ঈশ্বরের সৌন্দর্য ও মহিমা বোঝার চেষ্টা করি।

কখনো কখনো আমরা একটি গান, একটি শিল্পকর্ম, একটি কাহিনি, কিংবা অন্য কোনো ব্যক্তির সৌন্দর্যে বিস্ময় বোধ করি, কিন্তু ডেভিড ঈশ্বরের সৌন্দর্য ঘেঁটে দেখার আনন্দ বর্ণনা করেন। “One thing have I desired of the LORD, that will I seek after; that I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, to behold the beauty of the LORD, and to inquire in his temple” (Psalm 27:4). ঈশ্বর সুন্দর কারণ তাঁর উৎকৃষ্টতা আকর্ষণীয়—তাঁর চরিত্র নিখুঁত। ডেভিড পূর্ণতায় ঈশ্বরকে জানার এবং অভিজ্ঞতার যে আনন্দ পেয়েছিলেন তা অনুভব করেছিলেন। ঈশ্বর কীভাবে নিজের সৌন্দর্য প্রকাশ করেন?

Through the Gospel

“In whom the god of this world hath blinded the minds of them which believe not, lest the light of the glorious gospel of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine unto them. For we preach not ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus' sake. For God, who commanded the light to shine out of darkness, hath shined in our hearts, to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ” (2 Corinthians 4:4-6). খristo-এর যন্ত্রণা-পর্বের ভয়ঙ্করতায় আমরা গভীর ও সম্ভ্রমপূর্ণ একটি সৌন্দর্য পাই—একটি পুণ্যঝরা ত্যাগের সৌন্দর্য, যা পাপহীন উদ্ধারকর্তা অস্বার্থভাবে অপরাধী মানবতার জন্য করলেন। কখনো কখনো সবচেয়ে হৃদয়স্পর্শী সৌন্দর্য সেই সব জিনিসে থাকে যা আমরা সম্পূর্ণরূপে বুঝতে পারি না।

মেরি এবং শিষ্যদের ক্রুশের চারপাশে তাদের প্রিয় গুরু-র অলীহ্য শারীরিক দেহের সামনে কাঁদায় সৌন্দর্য আছে। কিন্তু পুনরুত্থানের সকালে ভোর যখন ফুটে উঠল, হতাশা আশা হয়ে উঠল এবং শোক আনন্দে রূপান্তরিত হল।

চল্লিশ দিন পর অলিভস পাহাড়ে আমরা একটি সুন্দর দৃশ্য দেখি: একই শিষ্যগণ ক্ষুব্ধবুদ্ধি করে আকাশের দিকে তাকিয়ে রইল, যখন তাদের রাইজেন স্বামী স্বর্গে অদৃশ্য হয়ে চললেন। তাঁরা বড় আনন্দে জেরুজালেমে ফিরে গেলেন, তাঁর প্রত্যাবর্তনের প্রতিশ্রুতি তাদের হৃদয়ে জ্বলন্ত রেখে, পবিত্র আত্মার আগমনের প্রতীক্ষায়।

আজ আমরা আশাভরে প্রতীক্ষা করি যে ঈশ্বরের পুত্র স্বর্গ হইতে শক্তি ও মহান মহিমায় Erschein মত প্রকাশ করবেন যাতে তৎপর্যরুপে তিলোত্তমায়নের কাজ সম্পন্ন হয়। তখন আমরা সম্পূর্ণরূপে সব তাঁর গৌরব ও সৌন্দর্যে চেয়ে দেখব। “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known” (1 Corinthians 13:12).

আমরা, ঈশ্বরের ছবির বাহক হিসাবে, কিভাবে পবিত্র বার্তায় তাঁর সৌন্দর্য প্রতিফলিত করব? ঈশ্বর অঅন্মিত চিরন্তন এক সত্তা, এবং মানুষ তাঁর প্রতিমায় সৃষ্ট হয়েছিল যাতে তিনি তাঁর গৌরব ও সৌন্দর্য প্রতিফলিত করতেন। কিন্তু এই সৌন্দর্য পাপ দ্বারা লাঞ্ছিত হয়েছে এবং আর ঈশ্বরের চরিত্রের যোগ্য প্রতিনিধিত্ব নয়। তবু, পুণরুত্তান রয়েছে! যে জীবন এককাল পাপে আঘাতপ্রাপ্ত ও ভাঙাচোরা ছিল কিন্তু এখন সুসংহত, মুক্তিপ্রাপ্ত ও সুস্থ করা হয়েছে সুসমাচারের মাধ্যমে—তার সৌন্দর্যের তুলনা খুব কমই হয়। “To appoint unto them that mourn in Zion, to give unto them beauty for ashes, the oil of joy for mourning, the garment of praise for the spirit of heaviness; that they might be called trees of righteousness, the planting of the LORD, that He might be glorified” (Isaiah 61:3). নাস্তিকরা ঈশ্বরের অস্তিত্বকে চ্যালেঞ্জ করে, বিজ্ঞানীরা বাইবেলীয় সৃষ্টির বিরোধিতা করে, পণ্ডিতরা শাস্ত্রের অপরাধ্যতা প্রশ্ন করে, কিন্তু কাউকে একজন পুনরুদ্ধৃত জীবনের সাক্ষ্য অস্বীকার করতে পারবে না।

Through Creation

“The heavens declare the glory of God; and the firmament showeth His handy work” (Psalm 19:1). সৃষ্ট জগতে সমস্ত সৌন্দর্য ঈশ্বরের কাছ থেকে আসে। একটি সুন্দর সূর্যাস্ত, একটি মনোরম গোলাপ, একটি বিশাল রেডউড, একটি মহিমান্বিত পাহাড়চূড়া—এসব সব সৃষ্টিতে ঈশ্বরের সৌন্দর্যের সাক্ষ্য দেয়। পথচিহ্নগুলো আমাদের গন্তব্যে পৌঁছাতে সাহায্য করে যেমনটি রাস্তায় থাকে, তেমনি সৃষ্টি মানবকে ঈশ্বরের প্রতি নির্দেশ করে। “For the invisible things of Him from the creation of the world are clearly seen . . .” (Romans 1:20). এই সৃষ্টির উপহারসমূহ আমাদেরকে সেগুলো সৃষ্ট করেছেন তিনি—তাঁর এক ক্ষুদ্র ঝলক দেখানোর উদ্দেশ্যে দেওয়া হয়েছে।

আমরা, ঈশ্বরের সৃষ্টির অংশ হিসেবে, কিভাবে তাঁর সৃষ্টিশীল সৌন্দর্য প্রতিফলিত করব? আমরা যেন শব্দশূন্য থেকে কিছু সৃষ্টি করতে না পারি, তবু ঈশ্বর আমাদের সৃষ্টিশীল হতে পরিকল্পিত করেছেন; তিনি আমাদের সৃষ্টির সম্পদ এবং আমাদের বুদ্ধিবৃত্তিক সক্ষমতা ব্যবহার করে জীবনকে বাস্তববান্ধব করার জন্য। ভালোভাবে সম্পন্ন কাজ থেকে যে পরিপূরণ আনন্দ আসে তা সৃষ্টিতেই মূলভিত্তি—যেখানে ঈশ্বর তাঁর কর্ম দেখলেন ও বললেন যে তা ভাল। বিলাসিতা এড়িয়ে বাঁচার চেষ্টায় আমরা কখনো কখনো জীবনের সুন্দর জিনিসগুলিতে আনন্দ নেওয়া ভুলে যাই। সুন্দর জিনিসে আনন্দ পাওয়া সঠিক ও ভাল এবং এটি আমাদের সৃষ্টি-উদ্দীপনার সঙ্গে সঙ্গতিপূর্ণ। অধর্মীরা বহুবার এই সৃষ্টিশীল উপহারটি অন্যায় কাজে ব্যবহার করেছে। এ কারণেই আমরা আরও বেশি করে ঈশ্বরকে মহিমান্বিত করি যখন আমরা তাঁর সৃষ্টিকে এমনভাবে ব্যবহার করি যা তাঁর চরিত্র প্রতিফলিত করে।

প্রকৃতি ও সৃষ্টিকে প্রেম করা প্রত্যেকের জন্য একটি সতর্কবার্তা (প্রাকৃতিক ও মানব-নির্মিত): আসুন আমরা সতর্ক থাকি যেন জাগতিক সৌন্দর্যকে স্রষ্টার ওপরে উন্নীত না করি, যা মূর্তিপূজার দিকে নিয়ে যায়। সূর্যাস্ত ক্ষয়িষ্ণু, রেডউড ছিন্ন হয়, গোলাপ নিস্তেজ হয়, মানবদেহ পুনরায় ধূলিতে পরিণত হয়, কিন্তু ঈশ্বর অমলিন থাকেন। জীবন ও তার সমস্ত সৌন্দর্য ঈশ্বর দিয়ে শুরু এবং ঈশ্বরেই শেষ।

Through Music and Sound

“And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps” (Revelation 14:2) প্রকাশিতির বই অনুসারে, ঈশ্বরের সিংহাসন শব্দে পরিবেষ্টিত: বজ্রধ্বনি ও বিদ্যুৎ; দেবদূতদের গাওয়া প্রশংসা, চারপাশের প্রাণীর ও বিশ বার্ষিক বয়স্কদের ধারা, এবং অগণিত বৃহৎ বহুবর্গের কণ্ঠ; এবং এক শত চল্লিশ চার হাজারের নতুন গান।

ঈশ্বর শব্দের সৌন্দর্য সৃষ্টি করেছেন যাতে তিনি নিজের মহিমা এমনভাবে উপস্থাপন করতে পারেন যা কেবল শব্দে প্রকাশ করা যায় না। বিভিন্ন শব্দ-আবর্তন একত্রে মিলিত হয়ে যে সুমধুর স্বর্গীয় সঙ্গীত সৃষ্টি করে, তাতে তাঁর সৃষ্টিশীলতার জটিলতা শক্তিমানেরূপে প্রদর্শিত হয়। মানুষ যখন তাঁর সৃষ্টি করা শব্দের সৌন্দর্যে আনন্দ লাভ করে তখন তা ঈশ্বরকে সম্মান দেখানো। ঈশ্বরকে ভালোবাসা যারা করেন তারা তিনি যখন আনন্দদায়ক শব্দে সুরোজ্জীবিত হন তখন তাঁর কাছে আকৃষ্ট হবেন: জিয়োনের লোকেরা যখন গীত গায়, সাধুদের প্রার্থনা, গাছের শীর্ষে বাতাসের ফিসফিস, পাখির স্রষ্টাকে প্রশংসা করা গান, বজ্রধ্বনির গর্জন, কিংবা ছাদে বৃষ্টির সরল টিপ টিপ ধ্বনি।

আমরা, শব্দের যন্ত্র হিসেবে, কিভাবে শব্দের মাধ্যমে ঈশ্বরের সৌন্দর্য প্রতিফলিত করব? আমাদের সবসময় স্বর্গীয় শব্দ ও সুরের মতো শুনতে এবং অনুকরণ করতে চেষ্টা করা উচিত। যদিও আমরা পৃথিবীতে কখনও পূর্ণতা অর্জন করতে পারব না, এটি আজীবন চেষ্টা হওয়া উচিৎ। প্রশ্নগুলো করা হয়েছে: “আমরা কি সর্বদা আমাদের সঙ্গীত-তৈরি উন্নত করতে চেষ্টা করা উচিত?” এবং “কখন আমরা ‘যতটা ঠিক আছে’ পর্যায়ে পৌঁছেছি?” আমরা কখনই স্বর্গীয় পরিপূর্ণতা অর্জন করতে পারব না, তাই বরং প্রশ্ন হওয়া উচিত, “আমরা কি ঈশ্বরকে আমাদের সেরাটা দিচ্ছি?” কারো কারো গানের সক্ষমতা অন্যের চেয়ে বেশি, তবে প্রশ্ন একই থাকে: “আমরা কি আমাদের সেরাটা দিচ্ছি, নাকি নিম্নমানের একটি ত্যাগে সন্তুষ্ট?” আসুন আমরা এমন সুর উৎপাদন করি যা ঈশ্বরকে সম্মানিত করে এবং যে সুর স্রষ্টার হৃদয়ে আনন্দ আনে!

Through the Church:

বাইবেল ব্যাপকভাবে ঈশ্বরের লোকদের সৌন্দর্য সম্পর্কে কথা বলে। “জিয়োন,” “মন্দির,” “ঈশ্বরের পাহাড়,” “জেরুজালেম,” এবং “গির্জা”—এসব সমার্থক প্রকাশ যা লেখ্যসমূহ জুড়ে ঈশ্বরের লোকদের বসবাসস্থলকে নির্দেশ করে। ঈশ্বর চান যে তাঁর সৌন্দর্য তাঁর লোকদের জীবনে প্রতিফলিত হোক। “Great is the LORD, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of His holiness. Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is Mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King” (Psalm 48:1-2).

ঈশ্বরের হৃদয়ের কাছে তাঁর গির্জার চেয়ে আর কিছুই প্রিয় নয়। ইস্রায়েলদের মরু পথে যাত্রার সময় তারা তাঁকে অধিবাসনের জন্য তাঁবু নির্মাণ করেছিল, যাতে ঈশ্বর তাঁদের মধ্যে বাস করতে পারেন। সলোমণ যখন মন্দিরকে ঈশ্বরের নিবাস হিসেবে উৎসর্গ করেছিলেন, ঈশ্বর অত্যন্ত সন্তুষ্ট হলেন এবং 2 Chronicles 7:1 বলে, প্রভুর মহিমা মন্দিরকে পূর্ণ করল। মন্দিরকে প্রভুর গৃহ বলা হত—যিনি নিজে বহুবার এই ঘরকে ঈশ্বরের ঘর হিসেবে উল্লেখ করেছেন এবং এটি পবিত্র রাখা নিয়ে তিনি অত্যন্ত আশান্বিত ছিলেন।

আজকাল, না তাঁবু ও না মন্দির ঈশ্বরের উপস্থিতি বহন করে; বরং তাঁর ঐশ্বরিক আবেগ যীশু খ্রিস্টের গির্জার উপর নিবদ্ধ। এখানে মানুষ আছে যারা সত্যিকার অর্থে তাঁকে ভালোবাসে এবং তাঁর জন্য প্রাণ পর্যন্ত বিসর্জন দিতে প্রস্তুত। এখানে লোক আছে যারা ব্যক্তিস্বত্ব ত্যাগ করে বৃহত্তর কারণে আত্মসমর্পণ করতে ইচ্ছুক। এখানে বহু সাধু তাদের জীবনের রক্ত সুসমাচারের জন্য় দিয়েছেন। এবং এখানেই এক দিন আমাদের উদ্ধারকর্তা তাঁর প্রতিশ্রুতির মতো প্রত্যাবর্তন করবেন, এবং তাঁর কনে—গির্জা—কে তাঁর চিরস্থায়ী নিবাসে নিয়ে যাবেন। “And I John saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them, and be their God” (Revelation 21:2-3).

আমরা, ঈশ্বরের লোকদেরূপে, গির্জায় কিভাবে তাঁর সৌন্দর্য প্রতিফলিত করব? একতায় এবং সকল মানুষের প্রতি, বিশেষত ঈশ্বরের গৃহের সদস্যদের প্রতি ভালোবাসায় ঐক্য ও সামঞ্জস্যে বসবাস করে। গির্জা এমন একটি স্থান হওয়া উচিত যেখানে পৃথিবী স্বর্গে যা ঘটে তার এক ঝলক পায়। এটি এমন একটি স্থান হওয়া উচিত যেখানে ক্রিস্টকে সর্বদা পাপ, মৃত্যু, ও নরকের উপর জয়ী বিজয়ী হিসেবে উত্থাপন করা হয়।

দুঃখজনকভাবে, বহু লোক গির্জার ব্যর্থতায় বিভ্রান্ত হয়ে সত্য আধবপোপান্তিক বিশ্বাস থেকে বিচলিত হয়ে গেছে। আমাদের হতাশার বিপরীতেও, আসুন আমরা “lift up the hands which hang down and the feeble knees” (Hebrews 12:12) করি এবং এগিয়ে চলি। আমাদের কখনোই বেশি উচ্চ আহ্বান থাকবে না, এবং কখনোই বেশি মহৎ যুদ্ধযজ্ঞ চলবে না।

অবশেষে, আমরা কিভাবে আমাদের জীবনে তাঁর সৌন্দর্য প্রতিফলিত করব? তাঁর মধ্যে আনন্দ দেখে। “Delight thyself also in the LORD; and He shall give thee the desires of thine heart” (Psalm 37:4). জীবনের সর্বোচ্চ পরিপূরণ আসে ঈশ্বরের মনের আনন্দে আনন্দ পাওয়ায়—যার মধ্যে তিনি আনন্দ পান তাতে আমরা আনন্দিত হয়ে এবং তিনি যাকে ভালোবাসেন আমরা তাতে প্রেম পোষণ করে। আসুন আমরা কখনোও আমাদের মুক্তির সৌন্দর্যের বিস্ময় হারাই না!
