The winter of 1882 unfolded in the small southern town of Tuscumbia, Alabama. A happy, normal two-year-old girl fell desperately ill with a strange fever. The fever came and went, came and went, and came again. The family doctor feared the child would die of the strain, but the child was strong and one day the fever finally left for good. The following day the mother waved a hand past her daughter's face, but the child did not blink. Subsequent efforts wrought no results and a new day dawned upon the family with a blind daughter.

As the child gained strength enough to resume play, the great dinner bell released its peal to all around, but Helen did not respond. Other noises produced similar results and the Keller family came to the stark realization that life would never be the same again. Most of us may never face the grim circumstances that Helen Keller's family did, but each of us will certainly endure hardships tailored specifically by our God.

The human mind is an amazing and intricate creation. Though many have sought to understand it, its operational ability remains incomprehensible to mankind. It is no small wonder that a portion of the keenest insight into the health of the mind is revealed in God's Word. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Fear is the ominous adversary to a sound mind. It towers over the soul and taunts the saint with its menacing derision. Fear can take a sunny meadow and turn it into a lonely wilderness. It can render a grand wedding celebration as dark as a cave, and turn a banquet fit for a king into a nauseating affair. It is the most powerful and devastating tool in the devil's employment. Despite many bold claims, none are exempt from its wielding. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) It is fear that stands to attack and quench all the prosperity of the soul. If we are to resist it in these days, we he must rise with all diligence in defiant warfare.

We do not need to look very far to behold the disarmament and weakening of man's mind. Medication for the mind ranks among the leading prescriptions consumed in America today. This is no pointed accusation at any individuals who may find themselves in need of medical assistance to control their mind. But it takes no scholar to look at obesity and consider the diet, to see rebellious teens and connect it to the infrastructure of the home, or to see men's hearts (minds) failing them and believe that fear is at the root. While some may totally master their diet, few can claim to be accomplished parents. Fewer yet are those who are not, at times, accosted by fear. Though pride and sense may keep the outward man in check, and remaining perfectly calm, the inward man, at least subconsciously, must deal with the strain. Americans love to claim the motto, "No fear!" but our medication consumption tells a different story. Paul claimed no exemption, for he was “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

What do we fear? Loss, pain, and humility. No one likes to lose something that we have fought to obtain. No one enjoys pain. No one loves to be humiliated. Still, we do not need to read far in the Scriptures to realize that these are often the avenues that God uses to further urge His servants down the path into His likeness. There is no insurance on earth that can secure the vibrancy of youth, the love of a family, or the respect of friends. The things that supply us with earth's greatest vanguard are all vulnerable to the risks of loss. Therefore, we fear. Though we lie in bed until the dawn of the morning, we can in no wise increase our stature nor alleviate the loss that God has laid upon our lives. This anxiety only furthers our grief and adds fuel to our fears.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Herein is the keeping of our hearts and minds: prayer, peace, and thanksgiving.

Like a skillful artisan we must carefully weave these two scriptures together on the loom of life for there seems to be a direct correlation between the fruitful - power, love and sound mind, to the “rootful”- prayer, peace, and thankfulness. There will be no conquering of our fears without these things, and every society that is anemic to these ingredients will certainly be handicapped.

Prayer Begets Power

In our weakened condition we cannot apprehend prayer as we ought. It is then we must rely on those who can or perhaps the Spirit, which maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Communing with the Omnipotent Head of the universe is a tremendously bold task. Many will administer prayer as merely a formal task, seeking to be perfectly reverent in it. This is not communing as with a friend, nor is it bold. It is more apt to fall under the description of fear. The remedial therapy for fear is in pouring out all our anxiety, bitterness, and complaint onto our God. The saints of yesteryear had been known to vehemently pour out their accusations and the bitterness of their soul unto God.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

All these spewed forth bold accusations and complaints against God in fervent prayer and none of them offended Him. On the contrary, God had not given them the spirit of fear but of power, and they serve as our examples. It was faithless Ahab who was told to ask of God a sign in the heavens or earth. In his pious reply he refused to "tempt" God. This lack of boldness and abundance of fear is more tempting to God than the abundance of bitterness in our complaint for “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Peace Begets Love

We are all at rest with the things we love. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) A sparkling young child who is at peace with his father worships the man and strives to imitate him. Through the lad's tender eyes, his father's character is unflawed. His skill is unmatched. Even the brand of vehicle he drives is the best, and he emulates his every action. Even though every father knows the limitations of his son's expectations, we all bask in the seasonal loyalty. It is knowledge and fear that undermines this loyal love. An abusive father will destroy such childhood esteem and fear will be its replacement. It was through base fear that the evil servant buried his talent and did not trade with it. In his eyes his master was austere and to be feared. But God has not given us the spirit of fear but of love.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) The soul who is affected by this love cannot but imitate it. He is at great peace with his Father’s love and the eyes through which he views his Father's character can only enlist replication. However dire the circumstances we may find ourselves in, this spirit of love and peace will carry us through whatever opposition we may meet with on life's pathway. Jacob made nothing of the hard service he was to endure for Rachel; the spirit of love to God will set us above the fear of man, and all the hurt that a man can do us.

Thankfulness Begets a Sound Mind

We do not need to study happy souls long to find buried within the bedrock of each one, a foundation of gratitude. The spirit of a sound mind, or quietness of mind, is a peaceable enjoyment of life. We are oftentimes discouraged in our way when the features of our environment do not measure not up to our own fancy and imagination. A mere sober, solid, thinking mind would obviate and defuse such fruitless notions, yet we are all tempted to entertain formidable ingratitude. It takes no brainpower to expose things we disdain, for Satan is certain to magnify and outline every unsatisfactory detail we encounter. We each may think ourselves into a deep cave, but we must thank ourselves out.

Fear of losing our health, wealth, reputation, and happiness is the biggest hindrance to securing it. To focus on our pain is to invite more. To be constantly analyzing our life to see if we are being fulfilled is a sure avenue to ingratitude. The world is constantly asking, "Are we having fun yet?" The answer is, "No". To these souls, life will never be adequate, and they must wander forth seeking the bigger fulfillment that the last one did not secure. It is the fear that we are not receiving our fair allotment in life that breeds discontentment. It is discontentment that produces more fear, and the downward spiral progresses. Such was the consternation of the soul who asked Christ to speak to his brother to divide the inheritance with him. This may be logical thinking, but it is not conducive to a sound and peaceable mind. This offended soul has no root in himself and will forever be wronged in some fashion and spend his days in search of a savior to come and fix the other party. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

There is no earthly level of attainment or perfect environment that will promote a sound mind. It can only be secured through prayer, peace, and thankfulness. This may take some reprogramming of our minds to reach into the subconscious recesses, but we must soberly gird up the loins of our minds and exercise them if we ever hope to obtain “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8

O inverno de 1882 desenrolou-se na pequena cidade do sul de Tuscumbia, Alabama. Uma feliz e comum menina de dois anos adoeceu gravemente com uma febre estranha. A febre ia e vinha, ia e vinha, e voltou novamente. O médico da família temeu que a criança morresse por causa do esforço, mas ela era forte e um dia a febre finalmente passou de vez. No dia seguinte, a mãe passou a mão diante do rosto da filha, mas a criança não piscou. Tentativas subsequentes não produziram resultado e um novo dia nasceu para a família com uma filha cega.

À medida que a criança recuperou forças suficientes para voltar a brincar, o grande sino do jantar ecoou para todos ao redor, mas Helen não respondeu. Outros ruídos produziram resultados semelhantes e a família Keller chegou à dura percepção de que a vida nunca mais seria a mesma. A maioria de nós talvez nunca enfrente as sombrias circunstâncias que a família de Helen Keller enfrentou, mas cada um de nós certamente suportará provações moldadas especificamente pelo nosso Deus.

A mente humana é uma criação incrível e intrincada. Embora muitos tenham procurado entendê-la, sua capacidade operacional permanece incompreensível para a humanidade. Não é pouca coisa que parte da percepção mais aguda sobre a saúde da mente seja revelada na Palavra de Deus. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

O medo é o ominoso adversário de uma mente sã. Ele se ergue sobre a alma e zomba do santo com sua derisão ameaçadora. O medo pode transformar um prado ensolarado em um deserto solitário. Pode tornar uma grande celebração de casamento tão escura quanto uma caverna e transformar um banquete digno de um rei em um acontecimento nauseante. É a ferramenta mais poderosa e devastadora no emprego do diabo. Apesar de muitas declarações ousadas, ninguém está isento de seu manejo. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) É o medo que está pronto para atacar e apagar toda a prosperidade da alma. Se quisermos resisti‑lo nestes dias, devemos erguer‑nos com toda diligência em guerra de desafio.

Não precisamos olhar muito longe para contemplar o desarmamento e o enfraquecimento da mente do homem. Medicamentos para a mente estão entre as prescrições mais consumidas na América hoje. Isto não é uma acusação direta contra quaisquer indivíduos que possam necessitar de assistência médica para controlar sua mente. Mas não é preciso ser erudito para olhar para a obesidade e considerar a dieta, ver adolescentes rebeldes e associá‑los à infraestrutura do lar, ou observar os corações (mentes) dos homens falharem e crer que o medo está na raiz. Enquanto alguns podem dominar totalmente sua dieta, poucos podem afirmar ser pais realizados. Ainda menos são aqueles que não são, às vezes, acometidos pelo medo. Embora o orgulho e o juízo possam manter o homem exterior sob controle, permanecendo perfeitamente calmo, o homem interior, ao menos subconscientemente, precisa lidar com a tensão. Os americanos adoram proclamar o lema, "No fear!" mas nosso consumo de medicamentos conta uma história diferente. Paulo não reivindicou isenção, pois ele foi “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

Do que temos medo? Perda, dor e humilhação. Ninguém gosta de perder algo pelo qual lutou para obter. Ninguém gosta de dor. Ninguém ama ser humilhado. Ainda assim, não precisamos ler muito nas Escrituras para perceber que estes costumam ser os caminhos que Deus usa para conduzir seus servos mais adiante no caminho de sua semelhança. Não existe seguro na terra que possa garantir a vivacidade da juventude, o amor de uma família ou o respeito de amigos. As coisas que nos fornecem a maior vanguarda terrena estão todas vulneráveis ao risco de perda. Portanto, temos medo. Embora possamos permanecer na cama até o amanhecer, de maneira alguma podemos aumentar nossa estatura nem aliviar a perda que Deus impôs sobre nossas vidas. Essa ansiedade apenas agrava nosso pesar e adiciona combustível aos nossos temores.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Aqui está a preservação de nossos corações e mentes: oração, paz e ação de graças.

Como um habilidoso artesão, devemos cuidadosamente entrelaçar estas duas escrituras no tear da vida, pois parece haver uma correlação direta entre o frutífero — poder, amor e mente sã — e o "enraizador" — oração, paz e gratidão. Não haverá conquista de nossos medos sem estas coisas, e toda sociedade que for anêmica a esses ingredientes certamente ficará prejudicada.

Prayer Begets Power

Em nossa condição enfraquecida não conseguimos apreender a oração como deveríamos. É então que devemos confiar naqueles que podem ou talvez no Espírito, que maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Comunicar‑se com o Cabeça Onipotente do universo é uma tarefa tremendamente ousada. Muitos administrarão a oração como mera formalidade, buscando ser perfeitamente reverentes nela. Isso não é comunhão como com um amigo, nem é ousadia. Está mais apto a cair sob a descrição de medo. A terapia remedial para o medo está em derramar toda a nossa ansiedade, amargura e queixa sobre o nosso Deus. Os santos de antigamente eram conhecidos por derramar veementemente suas acusações e a amargura de suas almas diante de Deus.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

Todos estes vomitaram acusações e queixas ousadas contra Deus em oração fervorosa e nenhum deles o ofendeu. Pelo contrário, Deus não lhes deu o espírito de medo, mas de poder, e eles servem como nossos exemplos. Foi Acabe, sem fé, que recebeu ordem de pedir a Deus um sinal nos céus ou na terra. Em sua resposta piedosa ele se recusou a "tempt" God. Essa falta de ousadia e abundância de medo é mais tentadora para Deus do que a abundância de amargura em nossa queixa, pois “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Peace Begets Love

Estamos todos em paz com as coisas que amamos. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) Uma criança jovem e brilhante que está em paz com seu pai adora o homem e esforça‑se para imitá‑lo. Pelos olhos tenros do menino, o caráter de seu pai é sem falhas. Sua habilidade é incomparável. Mesmo a marca do veículo que ele dirige é a melhor, e ele emula cada ação sua. Embora todo pai conheça as limitações das expectativas de seu filho, todos nós usufruímos da lealdade sazonal. É o conhecimento e o medo que minam esse amor leal. Um pai abusivo destruirá tal estima infantil e o medo será seu substituto. Foi por medo vil que o servo mau enterrou seu talento e não o negociou. Aos seus olhos, seu senhor era austero e digno de temor. Mas Deus não nos deu o espírito de medo, e sim de amor.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) A alma afetada por esse amor não pode deixar de imitá‑lo. Ela está em grande paz com o amor de seu Pai e os olhos com os quais vê o caráter do seu Pai só podem promover a replicação. Por mais terríveis que sejam as circunstâncias em que possamos nos encontrar, esse espírito de amor e paz nos conduzirá através de qualquer oposição que possamos encontrar no caminho da vida. Jacó não fez caso do serviço duro que deveria suportar por Raquel; o espírito de amor a Deus nos elevará acima do temor do homem e de todo o dano que um homem possa nos causar.

Thankfulness Begets a Sound Mind

Não precisamos estudar almas alegres por muito tempo para encontrar enterrado na rocha-mãe de cada uma, um alicerce de gratidão. O espírito de uma mente sã, ou tranquilidade de mente, é um desfrute pacífico da vida. Muitas vezes nos desencorajamos em nosso caminho quando as características do nosso ambiente não correspondem à nossa própria fantasia e imaginação. Uma mente sóbria, sólida e pensante obviaria e desarmaria tais noções infrutíferas, contudo todos somos tentados a entreter uma ingratidão formidável. Não é preciso poder cerebral para expor coisas que desprezamos, pois Satanás certamente ampliará e delineará cada detalhe insatisfatório que encontramos. Cada um de nós pode pensar‑se em uma caverna profunda, mas devemos nos agradecer para sair dela.

O medo de perder nossa saúde, riqueza, reputação e felicidade é o maior impedimento para garanti‑los. Focar em nossa dor é convidar mais dor. Analisar constantemente a vida para ver se estamos sendo realizados é uma via certa para a ingratidão. O mundo está constantemente perguntando: "Are we having fun yet?" A resposta é: "No". Para essas almas, a vida nunca será adequada, e elas devem vagar em busca de uma satisfação maior que a anterior não alcançou. É o medo de que não estamos recebendo nossa parte justa na vida que gera descontentamento. É o descontentamento que produz mais medo, e a espiral descendente avança. Tal era a consternação da alma que pediu a Cristo que falasse com seu irmão para dividir a herança com ele. Isto pode ser raciocínio lógico, mas não é propício a uma mente sã e pacífica. Essa alma ofendida não tem raiz em si mesma e estará para sempre injustiçada de alguma forma e passará seus dias em busca de um salvador que venha consertar a outra parte. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

Não existe nível terreno de conquista nem ambiente perfeito que promova uma mente sã. Só pode ser garantida por meio de oração, paz e gratidão. Isso pode exigir alguma reprogramação de nossas mentes para alcançar os recessos subconscientes, mas devemos cingir sóbria e exercitar as partes da nossa mente se algum dia esperamos obter “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8

Morals have to do with right and wrong behavior. Purity is being free from moral fault or guilt, marked by chastity, which is personal integrity. Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

Moral berhubungan dengan perilaku yang benar dan salah. Kemurnian adalah terbebas dari kesalahan moral atau rasa bersalah, ditandai oleh kesucian, yang merupakan integritas pribadi. Kemurnian tidak mengandung apa pun yang tidak semestinya ada di situ. Seperti judulnya, artikel ini akan membahas melakukan yang benar dan terbebas dari kesalahan serta rasa bersalah secara moral, hidup dengan integritas, dan menjaga bagian dalam dan luar kita tetap bebas dari apa pun yang tidak semestinya ada.

Perhatikan apa yang dikatakan tulisan suci tentang menjadi murni. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Menjadi murni secara moral tidak akan terjadi tanpa tekad kuat dan disiplin. Selalu begitu, tetapi apalagi di masa kini dengan kebangkitan teknologi dan ketersediaan kejahatan dalam genggaman kita.

Dosa seksual bukanlah hal asing bagi gereja. Bahkan, mereka tidak asing bagi siapa pun dari suku mana pun. Kita tidak bisa santai dan menurunkan kewaspadaan serta menganggap anak-anak kita aman dari kebejatan masyarakat dan kemanusiaan kita. Kita harus memberi teladan dan mengajar anak-anak serta kaum muda jika berharap mereka tetap bersih dalam masyarakat yang rusak ini. Kita tidak bisa berasumsi bahwa jika seseorang berpakaian dengan cara tertentu, semuanya baik-baik saja di dalam. Cerita tidak sepenuhnya diceritakan dari luar. Orang Farisi membuat bagian luar tampak baik, sementara bagian dalam penuh korupsi. Yesus berkata, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). Kita juga seharusnya memberi perhatian utama pada masalah hati. Ketika hati bersih, maka bagian luar juga dapat dibersihkan.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Kegelapan internal akan selalu merusak persekutuan dan membunuh hubungan—setiap waktu.

Ini dimaksudkan sebagai pesan pengharapan, bukan membuat putus asa. Jika Anda memiliki noda gelap yang tersembunyi, akuilah dan singkirkanlah. Anda bisa bebas! Mungkin untuk terbebas dari cengkeraman Iblis dan hidup terbuka, transparan dengan sukacita di dalam jiwa. Anda tidak perlu menjalani hidup mencoba menyembunyikan kegelapan kejahatan. Yesus ingin mengampuni dan menyembuhkan.

Iblis itu kejam. Dalam John 10:10, Yesus berkata, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. Tujuan-Nya adalah memecah belah rumah tanggamu, menghancurkan rasa hormatmu, dan mengirimmu ke neraka. Sementara itu, ia memikatmu melalui nafsu dagingmu, dengan pedangnya terhunus untuk mengikat dan membunuhmu.

Dosa moral begitu memalukan dan sulit diakui. Yang wajar adalah mencoba menyembunyikan ketika kita berbuat salah. Anak-anak yang belajar menyembunyikan kesalahan sejak dini secara alami berkembang menjadi remaja yang menyembunyikan hal dari orang tua, guru, dan pelayan rohani. Orang semacam ini perlu belajar terbuka dan transparan, atau waktunya akan tiba ketika mereka menyembunyikan hal dari pasangan mereka. Menyembunyikan mengakibatkan hidup ganda dan mengarah pada lebih banyak perbudakan dan hubungan yang rusak. Orang-orang yang memiliki pintu tertutup di beberapa sudut hidupnya akan posesif terhadap ponsel mereka dan enggan berbagi kata sandi kepada pasangan yang dipercaya. Tampaknya kita mudah lupa betapa sia-sianya menyembunyikan dari Tuhan. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” Bagaimana bisa kita sebodoh itu berpikir bisa menyembunyikan apa pun dari Tuhan? Atau melangkah lebih jauh: Mengapa kita ingin menyembunyikan sesuatu dari-Nya? Numbers 32:23 masih sangat benar, mengatakan, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” Tuhan mengasihimu terlalu dalam untuk membiarkanmu terus menyembunyikan apa yang perlu dibawa keluar dan diampuni.

Dosa seksual juga sangat menipu. Biasanya terjadi seperti yang digambarkan Yakobus di pasal satu. Kita terperdaya, terseret, ditarik seperti magnet ke luar pusat, merasakan gelombang hasrat, memastikan tidak ada yang melihat, menutup jejak, melangkah lebih dekat ke yang terlarang, merasakan lebih banyak hasrat, dan sangat cepat mulai kehilangan nalar dan pemikiran sehat, tidak mampu menghitung konsekuensi seperti orang mabuk, lalu Yakobus 1:15 terjadi: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

Yakobus akan mengatakan jangan mengingini apa yang bukan hak kita, bahkan bukan secuil pun. Alkitab menyuruh kita untuk melarikan diri dari tiga hal. Salah satunya adalah perzinahan, yang dapat diperluas ke semua dosa seksual. Jangan bermain-main dengannya; jangan menoleh dua kali; menjauhlah darinya! Gantikan pikiran-pikiran itu dengan pikiran yang membangun tentang Tuhan dan jalan-Nya. Nyanyikan himne lama; syukur hidup ini tidak bisa memikirkan dua hal sekaligus. Apapun caranya, jauhi hasrat cabul itu. Itu akan membawamu lebih jauh daripada yang kamu inginkan dan menelan biaya lebih mahal daripada yang mau kamu bayar. Putar pita sampai akhir dan tanyakan pada dirimu, jika aku mengikuti apa yang menggoda ini, akankah aku mendapatkan apa yang kumau? Setan selalu menjanjikan kenikmatan, tetapi lalu menyerahkan penderitaan. Ingat, Setan tidak pernah menciptakan kenikmatan; ia hanya mengambil apa yang Tuhan ciptakan murni dan baik, memperjalin keburukan padanya, dan menawarkan kembali dalam bentuk yang tercemar. Ingat, pedang Setan terhunus untuk membunuh pada titik ini. Jauhi keinginan jahat!

Jangan mengikuti nafsumu. Pornografi sangat adiktif dan telah menjebak banyak orang. Promise Keepers mengatakan 65% pria dalam survei mereka kecanduan. Kecanduan pornografi seperti alkohol atau obat bius. Mereka mengatakan bahwa otak meminta endorfin untuk dituangkan ke dalamnya, entah dari kecanduan alkohol, narkoba, atau pornografi. Saya tegaskan lagi bahwa pria dan wanita yang mencapai kemenangan akan menjadi mereka yang, seperti Daniel pada zaman dahulu, berniat di hati, untuk tidak mencemarkan diri mereka.

Topik ini juga ditujukan bagi saudari-saudari kita, dan beberapa pertanyaan tampak layak diajukan. Apa yang rapi tersimpan dan tersembunyi di dalam hidupmu? Apakah kekecewaan hidup menyebabkan kekosongan yang membuat mengambil 'Tylenol emosional' membuatmu merasa lebih baik untuk sementara? Apakah hubungan emosionalmu aman di tempat yang telah Allah rencanakan?

Gadis-gadis muda harus diajarkan mengembangkan sikap sedikit peminggiran yang sehat terhadap pria. Bukan dengan sikap angkuh dan tak pernah tersenyum, tetapi juga tidak terlalu bebas berhubungan dengan pemuda. Masyarakat kita diarahkan persis sebaliknya, dan sejak taman kanak-kanak, anak laki-laki dan perempuan digoda tentang persahabatan khusus. Akibatnya, anak-anak tumbuh dengan sedikit atau tanpa rasa menjaga jarak. Berkomunikasi lewat pesan antar gender sebaiknya dihindari di luar hubungan keluarga. Ini akan mengembangkan kebiasaan pada kaum muda yang suatu hari perlu diubah jika mereka berharap hidup terbuka dan transparan dengan pasangan. Pikirkan seperti ini: apakah Anda ingin pasangan Anda bersosialisasi dengan lawan jenis di media sosial?

Saudari-saudari, berhati-hatilah dengan buku yang Anda baca. Novel romantis mematikan nafsu terhadap Firman Allah dan memberi ekspektasi yang tidak realistis tentang kehidupan berumah tangga. Buku-buku ini memberi gagasan bahwa pria yang tepat di suatu tempat akan menjadi kunci pemenuhan dan kebahagiaan hidupmu. Hanya Yesus yang dapat mengisi lubang yang dibawa dosa kepada setiap manusia hari ini. Tak ada pria atau wanita yang pernah mampu memberi keamanan dan ketenangan jiwa yang sangat kita rindukan. Luka di hati ini tak akan pernah dipadamkan oleh plester atau pereda rasa sakit. Mereka hanya membantu untuk sesaat, dan ketika efeknya habis, jeritan hati menjadi lebih keras. Buku-buku yang tidak sehat mematikan selera terhadap perkara-perkara Allah, dan justru menciptakan hasrat terhadap makanan sampah dan pereda luka.

Kekhawatiran lain bagi saudari adalah jumlah waktu yang Anda habiskan daring. Tak ada habisnya memberi makan nafsu akan kemewahan, keunikan, pesona, dan kecantikan. Jangan biarkan hal-hal ini menjadi penggerak hidup Anda karena mereka tak akan pernah berteriak 'cukup' dan takkan memuaskan jiwa atau memberi teladan yang benar bagi anak-anak Anda. Pertimbangkan jumlah waktu yang Anda habiskan mengadakan pesta. Selama bertahun-tahun, saya telah melihat nama-nama peluang bisnis dan produk yang harus dimiliki datang dan pergi. Tetapi sayang, dalam beberapa tahun, kita bahkan tidak bisa mengingat nama-nama itu dan sementara itu anak-anak tumbuh dan kini menjadi dewasa. Pertimbangkan kebutuhan nyata dalam hidupmu dan tanggung jawabmu, lalu putuskan mana yang akan memberi investasi kekal. Wanita yang memiliki anak perlu membatasi hobi yang sangat mereka nikmati karena, saat ini, mereka diberkati dengan anak-anak yang memiliki jiwa yang tidak pernah mati dan waktu bersama mereka adalah investasi kekal. Ingatlah bahwa suami dan anak-anakmu jauh lebih layak mendapat waktumu dibanding menghabiskan jam di pesta lain.

Bagaimana kita dapat hidup secara moral murni?

Rendah hati. Yakobus 5 berkata, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” Dibutuhkan kerendahan hati dan keterhancuran untuk mengakui kebutuhan kita, tetapi keterhancuran adalah kunci kemenangan. 1 Peter 5:5 memberi tahu kita bahwa Allah memberikan kasih karunia kepada orang yang rendah hati. Salah satu definisi paling komprehensif tentang kasih karunia adalah pertolongan ilahi yang tidak layak diberikan kepada manusia untuk regenerasi dan pengudusan. Regenerasi adalah 'kasih karunia penebusan,' dan pengudusan adalah 'kasih karunia transformasi.' Kebenarannya adalah bahwa Allah memberikan 'kasih karunia transformasi' kepada orang yang rendah hati. Kasih karunia ini mengubah kita dari dalam ke luar menjadikan kita kudus. Aspek kasih karunia ini harus diinginkan dan dicari sama seperti kasih karunia penebusan ketika Allah menyelamatkan kita. Ini mungkin langkah paling penting dalam mengatasi kecanduan apa pun. Cukuplah rendah hati untuk menjadikannya doa harian kepada Allah untuk kasih karunia transformasi-Nya. Yesus mengajar dalam Matthew 23:26, di mana Dia berkata, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Jujur. Periksa pikiran, tindakan, godaan, hal-hal yang Anda perjuangkan, amarah, nafsu, kesombongan, kepahitan, dll. Apakah Anda se-spiritual yang Anda tampilkan di luar? Kupas lapisan tipis itu dan akui kebutuhan akan bantuan.

Transparan. Romans 2:16 berbicara tentang hari ketika Allah akan menghakimi rahasia manusia. Kita sangat bodoh jika berpikir bisa menyembunyikan kejahatan. Kita bisa menyembunyikan untuk sementara, tetapi suatu hari tindakan kita akan berdiri telanjang di hadapan Allah yang maha tahu. Mengapa kita mencoba menyembunyikan sesuatu sekarang? Hal-hal tersembunyi itu bisa dikirim dulu ke penghakiman, dan hidup tanpa rasa bersalah bisa menjadi kenyataan hari ini. Jadilah transparan; itu harus menjadi tujuan yang dikerjakan.

Katakanlah kebenaran kepada dirimu sendiri. Ketika Anda dicobai, pertimbangkan akhir dari keinginanmu yang penuh nafsu itu. Akankah kamu mendapatkan apa yang kamu inginkan? Apakah hasrat ini akan puas, atau hanya akan membuatnya semakin lapar? Jika Anda melihat saudaramu melakukan apa yang sedang Anda kejar, bagaimana kelihatannya? Bagaimana kelihatannya tiga puluh tahun ke depan jika Anda mengikuti keinginan jahatmu? Akankah membawa sukacita atau ratap? Akankah itu membantu seseorang, atau membuat orang lain takut? Katakanlah kebenaran pada dirimu sebelum kamu mabuk dan tak mampu membuat penilaian yang rasional.

Latihlah mata untuk memantul. Anda tidak bisa mengendalikan apa yang Anda lihat pertama kali, tetapi Anda bisa mengontrol apa yang Anda lihat kedua kali. Jadikan kebiasaan sampai menjadi rutinitas untuk mengalihkan pandangan setiap kali melihat pemandangan yang menimbulkan pikiran tak suci.

Mengajar anak-anak kita. Ini harus menjadi beban besar dalam hati kita sejak masa kanak-kanak. Jika kita tidak mengajarkan anak-anak bahwa Allah menciptakan kita menurut gambar-Nya, yang harus dijaga kesuciannya, orang lain akan mengajarkan mereka untuk bersikap rahasia dan membuat mereka merasa najis. Tetaplah dekat dengan anak-anakmu dan ajari mereka seiring mereka bertumbuh.

Jaga emosi Anda. Ini adalah keselamatan dalam masyarakat kita yang rusak. Semakin jauh Anda dari ini, semakin rentan Anda terhadap korupsi. Jaga suami/istri Anda menjadi yang utama dalam hidup, orang yang Anda bagi dan yang terikat secara emosional dengan Anda.

Jauhi nafsu dan perzinahan. Lari darinya! Nafsu-nafsu ini adalah kecanduan yang harus diputus. Ingat, apa yang Anda beri makan akan tumbuh, dan apa yang Anda biarkan kelaparan akan mati. Kecanduan ini dapat diputus, tetapi Anda perlu memberi makan hubungan yang telah Allah berikan dan membuat kelaparan hubungan yang merusak.

Tuhan menciptakan kita sedemikian rupa sehingga ketika kita mengasihi perkara yang Ia kasihi, hati kita tetap memiliki ruang untuk mengasihi lebih banyak. Tidak peduli berapa banyak anak, cucu, atau teman saleh yang kita miliki, hati kita masih punya ruang untuk mengasihi lebih banyak. Tetapi pada saat kita mulai mengasihi apa yang dilarang Tuhan, itu mulai menggantikan dan menghancurkan semua kasih yang lain, memenuhi hati kita dengan kekosongan, rasa sakit, dan kesepian, yang mengarah ke akhir yang pahit.

Banyak pria tersadar dan melihat kebodohan jalan yang telah mereka pilih. Beberapa mencoba menyembunyikan perilaku tak suci dan berhasil sampai akhir hayat. Lainnya menyimpannya tersembunyi sampai setelah mereka tiada. Pertanyaan untuk direnungkan, apakah itu sepadan? Tentu jawabannya adalah TIDAK yang tegas!

Sungguh indah hidup terbuka bebas dari rasa bersalah dan memiliki damai dengan Tuhan serta kepastian dosa-diampuni, sehingga suatu hari kita akan diambil dari dunia jahat ini dan diantarkan ke hadirat Allah yang Kudus.

Dua kekuatan terletak dalam dadaku,
Satu yang kucintai, satu yang kusekali.
Tetapi yang kuberi makan akan menguasai.

—Ayah penulis

Semakin jujur aku menamai
apa yang benar tentang diriku,
Semakin sedikit aku perlu menyembunyikan dan membela diri,
dan bergaya serta pura-pura.

—Dan Allender

Part 1

For Alice, life is exasperating. Each day feels like an endless grind. She loves her family, but in her heart, she questions if what she is working so hard to accomplish makes any difference at all. She didn’t always feel bogged down, and she wondered what changed to make her feel overwhelmed so much of the time.

Sometimes busyness increases so gradually that we barely recognize the change. Busyness, given the chance, will overload us with more obligations than we can realistically get done in one day, or one week, or even one lifetime. Then, without warning, we reach the overload point when we feel as though we cannot possibly handle any more. Relentless overload can cause physical and mental exhaustion to the point where we feel deprived of enthusiasm, energy, and purpose. Some women seem to have a built-in indicator of where the overload line is. Others, like myself, struggle to find that balance. Constantly. There are so many good, interesting, and exciting options right at our fingertips; without much thought, we fill our days.

Concepts that contribute to overload

Playing multiple roles can be stressful. Overloading yourself with responsibilities and commitments can make you forget what is most important. It is easy to equate busyness with self-worth. By default, we start believing that:

  • Homemakers are capable of handling everything.
  • Homemakers, especially godly homemakers, are never frustrated.
  • A homemaker should anticipate all her family’s needs.

If we are honest, we know that these statements are unrealistic. Homemakers cannot do everything. All homemakers experience frustration occasionally. A mother cannot consistently be one step ahead of her family’s needs.

Rethinking the busy life

Household duties and caring for our families fill our days. Sometimes those tasks alone make us extremely busy. But what about the extra-circular activities or the high standard we hold ourselves to? We may need to think differently so we can break free from habits that threaten to control us.

Accept your limits

Maybe you can go to a Tupperware party, attend a Bible study, and repaint the bathroom all in one week. But should you? Good homemakers allow themselves to simplify even if they prefer doing it another way. That means if you are an avid bread maker, it’s all right to toss a few loaves of bread into your shopping cart.

Evaluate what causes frustrations

Artificial smiles can hide inner frustrations, but it doesn’t cure them. It works best to admit that there is a problem and then seek a solution. I’ve had to learn this repeatedly. All my family members know that we eat dinner at 5:30. But a late arrival habit is trending, and it bothers me.

When I told my husband about the frustration, he simply said, “Why don’t you explain the issue and quit being so uptight about it?” Good point. Proactively seeking solutions works for many problem areas.

Imperfect women make good homemakers

Quit worrying about perfection and make decisions based on what is best for today. Fun-loving, happy, homemakers might have a few dust bunnies under the furniture, but they radiate an aura that draws people to their hearts and homes.

Everyone differs when it comes to how much we can handle. On the other hand, everyone is the same; we all have limits. In future installments, we will discuss how to deal with common points of overload.

Part 2

Many homemakers find themselves stretched thin among commitments that go with home, family, and other activities. As busy as we are, why do we continue to fill our schedules fuller?

It is easy for me to commit to a new project and then realize, halfway into the task, that I have overstepped my limits. Too often, I overestimate the amount of time I must have to complete a project and underestimate the amount of time a task will take.

Commitment overload happens by default. When we play multiple roles and add more responsibilities, we can easily become slaves to the promises we have made. Overload tends to drain our energy, dull our senses, and deaden our joy.

Recognizing Overload

Sometimes multiple activities take place in rapid sequence. Normally, we can flow with short-term spurts of busyness. But if the flow of activities is never-ending and we keep adding more obligations, we develop a pattern that becomes a way of life.

Too many commitments beyond normal duties make us candidates for depression and burnout. Personally, when I experience insomnia, apathy, or irritability, it is time to examine my schedule. If adjustments aren’t made, someone or something will suffer.

No one can overextend themselves indefinitely. Sometimes we suffer consequences for keeping a pace that is beyond our resources. Symptoms of overload can include lack of sleep, strained relationships, procrastination, fear of failure, and a susceptible immune system.

Breaking Free of Overload

Identifying overload takes an honest evaluation of yourself. How can you know if this is just a busy season or if busyness is the new normal? Are you declining a request because life is too full, or is it an excuse? Do you have to say “yes” on the spot? With practice, you can learn how to pull back before reaching the overload point.

Let an idea or request gel before committing

This has saved me a great deal of stress. There are so many good things to be involved in, and new inspirations come daily. Sometimes tasks can be incorporated into my/our schedule. Other times I must simply let them go and stay focused on what is most important. Consider waiting a few hours before incorporating new ideas and requests.

Seek advice, especially your husband’s

A renowned doughnut maker was asked to have a stand at an auction. She asked her husband what he thought about it. He said, “As long as you don’t complain and stress about it like you did last year, I don’t care.” Was her husband saying “yes” or “no”? This lady should take the cue that doughnut making was somehow adding stress. Either she should not do it, or together they must seek a workable solution.

Evaluate your schedule regularly

Keep a detailed calendar to have a picture of past, present, and future events. If your family had the flu last week and you plan to take an out-of-state trip next week, should you add more? What is the emotional health of your family? Is your husband stressed at work? Sometimes it is better to have a time slot of nothing so it can be filled with what is important now. You can’t do a good job at anything if you are spread too thin. Too many obligations make it hard to be personally refreshed and congenial. Choosing commitments wisely will help you invest your energy where it is most valuable for today.

Sehemu ya 1

Kwa Alice, maisha ni ya kukata tamaa. Kila siku inahisi kama kazi isiyokwisha. Anawapenda familia yake, lakini moyoni, anajiuliza kama yale anayoyafanyia kazi kwa bidii yanafaida yoyote kabisa. Hapakuwa kila wakati akihisi msongamano, na alishangaa ni nini kilibadilika kumfanya ahisi kuzidiwa mara nyingi hivi.

Wakati mwingine shughuli nyingi huongezeka taratibu kiasi kwamba tunapata shida kutambua mabadiliko. Shughuli nyingi, ikipewa nafasi, zitatukaribisha kwa wajibu zaidi kuliko yale tunayoweza kutimiza kwa kweli katika siku moja, au wiki moja, au hata maisha yote. Kisha, bila onyo, tunafika kwenye kiwango cha kuzidiwa ambacho tunahisi kama hatuwezi kubeba zaidi. Kuzidiwa kwa mara kwa mara kunaweza kusababisha uchovu wa kimwili na wa akili hadi tukahisi kukosa shauku, nguvu, na kusudi. Wanawake wengine wanaonekana kuwa na kiashiria kilichojengewa ndani kinachoonyesha wapi mstari wa kuzidiwa upo. Wengine, kama mimi, tunapata shida kupata uwiano huo. Mara kwa mara. Kuna fursa nyingi nzuri, za kuvutia, na za kusisimua zilizo karibu nasi; bila fikra nyingi, tunajaza siku zetu.

Dhana zinazochangia kuzidiwa

Kucheza nyenzo nyingi za majukumu kunaweza kuwa na msongo. Kujaza nafsi yako kwa majukumu na ahadi nyingi kunaweza kukufanya usisahau kile kilicho muhimu zaidi. Ni rahisi kuoanisha shughuli nyingi na thamani yako binafsi. Kwa kawaida, tunaanza kuamini kwamba:

  • Wenye kuendesha nyumba wana uwezo wa kushughulikia kila kitu.
  • Wenye kuendesha nyumba, hasa wenye kuendesha nyumba wema, hawawahi kukasirika.
  • Mwenye kuendesha nyumba anapaswa kutarajia mahitaji yote ya familia yake.

Ikiwa tutaweza kuwa waaminifu, tunajua kwamba taarifa hizi si za ukweli. Wenye kuendesha nyumba hawawezi kufanya kila kitu. Wenye kuendesha nyumba wote hupata kukasirika mara kwa mara. Mama aweza kushindwa kuwa hatua moja mbele ya mahitaji ya familia yake kila wakati.

Kufikiria upya maisha ya shughuli nyingi

Majukumu ya nyumbani na kutunza familia zetu hujaza siku zetu. Wakati mwingine yale majukumu peke yake hufanya tuwawe wenye shughuli nyingi sana. Lakini vipi kuhusu shughuli za ziada au kiwango cha juu tunachojiwekea wenyewe? Huenda tutalazimika kufikiria tofauti ili tuweze kujikomboa kutoka kwa tabia zinazoishia kutudhibiti.

Kubali mipaka yako

Pengine unaweza kwenda sherehe ya Tupperware, kuhudhuria masomo ya Biblia, na kupaka tena choo wiki moja yote. Lakini je, unapaswa? Wenye kuendesha nyumba wazuri wanajiruhusu kuifanya mambo kuwa rahisi hata kama wangependa kuyafanya kwa njia nyingine. Hii ina maana kwamba ikiwa wewe ni mpishi mkali wa mkate, sawa tu kutupa mikate michache kwenye gari lako la kununulia.

Tathmini kinachosababisha kukasirika

Tabasamu za uwongo zinaweza kuficha hasira za ndani, lakini hayo hayayotibu. Ni bora kukubali kwamba kuna tatizo kisha kutafuta suluhisho. Nimejifunza hili mara kwa mara. Wote wanachama wa familia yangu wanajua kwamba tunakula chakula cha jioni saa 5:30. Lakini tabia ya kuchelewa inazidi kuenea, na inanichosha.

Nilipoambia mume wangu kuhusu kukasirika kwangu, alisema tu, “Kwa nini usieleze tatizo na kuacha kuwa mkali kuhusu hilo?” Hoja nzuri. Kutafuta suluhisho kwa wepesi hufanya kazi kwa maeneo mengi ya shida.

Wanawake wasiokamilika hufanya wenye kuendesha nyumba wazuri

Acha kuwa na wasiwasi kuhusu ukamilifu na fanya maamuzi kwa msingi wa kile kilicho bora kwa leo. Wenye kuendesha nyumba wenye upendo wa furaha wanaweza kuwa na vumbi chini ya samani, lakini wanatoa mng’ao unaowavutia watu kwa mioyo na nyumba zao.

Kila mtu ni tofauti linapokuja suala la kiwango tunachoweza kushughulikia. Kwa upande mwingine, kila mtu ni sawa; sote tuna mipaka. Katika sehemu zijazo, tutajadili jinsi ya kushughulikia vidokezo vya kawaida vya kuzidiwa.

Sehemu ya 2

Wengi wa wenye kuendesha nyumba wanajikuta wakiwa wamesambazwa kwa ahadi zinazohusiana na nyumbani, familia, na shughuli nyingine. Japokuwa tunashughulika sana, kwa nini tunaendelea kujaza ratiba zetu zaidi?

Ninaona ni rahisi kujisajili kwa mradi mpya kisha kutambua, nusu ya njia ya kufanya kazi, kwamba nimezidi mipaka yangu. Mara nyingi sana, napunguzia kiasi cha muda ninachodhani nitahitaji kumaliza mradi na kupunguza kiasi cha muda kazi itachukua.

Kuzidiwa kwa ahadi hutokea kwa kawaida. Tunapoingia katika nyenzo nyingi za majukumu na kuongeza wajibu zaidi, tunaweza kwa urahisi kuwa watumwa wa ahadi tulizotoa. Kuzidiwa kwa kawaida kunatoa nguvu zetu, kunatulia hisia zetu, na kuua furaha yetu.

Kutambua Kuzidiwa

Wakati mwingine shughuli nyingi zinafanyika kwa mfululizo kwa haraka. Kwa kawaida, tunaweza kuendana na vipindi vya muda mfupi vya shughuli nyingi. Lakini ikiwa mfululizo wa shughuli hauishi na tunaendelea kuongeza wajibu zaidi, tunaunda mtindo unaokuwa njia ya maisha.

Ahadi nyingi zaidi za kawaida hufanya sisi kuwa wagombea wa unyogovu na uchovu wa kazi. Kwa upande wangu, ninapopata usingizi mdogo, kutokujali, au kukasirika, ni wakati wa kuchunguza ratiba yangu. Ikiwa marekebisho hayafanyiki, mtu au kitu kitateseka.

Hakuna mtu anayeweka mipaka ya kujizidi kwa muda usio na kikomo. Wakati mwingine tunapata matokeo kwa kuweka mwendo unaozidi rasilimali zetu. Dalili za kuzidiwa zinaweza kujumuisha ukosefu wa usingizi, mahusiano yaliyoshonwa, kuchelewesha kazi, hofu ya kushindwa, na mfumo wa kinga unaokabiliwa na matatizo.

Kujikomboa kutoka kwa Kuzidiwa

Kutambua kuzidiwa kunahitaji tathmini ya uaminifu ya nafsi yako. Unawezaje kujua ikiwa hii ni msimu wa shughuli nyingi tu au ikiwa shughuli nyingi zimekuwa kawaida mpya? Je, unakata ombi kwa sababu maisha yako yamejaa sana, au ni sababu tu? Je, lazima useme “ndiyo” papo hapo? Kwa mazoezi, unaweza kujifunza jinsi ya kujitoa nyuma kabla haujafikia kiwango cha kuzidiwa.

Ruhusu wazo au ombi lipitie muda kabla ya kujitoa

Hili limekunisamehe msongo mwingi. Kuna mambo mengi mazuri ya kushiriki, na msukumo mpya huja kila siku. Wakati mwingine kazi zinaweza kuingizwa kwenye ratiba yangu/yetu. Wengine wakati lazima niwape tu na kubaki na kuzingatia kile kilicho muhimu zaidi. Fikiria kusubiri masaa machache kabla ya kuingiza mawazo na maombi mapya.

Tafuta ushauri, hasa wa mumeo

Muumba maarufu wa donati aliombwa kuwa na banda kwenye mnada. Aliuliza mumewe alichofikiria. Alisema, “Iwapo hutalalamika na kujiweka mkandamizika juu yake kama ulivyoifanya mwaka jana, sitajiangusha.” Je, mumewe alikuwa anasema “ndiyo” au “hapana”? Bi huyu anapaswa kuchukua dalili kwamba kuumba donati kwa namna fulani kunaleta msongo. Ama asifanye, au pamoja wawatafute suluhisho linalofaa.

Tambua ratiba yako mara kwa mara

Hifadhi kalenda ya kina ili kupata picha ya matukio ya zamani, sasa, na yajayo. Ikiwa familia yako ilikuwa na mafua wiki iliyopita na unapanga safari ya nje ya jimbo wiki ijayo, je, unapaswa kuongezea zaidi? Je, afya ya kihemko ya familia yako iko aje? Je, mumeo yuko na msongo kazini? Wakati mwingine ni bora kuwa na kipindi bila kitu ili kiweze kujazwa na kile kinachokuwa muhimu sasa. Huwezi kufanya kazi vizuri kwa kitu chochote ikiwa umesambazwa sana. Ahadi nyingi zinafanya iwe vigumu kupumzika binafsi na kuwa mwema kwa wengine. Kuchagua ahadi kwa busara kutakusaidia kuwekeza nguvu zako mahali zilizo na thamani zaidi kwa leo.

“Adrianna, what’s the temperature outside?” asked Asher. He and Adrianna were sitting at the table doing school with their siblings Emily and Kianna.

“Probably about 50.” Adrianna glanced lazily at the thermometer. “Hey, it’s 65 degrees! Mom, may we eat lunch outside?”

Mom looked up from the sink. “If you do a good job with your school until then, you may,” she told them. “And if you get your school done before lunch, you may play outside for a while this afternoon.”

Asher let out a whoop and started writing fast. The girls grinned at each other and picked up their pencils.

Everyone worked diligently until lunchtime. Then Adrianna made sandwiches while Asher put cookies in bags, Emily collected bags of chips, and Kianna ran down to the basement to grab a few apples. They each packed their lunch in a shopping bag and went out to their picnic spot, a big, flat rock in a clearing in the woods.

They ate quickly, then Adrianna suggested, “Let’s go kayak on the pond!”

“I guess we could,” said Asher slowly. “But didn’t Mom say that Emily and Kianna are too small to handle the kayaks?”

“Oh, yes, I guess she did. Well, they can play on the swings or something,” she shrugged

“I think we should play something everyone can help with,” said Asher. He turned to Emily and Kianna. “What do you want to do?”

“Let’s make a playhouse!” suggested Kianna.

“Yes, let’s!” Emily agreed. “You could hunt for us,” she told Asher.

“And Adrianna could be the mom!” said Kianna.

Adrianna stood with a scowl on her face. Playhouse indeed! She was way too old for that! “I’m going kayaking,” she announced. “You can just have your playhouse.” She picked up her shopping bag and put her sandwich and cookie bags into it. She threw her apple core to the dogs and started for the house.

“Adrianna, can you please take ours too?” begged Emily. “You're going to the house anyway.”

“You can take care of your own stuff,” Adrianna called back, crossly. She dropped her shopping bag on the counter, hoping to slip out of the house before Mom saw her.

She heard her mom’s voice. “Wait, Adrianna, what’s wrong? Your face looks like a thunderstorm!”

Adrianna sighed. She hadn’t been fast enough. “I wanted to go kayaking, but Asher doesn’t want to,” she grumbled.

“Well,” said Mom slowly, “I think Asher is remembering that the other girls can't handle kayaks yet. What are they doing?”

“They’re building a playhouse. I'm way too old for that!” Adrianna burst out.

Mom smiled, “What makes you think that?”

“I'm sure none of the girls my age do stuff like that with their little siblings.”

“Are you sure you're not being selfish?” Mom asked. “Sometimes, we need to give up what we want so that others can be happy.”

Adrianna shrugged and went out to the shed to get a kayak. She lifted her blue kayak off the rack and hauled it down to the pond. She snapped the paddle together, hopped into the seat, and pushed the kayak onto the smooth surface of the water. She sighed with pleasure. This was way better than building a playhouse in the woods! She took a few loops around the pond before her paddle began to slow. Somehow it wasn’t as fun this time. She heard Asher and the girls laughing and shouting as they played. Maybe Mom was right, she thought. Maybe I would be happier if I gave up what I want so that we can all play together. Slowly she paddled to the edge of the pond. She stepped out of the kayak, pulled it out of the water, and flipped it over to dry. Resolutely, she walked out of the pasture to find Asher and the girls.

“Hey! Here comes Adrianna!” called Emily happily as Adrianna walked up.

Adrianna grinned, “It looks like you have your house about set up,” she said encouragingly. “What do you need to finish it?”

“We still need a stove, and something for a countertop,” said Kianna.

“I can help you find something,” Adrianna told them. Together they hunted in the woods and the shed for boards and logs to finish the house. When suppertime came and they went in for supper, Adrianna was very happy. Mom was right, she thought. It is more fun to give up my way and do what everyone else wants to.

«Αντριάνα, τι θερμοκρασία έχει έξω;» ρώτησε ο Άσερ. Εκείνος και η Αντριάνα κάθονταν στο τραπέζι και διάβαζαν μαζί με τις αδελφές τους Έμιλι και Κιάνα.

«Πιθανότατα γύρω στους 10.» Η Αντριάνα κοίταξε νωχελικά το θερμόμετρο. «Ωω, είναι 18 βαθμοί! Μαμά, μπορούμε να φάμε έξω;»

Η μαμά σήκωσε το βλέμμα από το νεροχύτη. «Αν τελειώσετε το μάθημά σας καλά μέχρι τότε, μπορείτε», τους είπε. «Και αν τελειώσετε πριν το μεσημέρι, μπορείτε να παίξετε έξω για λίγο το απόγευμα.»

Ο Άσερ φώναξε από χαρά και άρχισε να γράφει γρήγορα. Τα κορίτσια χαμογέλασαν η μία στην άλλη και πήραν τα μολύβια τους.

Όλοι δούλεψαν επιμελώς μέχρι το μεσημεριανό. Τότε η Αντριάνα έφτιαξε σάντουιτς ενώ ο Άσερ έβαζε μπισκότα σε σακουλάκια, η Έμιλι μάζευε σακουλάκια με πατατάκια και η Κιάνα έτρεξε στο υπόγειο να πάρει μερικά μήλα. Ο καθένας πακετάρισε το φαγητό του σε μια σακούλα αγορών και πήγαν στο σημείο του πικνίκ, μια μεγάλη, επίπεδη πέτρα σε ένα ξέφωτο στο δάσος.

Έφαγαν γρήγορα, και τότε η Αντριάνα πρότεινε: «Ας κάνουμε κανό στη λίμνη!»

«Υποθέτω ότι μπορούμε», είπε ο Άσερ αργά. «Αλλά δεν είπε η μαμά ότι η Έμιλι και η Κιάνα είναι πολύ μικρές για να χειριστούν τα κανό;»

«Ω, ναι, νομίζω ότι το είπε. Λοιπόν, μπορούν να παίξουν στις κούνιες ή κάτι τέτοιο», είπε αδιάφορα.

«Νομίζω ότι πρέπει να κάνουμε κάτι που να μπορούν να βοηθήσουν όλοι», είπε ο Άσερ. Γύρισε στην Έμιλι και την Κιάνα. «Τι θέλετε να κάνετε;»

«Ας φτιάξουμε ένα σπιτάκι παιχνιδιού!» πρότεινε η Κιάνα.

«Ναι, ας το κάνουμε!» συμφώνησε η Έμιλι. «Εσύ μπορείς να ψάξεις για πράγματα για μας», είπε στον Άσερ.

«Και η Αντριάνα μπορεί να είναι η μαμά!» είπε η Κιάνα.

Η Αντριάνα στάθηκε με μούτρα. Σπιτάκι παιχνιδιού! Πραγματικά; Ήταν πολύ μεγάλη γι’ αυτό! «Πάω να κάνω κανό», ανακοίνωσε. «Μπορείτε να κρατήσετε το σπιτάκι σας.» Άρπαξε τη σακούλα της και έβαλε μέσα το σάντουιτς και τα μπισκότα. Έριξε το φλούδι του μήλου στους σκύλους και ξεκίνησε για το σπίτι.

«Αντριάνα, μπορείς σε παρακαλώ να πάρεις και τα δικά μας;» παρακάλεσε η Έμιλι. «Πάντως πας στο σπίτι.»

«Μπορείτε να φροντίσετε τα δικά σας», φώναξε η Αντριάνα, θυμωμένα. Έριξε τη σακούλα της πάνω στον πάγκο, ελπίζοντας να βγει απ’ το σπίτι πριν τη δει η μαμά.

Άκουσε τη φωνή της μαμάς. «Περίμενε, Αντριάνα, τι συμβαίνει; Το πρόσωπό σου μοιάζει με καταιγίδα!»

Η Αντριάνα αναστέναξε. Δεν είχε προλάβει αρκετά γρήγορα. «Ήθελα να κάνω κανό, αλλά ο Άσερ δεν θέλει», γκρίνιαξε.

«Λοιπόν», είπε η μαμά αργά, «νομίζω ότι ο Άσερ θυμάται πως τα άλλα κορίτσια δεν μπορούν να χειριστούν ακόμα τα κανό. Τι κάνουν;»

«Φτιάχνουν ένα σπιτάκι παιχνιδιού. Είμαι πολύ μεγάλη γι’ αυτό!» ξέσπασε η Αντριάνα.

Η μαμά χαμογέλασε, «Τι σε κάνει να το νομίζεις αυτό;»

«Είμαι σίγουρη ότι κανένα από τα κορίτσια της ηλικίας μου δεν κάνει τέτοια πράγματα με τα μικρά τους αδελφάκια.»

«Είσαι σίγουρη ότι δεν είσαι εγωίστρια;» ρώτησε η μαμά. «Μερικές φορές πρέπει να παραχωρούμε αυτό που θέλουμε για να είναι κι οι άλλοι χαρούμενοι.»

Η Αντριάνα σήκωσε τους ώμους και πήγε στο υπόστεγο να πάρει ένα κανό. Κατέβασε το μπλε κανό από τη σχάρα και το κουβάλησε μέχρι τη λίμνη. Σύνδεσε την κουπαστή, κάθισε στη θέση και πέταξε το κανό πάνω στην ήρεμη επιφάνεια του νερού. Αναστέναξε ευχάριστα. Αυτό ήταν πολύ καλύτερο από το να φτιάχνει ένα σπιτάκι στο δάσος! Έκανε μερικούς κύκλους στη λίμνη πριν το κουπί της αρχίσει να επιβραδύνει. Κάπως δεν ήταν τόσο διασκεδαστικό αυτή τη φορά. Άκουγε τον Άσερ και τα κορίτσια να γελούν και να φωνάζουν καθώς έπαιζαν. Ίσως η μαμά να είχε δίκιο, σκέφτηκε. Ίσως θα ήμουν πιο ευτυχισμένη αν παράχω αυτό που θέλω έτσι ώστε να παίξουμε όλοι μαζί. Αργά κουνούσε το κουπί προς την άκρη της λίμνης. Βγήκε από το κανό, το τράβηξε έξω από το νερό και το γύρισε ανάποδα για να στεγνώσει. Με αποφασιστικότητα, βγήκε από το λιβάδι για να βρει τον Άσερ και τα κορίτσια.

«Κοίτα! Έρχεται η Αντριάνα!» φώναξε η Έμιλι χαρούμενα καθώς η Αντριάνα πλησίαζε.

Η Αντριάνα χαμογέλασε, «Φαίνεται ότι σχεδόν έχετε το σπιτάκι έτοιμο», είπε ενθαρρυντικά. «Τι χρειάζεστε για να το τελειώσετε;»

«Μας χρειάζεται ακόμα μια κουζίνα και κάτι για πάγκο», είπε η Κιάνα.

«Μπορώ να σας βοηθήσω να βρείτε κάτι», τους είπε η Αντριάνα. Μαζί έψαξαν στο δάσος και στο υπόστεγο για σανίδες και κορμούς για να τελειώσουν το σπιτάκι. Όταν ήρθε η ώρα του δείπνου και μπήκαν μέσα για φαγητό, η Αντριάνα ήταν πολύ ευτυχισμένη. Η μαμά είχε δίκιο, σκέφτηκε. Είναι πιο διασκεδαστικό να παραχωρώ τον δικό μου τρόπο και να κάνω ό,τι θέλει όλη η ομάδα.
