Οι πνευματικοί μας πρόγονοι είχαν πολλά να πουν για τα πολλά ζητήματα που αντιμετώπιζε η αμερικανική μεννονιτική εκκλησία στην εποχή τους, και μπορούμε ακόμη να μάθουμε από τους συλλεγόμενους λόγους αυτών των εκκλησιαστικών ηγετών και αδελφών. Θα εξετάσουμε πρώτα την ερμηνευτική των πρώτων αμερικανών Μεννονιτών, προσπαθώντας να αντλήσουμε παραδείγματα από τα οποία εμείς, ως χριστιανοί του 21ου αιώνα, μπορούμε να διδαχθούμε.

Πρώτον, η σωστή ερμηνεία της Γραφής ήταν θέμα μεγάλης σημασίας γι’ αυτούς τους πρώιμους χριστιανούς. Είχαν μόλις μεταναστεύσει από μια κατά κύριο λόγο εχθρική περιοχή, όπου είχαν συνέχεια δοκιμαστεί μέχρι και τον θάνατο για θέματα πίστης και τώρα αντιμετώπιζαν ένα διαφορετικό σύνολο προκλήσεων όταν βρέθηκαν σε ειρήνη και θρησκευτική ελευθερία. Θα δούμε πώς διαπέρασαν αυτές τις προκλήσεις μελετώντας αρκετές από τις δοξασίες και τις πρακτικές τους.

Η Δόγμα της Μη Αντίστασης

Ένα ζήτημα που ερμηνεύτηκε και εφάρμοσαν καλά πολλοί από τους πρώιμους μεννονιτικούς συγγραφείς είναι ο κανόνας και η διδασκαλία του μη αντιστεκόμενου χριστιανού. Αν και πολλοί από τους αναβαπτιστικούς απογόνους τους σήμερα διατηρούν, σε διάφορους βαθμούς, αυτή τη διδασκαλία, συχνά δεν γίνεται με την καθαρότητα και τη σοβαρότητα των προγόνων τους. Οι πρώιμοι αμερικανοί Μεννονίτες κατάλαβαν τη μη αντίσταση ως θεμελιώδη πτυχή της χριστιανικής ζωής, όπως θα έπρεπε να είναι, και δίδαξαν εκτενώς για την πρακτική εφαρμογή και την εμφάνιση της μη αντίστασης στη ζωή του πιστού. Το κύριο κίνητρό τους για να ζουν ειρηνικά και χωρίς εχθρότητα προς τον πλησίον ήταν το δοσμένο παράδειγμα του Ιησού. Ο Χριστός τύπωσε την αποδεκτή απάντηση στη βία και την κακοβουλία: πραότητα, ταπεινότητα, όπως αρμόζει σε αυτόν που καλείται Αρνίον.

Η Έμφαση στα Βιβλικά Θεμέλια

Υπήρχε επίσης μια στερεή εστίαση μεταξύ των πρώτων μεννονιτικών συγγραφέων κατά της οικοδόμησης δόγματος επάνω στα γραπτά ανθρώπων. Αυτή η έμφαση διακρίνεται έντονα στα έργα τους, καθώς παραθέτουν εκτενώς τη Γραφή. Ενίσχυσαν το σημείο τους φέρνοντας ένα παράδειγμα από τον Χριστό ή με τη χρήση ενός εφαρμοστέου εδαφίου της Γραφής, αντί να κτίζουν πάνω στο αμμώδες έδαφος της γνώμης ενός ανθρώπου. Ένα από τα πεδία στα οποία το έκαναν αυτό ήταν το ζήτημα της σωτηρίας.

Σημασία της Πρακτικής Σωτηρίας

Μπορούμε να μάθουμε πολλά από τους πρώιμους Μεννονίτες σχετικά με την πρακτική εργασία της σωτηρίας. Πρώτον, η σωτηρία παριστάνεται ως μια εσωτερική και μια εξωτερική αλλαγή. Η εσωτερική επηρεάζεται πρώτα μέσα από το έργο του Αγίου Πνεύματος στη ζωή του βουλόμενου αμαρτωλού. Είναι σημαντική η διάκριση ότι ο αμαρτωλός είναι βουλόμενος. Αυτή η θέση αντιτάχθηκε στις περισσότερες από τις μεγαλύτερες εδραιωμένες εκκλησίες της εποχής. Εάν ένας αμαρτωλός πρέπει να είναι βουλόμενος, τότε αυτό υποδηλώνει ότι όλοι οι άνθρωποι μπορούν με θέληση να αποδεχθούν τη σωτηρία, μια ιδέα που είναι θεμελιώδης στη φύση, αν και δεν εκφράζεται πάντα με λόγια, για την εκκλησία του σήμερα.

Στην εποχή των πρώιμων Μεννονιτών, η δογματική της προοριστικότητας όπως διδάσκεται από τον καλβινισμό φαίνεται ότι έκανε αναγκαία αυτή την έμφαση στην ικανότητα του ανθρώπου να επιλέγει ελεύθερα, κάτι που εξακολουθεί να ισχύει και σήμερα. Υπάρχει επίσης μια άλλη παραλλαγή της ερμηνείας της «μη εκούσιας σωτηρίας», η οποία προέρχεται από τα μετέπειτα αποτελέσματα του χαρισματικού κινήματος και την επίδρασή του στους μεννονιτικούς και αμις κύκλους. Αυτή η «μη εκούσια σωτηρία» δεν είναι ζήτημα προορισμού, αλλά περιγράφεται ως σχεδόν εξαναγκαστικό κάλεσμα από το Πνεύμα. Έχει παρατηρηθεί σε αρκετές μαρτυρίες σωτηρίας, όπου οι μαρτυρούντες θυμούνταν πως ήταν εντελώς άνετοι στη ζωή τους της αμαρτίας και της ακολασίας όταν ξαφνικά έπεφταν σαν τον Σαούλ και δεν μπορούσαν να κάνουν αλλιώς παρά να ακολουθήσουν τον Θεό και να Του αφιερώσουν τη ζωή τους. Υπάρχουν πολυάριθμες παγίδες με αυτή τη δραματική κατανόηση της μεταστροφής, κυρίως ότι απαλλάσσει από την ευθύνη τον μεταστραφέντα για την απόφασή του να μεταστραφεί. Αυτό οδηγεί σε έλλειψη εξέτασης του κόστους του Χριστιανισμού, το οποίο είναι θάνατος του εαυτού, θάνατος της περηφάνειας και θάνατος της εύνοιας προς τον άνθρωπο. Εάν ο πιστός πέσει κεφαλά πρώτα στον Χριστιανισμό, χωρίς να λογαριάσει ότι πρέπει να εγκαταλείψει όλα αυτά τα αυτο-ευαρεστούμενα χαρακτηριστικά, πώς θα μπορέσει να ωριμάσει πνευματικά αν δεν μπορεί να αφήσει τις παλιές του συνήθειες; Ενώ αυτή η μορφή μεταστροφής μπορεί να είναι γνήσια στην αρχή, δεν προοδεύει συχνά πέρα από το γάλα του Λόγου στο κρέας στο οποίο πρέπει να μετέχει ο ώριμος χριστιανός. Αυτή η ωρίμανση του χριστιανού τονίζεται σε γραπτά που εκτείνονται από τον Menno Simons έως και τον Abraham Goshalk. Είναι επίσης σημαντικό για χάρη της εκκλησίας ο πιστός να είναι σταθερά δεσμευμένος και εμπλεκόμενος στη σταθερή ανάπτυξη της πίστης του.

Η Σοβαρότητα μιας Αγνής Εκκλησίας

Η ιδέα της εκκλησίας για τους πρώιμους αμερικανούς Μεννονίτες φαίνεται ότι ήταν πιο σοβαρή σκέψη, λιγότερο ατομικιστική από την τρέχουσα κατάστασή μας. Είναι η αξιοθρήνητη κατάσταση της ονομαστικής χριστιανοσύνης ότι η εκκλησία έχει γίνει μια κοινωνική οργάνωση με χώρο για κάθε αμαρτία και διαφθορά.

Είναι προς όφελός μας να εξετάσουμε κοντά τον χαρακτήρα της εκκλησίας που ίδρυσε ο Χριστός και να σημειώσουμε επίσης τον χαρακτήρα των αληθινών εκκλησιών, ανεμπόδιστων από αίρεση και χαλαρότητα. Αυτός ο χαρακτήρας είναι, όπως και ο Χριστός ο ίδιος, απλός και όμως απίστευτα γεμάτος νόημα και πνευματική ζωτικότητα.

Η πρώτη πτυχή της εκκλησίας που πρέπει να αναγνωρίσουμε είναι η αγνή της κατάσταση ως της νύμφης του Χριστού. Και εδώ, πρέπει να σκεφτούμε τον χαρακτήρα του Χριστού. Έδωσε ποτέ στον εαυτό Του χώρο για αμαρτία; Τον βρίσκουμε να απολαμβάνει περιστασιακά μια σύντομη απόλαυση μιας «ενοχικής ηδονής»; Ο αναγνώστης με κατανόηση θα συμφωνήσει ότι ο Χριστός ήταν αγνός σε ολότητά Του, και πώς αλλιώς πρέπει να είναι και η νύμφη με την οποία πρόκειται να ενωθεί οικεία και αιώνια; Για να βοηθήσουμε το νου μας να απαντήσει σε τέτοια ερώτηση, ας εξετάσουμε το γήινο σύμβολο αυτής της ουράνιας ένωσης: αυτό ενός άντρα και μιας γυναίκας ενωμένων για τη ζωή. Αυτή η επίγεια ένωση αναγνωρίζεται ακόμη και από μη χριστιανούς ως κάτι αφιερωμένο καθαρά για τα δύο άτομα που εμπλέκονται, μια σχέση και μια ανταλλαγή του ενός με τον άλλον που δεν είναι και ποτέ δεν πρέπει να μοιραστεί με κανέναν έξω από την οικεία ένωση. Αυτό ζωγραφίζει καθαρά για το γήινο μυαλό μας τη διάνοια του Χριστού, αφού ο γάμος είναι σύμβολο του Χριστού και της νύμφης Του. Η νύμφη και ο Χριστός είναι ο ένας για τον άλλον και δεν δίνουν τους εαυτούς τους σε τίποτα και σε κανέναν άλλον.

Τώρα που μπορούμε να δούμε την αγνότητα της εκκλησίας, ας εξετάσουμε την πρακτική της λειτουργία ανάμεσα σε πεσμένους ανθρώπους. Εάν πρόκειται να είναι αγνή, τότε πώς θα γίνουμε μέρος της; Εδώ εισέρχεται η ανάγκη για σαφή κατανόηση της αναγεννήσεως, μιας διδασκαλίας που κρατήθηκε σε υψηλό σεβασμό από αυτούς τους μεννονιτικούς προγόνους. Δίδασκαν ότι το Πνεύμα επιφέρει το πνευματικό πλύσιμο και τον καθαρισμό που θα γίνει ορατός σε μια μεταβλημένη κατάσταση σκέψης και πράξης στον πιστό. Αυτή η αλλαγή εξακολουθεί να βρίσκεται σε αντίθεση με τη πεσμένη φύση μας, αλλά μέσω της συνεχούς παράδοσης και μιας βαθιάς ταπεινότητας, το Πνεύμα θα γεμίσει τον πιστό μέχρι η φύση της αμαρτίας να γίνει η κυριαρχούμενη αντί για την κυριαρχούσα. Είναι σημαντικό να συνειδητοποιήσουμε, ωστόσο, ότι αυτή η νίκη επί της αμαρτίας γίνεται πραγματικότητα όταν ο πιστός παραδίδει τη θέλησή του και επιτρέπει στο Πνεύμα τον πλήρη έλεγχο.

Έτσι, μια αγνή εκκλησία είναι μια παραδομένη, γεμάτη Πνεύμα ομάδα πιστών που αναγνωρίζουν με αληθινή ταπείνωση ότι η δύναμή τους δεν συνδέεται με κανένα τρόπο με το δικό τους αξίωμα. Η απουσία περηφάνειας, επιτυγχάνεται μόνο με τη συνεχή βοήθεια του Πνεύματος, δίδει περαιτέρω χώρο για τον καθαρισμό του βουλόμενου πιστού. Με αυτόν τον τρόπο, μπορούμε να δούμε τη χριστιανική ζωή στην πράξη.

Οι Διδασκαλίες της Πρακτικής Χριστιανοσύνης

Η πρακτικότητα της πίστης των πρώιμων αμερικανών Μεννονιτών ήταν συνεχώς εμφανής. Στο βιβλίο του, «Υπερηφάνεια και Ταπείνωση», ο John M. Brenneman υποστηρίζει ότι η εξωτερική εμφάνιση ενός ανθρώπου συνδέεται άμεσα με την εσωτερική του καρδιά, άποψη που εκτείνεται επίσης στις πράξεις του ατόμου. Είναι απαραίτητο να οικοδομήσουμε πάνω στις πεποιθήσεις της βουλητικής σωτηρίας, της αναγεννήσεως και μιας αγνής εκκλησίας που εξετάστηκαν προηγουμένως, για να πλαισιώσουμε τη νοοτροπία των αλληλεπιδράσεων ενός Μεννονίτη στην καθημερινή ζωή.

Για αυτούς τους σοβαροπρεπείς χριστιανούς, δεν υπήρχε διαφορά στη σημασία μεταξύ της θρησκευτικής πεποίθησης που εκφραζόταν τις Κυριακές και των καθημερινών πράξεων της υπόλοιπης εβδομάδας. Αυτό τεκμηριώνεται από την γενική αποχή τους από πολιτικά θέματα και άλλα στοιχεία κοσμικής φύσης που θα παρεμπόδιζαν τις πεποιθήσεις που είχαν. Αυτό τους έθετε σε άμεση αντιπαράθεση με πολλές από τις εκκλησίες της εποχής τους, όπου ευημερούσαν δύο σχολές σκέψης: είτε ότι τα επίγεια καθήκοντα κάποιου σε πολιτικό επίπεδο εκτελούνταν εντελώς ξεχωριστά από την πίστη του, είτε ότι η εκπλήρωση αυτών των πολιτικών καθηκόντων ενσωματωνόταν στο θέλημα του Θεού και έτσι ήταν επιτρεπτή για τον χριστιανό να τα επιδίδεται ελεύθερα.

Για τον πρώιμο αμερικανό Μεννονίτη, αυτές οι στάσεις πρόδιδαν το ίδιο το νόημα του χριστιανισμού του: ήταν καινούργιο πρόσωπο, ζωντανό μόνο στη δύναμη του Χριστού που έρρεε μέσα του. Αυτό επηρέαζε και διεύθυνε κάθε πτυχή της ζωής του, από τις επιχειρηματικές του συναλλαγές, οι οποίες διεξήγοντο με τρόπο ώστε να μην εκμεταλλευτεί κανένα εμπλεκόμενο μέρος, μέχρι την ενδυμασία και τον τρόπο συμπεριφοράς, που θα έπρεπε να βασίζεται στην ταπείνωση και την απλότητα, και μέχρι τον τρόπο συνομιλίας του με τον πλησίον, ο οποίος έπρεπε να δείχνει γνήσια φροντίδα για την πνευματική ευημερία και την αιώνια μοίρα.

Συμπέρασμα

Το σύνολο όλων αυτών των αποικιακών μεννονιτικών πεποιθήσεων ήταν η διδασκαλία του πώς να γίνεις ένας ώριμος, ταπεινός, μετανοημένος αλλά πνευματικά δυνατός υπηρέτης του Θεού. Αρνιόταν τα δελεαστικά πράγματα του κόσμου γύρω του υπέρ μιας αιώνιας ανταμοιβής που υποσχόταν με βάση την αγνότητα της πίστης του και την εκούσια αποκήρυξη της αμαρτίας στην οποία άλλοτε ζούσε. Αυτό το παράδειγμα, που ζει μέσα σε πιστούς όπως εμείς, θα έπρεπε να μας εμπνέει να πιέσουμε περαιτέρω μέσα στη Βασιλεία του Θεού, εργαζόμενοι την πίστη μας με ταπείνωση και μετάνοια.

The glory of the spring, how sweet!
The newborn life, how glad!
What joy the happy earth to greet
In new, bright raiment clad!

Divine Redeemer, Thee I bless;
I greet Thy going forth;
I love Thee in the loveliness
Of Thy renewed earth.

But O these wonders of Thy grace,
These nobler works of Thine,
These marvels sweeter far to trace,
These new births more divine:

This new-born glow of faith so strong,
This bloom of love so fair,
This new-born ecstasy of song,
And fragrancy of prayer!

Creator Spirit, work in me
These wonders sweet of Thine;
Divine Redeemer, graciously
Renew this heart of mine.

Still, let new life and strength upspring,
Still, let new joy be given;
And grant the glad new song to ring
Through the new earth and Heaven.

“Adrianna, what’s the temperature outside?” asked Asher. He and Adrianna were sitting at the table doing school with their siblings Emily and Kianna.

“Probably about 50.” Adrianna glanced lazily at the thermometer. “Hey, it’s 65 degrees! Mom, may we eat lunch outside?”

Mom looked up from the sink. “If you do a good job with your school until then, you may,” she told them. “And if you get your school done before lunch, you may play outside for a while this afternoon.”

Asher let out a whoop and started writing fast. The girls grinned at each other and picked up their pencils.

Everyone worked diligently until lunchtime. Then Adrianna made sandwiches while Asher put cookies in bags, Emily collected bags of chips, and Kianna ran down to the basement to grab a few apples. They each packed their lunch in a shopping bag and went out to their picnic spot, a big, flat rock in a clearing in the woods.

They ate quickly, then Adrianna suggested, “Let’s go kayak on the pond!”

“I guess we could,” said Asher slowly. “But didn’t Mom say that Emily and Kianna are too small to handle the kayaks?”

“Oh, yes, I guess she did. Well, they can play on the swings or something,” she shrugged

“I think we should play something everyone can help with,” said Asher. He turned to Emily and Kianna. “What do you want to do?”

“Let’s make a playhouse!” suggested Kianna.

“Yes, let’s!” Emily agreed. “You could hunt for us,” she told Asher.

“And Adrianna could be the mom!” said Kianna.

Adrianna stood with a scowl on her face. Playhouse indeed! She was way too old for that! “I’m going kayaking,” she announced. “You can just have your playhouse.” She picked up her shopping bag and put her sandwich and cookie bags into it. She threw her apple core to the dogs and started for the house.

“Adrianna, can you please take ours too?” begged Emily. “You're going to the house anyway.”

“You can take care of your own stuff,” Adrianna called back, crossly. She dropped her shopping bag on the counter, hoping to slip out of the house before Mom saw her.

She heard her mom’s voice. “Wait, Adrianna, what’s wrong? Your face looks like a thunderstorm!”

Adrianna sighed. She hadn’t been fast enough. “I wanted to go kayaking, but Asher doesn’t want to,” she grumbled.

“Well,” said Mom slowly, “I think Asher is remembering that the other girls can't handle kayaks yet. What are they doing?”

“They’re building a playhouse. I'm way too old for that!” Adrianna burst out.

Mom smiled, “What makes you think that?”

“I'm sure none of the girls my age do stuff like that with their little siblings.”

“Are you sure you're not being selfish?” Mom asked. “Sometimes, we need to give up what we want so that others can be happy.”

Adrianna shrugged and went out to the shed to get a kayak. She lifted her blue kayak off the rack and hauled it down to the pond. She snapped the paddle together, hopped into the seat, and pushed the kayak onto the smooth surface of the water. She sighed with pleasure. This was way better than building a playhouse in the woods! She took a few loops around the pond before her paddle began to slow. Somehow it wasn’t as fun this time. She heard Asher and the girls laughing and shouting as they played. Maybe Mom was right, she thought. Maybe I would be happier if I gave up what I want so that we can all play together. Slowly she paddled to the edge of the pond. She stepped out of the kayak, pulled it out of the water, and flipped it over to dry. Resolutely, she walked out of the pasture to find Asher and the girls.

“Hey! Here comes Adrianna!” called Emily happily as Adrianna walked up.

Adrianna grinned, “It looks like you have your house about set up,” she said encouragingly. “What do you need to finish it?”

“We still need a stove, and something for a countertop,” said Kianna.

“I can help you find something,” Adrianna told them. Together they hunted in the woods and the shed for boards and logs to finish the house. When suppertime came and they went in for supper, Adrianna was very happy. Mom was right, she thought. It is more fun to give up my way and do what everyone else wants to.

“Adrianna, qual é a temperatura lá fora?” perguntou Asher. Ele e Adrianna estavam sentados à mesa estudando com as irmãs Emily e Kianna.

“Provavelmente uns 10.” Adrianna olhou preguiçosamente para o termômetro. “Ei, está 18 graus! Mãe, podemos almoçar lá fora?”

A mãe levantou os olhos da pia. “Se vocês fizerem um bom trabalho nos estudos até lá, podem,” disse ela. “E se terminarem os deveres antes do almoço, podem brincar lá fora um pouco esta tarde.”

Asher soltou um grito de alegria e começou a escrever rapidamente. As meninas sorriram uma para a outra e pegaram seus lápis.

Todos trabalharam diligentemente até a hora do almoço. Então Adrianna preparou sanduíches enquanto Asher colocava biscoitos em saquinhos, Emily recolhia pacotes de salgadinhos e Kianna descia ao porão para pegar algumas maçãs. Cada um arrumou seu almoço numa sacola de compras e foram para o local do piquenique, uma grande pedra plana numa clareira na mata.

Comeram depressa, então Adrianna sugeriu: “Vamos andar de caiaque no lago!”

“Acho que poderíamos,” disse Asher devagar. “Mas a mamãe não disse que a Emily e a Kianna ainda são pequenas demais para os caiaques?”

“Ah, é, acho que ela disse. Bem, elas podem brincar nos balanços ou algo assim,” ela deu de ombros.

“Acho que deveríamos brincar de algo em que todo mundo possa ajudar,” disse Asher. Ele se virou para Emily e Kianna. “O que vocês querem fazer?”

“Vamos construir uma casinha de brincar!” sugeriu Kianna.

“Sim, vamos!” concordou Emily. “Você poderia procurar as coisas para nós,” disse ela a Asher.

“E a Adrianna poderia ser a mamãe!” disse Kianna.

Adrianna ficou em pé com um cenho carrancudo. Casinha de brincar, é? Ela era muito velha para isso! “Vou andar de caiaque,” anunciou. “Vocês fiquem com a casinha.” Pegou sua sacola de compras e colocou nela o sanduíche e os saquinhos de biscoito. Jogou o caroço da maçã para os cachorros e se dirigiu para a casa.

“Adrianna, você pode pegar as nossas também, por favor?” implorou Emily. “Você vai para a casa de qualquer jeito.”

“Cuidem das suas próprias coisas,” Adrianna respondeu, irritada. Largou a sacola de compras no balcão, esperando escapar de casa antes que a mãe a visse.

Ouviu a voz da mãe. “Espere, Adrianna, o que aconteceu? Seu rosto parece uma tempestade!”

Adrianna suspirou. Ela não havia sido rápida o suficiente. “Eu queria ir andar de caiaque, mas o Asher não quer,” resmungou.

“Bem,” disse a mãe devagar, “acho que o Asher está lembrando que as outras meninas ainda não sabem lidar com os caiaques. O que elas estão fazendo?”

“Estão construindo uma casinha de brincar. Eu sou muito velha para isso!” explodiu Adrianna.

A mãe sorriu, “O que te faz pensar isso?”

“Tenho certeza de que nenhuma das garotas da minha idade faz essas coisas com as irmãs pequenas.”

“Você tem certeza de que não está sendo egoísta?” perguntou a mãe. “Às vezes precisamos abrir mão do que queremos para que os outros possam ser felizes.”

Adrianna deu de ombros e foi ao galpão buscar um caiaque. Tirou seu caiaque azul do suporte e o levou até o lago. Encaixou o remo, sentou-se e empurrou o caiaque para a superfície lisa da água. Suspirou de prazer. Isso era muito melhor do que construir uma casinha na mata! Deu algumas voltas no lago antes de o remo começar a perder velocidade. De alguma forma não estava tão divertido dessa vez. Ouviu Asher e as meninas rindo e gritando enquanto brincavam. Talvez a mãe estivesse certa, pensou ela. Talvez eu fique mais feliz se abrir mão do que quero para que possamos todos brincar juntos. Lentamente remou até a margem do lago. Saiu do caiaque, puxou-o para fora da água e o virou para secar. Resoluta, saiu da pastagem para procurar Asher e as meninas.

“Ei! Lá vem a Adrianna!” chamou Emily feliz quando Adrianna apareceu.

Adrianna sorriu, “Parece que a casinha já está quase pronta,” disse ela, encorajadora. “O que vocês ainda precisam para terminá-la?”

“Ainda precisamos de um fogão e de algo para bancada,” disse Kianna.

“Posso ajudar a encontrar alguma coisa,” disse Adrianna. Juntas procuraram na mata e no galpão tábuas e troncos para terminar a casa. Quando chegou a hora do jantar e foram para dentro, Adrianna estava muito feliz. A mãe estava certa, pensou. É mais divertido abrir mão do meu jeito e fazer o que todo mundo quer.

This hymn became precious to my family and me several years ago as we awaited the birth of our fourth genetically challenged baby. We knew she couldn't stay with us very long. She passed away at just three days old. After researching this hymn, I was amazed to find out that the man whose story had inspired this hymn had lost eight out of his nine children.

The story of this man is a notable one. His 61 years on earth were marked by grief and loss, persecution and imprisonment. Yet, his dedication to Christ was outstanding, and his fire for God and zeal for preaching the gospel never waned until his last day.

Samuel Rutherford, son of a prosperous farmer, was born in the year 1600. His life began in the small village of Nisbet, Scotland. As we glimpse into his life, we notice the hand of God at work in Samuel’s early years. At only three years old, he was playing with his friends when he fell into the town well. His sister and friends ran to get help. When they returned, they found a very wet Samuel sitting on the grass beside the well. They asked him how he got out, and his reply was, "A bonny white man came and drew me out of the well." His family believed that God sent an angel to rescue him that day.

From what we know about Samuel Rutherford, he had two brothers and one sister. He was sent to school when he was young, and he became a very diligent scholar. He learned Latin and Greek so well that he eventually became a professor. He married Eupham Hamilton around 1624, soon after he began teaching at Edinburgh University. At this time, Samuel was yet unconverted and cared only for pursuing his academic goals.

In 1626, at the age of 26, Samuel came to a clear and saving faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. He said, "O but Christ hath a saving eye. When He first looked on me I was saved. It cost Him but a look to make hell quit to me." From that moment he was filled with a passion to preach and to speak about his Saviour. This change of life caused such a stir in the university that Rutherford ended up resigning his professorship.

In 1627, Samuel took his wife and two young children to Galloway, Scotland, where he began pastoring the small church of Anwoth. As he commenced his calling there he said, "I have received the commission from the royal and princely Master, my Lord Jesus, to preach Christ to the people." His passion was for the conversion of the people, and it is said that he seemed to be always praying, always preaching, always visiting the sick, always teaching and instructing, always writing or studying. The zeal with which he preached and his concern for the welfare of his congregation had a great effect on them. Not only them, but folks came from the surrounding towns and villages to hear his preaching. A friend once reported, "Many times I thought he would have flown out of the pulpit when he came to speak of Jesus Christ."

Samuel was not estranged from grief and sorrow. In 1631, only four short years after he began his work as a pastor, his wife passed away. His two children also became ill and left this world. In 1636, after nine years of preaching, he was banished to Aberdeen, where he was forbidden to preach the gospel. This was a very difficult time for him as he greatly missed his wife and children as well as his congregation, the Church at Anwoth. This time in his life is indeed one reason he is so well remembered, for he began writing letters back to his church people and friends. Out of the 365 letters he wrote, 220 of them were written during these 22 months of banishment.

The government eventually changed hands, which gave more liberty to the non-conformist Covenanters. Thereupon Rutherford quickly returned to his beloved flock at Anwoth. About a year later, in the fall of 1639, he again reluctantly left Anwoth but this time to fulfill an appointment to become Professor of Divinity at St Mary's College in St. Andrews. This change was difficult for him, as he again greatly missed his congregation. He writes, "My removal from my flock is so heavy to me, that it maketh my life a burden to me, I had never such a longing for death. The Lord help and hold up this sad clay."

After five months in his new position and having been alone for nearly ten years, the 40-year-old Samuel married Jean McMath. Together they had seven children. Sadly, six of them died in infancy and early childhood. Only a daughter named Agnes survived to adulthood.

Rutherford continued to be an influential leader in the non-conformist movement in Scotland for the next 20 years until 1660. With the death of Cromwell, the rule of the commonwealth came to an end, and Charles II was restored to power. Once again, the wrath of the monarchy fell on Samuel. He was summoned to appear before the judge and charged with high treason against the government for preaching the truth. He was put in prison to await execution. However, before the king could put him to death, Samuel became quite sick. He said, "I have a summons already from a superior Judge, and I behoove to answer my first summons and when your day arrives I shall be where few Kings and great folks come."

Late in the afternoon of the last day of his life in answer to the question, "What think ye now of Christ?" answered thusly, "Oh, that all my brethren in the land may know what a Master I have served, and what peace I have this day! I shall sleep in Christ, and when I awake, I shall be satisfied with His likeness. This night shall close the door, and put my anchor within the veil, and I shall go away in a sleep by five of the clock in the morning. Glory! glory to my Creator and my Redeemer forever! I Shall live and adore Him. Oh, for arms to embrace Him! Oh, for a well-tuned harp! Glory! glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land!" These words were heard by his wife, daughter and friends, and he was indeed with his Lord by five in the morning.

Nearly two centuries later, Annie Ross Cousin, a Scottish poet and hymn writer and the wife of a minister, was inspired by the life and writings of Samuel Rutherford. She summarized his life in a biographical hymn,"The Sands of Time are Sinking". This hymn was first published in 1857 in the Christian Treasury. Out of the nineteen original verses, only four are used in our hymn books. (in bold copy)

The sands of time are sinking,
The dawn of heaven breaks,
The summer morn I’ve sighed for,
The fair, sweet morn awakes:
Dark, dark hath been the midnight,
But dayspring is at hand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

2. Oh! well it is forever,
Oh! well forevermore
My nest hung in no forest
Of all this death-doomed shore!
Yea, let the vain world vanish,
As from the ship the stand,
While glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

3. There the Red Rose of Sharon
Unfolds its heart-most bloom.
And fills the air of Heaven
With ravishing perfume;
Oh, to behold its blossom,
While by its fragrance fann’d
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

4. The King there in His beauty,
Without a veil is seen:
It were a well-spent journey
Though seven deaths lay between:
The Lamb with His fair army,
Doth on Mount Zion stand;
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

5. Oh! Christ He is the fountain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above;
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

6. E’en Anwoth was not heaven—
E’en preaching was not Christ;
And in my sea-beat prison
My Lord and I held tryst:
And aye my murkiest storm-cloud
Was by a rainbow spann’d,
Caught from the glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land.

7. But that He built a heaven
Of His surpassing love,
A little New Jerus’lem,
Like to the one above,—
“Lord, take me o’er the water,”
Had been my loud demand,
“Take me to love’s own country,
Unto Immanuel’s land.”

8. But flowers need night’s cool darkness,
The moonlight and the dew;
So Christ, from one who loved it,
His shining oft withdrew;
And then, for cause of absence,
My troubled soul I scann’d—
But glory, shadeless, shineth
In Immanuel’s land.

9. The little birds of Anwoth,
used to count them blest,—
Now, beside happier alters,
go to built my nest:
O’er these there broods no silence,
No graves around them stand,
For glory, deathless, dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

10. Fair Anwoth by the Solway,
To me thou still art dear!
E’en from the verge of Heaven
I drop for thee a tear.
Oh! if one soul from Anwoth
Meet me at God’s right hand,
My Heaven will be two Heavens,
In Immanuel’s land!

11. I’ve wrestled on towards Heaven,
‘Ganst storm, and wind, and tide;—
Now, like a weary traveler,
That leaneth on his guide,
Amid the shades of evening,
While sinks life’s ling’ring sand,
I hail the glory dawning
From Immanuel’s land.

12. Deep waters cross’d life’s pathway,
The hedge of thorns was sharp;
Now these lie all behind me,—
Oh, for a well-tuned harp!
Oh, to join Hallelujah
With yon triumphant band,
Who sing where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land!

13. With mercy and with judgment
My web of time He wove,
And aye the dews of sorrow
Were lustered with His love!
I’ll bless the hand that guided,
I’ll bless the heart that plann’d,
When throned where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

14. Soon shall the cup of glory
Wash down earth’s bitterest woes,
Soon shall the desert brier
Break into Eden’s rose:
The curse shall change to blessing–
The name on earth that’s bann’d,
Be graven on the white stone
In Immanuel’s land.

15. Oh! I am my Beloved’s,
And my Beloved’s mine!
He brings a poor vile sinner
Into His “house of wine:”
I stand upon His merit,
I know no other stand,
Not e’en where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

16. I shall sleep sound in Jesus,
Fill’d with His likeness rise,
To live and to adore Him,
To see Him with these eyes:
‘Tween me and resurrection
But Paradise doth stand;
Then—then for glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land!

17. The bride eyes not her garment,
But her dear Bridegroom’s face;
I will not gaze at glory,
But on my King of Grace—
Not at the crown He giveth,
But on His pierced hand:
The Lamb is all the glory
Of Immanuel’s land.

18. I have borne scorn and hatred,
I have borne wrong and shame,
Earth’s proud ones have reproach’d me,
For Christ’s thrice blessed name:
Where God His seal set fairest
They’ve stamp’d their foulest brand;
But judgment shines like noonday
In Immanuel’s land.

19. They’ve summoned me before them,
But there I may not come,—
My Lord says, “Come up hither,”
My Lord says, “Welcome home!
My King now at His white throne,
My presence doth command,
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

The fine complementary tune for this text was composed in the early 1800s by a French musician, Chretien D`Urhan. It is well fitted to the words of the hymn—its solemn tempo matches the solemnity of the words. The rising melodic line of the last phrase perfectly matches the anticipated joy expressed by the refrain—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

As we conclude this hymn history, let us continue to marvel at the providence of God in the lives of those who have gone before us. May we follow Christ with all our hearts and be vessels ready for the Master's use! One last quote by Samuel Rutherford to take with us. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."

The information for this article was sourced from 101 Hymn Stories, A Treasury of Hymns, Crichbaptist.org.

Il m'est incroyable de voir comment Dieu utilise Son peuple à travers l'histoire pour glorifier Son nom. Il use des choses faibles pour confondre les sages ; des choses viles pour réduire à néant la sagesse des hommes de ce monde. Dieu se sert de la faiblesse physique, des épreuves, de la perte, du deuil, du travail et de la douleur pour accroître nos trésors spirituels et bâtir Son royaume ici sur la terre !

Ce cantique est devenu précieux pour ma famille et moi il y a plusieurs années, alors que nous attendions la naissance de notre quatrième enfant porteur d'une anomalie génétique. Nous savions qu'elle ne pourrait pas rester longtemps avec nous. Elle est décédée à seulement trois jours. En recherchant l'histoire de ce cantique, j'ai été étonné d'apprendre que l'homme dont l'histoire avait inspiré ce chant avait perdu huit de ses neuf enfants.

L'histoire de cet homme est remarquable. Ses 61 années sur terre furent marquées par le chagrin et la perte, la persécution et l'emprisonnement. Pourtant, son dévouement envers le Christ était remarquable, et son zèle pour Dieu et pour la prédication de l'Évangile ne faiblit jamais jusqu'à son dernier jour.

Samuel Rutherford, fils d'un fermier prospère, naquit en l'an 1600. Sa vie commença dans le petit village de Nisbet, en Écosse. En jetant un coup d'œil sur son existence, on remarque la main de Dieu à l'œuvre durant les premières années de Samuel. À seulement trois ans, il jouait avec ses amis lorsqu'il tomba dans le puits de la ville. Sa sœur et ses amis coururent chercher de l'aide. À leur retour, ils trouvèrent un Samuel très mouillé assis sur l'herbe près du puits. Ils lui demandèrent comment il était sorti, et il répondit : « Un bel homme blanc est venu et m'a tiré du puits. » Sa famille crut que Dieu avait envoyé un ange pour le secourir ce jour-là.

D'après ce que nous savons de Samuel Rutherford, il avait deux frères et une sœur. Il fut envoyé à l'école dès son jeune âge et devint un étudiant très assidu. Il apprit si bien le latin et le grec qu'il devint finalement professeur. Il épousa Eupham Hamilton vers 1624, peu après avoir commencé à enseigner à l'Université d'Édimbourg. À cette époque, Samuel n'était pas encore converti et ne se préoccupait que de poursuivre ses objectifs académiques.

En 1626, à l'âge de 26 ans, Samuel arriva à une foi claire et salvatrice en le Seigneur Jésus-Christ. Il déclara : « Ô mais Christ a un œil qui sauve. Quand Il me regarda pour la première fois j'étais sauvé. Il ne Lui coûta qu'un regard pour rendre l'enfer vain pour moi. » Dès ce moment, il fut rempli d'une passion pour prêcher et parler de son Sauveur. Ce changement de vie provoqua un tel remous à l'université que Rutherford finit par démissionner de sa chaire.

En 1627, Samuel emmena sa femme et leurs deux jeunes enfants à Galloway, en Écosse, où il commença à diriger la petite église d'Anwoth. En entreprenant son ministère, il déclara : « J'ai reçu la commission du Maître royal et princier, mon Seigneur Jésus, pour prêcher Christ au peuple. » Sa passion visait la conversion des gens, et l'on disait qu'il semblait toujours en prière, toujours en train de prêcher, toujours en visite aux malades, toujours enseignant et instruisant, toujours écrivant ou étudiant. Le zèle de sa prédication et son souci du bien-être de sa congrégation eurent un grand effet sur eux. Non seulement les habitants d'Anwoth, mais des gens des villes et villages voisins vinrent entendre sa prédication. Un ami rapporta un jour : « Bien des fois j'ai cru qu'il allait s'envoler de la chaire quand il venait parler de Jésus-Christ. »

Samuel n'était pas étranger au chagrin et à la souffrance. En 1631, seulement quatre courtes années après le début de son ministère pastoral, sa femme mourut. Ses deux enfants tombèrent aussi malades et quittèrent ce monde. En 1636, après neuf ans de prédication, il fut banni à Aberdeen, où il se vit interdire de prêcher l'Évangile. Ce fut une période très difficile pour lui, car sa femme, ses enfants et sa congrégation d'Anwoth lui manquaient énormément. Cette période de sa vie est d'ailleurs une des raisons pour lesquelles on se souvient si bien de lui, car il commença à écrire des lettres à son peuple et à ses amis. Sur les 365 lettres qu'il écrivit, 220 furent rédigées durant ces 22 mois d'exil.

Le gouvernement changea finalement de mains, ce qui donna plus de liberté aux presbytériens non-conformistes (les Covenanters). Rutherford retourna promptement auprès de son troupeau bien-aimé à Anwoth. Environ un an plus tard, à l'automne 1639, il quitta de nouveau à regret Anwoth mais cette fois pour accepter une nomination comme professeur de théologie au St Mary's College à St. Andrews. Ce changement fut difficile pour lui, car sa congrégation lui manquait de nouveau profondément. Il écrit : « Mon éloignement de mon troupeau m'est si pénible, que cela fait de ma vie un fardeau pour moi, je n'ai jamais eu un tel désir de la mort. Que le Seigneur aide et soutienne cette pauvre chair. »

Après cinq mois dans sa nouvelle charge et ayant été seul pendant près de dix ans, le Samuel de 40 ans épousa Jean McMath. Ensemble ils eurent sept enfants. Hélas, six d'entre eux moururent en bas âge et durant la petite enfance. Seule une fille nommée Agnes survécut jusqu'à l'âge adulte.

Rutherford continua d'être un dirigeant influent du mouvement non-conformiste en Écosse pendant les vingt années suivantes, jusqu'en 1660. Avec la mort de Cromwell, le régime du Commonwealth prit fin et Charles II retrouva le pouvoir. Une fois de plus, la colère de la monarchie se déchaîna contre Samuel. Il fut sommé de comparaître devant le juge et accusé de haute trahison contre le gouvernement pour avoir prêché la vérité. Il fut emprisonné en attendant l'exécution. Cependant, avant que le roi ne put le faire mettre à mort, Samuel tomba gravement malade. Il dit : « J'ai déjà une convocation d'un Juge supérieur, et je dois répondre à ma première convocation et quand votre jour arrivera je serai là où peu de rois et de grands viennent. »

Tard dans l'après-midi du dernier jour de sa vie, en réponse à la question « Que pensez-vous maintenant du Christ ? » il répondit ainsi : « Oh, que tous mes frères dans le pays sachent quel Maître j'ai servi, et quelle paix j'ai aujourd'hui ! Je dormirai en Christ, et quand je me réveillerai, je serai rassasié de Sa ressemblance. Cette nuit fermera la porte, et mettra mon ancre au-dedans du voile, et je m'en irai dormir à cinq heures du matin. Gloire ! gloire à mon Créateur et mon Rédempteur pour toujours ! Je vivrai et L'adorerai. Oh, pour des bras afin de L'embrasser ! Oh, pour une harpe bien accordée ! Gloire ! la gloire habite dans la terre d'Emmanuel ! » Ces paroles furent entendues par sa femme, sa fille et ses amis, et il fut effectivement auprès de son Seigneur à cinq heures du matin.

Près de deux siècles plus tard, Annie Ross Cousin, poétesse et auteure de cantiques écossaise et épouse d'un pasteur, fut inspirée par la vie et les écrits de Samuel Rutherford. Elle résuma sa vie dans un cantique biographique, « The Sands of Time are Sinking ». Ce cantique fut publié pour la première fois en 1857 dans le Christian Treasury. Sur les dix-neuf couplets originaux, seulement quatre sont utilisés dans nos recueils de cantiques. (en copie en gras)

Les sables du temps s'ENFONCENT,
L'aube du ciel se lève,
Le matin d'été que j'ai soupiré,
Le beau et doux matin s'éveille :
Sombre, sombre a été la minuit,
Mais l'aurore est proche,
Et la gloire—la gloire habite
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

2. Oh ! que c'est pour toujours heureux,
Oh ! que pour toujours encore
Mon nid ne fut pas accroché
Dans quelque forêt de ce rivage voué à la mort !
Oui, que le monde vain s'évanouisse,
Comme on jette du bord le fardiau,
Tandis que la gloire—la gloire habite
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

3. Là la Rose rouge de Saron
Déploie son plus intime fleur.
Et emplit l'air du Ciel
D'un parfum ravissant ;
Oh, contempler sa floraison,
Tandis qu'on en est caressé par le souffle,
Où la gloire—la gloire habite
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

4. Le Roi là, dans Sa beauté,
Sans voile est vu :
Ce serait un voyage bien employé
Même si sept morts se trouvaient entre :
L'Agneau avec sa belle armée
Se tient sur le mont Sion ;
Et la gloire—la gloire habite
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

5. Oh ! Christ Il est la fontaine,
La profonde et douce source d'Amour !
Les ruisseaux que j'ai goûtés sur terre,
Plus profondément j'en boirai au-dessus ;
Là, jusqu'à une plénitude océanique,
Sa miséricorde s'étend,
Et la gloire—la gloire habite
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

6. Même Anwoth n'était pas le ciel—
Même la prédication n'était pas Christ ;
Et dans ma prison battue par la mer
Mon Seigneur et moi fîmes rendez-vous :
Et toujours mon nuage de tempête le plus sombre
Fut orné d'un arc-en-ciel,
Pris de la gloire habitant
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

7. Mais qu'il ait bâti un ciel
De Son amour surpassant,
Un petit Nouveau Jérusalem,
Semblable à celui d'en haut,—
« Seigneur, fais-moi passer par-dessus les eaux, »
Tel eût été mon cri ardent,
« Conduis-moi vers le pays de l'amour,
Vers la terre d'Emmanuel. »

8. Mais les fleurs ont besoin de l'obscurité fraîche de la nuit,
De la lumière de la lune et de la rosée ;
Ainsi Christ, de celui qui l'aimait,
Retirait souvent Sa lumière ;
Et alors, à cause de Son absence,
J'examinai mon âme troublée—
Mais la gloire, sans ombre, resplendit
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

9. Les petits oiseaux d'Anwoth,
que l'on jugeait bénis,—
Maintenant, près d'autels plus heureux,
vont y bâtir mon nid :
Sur eux ne plane aucun silence,
Aucune tombe autour d'eux ne se dresse,
Car la gloire, immortelle, habite
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

10. Belle Anwoth au bord du Solway,
Tu m'es toujours chère !
Même du seuil du Ciel
Je verse pour toi une larme.
Oh ! si une âme d'Anwoth
Me rencontre à la droite de Dieu,
Mon Ciel sera deux Cieux,
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel !

11. J'ai lutté vers le Ciel,
Contre la tempête, le vent et la marée ;—
Maintenant, comme un voyageur las,
Qui s'appuie sur son guide,
Parmi les ombres du soir,
Tandis que s'enfuit le sable de la vie,
J'accueille l'éclat de la gloire naissante
De la terre d'Emmanuel.

12. Des eaux profondes ont croisé le chemin de la vie,
Le roncier fut aigu ;
Maintenant tout cela est derrière moi,—
Oh, pour une harpe bien accordée !
Oh, pour joindre le Hallelujah
Au sein de cette troupe triomphante,
Qui chantent où la gloire habite
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel !

13. Avec miséricorde et jugement
Il tissa ma toile de temps,
Et toujours les rosées du chagrin
Brillaient de Son amour !
Je bénirai la main qui guida,
Je bénirai le cœur qui conçut le plan,
Quand je serai couronné là où la gloire habite
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

14. Bientôt la coupe de gloire
Laver[a] les plus amères douleurs de la terre,
Bientôt l'épine du désert
Rompra en la rose d'Éden :
La malédiction se changera en bénédiction—
Le nom sur terre qui est maudit,
Sera gravé sur la pierre blanche
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

15. Oh ! je suis à mon Bien-Aimé,
Et mon Bien-Aimé est à moi !
Il amène un pauvre pécheur vil
Dans Sa « maison de vin » :
Je tiens sur Son mérite,
Je ne connais aucun autre appui,
Même là où la gloire habite
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

16. Je dormirai profondément en Jésus,
Rempli de Sa ressemblance je ressusciterai,
Pour vivre et L'adorer,
Pour Le voir de mes propres yeux :
Entre moi et la résurrection
Se tient seulement le Paradis ;
Alors—alors pour habiter la gloire
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel !

17. La fiancée ne regarde pas sa robe,
Mais le visage de son cher Époux ;
Je ne contemplerai pas la gloire,
Mais mon Roi de Grâce—
Pas la couronne qu'Il donne,
Mais Sa main percée :
L'Agneau est toute la gloire
De la terre d'Emmanuel.

18. J'ai supporté le mépris et la haine,
J'ai supporté l'injustice et la honte,
Les orgueilleux de la terre m'ont insulté,
Pour le nom trois fois béni du Christ :
Là où Dieu plaça Son sceau le plus beau
Ils ont apposé leur marque la plus infâme ;
Mais le jugement resplendit comme le zénith
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

19. Ils m'ont convoqué devant eux,
Mais là je ne puis venir,—
Mon Seigneur dit, « Montez ici, »
Mon Seigneur dit, « Bienvenue chez toi ! »
Mon Roi maintenant à Son trône blanc,
Ma présence y commande,
Où la gloire—la gloire habite
Dans la terre d'Emmanuel.

La belle mélodie complémentaire pour ce texte fut composée au début des années 1800 par un musicien français, Chretien D'Urhan. Elle convient bien aux paroles du cantique—son tempo solennel correspond à la solennité des paroles. La ligne mélodique ascendante de la dernière phrase correspond parfaitement à la joie anticipée exprimée par le refrain—« And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land. »

En concluant cette histoire du cantique, continuons d'admirer la providence de Dieu dans la vie de ceux qui nous ont précédés. Puissions-nous suivre Christ de tout notre cœur et être des vases prêts à l'usage du Maître ! Une dernière citation de Samuel Rutherford à emporter : « They lose nothing who gain Christ. »

Spring is my favorite time of the year. Everything is new. Hyacinths are trying their noble best to poke their buds through the cold constraint of the winter-bound earth. Migrating waterfowl bring new sounds as they honk and quack their way to their final nesting places. This year the spring peepers in our area were “winter peepers” as they feebly squeaked their greetings to the arriving spring in mid-February. Tree buds are swelling, waiting to burst forth in full glory.

Oh, the magnificence of God’s nature joining forces to proclaim the glory of new life. Surely it must have been during this exuberant time of the year when the Psalmist wrote, “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9). This display of new life springing from the earth is a beautiful representation of new life found in Christ Jesus. The wonders of the newness of life springing from the deadness of sin cannot be fully displayed by even the best show of God’s creation. It can only be experienced within the soul.

As I write this, I am flying 35,000 feet over the sub-Saharan desert land of Chad and Niger. The stark contrast between the landscape described in the previous paragraphs and the parched desert land hurrying by six miles below me is nearly beyond my comprehension. The dry earth begs for rain as livestock scrounge for anything green to fulfill their appetite. The vast dryness loudly proclaims a reminder of the millions of parched souls who have never heard of the “well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14). Millions who never experienced Christ the fountain as described in the Hymn History article in this issue:

Oh! Christ He is the foutain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above:
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

At times a yearning stirs in my heart to live the relaxed, relational lifestyle experienced in these impoverished tribal communities. Family and friends are more important than calendars and commitments. As we read in the Sister to Sister article, commitments and busyness can bring us to the overload point when we feel we cannot handle anything more. Read more to learn how to take practical steps to avoid that breaking point.

Most people in this area are Muslims. As I write this, Muslims are in the middle of Ramadan, a month-long season of fasting. They fast from food and water every day from dawn to dusk, even though daytime temperatures exceed 110 degrees. Their rigorous fasting, along with stopping their work to pray many times a day, is driven by a fervent desire to seek forgiveness of sins and obtain enough merit to enter heaven. If they only knew that true grace and mercy comes from God through the salvation of his Son, Jesus Christ. Our works can never bring us into right standing with God. The writer of the article “How to Increase Your Faith” clearly points this out “Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety.”

As we plant our gardens and watch the trees burst forth in bloom, let us be reminded of the words of the prophet Isaiah, “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” (Isaiah 61:11).

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

La primavera è la mia stagione preferita. Tutto è nuovo. I giacinti fanno del loro meglio per far uscire i boccioli attraverso la fredda costrizione della terra legata all'inverno. Gli anatidi migratori portano nuovi suoni mentre onorano e starnazzano il loro cammino verso i luoghi di nidificazione finali. Quest'anno i piccoli grilli primaverili della nostra zona sono stati “grilli invernali”, mentre gracchiavano debolmente i loro saluti all'arrivo della primavera a metà febbraio. I germogli degli alberi si stanno gonfiando, in attesa di esplodere in piena gloria.

Oh, la magnificenza della natura di Dio che unisce le forze per proclamare la gloria della nuova vita. Dev'essere stato sicuramente durante questo periodo esuberante dell'anno che il Salmista scrisse, “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9). Questa manifestazione di nuova vita che sgorga dalla terra è una bellissima rappresentazione della nuova vita che si trova in Cristo Gesù. Le meraviglie della novità di vita che nasce dalla morte del peccato non possono essere pienamente mostrate nemmeno dalla migliore esposizione della creazione di Dio. Possono essere sperimentate soltanto nell'anima.

Mentre scrivo, sto volando a 35.000 piedi sopra le terre desertiche subsahariane del Ciad e del Niger. Il netto contrasto tra il paesaggio descritto nei paragrafi precedenti e la terra arida che scorre sotto di me a sei miglia di distanza è quasi al di là della mia comprensione. La terra secca implora la pioggia mentre il bestiame fruga qualsiasi cosa di verde per soddisfare l'appetito. L'enorme secchezza proclama ad alta voce un richiamo ai milioni di anime assetate che non hanno mai sentito parlare del “well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14). Milioni che non hanno mai sperimentato Cristo, la fonte descritta nell'articolo sulla Storia degli Inni in questo numero:

Oh! Cristo egli è la fonte,
Il profondo dolce pozzo d'amore!
I ruscelli sulla terra che ho gustato,
Più profondamente berrò lassù:
Là, fino a un'abbondanza oceanica,
La sua misericordia si espande,
E gloria—gloria dimora
Nella terra di Immanuel.

A volte nel mio cuore si risveglia il desiderio di vivere lo stile di vita rilassato e relazionale sperimentato in queste povere comunità tribali. Famiglia e amici sono più importanti di calendari e impegni. Come leggiamo nell'articolo Sorella a Sorella, gli impegni e la frenesia possono portarci al punto di sovraccarico quando sentiamo di non poter gestire altro. Continua a leggere per imparare come prendere passi pratici per evitare quel punto di rottura.

La maggior parte delle persone in quest'area sono musulmane. Mentre scrivo, i musulmani sono nel mezzo del Ramadan, un periodo di digiuno che dura un mese. Digiunano da cibo e acqua ogni giorno dall'alba al tramonto, anche se le temperature diurne superano i 110 gradi. Il loro rigoroso digiuno, insieme al fatto di interrompere il lavoro per pregare più volte al giorno, è guidato dal fervente desiderio di cercare il perdono dei peccati e ottenere abbastanza meriti per entrare in paradiso. Se sapessero solo che la vera grazia e misericordia vengono da Dio attraverso la salvezza del suo Figlio, Gesù Cristo. Le nostre opere non possono mai portarci a una giusta condizione davanti a Dio. L'autore dell'articolo “How to Increase Your Faith” lo evidenzia chiaramente: “Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety.”

Mentre piantiamo i nostri giardini e guardiamo gli alberi esplodere in fiore, ricordiamoci le parole del profeta Isaia, “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” (Isaiah 61:11).

Benedizioni a tutti,

Edward Martin

Spring is my favorite time of the year. Everything is new. Hyacinths are trying their noble best to poke their buds through the cold constraint of the winter-bound earth. Migrating waterfowl bring new sounds as they honk and quack their way to their final nesting places. This year the spring peepers in our area were “winter peepers” as they feebly squeaked their greetings to the arriving spring in mid-February. Tree buds are swelling, waiting to burst forth in full glory.

Oh, the magnificence of God’s nature joining forces to proclaim the glory of new life. Surely it must have been during this exuberant time of the year when the Psalmist wrote, “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9). This display of new life springing from the earth is a beautiful representation of new life found in Christ Jesus. The wonders of the newness of life springing from the deadness of sin cannot be fully displayed by even the best show of God’s creation. It can only be experienced within the soul.

As I write this, I am flying 35,000 feet over the sub-Saharan desert land of Chad and Niger. The stark contrast between the landscape described in the previous paragraphs and the parched desert land hurrying by six miles below me is nearly beyond my comprehension. The dry earth begs for rain as livestock scrounge for anything green to fulfill their appetite. The vast dryness loudly proclaims a reminder of the millions of parched souls who have never heard of the “well of water springing up into everlasting life” (John 4:14). Millions who never experienced Christ the fountain as described in the Hymn History article in this issue:

Oh! Christ He is the foutain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above:
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

At times a yearning stirs in my heart to live the relaxed, relational lifestyle experienced in these impoverished tribal communities. Family and friends are more important than calendars and commitments. As we read in the Sister to Sister article, commitments and busyness can bring us to the overload point when we feel we cannot handle anything more. Read more to learn how to take practical steps to avoid that breaking point.

Most people in this area are Muslims. As I write this, Muslims are in the middle of Ramadan, a month-long season of fasting. They fast from food and water every day from dawn to dusk, even though daytime temperatures exceed 110 degrees. Their rigorous fasting, along with stopping their work to pray many times a day, is driven by a fervent desire to seek forgiveness of sins and obtain enough merit to enter heaven. If they only knew that true grace and mercy comes from God through the salvation of his Son, Jesus Christ. Our works can never bring us into right standing with God. The writer of the article “How to Increase Your Faith” clearly points this out “Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety.”

As we plant our gardens and watch the trees burst forth in bloom, let us be reminded of the words of the prophet Isaiah, “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” (Isaiah 61:11).

Blessings to all,

Edward Martin

الربيع هو فصلي المفضل في السنة. كل شيء جديد. تحاول زهور الزيزيون بذل قصارى جهدها لتبرز براعمها من خلال قسوة الأرض المحكومة بالشتاء. تجلب الطيور المائية المهاجرة أصواتًا جديدة وهي تنقنق وتزمجر في طريقها إلى مواضع تعشيشها النهائية. هذا العام كانت أصوات ضفادع الربيع في منطقتنا "ضفادع شتوية" إذ أصدرت بضع نقيقات ضعيفة لتحيّي حلول الربيع في منتصف فبراير. براعم الأشجار تتورم، تنتظر الانفجار لتظهر بجلالها الكامل.

يا لعظمة طبيعة الله وهي تتحد لتعلن مجد الحياة الجديدة. لا بد وأنه في هذا الموسم المفعم بالحياة كتب المزمور: “Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity” (Psalms 98:8-9). هذا العرض من الحياة الجديدة الناشئة من الأرض هو تمثيل جميل للحياة الجديدة الموجودة في المسيح يسوع. عجائب حداثة الحياة الناشئة من موت الخطيئة لا يمكنها أن تُعرض بالكامل حتى بأفضل عروض خلق الله. لا يمكن تجربتها إلا في داخل النفس.

بينما أكتب هذا، أطير على ارتفاع 35,000 قدم فوق أراضي الصحراء جنوب الصحراء الكبرى في تشاد والنيجر. التباين الحاد بين المنظر الطبيعي الموصوف في الفقرات السابقة والأرض الجافة المتسارعة في الأسفل على بعد ستة أميال يكاد يفوق إدراكي. الأرض الجافة تتوسل للمطر بينما تفتش المواشي عن أي شيء أخضر لتسد جوعها. هذا الجفاف الشاسع يعلن بصوت عالٍ تذكرة بالملايين من النفوس العطشى التي لم تسمع قط بـ "well of water springing up into everlasting life" (John 4:14). ملايين لم يختبروا المسيح الينبوع كما وُصف في مقالة تاريخ الترانيم في هذا العدد:

يا روح المسيح هو الينبوع،
البئر العميق الحلو للمحبة!
التيارات على الأرض ذقتها،
أعمق سأشرب فوق:
هناك، إلى فيض المحيط،
رحمته تتسع،
والمجد—المجد يسكن
في أرض عمانوئيل.

أحيانًا يثار في قلبي شوق للعيش بأسلوب الحياة المريح والعلاقي الذي تختبره هذه المجتمعات القبلية الفقيرة. الأسرة والأصدقاء أهم من الجداول والالتزامات. كما نقرأ في مقالة "أخت لأخت"، يمكن أن تقودنا الالتزامات والانشغال إلى نقطة التحميل الزائد حين نشعر أننا لا نستطيع التحمل أكثر. اقرأ المزيد لتتعلم كيفية اتخاذ خطوات عملية لتجنب نقطة الانهيار تلك.

معظم الناس في هذه المنطقة مسلمون. بينما أكتب هذا، المسلمون في وسط رمضان، شهر الصوم الطويل. يصومون عن الطعام والماء كل يوم من الفجر حتى الغسق، رغم أن درجات الحرارة النهارية تتجاوز 110 درجات. صومهم الصارم، إلى جانب توقفهم عن العمل للصلاة عدة مرات في اليوم، مدفوع برغبة شديدة في طلب مغفرة الذنوب ونيل قدر كافٍ من الحسنات لدخول الجنة. لو كانوا يعلمون فقط أن النعمة الحقيقية والرحمة تأتي من الله عبر خلاص ابنه، يسوع المسيح. أعمالنا لا تستطيع أن تدخلنا في حالة صِحّة أمام الله. كاتب المقال "How to Increase Your Faith" يوضح هذا بجلاء: “Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety.”

بينما نزرع حدائقنا ونراقب الأشجار تتفتح، فلنذكر بكلمات النبي أشعيا، “For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations” (Isaiah 61:11).

بركات للجميع،

إدوارد مارتن

Våren är min favorittid på året. Allt är nytt. Hyacinter gör sitt ärliga yttersta för att pressa sina knoppar genom den vinterskylda jordens hårda grepp. Flyttfåglar för med sig nya ljud när de knorrar och kvackar sig fram till sina slutliga häckningsplatser. I år var vårens vårpinglor i vårt område ”vinterpinglor” när de svagt pipande hälsade den anländande våren i mitten av februari. Trädens knoppar sväller och väntar på att brista ut i full prakt.

Åh, naturens storslagenhet där Guds skapelse förenar krafter för att förkunna härligheten av nytt liv. Det måste säkert ha varit under denna yviga årstid som psalmisten skrev, "Let the floods clap their hands: let the hills be joyful together before the LORD; for he cometh to judge the earth: with righteousness shall he judge the world, and the people with equity" (Psalms 98:8-9). Denna uppvisning av nytt liv som spirar ur jorden är en vacker framställning av det nya liv som finns i Kristus Jesus. Underverken i detta nya liv som uppstår ur syndens död kan inte fullt ut visas ens av Guds skapelses bästa skådespel. Det kan bara erfaras i själen.

När jag skriver detta flyger jag 35 000 fot över det subsahariska ökenlandskapet i Tchad och Niger. Kontrasten mellan landskapet som beskrivs i de föregående styckena och den uttorkade ökenmarken som skyndar förbi sex mil under mig är nästan bortom min förståelse. Den torra jorden bönfaller om regn medan boskapen söker efter något grönt att stilla sin aptit med. Den vidsträckta torrheten proklamerar högljutt en påminnelse om de miljontals uttorkade själar som aldrig har hört talas om "the well of water springing up into everlasting life" (John 4:14). Miljoner som aldrig har upplevt Kristus som källan, som beskrivs i artikeln om psalmhistorik i detta nummer:

Åh! Kristus Han är källan,
Den djupa ljuva kärleksbrunnen!
Strömmarna jag smakat här på jorden,
Djupare skall jag dricka där ovan:
Där, till ett oceans fyllnad,
Utbreder sig Hans barmhärtighet,
Och härlighet—härlighet bor
I Immanuels land.

Ibland väcks en längtan i mitt hjärta att leva det avslappnade, relationsinriktade livet som finns i dessa fattiga stamgemenskaper. Familj och vänner är viktigare än kalendrar och åtaganden. Som vi läser i artikeln "Syster till syster" kan åtaganden och upptagenhet föra oss till brytpunkten där vi känner att vi inte orkar med något mer. Läs vidare för att lära dig hur du kan ta praktiska steg för att undvika den punkten då allt brister.

Majoriteten i detta område är muslimer. När jag skriver detta är muslimer mitt uppe i Ramadan, en månadslång fasteperiod. De fastar från mat och vatten varje dag från gryning till skymning, även om dagstemperaturerna överstiger 110 grader. Deras stränga fasta, tillsammans med att de upphör med sitt arbete för att be många gånger om dagen, drivs av en brinnande önskan att söka syndernas förlåtelse och skaffa sig tillräckliga meriter för att komma till himlen. Om de bara visste att sann nåd och barmhärtighet kommer från Gud genom frälsningen i hans Son, Jesus Kristus. Våra gärningar kan aldrig föra oss i rätt relation till Gud. Författaren till artikeln "How to Increase Your Faith" påpekar detta tydligt: "Faith is one of the basic ingredients in getting right with God. We come into the Christian life (and receive the forgiveness of sins) through faith. . . We abandon all hope for saving ourselves by our own abilities, and instead, we put complete trust in Jesus Christ for our eternal safety."

När vi planterar våra trädgårdar och ser träden brista ut i blom, låt oss då minnas profeten Jesajas ord, "For as the earth bringeth forth her bud, and as the garden causeth the things that are sown in it to spring forth; so the Lord GOD will cause righteousness and praise to spring forth before all the nations" (Isaiah 61:11).

Välsignelser till er alla,

Edward Martin

“It is so hard,” the man sitting across from me said. “We’ve been married for nearly fifty years, but I never expected anything like this.”

“What is going on?” I asked Al, sympathetically.

“It’s Lisa,” he said. “You know her memory has been slipping for a little while. Well, we went to the neurologist like you told us to, and they ordered a whole bunch of tests and a brain scan of some sort. Then, they told her she had dementia.”

“I thought that was what was going on,” I replied.

“I know you told us that,” Al said. “Well, there are times she doesn’t recognize me. She looks at me blankly like she is wondering what crazy stranger has gotten into her house.”

“That’s got to be hard,” I said.

“The only thing I’ve found that brings her back to herself is to go outside and call her on her cell phone. I tell her to come out to the garage, I’ve got something to show her. Somehow when I do that, it brings her back to the present and lets her know who I am – for a little bit, anyway.”

We moved on to talking about other things, but I could tell that Al’s heart was breaking. His wife of 48 years looked the same as ever on the outside and yet, she was a completely different person.

I’d like to explore some of the challenges in dealing with dementia.

Dementia in the Bible

Ecclesiastes 12:1-7 gives a somewhat dismal view of the aging process. “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them; While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low; Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

In this passage, the poetic description seems to speak of loss of teeth, loss of hearing, unsteady gait, and general frailty. It is hard to say if any of these images speak of memory loss. What is certain is that the passage begins with a command: “Remember!”

This is not the only place in Scripture where humans are commanded to remember. Over and over, we are told to remember God. We are to make certain that we instruct our children about Him. “And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (Deuteronomy 6:7).

The time may come when we are not able to remember anymore. The most important thing – even as we think about the subject of dementia is that we remember the One who made us and follow Him with all our hearts.

What Dementia is

Dementia is any illness that causes a loss of memory, reasoning, and social functioning. Most people think mostly of the loss of memory. I suppose this is because early in the illness other people notice things like difficulty finding words and frequent repetition of stories.

Social functioning is often maintained until late in the illness. If you ask someone with mild dementia if they know today’s date, they will likely answer, “Oh, you know, I stopped paying attention to things like that when I retired.”

The most common cause of dementia is Alzheimer’s dementia – at least 70 percent of people who have progressive memory loss have Alzheimer’s dementia. Alzheimer’s seems to be related to proteins called amyloid, which get deposited in the brain and prevent nerve cells from communicating with each other.

Other causes are vascular dementia, where blockages in the blood vessels in the brain cause the death of nerve cells. Lewy Body Dementia is a sort of memory loss that is associated with Parkinson’s Disease. Approximately eighty percent of people with Parkinson’s Disease will eventually develop dementia.

Diagnosing Dementia

If family members suspect someone is developing memory loss, the best thing is to bring them to their primary care provider for an evaluation. Along with doing a physical exam, the doctor will typically do things like have the patient draw a clock and do a mini mental status exam, which asks the patient to answer a lot of simple questions and do some short-term recall of items.

Blood tests including a thyroid and Vitamin B12 level would be done. A brain scan or ultrasound of the neck arteries might be done as well.

The goal is to identify areas that can be treated and take care of those.

Eliminate Medications

Many medications increase the risk of memory issues. As people get older, trying to avoid these medications is helpful to prevent the development of dementia.

Anticholinergic medications are probably the biggest culprit that I encounter. The most common of these medications are older antihistamines like diphenhydramine (used as either a sleep aid or allergy pill) and doxylamine (used as a sleep aid). In one study, patients who took an anticholinergic medication for the equivalent of three years had a significantly higher risk of dementia than patients who took these sorts of medications for less than three months.1 Older depression medications can also fall into this category.

Anxiety medications, called benzodiazepines, have also been associated with memory issues. Studies indicate that patients who take these medications have a higher risk of developing dementia than patients who do not take them.2

Seizure medications may make thinking ability worse as well. Having a seizure disorder seems to increase the risk of dementia, but certain older medications like valproate and gabapentin seem to make it harder for older people to think clearly, and shifting to lower-risk seizure medications is in order (if possible) for older people.

There are times when someone needs to take medication, but as patients get older, it is important to think about the risks of those medications. There is a list of medications that are wisest to avoid for patients over 65 years of age, called the Beers List. Substituting similar medications with fewer side effects or using lower doses is recommended.3

Medical Treatments

The first rule when dealing with dementia is to make certain that all of the metabolic things are in as good control as possible. So, if someone has diabetes, it is best to make certain that their sugar is in as good control as possible. If someone has high blood pressure, make certain that it is well-regulated (this is particularly true if someone has vascular dementia).

There are several different classes of medications that are approved for treating dementia. One group is the cholinesterase inhibitors. These medications raise the level of a chemical called acetylcholine in the brain and peripheral nervous system. These medications are certainly not miracle drugs and at best they seem to slow the progression of memory loss and do not really restore previous brain function.

The other medication is called memantine. It works by targeting the glutamate receptor in the brain. Just as with the cholinesterase inhibitors, the effects are not huge and the end result only slows the memory loss.

Both of these medications are generic, and it is reasonable to try them and see how someone responds to them.

One last medication to mention is called lecanemab. It is an IV infusion that targets amyloid, a kind of protein that develops in the brain of people with Alzheimer’s dementia. The medication seems to work quite well at clearing amyloid from patient’s brains. This medication is very expensive ($26,500 per year)and it has been linked to an increase in strokes. In the studies, dementia symptoms were only slowed by about 30 percent compared with a placebo.

There are no other medications currently approved to treat dementia.

Non-medication Therapies

There are several things that people can do to help slow the progression of dementia. These can be helpful for people who have a strong family history of dementia and want to prevent its onset.

Cardiovascular exercise is very important. Doctors mention exercise in relation to nearly every chronic illness because it has been shown to work. In the case of dementia, people who exercise regularly have about 30 percent decreased risk of developing the disease. Regular exercise seems to slow the progression of dementia.4

Doing puzzles that require mental activity, like Sudoku or crossword puzzles seems to help slow the progression of memory loss and may also reduce the chance of developing dementia.

Lastly, it is helpful to learn something new. People who learn a new skill or focus on learning a new language help their memories quite a bit. A study compared older people who learned a new skill with people who went to social events.

The point seems to be that our brains need to be pushed to create new pathways or they will tend to break down.5

Caring For Someone with Dementia

Caring for someone with dementia is challenging in a number of ways. It is often difficult to know how much independence to allow the person. There have been many books written on this subject, but there are a few things that are worth mentioning.

It is important to avoid dangerous things. The two most dangerous things for someone with faulty memory are driving and cooking. Both of these seem commonplace, and the person may seem to be doing fine, but they can become a problem very quickly.

The danger of driving a car or a buggy is twofold. First, some people freeze at certain points, not remembering how to do a particular skill. This can be a problem, not only for them but also for others on the road.

Second, older people can start off on short journeys to a local store or restaurant and end up getting lost. I have had patients who ended up driving around for hours trying to find their way home when they got confused driving to town.

Cooking, of course, really comes down to a question of remembering to set timers and take things off the stove or out of the oven at the appropriate time.

Many times, people who have dementia do not realize how much their abilities have slipped and resist the idea that they need to give up the car keys. Maybe it simply comes down to a loss of independence, but it is hard to face the fact that you are no longer safe behind the wheel.

Try to keep things the same within the room and the home. Even small changes in room arrangement can be enough to upset the situation. Taking someone out of their home – for instance, admitting them to the hospital often makes things a lot worse. Suddenly, confusion that only seemed mild before is now extremely high.

If there is a fruit of the spirit that is key for dealing with someone with dementia, it is patience. None of us has as much patience as we need, as dementia spreads that patience awfully thin.

People with dementia often act like children on a long trip. They ask over and over when they are going home. They wonder where dead relatives are or why the children aren’t home yet. No amount of explanation helps, because only a minute or two after they ask the question, they have forgotten the answer and are asking again.

Their skills often wax and wane. One day, they can button their shirt, and the next day, that skill seems to have flown out the window. It is easy to believe that they aren’t “trying hard” and that they could do more if they would only make the effort.

Unfortunately, the fact that someone with dementia could do something yesterday doesn’t mean that they can remember how to do it today. Getting upset with them only makes these things worse as it adds anxiety to a person who already lacks the memory of how to do a skill.

As much as possible, answer the person gently even if it is the fifty-third time that you have answered the same question. Use distractions as well. If there is an activity that they can still do, such as sewing or jigsaw puzzles (even children’s puzzles with really big pieces), get them to do it. Late in the illness, letting them look at books with pretty pictures or sometimes even giving them a baby doll to hold can help settle them and distract them from their anxieties of the moment.

Get Others to Help

It is easy to become frustrated. Trying to provide all of the care needed by yourself is not a long-term solution. Dementia care is a marathon and not a sprint. Many people live for years after the diagnosis, and even though their physical body remains relatively strong, they require more and more care.

One of the blessings of having family connections and church communities is that we have people who are available to provide assistance.

Having family members or friends step in to give you some respite is key to not becoming seriously burned out or even angry with someone that you care about. It is best to take some time away periodically before you are mentally depleted. You may think you are doing fairly well, but all of us have a tendency to get weary in well doing if we never get a break.

Conclusion

I wish there were more medical solutions for dementia. Perhaps more will come later. For now, medications are quite limited.

The key is to put the fruit of the Spirit into practice. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (Galatians 5:22-23).

Even on the most frustrating days, people who are dealing with severe memory loss need love, gentleness, and patience from their family members. It is only through the Holy Spirit’s power that we can provide the care that is needed for someone whose body is strong, but who no longer even recognizes you.
