“É tão difícil”, disse o homem sentado à minha frente. “Somos casados há quase cinquenta anos, mas eu nunca esperava algo assim.”

“O que está acontecendo?” perguntei a Al, com simpatia.

“É a Lisa”, ele disse. “Você sabe que a memória dela vem falhando há algum tempo. Bem, fomos ao neurologista como você nos disse, e eles pediram uma série de exames e uma espécie de tomografia cerebral. Aí, disseram a ela que tinha demência.”

“Achei que era isso que estava acontecendo”, respondi.

“Eu sei que você nos falou isso”, disse Al. “Então, há momentos em que ela não me reconhece. Ela me olha com um ar vazio como se estivesse se perguntando que estranho enlouquecido entrou na casa dela.”

“Deve ser difícil”, disse eu.

“A única coisa que eu descobri que a traz de volta para si é sair e chamá-la no celular. Eu digo para ela sair para a garagem, que tenho algo para mostrar. De algum modo, quando faço isso, isso a traz de volta ao presente e a faz saber quem eu sou – por um tempo, pelo menos.”

Passamos a falar de outras coisas, mas eu podia ver que o coração de Al estava partido. Sua esposa de 48 anos parecia a mesma de sempre por fora e, ainda assim, era uma pessoa completamente diferente.

Gostaria de explorar alguns dos desafios ao lidar com a demência.

Dementia in the Bible

Ecclesiastes 12:1-7 gives a somewhat dismal view of the aging process. “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them; While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low; Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

Neste trecho, a descrição poética parece falar da perda dos dentes, perda de audição, marcha instável e fragilidade geral. É difícil dizer se alguma dessas imagens se refere à perda de memória. O que é certo é que a passagem começa com um comando: “Remember!”

Este não é o único lugar nas Escrituras onde os seres humanos são instruídos a lembrar. Repetidamente, somos ordenados a lembrar de Deus. Devemos certificar‑nos de instruir nossos filhos sobre Ele. “And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (Deuteronomy 6:7).

Chegará um momento em que talvez não sejamos mais capazes de lembrar. A coisa mais importante – mesmo quando pensamos sobre o tema da demência – é que nos lembremos Aquele que nos fez e o sigamos de todo o coração.

What Dementia is

Demência é qualquer doença que causa perda de memória, raciocínio e funcionamento social. A maioria das pessoas pensa principalmente na perda de memória. Imagino que isso aconteça porque, no início da doença, outras pessoas notam coisas como dificuldade em encontrar palavras e repetição frequente de histórias.

O funcionamento social costuma ser mantido até estágios avançados da doença. Se você perguntar a alguém com demência leve se sabe a data de hoje, provavelmente ouvirá: “Ah, sabe, parei de prestar atenção a coisas assim quando me aposentei.”

A causa mais comum de demência é a demência de Alzheimer – pelo menos 70% das pessoas com perda progressiva de memória têm demência de Alzheimer. O Alzheimer parece estar relacionado a proteínas chamadas amiloide, que são depositadas no cérebro e impedem as células nervosas de se comunicarem entre si.

Outras causas são a demência vascular, em que obstruções nos vasos sanguíneos do cérebro causam a morte de células nervosas. A demência por corpos de Lewy é um tipo de perda de memória associada à Doença de Parkinson. Aproximadamente oitenta por cento das pessoas com Parkinson desenvolverão eventualmente demência.

Diagnosing Dementia

Se familiares suspeitam que alguém está desenvolvendo perda de memória, o melhor é levá‑lo ao médico de clínica geral para uma avaliação. Além de realizar um exame físico, o médico normalmente pede que o paciente desenhe um relógio e faça um mini exame do estado mental, que pede ao paciente para responder muitas perguntas simples e fazer algumas recordações de curto prazo.

Serão feitos exames de sangue, incluindo função da tiróide e nível de vitamina B12. Também pode ser solicitada uma tomografia cerebral ou um ultrassom das artérias do pescoço.

O objetivo é identificar áreas que podem ser tratadas e cuidar delas.

Eliminate Medications

Muitos medicamentos aumentam o risco de problemas de memória. À medida que as pessoas envelhecem, evitar esses medicamentos é útil para prevenir o desenvolvimento da demência.

Os medicamentos anticolinérgicos são provavelmente os maiores culpados que encontro. Os mais comuns desses medicamentos são anti‑histamínicos mais antigos como difenidramina (usada como auxílio para dormir ou comprimido para alergia) e doxilamina (usada como auxílio para dormir). Em um estudo, pacientes que tomaram um medicamento anticolinérgico pelo equivalente a três anos tiveram risco significativamente maior de demência do que pacientes que tomaram esses tipos de medicamentos por menos de três meses.1 Antidepressivos mais antigos também podem entrar nessa categoria.

Medicamentos para ansiedade, chamados benzodiazepínicos, também têm sido associados a problemas de memória. Estudos indicam que pacientes que tomam esses medicamentos têm maior risco de desenvolver demência do que pacientes que não os tomam.2

Medicamentos para convulsões podem também prejudicar a capacidade de raciocinar. Ter um transtorno convulsivo parece aumentar o risco de demência, mas certos medicamentos mais antigos, como valproato e gabapentina, parecem dificultar o pensamento claro em pessoas idosas, sendo aconselhável, quando possível, migrar para medicamentos antiepilépticos de menor risco em pacientes mais velhos.

Há momentos em que alguém precisa tomar medicação, mas, à medida que os pacientes envelhecem, é importante pensar nos riscos desses medicamentos. Existe uma lista de medicamentos que é mais prudente evitar em pacientes com mais de 65 anos, chamada Lista de Beers. Substituir por medicamentos semelhantes com menos efeitos colaterais ou usar doses menores é recomendado.3

Medical Treatments

A primeira regra ao lidar com demência é garantir que todos os aspectos metabólicos estejam o melhor controlados possível. Assim, se alguém tem diabetes, é melhor certificar‑se de que o açúcar esteja bem controlado. Se alguém tem pressão alta, assegure‑se de que ela esteja bem regulada (isso é particularmente verdadeiro se a pessoa tem demência vascular).

Existem várias classes de medicamentos aprovadas para tratar a demência. Um grupo é o dos inibidores da colinesterase. Esses medicamentos aumentam o nível de uma substância chamada acetilcolina no cérebro e no sistema nervoso periférico. Esses medicamentos certamente não são milagrosos e, no melhor dos casos, parecem retardar a progressão da perda de memória, não restaurando realmente a função cerebral anterior.

O outro medicamento chama‑se memantina. Age ao direcionar o receptor do glutamato no cérebro. Assim como os inibidores da colinesterase, os efeitos não são grandes e o resultado final apenas desacelera a perda de memória.

Ambos os medicamentos são genéricos, e é razoável experimentá‑los para ver como alguém responde.

Um último medicamento a mencionar chama‑se lecanemabe. É uma infusão intravenosa que tem como alvo a amiloide, um tipo de proteína que se desenvolve no cérebro de pessoas com demência de Alzheimer. O medicamento parece funcionar bastante bem para limpar a amiloide do cérebro dos pacientes. Esse medicamento é muito caro (US$26.500 por ano) e foi associado a um aumento de acidentes vasculares cerebrais. Nos estudos, os sintomas da demência foram retardados em cerca de 30% em comparação com placebo.

Não existem outros medicamentos atualmente aprovados para tratar a demência.

Non-medication Therapies

Existem várias coisas que as pessoas podem fazer para ajudar a retardar a progressão da demência. Isso pode ser útil para pessoas com forte histórico familiar de demência que desejam prevenir seu aparecimento.

Exercício cardiovascular é muito importante. Os médicos mencionam exercício em relação a quase todas as doenças crônicas porque se demonstrou que funciona. No caso da demência, pessoas que se exercitam regularmente têm cerca de 30% de redução no risco de desenvolver a doença. Exercício regular parece retardar a progressão da demência.4

Fazer quebra‑cabeças que exigem atividade mental, como Sudoku ou palavras cruzadas, parece ajudar a retardar a progressão da perda de memória e pode também reduzir a chance de desenvolver demência.

Por fim, é útil aprender algo novo. Pessoas que aprendem uma nova habilidade ou se dedicam a aprender uma nova língua ajudam bastante sua memória. Um estudo comparou idosos que aprenderam uma nova habilidade com pessoas que participaram de eventos sociais.

O ponto parece ser que nossos cérebros precisam ser desafiados a criar novas vias, ou tenderão a se degradar.5

Caring For Someone with Dementia

Cuidar de alguém com demência é desafiador por várias razões. Muitas vezes é difícil saber quanta independência permitir à pessoa. Foram escritos muitos livros sobre esse assunto, mas há algumas coisas que valem a pena mencionar.

É importante evitar situações perigosas. As duas coisas mais perigosas para alguém com memória deficitária são dirigir e cozinhar. Ambas parecem corriqueiras, e a pessoa pode aparentar estar bem, mas podem se tornar um problema muito rapidamente.

O perigo de dirigir um carro ou um veículo é duplo. Primeiro, algumas pessoas travam em certos pontos, não lembrando como executar uma habilidade específica. Isso pode ser um problema não apenas para elas, mas também para outras pessoas na via.

Segundo, pessoas mais velhas podem partir em pequenas viagens até uma loja ou restaurante e acabar perdendo‑se. Tive pacientes que passaram horas dirigindo tentando encontrar o caminho de volta para casa quando ficaram confusos ao dirigir até a cidade.

Cozinhar, claro, resume‑se a lembrar de acertar timers e tirar coisas do fogão ou do forno no momento apropriado.

Muitas vezes, pessoas com demência não percebem o quanto suas habilidades diminuíram e resistem à ideia de entregar as chaves do carro. Talvez isso se resuma simplesmente à perda de independência, mas é difícil encarar o fato de que você já não é mais seguro ao volante.

Tente manter as coisas iguais no quarto e na casa. Mesmo pequenas mudanças na disposição dos móveis podem ser suficientes para perturbar a situação. Tirar alguém de sua casa – por exemplo, interná‑lo no hospital – frequentemente piora muito as coisas. De repente, uma confusão que antes parecia leve fica extremamente intensa.

Se há um fruto do Espírito que é fundamental para lidar com alguém com demência, é a paciência. Nenhum de nós tem tanta paciência quanto precisa; à medida que a demência se espalha, essa paciência se esgota rapidamente.

Pessoas com demência muitas vezes agem como crianças numa longa viagem. Perguntam repetidamente quando vão para casa. Perguntam onde estão parentes mortos ou por que as crianças ainda não chegaram. Nenhuma quantidade de explicação ajuda, porque apenas um minuto ou dois depois de fazerem a pergunta, já esqueceram a resposta e a fazem novamente.

As habilidades delas frequentemente variam. Um dia conseguem abotoar a camisa e, no dia seguinte, essa habilidade parece ter desaparecido. É fácil achar que elas não estão “se esforçando” e que poderiam fazer mais se apenas quisessem.

Infelizmente, o fato de alguém com demência ter conseguido fazer algo ontem não significa que lembrará como fazê‑lo hoje. Irritar‑se com elas só piora as coisas, pois adiciona ansiedade a uma pessoa que já não lembra como realizar determinada habilidade.

Na medida do possível, responda à pessoa com suavidade mesmo que seja a quinquagésima terceira vez que você responde à mesma pergunta. Use também distrações. Se houver uma atividade que ainda possam realizar, como costurar ou montar quebra‑cabeças (até mesmo quebra‑cabeças infantis com peças bem grandes), convide‑as a fazê‑la. Em estágios finais da doença, deixá‑las folhear livros com imagens bonitas ou, às vezes, dar‑lhes uma boneca para segurar pode acalmá‑las e distraí‑las de suas ansiedades do momento.

Get Others to Help

É fácil ficar frustrado. Tentar prover todo o cuidado sozinho não é uma solução a longo prazo. O cuidado com demência é uma maratona, não um sprint. Muitas pessoas vivem por anos após o diagnóstico e, mesmo que o corpo físico permaneça relativamente forte, exigem cada vez mais cuidados.

Uma das bênçãos de ter conexões familiares e comunidades eclesiais é que temos pessoas disponíveis para oferecer assistência.

Ter familiares ou amigos que ajudem para lhe dar algum descanso é fundamental para não ficar seriamente esgotado ou até com raiva de alguém de quem você cuida. É melhor tirar um tempo para si periodicamente antes de ficar mentalmente exaurido. Você pode achar que está se saindo bem, mas todos nós tendemos a nos cansar no bem que fazemos se nunca descansarmos.

Conclusion

Gostaria que houvesse mais soluções médicas para a demência. Talvez surjam mais adiante. Por enquanto, os medicamentos são bastante limitados.

A chave é praticar o fruto do Espírito. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (Galatians 5:22-23).

Mesmo nos dias mais frustrantes, pessoas que enfrentam perda severa de memória precisam de amor, gentileza e paciência de seus familiares. Só pelo poder do Espírito Santo podemos fornecer o cuidado necessário a alguém cujo corpo é forte, mas que já nem mesmo o reconhece.

The glory of the spring, how sweet!
The newborn life, how glad!
What joy the happy earth to greet
In new, bright raiment clad!

Divine Redeemer, Thee I bless;
I greet Thy going forth;
I love Thee in the loveliness
Of Thy renewed earth.

But O these wonders of Thy grace,
These nobler works of Thine,
These marvels sweeter far to trace,
These new births more divine:

This new-born glow of faith so strong,
This bloom of love so fair,
This new-born ecstasy of song,
And fragrancy of prayer!

Creator Spirit, work in me
These wonders sweet of Thine;
Divine Redeemer, graciously
Renew this heart of mine.

Still, let new life and strength upspring,
Still, let new joy be given;
And grant the glad new song to ring
Through the new earth and Heaven.

Morals have to do with right and wrong behavior. Purity is being free from moral fault or guilt, marked by chastity, which is personal integrity. Purity contains nothing that does not properly belong there. As the title suggests, this article will be about doing right and being free from moral fault and guilt, living a life of integrity, and keeping our inside and outside free of anything that doesn’t properly belong.

Notice what scripture says about being pure. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Being morally pure will not happen without strong determination and discipline. It has always been this way, but even more so today with the rise of technology and the availability of evil at our fingertips.

Sexual sins are not foreign to the church. In fact, they are not foreign to any people of any race. We cannot relax and let down our guard and suppose that our children will be safe from the evils of society and our humanity. We must show by example and teach our children and youth if we expect them to stay clean in this corrupt society. We cannot assume that if a person dresses a certain way, all is well on the inside. The story is not told fully by the outside. The Pharisees made the outside look good, while the inside was full of corruption. Jesus said, “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). We too should give primary attention to heart issues. When the heart is clean, then the outside will be able to be cleansed also.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Internal darkness will always destroy fellowship and kill relationships—every time.

This is intended to be a message of hope, not discouragement. If you have a hidden dark spot, confess it and get rid of it. You can be free! It is possible to be free from Satan's clutches and live an open, transparent life with joy in your soul. You don't need to go through life trying to hide the darkness of evil. Jesus wants to forgive and heal.

Satan is cruel. In John 10:10, Jesus said, “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” all godly relationships. His interest is to break up your home, destroy your respect, and send you to hell. All the while, he is luring you through the lust of your flesh, with his sword drawn to bind and kill you.

Moral sin is so shameful and hard to admit. The natural thing is to try to hide when we do wrong. Children who learn to hide wrongdoing early in life naturally develop into youth who hide things from parents, schoolteachers, and ministers. This person will need to learn to be open and transparent, or the time will come when they will be hiding things from their companion. Hiding results is a double life and leads to more bondage and broken relationships. People who have closed doors in some corners of their lives will be possessive of their phones and unwilling to share their passwords with a trusted partner. It seems we easily forget how futile it is to hide from God. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” How can we be so naive and foolish to think we can hide anything from God? Or take it a step further: Why would we want to hide something from Him? Numbers 32:23 is still very true, saying, “Be sure your sin will find you out.” God loves you too much to let you keep hiding what needs to be brought out and forgiven.

Sexual sins are also extremely deceptive. It usually happens the way James described it in chapter one. We are enticed, drawn away, pulled like a magnet off-center, feel a surge of desire, make sure no one is looking, and our tracks are covered, step closer to the forbidden, feel more desire, and begin very quickly to lose reasoning and sound thinking, not able to calculate consequences much like an intoxicated person, then James 1:15 happens: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Verse 16 says, “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James would tell us not to lust after what isn't ours, not even a hint. The Bible tells us to flee three things. One of these is fornication, which can be broadened to all sexual sins. Don't dabble with it; don't take a second look; get away from it! Replace those thoughts with upbuilding thoughts of God and His way. Sing an old hymn; thankfully we can't think of two things at once. Whatever it takes, flee from that lustful desire. It will take you farther than you want to go and cost more than you want to pay. Run the tape to the end and ask yourself, if I follow what I am being tempted for, will I have what I want? Satan always promises pleasure, but then delivers pain. Remember, Satan has never invented a pleasure; he only takes what God made to be pure and good, perverts it, and offers it back in its perverted form. Remember, Satan's sword is drawn to kill at this point. Flee evil desires!

Don’t follow your lust. Pornography is extremely addictive and has ensnared many a person. Promise Keepers said 65% of men in their survey were addicted. Porn addiction is like alcohol or drugs. They tell us that the brain is calling for endorphins to be poured into it, whether from addiction to alcohol, drugs, or porn. I emphasize again that the men and women who make it to victory will be those who, like Daniel of old, purpose in their hearts, not to defile themselves.

This subject is also for our sisters, and a few questions seem appropriate. What inside your life is neatly tucked away and hidden? Have life's disappointments caused an emptiness that makes taking an 'emotional Tylenol' make you feel better for a short while? Is your emotional connection secure where God has planned it to be?

Young girls should be taught to develop a healthy reserve with men. Not with a haughty attitude and never a smile, but also not too free in relating to young men. Our society is geared exactly the opposite, and from kindergarten on, boys and girls are being teased about special friendships. As a result, children grow up with little to no reserve. Socializing in messaging between genders should be avoided outside of family relationships. This will develop a habit in youth that will one day need to be broken if they expect to live an open, transparent life with a spouse. Think of it this way: would you want your spouse to socialize with the opposite gender on social media?

Sisters, be careful what books you read. Romance novels deaden the desire for the Word of God and give unrealistic expectations of married life. These books give the idea that the right man somewhere would be your key to fulfillment and happiness in life. Only Jesus can fill the hole that sin has brought to every human being today. No man or woman will ever be able to give the security and tranquility of the soul that we all want so badly. This hurt in the heart will never be quenched by Band-Aids or pain relievers. They help only for a moment, and when they wear off, the cry of the heart is even louder. Unwholesome books deaden a taste for the things of God, and instead create a craving for junk food and pain relievers.

Another concern to the sisters is the amount of time you spend online. There is no end to feeding the craving for finery, uniqueness, charm, and beauty. Don't let these things be the drive of your life as they will never cry out 'enough' and will do nothing to satisfy the soul or point your children in the right direction. Consider the amount of time you spend hosting parties. Over the years, I have seen names come and go of business opportunities and products that one must have. But alas, in a few years, we cannot even remember those names and all the while the children were growing and by now are adults. Consider the real needs in your life and your responsibilities, and then decide which will bring eternal investments. Women with children need to limit hobbies they so much enjoy because, at this moment, they are blessed with children who have never-dying souls and time with them is an eternal investment. Remember that your husband and children are far more worthy of your time than spending hours at another party.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” It takes humility and brokenness to acknowledge our needs, but brokenness is the key to victory. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. One of the most comprehensive definitions of grace is unmerited divine assistance given to humans for regeneration and sanctification. Regeneration is 'redeeming grace,' and sanctification is 'transforming grace.' The truth of this is that God gives 'transforming grace' to the humble. This grace changes us from the inside out making us holy. This aspect of grace must be desired and sought after as much as redeeming grace was when God saved us. This is probably the single most important step in overcoming addictions of any kind. Be humble enough to make it a daily prayer to God for His transforming grace. Jesus taught in Matthew 23:26, where He said, "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Examine your thoughts, actions, temptations, the things you struggle with, anger, lust, pride, bitterness, etc. Are you as spiritual as you portray yourself to be on the outside? Strip the veneer and admit the need for help.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. We are so foolish to think we can hide evil. We can hide for a while, but someday our actions will stand naked before an all-knowing God. Why would we try to hide something now? Those hidden things can be sent before to judgment, and a guilt-free life can be a reality today. Be transparent; it must be a working goal.

Tell yourself the truth. When you are tempted, consider the end of your lustful desire. Will you get what you want? Will this craving be satisfied, or will it only crave more? If you saw your brother doing what you are going after, how would it look? How will it look thirty years down the road if you follow your evil desire? Will it bring joy or sorrow? Will it be a help to someone, or will someone else be scared? Tell yourself the truth before you become intoxicated and unable to make rational judgments.

Teach your eyes to bounce. You can't help what you look at the first time, but you can control what you look at twice. Make it a practice till it becomes a habit to turn your eyes in a different direction whenever you see a sight that leads to impure thoughts.

Teaching our children. This should be heavy on our hearts from early childhood. If we don’t teach our children that God made us in the image of Himself, which needs to be kept pure, someone else will teach them to be secretive and make them feel impure. Stay close to your children and teach them as they mature.

Keep your emotions. This is a safety in our corrupt society. The further you get from this, the more vulnerable you will be to corruption. Keep your spouse first in life, the one you share with and are tied to emotionally.

Flee lust and fornication. Run from it! These cravings are addictions that must be broken. Remember, what you feed grows, and what you starve dies. These addictions can be broken, but you will need to feed the relationships that God has given and starve the hurtful ones.

God has made us in a way that when we love the things He loves, our heart still has room to love more. No matter how many children, grandchildren, or godly friends we have, our hearts still have room to love more. But the moment we start to love what God has forbidden, it begins to replace and destroy all other love, filling our hearts with emptiness, pain, and loneliness, which leads to a bitter end.

Many a man has come to his senses and seen the utter foolishness of the path he took. Some tried to hide impure conduct and were successful until late in life. Others kept it hidden till after they were gone. A question to ponder, Is it worth it? Of course, the answer is a resounding NO!

How wonderful to live an open life free of guilt and have peace with God and the assurance of sins forgiven, so that one day we will be taken out of this evil world and ushered into the presence of our Holy God.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

Moralisches Verhalten betrifft richtiges und falsches Handeln. Reinheit bedeutet frei von moralischem Fehler oder Schuld zu sein, gekennzeichnet durch Keuschheit, was persönliche Integrität ist. Reinheit enthält nichts, was dort nicht hingehört. Wie der Titel andeutet, wird es in diesem Artikel um richtiges Handeln und das Frei-Sein von moralischem Fehler und Schuld gehen, ein Leben in Integrität zu führen und unser Inneres und Äußeres frei von allem zu halten, was dort nicht hingehört.

Beachte, was die Schrift über Reinheit sagt. “Blessed are the pure in heart” (Matthew 5:8). “That ye may approve things that are excellent; that ye may be sincere (pure) and without offense till the day of Christ” (Philippians 1:10). “Think on things that are pure” (Philippians 4:8). “Keep thyself pure” (1Timothy 5:22). Revelation 19 says “The pure in heart shall see God.” Psalm 24:3-4 asks “Who shall see God?” The answer is “he that hath clean hands and a pure heart.” In other words, it is the people who are clean inside and out who will see God and enter His presence.

Moralisch rein zu sein wird nicht ohne starken Willen und Disziplin geschehen. Es war schon immer so, doch heute noch mehr mit dem Aufstieg der Technologie und der Verfügbarkeit des Bösen in unseren Fingerspitzen.

Sexuelle Sünden sind der Kirche nicht fremd. Tatsächlich sind sie keinem Volk irgendwelcher Rasse fremd. Wir können uns nicht entspannen und unsere Wachsamkeit verlieren und annehmen, dass unsere Kinder vor den Übeln der Gesellschaft und unserer Menschlichkeit sicher sein werden. Wir müssen durch Beispiel vorangehen und unsere Kinder und Jugendlichen lehren, wenn wir erwarten, dass sie in dieser verdorbenen Gesellschaft rein bleiben. Wir dürfen nicht davon ausgehen, dass, wenn sich jemand auf eine bestimmte Weise kleidet, auch alles innerlich in Ordnung ist. Die Geschichte wird nicht vollständig durch das Äußere erzählt. Die Pharisäer ließen das Äußere gut aussehen, während das Innere voller Verderbnis war. Jesus sagte: “Cleanse first the inside of the cup and platter that the outside may be clean also” (Matthew 23:26). Auch wir sollten primär Herzangelegenheiten Aufmerksamkeit schenken. Wenn das Herz rein ist, dann kann auch das Äußere gereinigt werden.

I John 1:6 says, “if we say that we have fellowship with Him and walk in darkness (light on the outside and darkness on the inside), we lie and do not practice the truth.” Innerliche Dunkelheit wird immer die Gemeinschaft zerstören und Beziehungen töten—jedes Mal.

Dies soll eine Botschaft der Hoffnung sein, nicht der Entmutigung. Wenn du einen versteckten dunklen Punkt hast, bekenne ihn und entferne ihn. Du kannst frei sein! Es ist möglich, frei von Satans Klauen zu sein und ein offenes, transparentes Leben mit Freude in deiner Seele zu führen. Du musst dein Leben nicht damit verbringen, die Dunkelheit des Bösen zu verbergen. Jesus will vergeben und heilen.

Satan ist grausam. In John 10:10 sagte Jesus: “the devil wants to steal, kill, and destroy. He wants to steal your purity, kill your character, and destroy” alle gottesfürchtigen Beziehungen. Sein Interesse ist es, dein Heim auseinanderzubringen, deinen Respekt zu zerstören und dich zur Hölle zu schicken. Unterdessen lockt er dich durch die Begierde deines Fleisches, mit seinem gezückten Schwert, um dich zu binden und zu töten.

Moralische Sünde ist so beschämend und schwer zuzugeben. Das Natürliche ist zu versuchen, sich zu verstecken, wenn wir Unrecht tun. Kinder, die früh im Leben lernen, Fehlverhalten zu verbergen, entwickeln sich natürlicherweise zu Jugendlichen, die Dinge vor Eltern, Lehrern und Predigern verbergen. Diese Person wird lernen müssen, offen und transparent zu sein, sonst wird die Zeit kommen, in der sie Dinge vor ihrem Lebensgefährten verbergen wird. Verbergen führt zu einem Doppelleben und führt zu mehr Knechtschaft und zerbrochenen Beziehungen. Menschen, die in manchen Bereichen ihres Lebens geschlossene Türen haben, werden besitzergreifend mit ihren Handys sein und nicht bereit, ihre Passwörter mit einem vertrauten Partner zu teilen. Es scheint, wir vergessen leicht, wie aussichtslos es ist, sich vor Gott zu verbergen. Hebrews 4:13 says, “Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom (we will give account to).” Wie können wir so naiv und töricht sein zu denken, wir könnten Gott etwas verbergen? Oder noch weiter: Warum sollten wir überhaupt etwas vor Ihm verbergen wollen? Numbers 32:23 ist weiterhin sehr wahr und sagt: “Be sure your sin will find you out.” Gott liebt dich zu sehr, um dir zu erlauben, weiterhin zu verbergen, was hervorgebracht und vergeben werden muss.

Sexuelle Sünden sind außerdem extrem täuschend. Meist geschieht es so, wie James es in Kapitel eins beschrieb. Wir werden verlockt, weggezogen, wie ein Magnet aus der Mitte gezogen, fühlen einen Ansturm der Begierde, stellen sicher, dass niemand zusieht, decken unsere Spuren, treten näher an das Verbotene, fühlen mehr Verlangen und beginnen sehr schnell, die Vernunft und gesundes Denken zu verlieren, unfähig, die Konsequenzen zu berechnen, ähnlich einem Betrunkenen, dann tritt James 1:15 ein: “Then when lust hath conceived, it bringeth forth sin: and sin, when it is finished, bringeth forth death” Vers 16 sagt: “Do not (be deceived) my beloved brethren.”

James würde uns sagen, nicht nach dem zu begehren, was nicht unser ist, nicht einmal eine Andeutung davon. Die Bibel sagt uns, vor drei Dingen zu fliehen. Eines davon ist Unzucht, was auf alle sexuellen Sünden erweitert werden kann. Spiel nicht damit; wirf ihm keinen zweiten Blick zu; geh weg davon! Ersetze diese Gedanken durch aufbauende Gedanken über Gott und seinen Weg. Sing ein altes Lied; glücklicherweise können wir nicht an zwei Dinge gleichzeitig denken. Was immer nötig ist, fliehe vor dieser lüsternen Begierde. Sie wird dich weiter bringen, als du gehen willst, und mehr kosten, als du bezahlen willst. Spiele das Band bis zum Ende ab und frage dich, wenn ich der Versuchung folge, werde ich bekommen, was ich will? Satan verspricht immer Vergnügen, liefert dann aber Schmerz. Denk daran, Satan hat noch nie ein Vergnügen erfunden; er nimmt nur, was Gott rein und gut geschaffen hat, pervertiert es und bietet es in seiner pervertierten Form an. Denk daran, Satans Schwert ist in diesem Moment gezückt, um zu töten. Fliehe böse Begierden!

Folge nicht deiner Lust. Pornografie ist extrem süchtig machend und hat viele Menschen gefangen. Promise Keepers sagten, 65% der Männer in ihrer Umfrage seien abhängig. Pornosucht ist wie Alkohol- oder Drogenabhängigkeit. Man sagt uns, dass das Gehirn Endorphine fordert, ob durch Sucht nach Alkohol, Drogen oder Pornos. Ich betone erneut, dass die Männer und Frauen, die den Sieg erreichen, diejenigen sein werden, die, wie Daniel früher, in ihrem Herzen Vorsatz fassen, sich nicht zu verunreinigen.

Dieses Thema richtet sich auch an unsere Schwestern, und einige Fragen scheinen angebracht. Was in deinem Leben ist ordentlich verstaut und verborgen? Haben Enttäuschungen des Lebens eine Leere verursacht, die dich dazu bringt, ein „emotionales Tylenol“ zu nehmen, das dich für kurze Zeit besser fühlen lässt? Ist deine emotionale Bindung dort gesichert, wo Gott sie vorgesehen hat?

Junge Mädchen sollten gelehrt werden, mit Männern eine gesunde Zurückhaltung zu entwickeln. Nicht mit einer hochmütigen Haltung und nie einem Lächeln, aber auch nicht zu frei im Umgang mit jungen Männern. Unsere Gesellschaft ist genau gegensätzlich ausgerichtet, und vom Kindergarten an werden Jungen und Mädchen wegen besonderer Freundschaften gehänselt. Infolgedessen wachsen Kinder mit wenig bis keiner Zurückhaltung auf. Soziales Kontaktieren per Nachrichten zwischen den Geschlechtern sollte außerhalb familiärer Beziehungen vermieden werden. Dies wird bei Jugendlichen eine Gewohnheit entwickeln, die eines Tages gebrochen werden muss, wenn sie erwarten, ein offenes, transparentes Leben mit einem Ehepartner zu führen. Denk so: Würdest du wollen, dass dein Ehepartner auf sozialen Medien mit dem anderen Geschlecht sozialisiert?

Schwestern, seid vorsichtig, welche Bücher ihr lest. Liebesromane betäuben das Verlangen nach dem Wort Gottes und geben unrealistische Erwartungen an das Eheleben. Diese Bücher vermitteln die Idee, dass der richtige Mann irgendwo der Schlüssel zu Erfüllung und Glück im Leben wäre. Nur Jesus kann das Loch füllen, das die Sünde heute jedem Menschen gebracht hat. Kein Mann und keine Frau wird jemals die Sicherheit und die Seelenruhe geben können, die wir uns so sehr wünschen. Dieser Schmerz im Herzen wird niemals durch Pflaster oder Schmerzmittel gelöscht. Sie helfen nur einen Moment, und wenn sie nachlassen, ist der Ruf des Herzens noch lauter. Unheilsame Bücher betäuben den Geschmack für die Dinge Gottes und schaffen stattdessen ein Verlangen nach Junkfood und Schmerzmitteln.

Eine weitere Sorge für die Schwestern ist die Zeit, die ihr online verbringt. Es gibt kein Ende, die Gier nach Zierlichkeit, Einzigartigkeit, Charm und Schönheit zu füttern. Lass diese Dinge nicht der Antrieb deines Lebens sein, denn sie werden niemals „genug“ rufen und nichts tun, um die Seele zu befriedigen oder deine Kinder in die richtige Richtung zu weisen. Überlege, wie viel Zeit du für das Ausrichten von Partys aufwendest. Im Laufe der Jahre habe ich Namen gesehen kommen und gehen von Geschäftsmöglichkeiten und Produkten, die man unbedingt haben musste. Aber leider können wir in ein paar Jahren diese Namen nicht einmal mehr erinnern, und währenddessen wuchsen die Kinder und sind inzwischen Erwachsene. Überlege die wirklichen Bedürfnisse in deinem Leben und deine Verantwortlichkeiten und entscheide dann, welches ewige Investitionen bringen wird. Frauen mit Kindern müssen die Hobbys, die sie so sehr genießen, einschränken, weil sie in diesem Moment gesegnet sind mit Kindern, die unsterbliche Seelen haben, und Zeit mit ihnen ist eine ewige Investition. Denk daran, dass dein Mann und deine Kinder weit mehr würdig sind deiner Zeit als Stunden auf einer weiteren Party zu verbringen.

How can we live a morally pure life?

Be Humble. James 5 says, “Confess your faults one to another that ye may be healed.” Es erfordert Demut und Zerbrochenheit, unsere Bedürfnisse anzuerkennen, aber Zerbrochenheit ist der Schlüssel zum Sieg. I Peter 5:5 tells us that God gives grace to the humble. Eine der umfassendsten Definitionen von Gnade ist unverdiente göttliche Hilfe, die Menschen zur Wiedergeburt und Heiligung gegeben wird. Wiedergeburt ist 'erlösende Gnade' und Heiligung ist 'verwandelnde Gnade.' Die Wahrheit ist, dass Gott den Demütigen 'verwandelnde Gnade' gibt. Diese Gnade verändert uns von innen nach außen und macht uns heilig. Dieser Aspekt der Gnade muss ebenso begehrt und gesucht werden wie die erlösende Gnade, als Gott uns rettete. Dies ist wahrscheinlich der einzelne wichtigste Schritt, um Süchte jeder Art zu überwinden. Sei demütig genug, es zu einem täglichen Gebet an Gott um seine verwandelnde Gnade zu machen. Jesus lehrte in Matthew 23:26, wo Er sagte: "First clean the inside of the cup, so that the outside may be clean also."

Be Honest. Prüfe deine Gedanken, Handlungen, Versuchungen, die Dinge, mit denen du kämpfst, Zorn, Lust, Stolz, Bitterkeit usw. Bist du so geistlich, wie du dich äußerlich darstellst? Entferne die Fassade und gib die Notwendigkeit von Hilfe zu.

Be transparent. Romans 2:16 tells of the day when God will judge the secrets of men. Wir sind so töricht zu denken, wir könnten das Böse verbergen. Wir können eine Weile verbergen, aber eines Tages werden unsere Taten nackt vor einem allwissenden Gott stehen. Warum sollten wir jetzt versuchen, etwas zu verbergen? Diese verborgenen Dinge können vor Gericht gebracht werden, und ein schuldfreies Leben kann heute Wirklichkeit werden. Sei transparent; es muss ein praktisches Ziel sein.

Tell yourself the truth. Wenn du versucht wirst, bedenke das Ende deiner lüsternen Begierde. Wirst du bekommen, was du willst? Wird dieses Verlangen befriedigt, oder wird es nur nach mehr verlangen? Wenn du deinen Bruder so sähe, wie er das tut, wonach du gehst, wie würde es aussehen? Wie wird es in dreißig Jahren aussehen, wenn du deiner bösen Begierde folgst? Wird es Freude oder Leid bringen? Wird es jemandem helfen, oder wird jemand anders verängstigt sein? Sag dir die Wahrheit, bevor du betrunken wirst und nicht mehr rational urteilen kannst.

Teach your eyes to bounce. Du kannst nicht kontrollieren, was du beim ersten Blick ansiehst, aber du kannst kontrollieren, was du ein zweites Mal ansiehst. Mach es zur Gewohnheit, bis es eine Routine wird, deine Augen in eine andere Richtung zu wenden, wann immer du etwas siehst, das zu unreinen Gedanken führt.

Teaching our children. Dies sollte uns von frühester Kindheit an sehr am Herzen liegen. Wenn wir unseren Kindern nicht beibringen, dass Gott uns nach seinem Ebenbild geschaffen hat, das rein gehalten werden muss, wird es jemand anderes sie lehren, geheimnisvoll zu sein und sie sich unrein fühlen zu lassen. Bleib nah bei deinen Kindern und lehre sie, während sie reifen.

Keep your emotions. Dies ist ein Schutz in unserer verdorbenen Gesellschaft. Je weiter du dich davon entfernst, desto verwundbarer wirst du für Verderbnis. Halte deinen Ehepartner an erster Stelle im Leben, denjenigen, mit dem du teilst und an den du emotional gebunden bist.

Flee lust and fornication. Lauf davon! Diese Begierden sind Süchte, die gebrochen werden müssen. Denk daran, was du nährst, wächst, und was du verhungerst, stirbt. Diese Süchte können gebrochen werden, aber du wirst die Beziehungen nähren müssen, die Gott dir gegeben hat, und die schädlichen verhungern lassen.

Gott hat uns so geschaffen, dass, wenn wir die Dinge lieben, die Er liebt, unser Herz noch Raum hat, mehr zu lieben. Egal wie viele Kinder, Enkelkinder oder gottesfürchtige Freunde wir haben, unsere Herzen haben noch Raum, mehr zu lieben. Aber in dem Moment, in dem wir anfangen, das zu lieben, was Gott verboten hat, beginnt es, alle andere Liebe zu ersetzen und zu zerstören, füllt unser Herz mit Leere, Schmerz und Einsamkeit, was zu einem bitteren Ende führt.

Mancher Mann ist zur Vernunft gekommen und hat die ungeheure Torheit des Weges gesehen, den er eingeschlagen hat. Einige versuchten, unreines Verhalten zu verbergen und hatten bis ins hohe Alter damit Erfolg. Andere hielten es versteckt, bis sie tot waren. Eine Frage zum Nachdenken: War es das wert? Natürlich ist die Antwort ein lautes NEIN!

Wie wunderbar ist es, ein offenes Leben frei von Schuld zu führen und Frieden mit Gott und die Gewissheit der vergebenen Sünden zu haben, sodass eines Tages wir aus dieser bösen Welt herausgenommen und in die Gegenwart unseres heiligen Gottes eingeführt werden.

Two forces lie within my breast,
The one I love, the one I hate.
But the one I feed will dominate.

—The author’s dad

The more honestly I name
what is true about myself,
The less I need to hide and defend,
and posture and pretend.

—Dan Allender

“Get out of my shop! I don’t need people like you around me! And never come back!” My lips quivered as I looked into the dark, angry eyes of the yelling man. I blinked back the unbidden tears, realizing that once more, I had to leave this man that I loved. All night I could sense that we were coming to this, and I had tried so hard not to let it happen. With one last attempt, I feebly yelled above the tension, “Ken, we don’t want to ...” but once more, I was rudely cut off. With slumped shoulders and downcast eyes, I turned to escape the confines of his dingy, pawn shop, his ever-crescendoing voice drowning the last hope of respite.

The lingering smell of smoke and the echo of his angry voice joined the troubled thoughts of my emotionally overwrought mind, as I slowly walked up the street. “What do you think, Josh?” I asked my faithful, quiet friend.

“I don’t know, " he responded, and we fell back into silent anguish at the outcome of our supposed Bible study, grasping for an explanation for the terrible response. What could we have done differently? Why could he not accept the truth? What lay behind those flashing eyes, and what memories are stored beneath his ever-crowning beanie?

Ken was born on a country farm in the rolling hills of Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, a splendid place for a curious and adventurous little boy to live.

When Ken was four years old, his parents separated. He had heard them fighting a lot, but he didn’t know that it was possible for Mom and Dad to separate. It crushed his heart and confused his innocent soul. He did not know how to handle the stress and change that was tossed on his peaceful life.

The terror and confusion of his mom hurriedly packing their belongings, loading him and his siblings in the car, and driving away are still riveted in his mind. It made no sense! Why couldn’t they just go home? In his musty bedroom at their little, dingy apartment, he lay staring at the moldy ceiling, wondering endlessly what had gone so wrong.

Ken soon adjusted to his new home in the city of Pottsville with only cars, people, and sidewalks instead of cows, frogs, and mud. But fate did not leave the small security his new lifestyle provided him. His mom was not able to properly care for him and his siblings, and so the children were placed in different foster homes. That was even worse than leaving Dad! The clothes he wore were the only things familiar to him. Instead of understanding and loving him, each new family brought more yelling, hatred, and beating. Terror, tears, loneliness, and pain accompanied him.

Ken thought the second foster home that he was placed in would be a safe, loving home. The dad was tall and strong and appeared to be gentle. The mom was overweight, but her friendly smile resolved his fears. But the first night, when he reached for the food, he accidentally dumped a cup of water. She screamed at him and told him that he was worthless, and she wished they had never gotten him. The dad continued eating as if he didn't hear or care. Why didn’t the strong man stop her?

That evening, Ken crawled into his big, strange bed, already crying in loneliness, when he heard the mom yell. He quickly jumped out of bed and, with trembling legs, slipped behind the door to hide. She charged up the stairs bellowing angrily, and Ken was sure that he was in trouble. To his relief, she continued down the hall. He was still too scared to leave his hiding place for fear of receiving a beating. He wiped his tears as he began to sing under his breath a song he had heard in Sunday school, “Jesus loves the little children, all the children of the world.” He stopped to think, and his crying quit. “Then why am I here? " he wondered. “Have I done something wrong? God must not love little children. That song is not true! If God loved me I would not be here!" With that conclusion, he burst into tears and lost hope in God. He woke the next morning, still hidden behind the door.

Darkness had long fallen, and my family was all peacefully sleeping in our old farmhouse. I cried myself to sleep, crying for Ken's soul, crying because I didn’t know what to do, crying because my friend, the man I longed to see at peace with God, hated me.

Ken continued to fire questions. “How can God be good and allow so much bad? How could God let children suffer?” I listened on as he continued saying the same things that I heard so many times before, giving me no chance to talk.

Again, it was time to leave, and I was so glad to do so. He kept talking as we backed out the door. Once more, my friend and I walked up the street —tired, frustrated, and wishing never to come back.

Ken was 13 years old, and his life was no better than it had been when he was first put into the foster system. His life was in turmoil. He was continually yelled at and belittled at home. Ken was tired of crying. No one cared, and there was no one with whom he could share his problem. That’s when he came up with his clever plan. His school friend was a hippie, and his parents traveled a lot. They were called Gypsies. He heard that they were headed to California. So, Ken told them about his terrible life and asked if they would give him a ride. They were glad to help.

That exciting morning, he just did his usual thing. He left for school and instead went to California. He didn’t mind leaving all his stuff behind—he really didn’t have much anyway. His foster parents didn’t even care that he left.

In California, Ken lived on the beach and worked for fishermen, and whoever else needed help. He always had enough to eat and something to do. He had his fellow beach bums, but he was still alone inside. His heart was still empty. He longed for love.

Ken lived on the beach for a year and a half and then hitchhiked to Arizona. There he found a home in a homeless shelter and got a job. He did well and soon was on his own, but his search for love took him down the wrong roads. Ken really wanted to be married to a loving wife and have a family, but the girl he married did not marry him because of love. She was hurt, and Ken’s own hurt soul was attracted to her. They got married and all was well for a few years until he found out that his wife was seeing other men. His heart was broken, and his world was thrown into turmoil. Ken wanted desperately to provide security for the children that were born to them, and so he tried his best to stay together. He did not want to put his children through the life that he experienced. But after eight rough years, they got a divorce.

Ken moved on and tried to recover from the devastation of the divorce. His search for love brought him only more sadness and pain. Since Ken was hurt and unhappy, he found satisfaction in making others happy. He spent all his money on them, and when he had nothing more to offer, they left.

Now Ken is sitting in his pawn shop, alone, hurt, sad, and hiding. He found through his sad life that no one cared. Every time that he opened himself to love, he was always hurt. Deep down inside, he truly felt that God did not care. He lost hope in God, people, and last of all, he lost hope in love itself. That is why we were still visiting the dingy, smoke-stained shop after six years of very little apparent success. God kept bringing us back. He put in us a persistent love and relentless burden for this wounded soul. That is why we spent many hours hearing the same criticisms over and over. The same problems, the same confusion.

Nearly every month, he would fluctuate between hope and despair, love and hate, new life in God, and sadness and sin. We never knew what the next visit would bring. We could be swelling with hope and filled with blessing, or torn with angry words and sickened with dread. But we kept going back, and slowly he emerged from the pit of despair, and slowly allowed himself to be wrapped in the wonderful love of God and the glorious message of His redeeming grace. It was amazing to see the change in his life and to hear his ever-growing confidence in the love of Christ.

Today Ken loves the Lord. He is learning to walk with God. He has seen the love of God. He has found hope in God. He has experienced the unconditional love of God. He is still growing, and we are excited to see what God has for him.

I’m so glad that God brought Ken into my life. God had a plan for Ken and I. God wanted to show Ken that He loved him and that He would be there for him even when Josh turned his back on Him. God also wanted me to carry a burden in my youth. He knew how easily I would be distracted with money and fun. He knew that I needed a burden to carry, a soul to care for. He wanted me to be able to see beneath the shell of a hard soul and see a hurting child within. He wanted to give me a burden too big for me to carry so that I would learn to lean on Him. And most of all, He wanted to equip me to serve Him in broader ways.

Fellow Christians, open your lives to the work of God. Find an opportunity to love a hurting soul. Search out someone who needs a friend and love them, and wait and see what God has in store for you. Love until it hurts so badly that you don’t know what to do, and then turn to Jesus, who is there to help you through. God may be waiting for you to make the first step before He will use you. Your life is before you. You can choose to live a comfortable, happy life, or you can open yourself up to be hurt and find that after years pass, your life is overflowing with meaning and purpose. Jesus opened Himself to the pain and anguish of this world, and only through that do we have hope. He is asking us to follow His example, to open ourselves to pain so that others can have hope. And as He was glorified, so will we be glorified, in some measure, someday, and we will never regret the pain that we faced.

“मेरी दुकान से निकल जाओ! मुझे तुम्हारे जैसे लोग अपने आस-पास नहीं चाहिए! और फिर कभी मत आना!” मैं कांपती होंठों के साथ उस आदमी की गहरी, क्रोधित आँखों में देख रही थी जो चिल्ला रहा था। अनायास टूट पड़े आंसुओं को मैंने झपकाकर दबाया, और अहसास हुआ कि एक बार फिर मुझे उस पुरुष को छोड़ना होगा जिसे मैं प्यार करती थी। पूरी रात मुझे यह आभास था कि हम इसी मुकाम पर पहुँचने वाले हैं, और मैंने इसे होने से रोकने के लिए खूब कोशिश की थी। एक आखिरी प्रयास में, मैंने तनाव के ऊपर हल्की आवाज़ में चिल्लाते हुए कहा, “केन, हम नहीं चाहते कि ...” पर फिर से मुझे कठोरता से काट दिया गया। कंधे झुके और नयनहीन होकर, मैं उसके गंदे, जुआ की दुकान की सीमाओं से बाहर भागने के लिए मुड़ी, उसकी बढ़ती हुई आवाज़ आख़िरी छोटे से विश्राम की आशा को डूबा रही थी।

धुएँ की बासी गंध और उसकी क्रोधित आवाज़ की गूँज मेरे भावनात्मक रूप से थके हुए मन के परेशान विचारों से मिल गया, और मैं धीरे-धीरे सड़क ऊपर चलने लगी। “तुम क्या सोचते हो, जोश?” मैंने अपने वफादार, शांत मित्र से पूछा।

“मुझे नहीं पता,” उसने जवाब दिया, और हम दोनों चुप्पी में अपनी पीड़ा में लौट गए, अपनी कथित बाइबल स्टडी के परिणाम पर व्याकुलता में यह समझने की कोशिश करते हुए कि ऐसा भयंकर उत्तर क्यों मिला। हम क्या अलग कर सकते थे? वह सच क्यों स्वीकार नहीं कर सका? उन चमकती आँखों के पीछे क्या था, और उसके हमेशा पहने रहने वाले टोपी के नीचे कौन-सी यादें भरी थीं?

केन का जन्म पेंसिल्वेनिया के श्युलकिल की लहरदार पहाड़ियों में एक दिहाती खेत पर हुआ था, जो एक जिज्ञासु और साहसी छोटे लड़के के लिए रहने की एक शानदार जगह थी।

जब केन चार साल का था, उसके माता-पिता अलग हो गए। वह अक्सर उन्हें झगड़ते सुनता था, पर उसे नहीं पता था कि माँ और पिताजी अलग भी हो सकते हैं। इस बात ने उसका दिल तोड़ दिया और उसकी मासूम आत्मा को भ्रमित कर दिया। वह उस दबाव और बदलाव को संभालना नहीं जानता था जो उसकी शांत जिंदगी पर थोप दिया गया था।

माँ के जल्दी-जल्दी उनके समान ढोकर, उसे और उसके भाई-बहनों को कार में बैठाकर कहीं चल देने का आतंक और भ्रम अब भी उसकी यादों में गड़ा हुआ है। इसका कोई मतलब नहीं होता था! वे बस घर क्यों नहीं जा सकते थे? अपने छोटे, घिसे-पिटे अपार्टमेंट के अपनी बदबूदार शयनकक्ष में वह सड़े-गले छत की ओर घूरता रहता और अनंत समय तक सोचता कि आखिर क्या इतना गलत हो गया।

केन जल्द ही पॉट्सविले शहर में अपनी नई ज़िंदगी के साथ ढल गया—अब उसके आसपास गायों, मेंढकों और कीचड़ की जगह केवल कारें, लोग और फुटपाथ थे। पर भाग्य ने उस नई जीवनशैली से जो थोड़ी-सी सुरक्षा मिली थी, उसे भी नहीं छोड़ा। उसकी माँ उसे और उसके भाई-बहनों की ठीक तरह से देखभाल करने में असमर्थ थी, और इसलिए बच्चों को अलग-अलग फोस्टर घरों में रखा गया। यह तो पिताजी को छोड़ देने से भी बदतर था! जो कपड़े वह पहनता था वही उसके लिए परिचित चीज़ें रह गईं। समझने और प्यार करने के बजाय, हर नए परिवार ने और ज्यादा चिल्लाना, नफरत और पीटना दिया। आतंक, आँसू, अकेलेपन और दर्द उसका साथ देते रहे।

केन को लगा कि दूसरे फोस्टर घर में जहाँ उसे रखा गया है, वह एक सुरक्षित, प्यार करने वाला घर होगा। पिता लंबा और मजबूत था और दयी दिखाई देता था। माँ मोटी थी, लेकिन उसकी मित्रवत मुस्कान ने उसके डर को कम कर दिया। पर पहली रात, जब उसने खाने के लिए हाथ बढ़ाया, तो उसने अनजाने में एक कप पानी गिरा दिया। उसने उस पर चीखते हुए कहा कि वह बेकार है, और काश वे उसे कभी नहीं लाए होते। पिता चबाते रहे जैसे उसने सुना ही न हो या उसे परवाह न हो। मजबूत आदमी ने उसे रोका क्यों नहीं?

उस शाम, केन अपने बड़े, अजनबी बिस्तर में घुस गया, पहले से ही अकेलेपन में रो रहा था, जब उसने माँ की चिल्लाहट सुनी। वह जल्दी से बिस्तर से कूद गया और काँपती टाँगों के साथ दरवाज़े के पीछे छिप गया। वह ऊपर की सीढ़ियाँ चढ़कर गुस्से में दहाड़ती हुई आई, और केन पक्का मान बैठा कि वह मुश्किल में है। लेकिन उसकी राहत के लिए, वह हॉल के नीचे चली गई। वह तब तक अपने छुपने की जगह से बाहर निकलने के लिए बहुत डर गया कि उसे मार पड़ेगी। उसने अपने आंसू पोंछे और नीचे से सुर में सन्डे स्कूल में सुना गया एक गीत गुनगुनाने लगा, “Jesus loves the little children, all the children of the world.” वह सोच में पड़ गया और रोना बंद कर दिया। “तो फिर मैं यहाँ क्यों हूँ?” उसने आश्चर्य किया। “क्या मैंने कुछ गलत किया है? भगवान छोटे बच्चों से प्रेम नहीं करता। वह गीत सच नहीं है! अगर भगवान मुझसे प्यार करता तो मैं यहाँ नहीं होता!” इस निष्कर्ष के साथ वह फूट-फूट कर रो पड़ा और भगवान में अपनी आशा खो बैठा। अगली सुबह वह अभी भी दरवाज़े के पीछे छिपा हुआ उठा।

अंधेरा काफी समय से छाया हुआ था, और मेरा परिवार हमारे पुराने फार्महाउस में शांति से सो रहा था। मैं केन की आत्मा के लिए रोती-रोती सो गई, रो रही थी क्योंकि मुझे नहीं पता था क्या करना है, रो रही थी क्योंकि मेरा मित्र, वह आदमी जिसके मैं चाहती थी कि वह परमेश्वर के साथ शांति में रहे, मुझसे नफरत करता था।

केन ने सवालों का सिलसिला जारी रखा। “भगवान कैसे अच्छा हो सकता है और इतना बुरा होने दे सकता है? भगवान बच्चों को कैसे दुख सहने दे सकता है?” मैं सुनती रही जब तक कि उसने वही बातें दोहराईं जिन्हें मैंने पहले कई बार सुना था, मुझे बोलने का कोई मौका दिए बिना।

फिर से, छोड़ने का समय आ गया, और मैं ऐसा करने के लिए बेहद खुश थी। हम पीछे दरवाज़े से निकले तो वह बोलता रहा। एक बार फिर, मेरा मित्र और मैं सड़क ऊपर चले—थके हुए, हतोत्साहित, और फिर कभी लौटने की कामना करते हुए।

केन 13 साल का था, और उसकी ज़िंदगी उस समय से भी बेहतर नहीं थी जब उसे पहली बार फोस्टर सिस्टम में रखा गया था। उसकी ज़िंदगी अशांत थी। उसे लगातार घर पर डांटा और नीचा दिखाया जाता। केन रो-रोकर थक चुका था। किसी को परवाह नहीं थी, और उसके पास अपनी समस्या साझा करने के लिए कोई नहीं था। तभी उसने अपना चतुर प्लान बनाया। उसके स्कूल का एक दोस्त हिप्पी था, और उसके माता-पिता अक्सर यात्रा करते थे। उन्हें Gypsies कहा जाता था। उसने सुना कि वे कैलिफ़ोर्निया जा रहे हैं। इसलिए, केन ने उन्हें अपनी भयानक ज़िंदगी के बारे में बताया और उनसे कहा कि क्या वे उसे साथ ले चलेंगे। वे खुश थे मदद करने के लिए।

उस उत्साहभरी सुबह, उसने बस अपनी रोज़मर्रा की ही चीज़ कर दी। वह स्कूल के लिए निकला पर असल में कैलिफ़ोर्निया चला गया। उसे अपनी सारी चीज़ें पीछे छोड़ने में कोई आपत्ति नहीं थी—वैसे भी उसके पास ज्यादा कुछ था ही नहीं। उसके फोस्टर माता-पिता को यह भी फर्क नहीं पड़ा कि वह चला गया।

कैलिफ़ोर्निया में, केन समुद्र तट पर रहा और मछुआरों के लिए और जो भी मदद चाहिए उसके लिए काम किया। उसके पास हमेशा खाने को कुछ और करने के लिए कुछ होता। उसके अपने समुद्र तटीय साथी थे, पर वह अंदर से फिर भी अकेला था। उसका दिल अभी भी खाली था। वह प्यार की चाह में तरसता रहा।

केन डेढ़ साल समुद्र तट पर रहा और फिर वो एरिज़ोना की ओर हिचहाइक कर गया। वहाँ उसे एक बेघर शेल्टर में घर मिला और एक नौकरी मिल गई। उसने अच्छा किया और जल्द ही वह अपने पैरों पर खड़ा हो गया, पर उसका प्यार की खोज उसे गलत रास्तों पर ले गई। केन सचमुच एक प्यार करने वाली पत्नी से शादी करना चाहता था और परिवार पाना चाहता था, पर जिस लड़की से उसने शादी की वह उससे प्यार की वजह से नहीं मिली थी। वह आहत थी, और केन की खुद आहत आत्मा उससे आकर्षित हुई। वे शादी कर बैठे और कुछ सालों तक सब ठीक रहा जब तक कि उसे पता नहीं चला कि उसकी पत्नी दूसरे पुरुषों को भी देखती है। उसका दिल टूट गया, और उसकी दुनिया अराजक हो गई। केन बच्चों को सुरक्षा देने के लिए बेताब था, इसलिए उसने साथ रहने की भरसक कोशिश की। वह अपने बच्चों को वह जीवन नहीं देना चाहता था जो उसने झेला था। पर आठ कठिन वर्षों के बाद, उनका तलाक हो गया।

केन आगे बढ़ा और तलाक के विनाश से उबरने की कोशिश की। प्यार की उसकी खोज ने उसे केवल और उदासी और दर्द दिया। चूँकि केन आहत और दुखी था, उसने दूसरों को खुश करने में संतोष पाया। उसने अपने सभी पैसे उन पर खर्च कर दिए, और जब उसके पास देने के लिए कुछ नहीं बचा, तो वे चले गए।

अब केन अपनी जुआ-नुमा दुकान में बैठा है—अकेला, आहत, दुखी और छिपा हुआ। उसने अपनी दुखभरी ज़िंदगी से यह जान लिया कि किसी को परवाह नहीं है। हर बार जब उसने प्यार के लिए खुद को खोला़, वह हमेशा आहत हुआ। अंदर गहराई में, उसने सचमुच महसूस किया कि भगवान को परवाह नहीं है। उसने भगवान में उम्मीद खो दी, लोगों में उम्मीद खो दी, और आखिर में उसने प्यार में ही उम्मीद खो दी। इसी कारण हम छह वर्षों तक बहुत कम दिखाई देने वाली सफलता के बावजूद उस कड़े, धुएँ-धब्बेदार दुकान में अभी भी जाते रहे। परमेश्वर हमें बार-बार वापस लाता रहा। उसने हमारे अंदर एक अडिग प्रेम और इस जख्मी आत्मा के लिए अटल बोझ डाला। इसीलिए हमने कई घंटे एक ही आलोचनाओं को बार-बार सुना। वही समस्याएँ, वही भ्रम।

लगभग हर महीने, वह आशा और निराशा, प्रेम और घृणा, परमेश्वर में नया जीवन और उदासी और पाप के बीच झूलता रहता। हमें कभी नहीं पता होता था कि अगली मुलाकात क्या लेकर आएगी। हम आशा से भरे और आशीर्वाद से परिपूर्ण हो सकते थे, या गुस्से भरे शब्दों से फटे और भय से बीमार हो सकते थे। पर हम वापस जाते रहे, और धीरे-धीरे वह निराशा की खाई से उभर कर, खुद को परमेश्वर के अद्भुत प्रेम और उसकी उद्धारात्मक अनुग्रह की बहुमूल्य बातों में लिपटा हुआ आने देने लगा। उसकी ज़िंदगी में बदलाव देखना और मसीह के प्रेम में उसकी बढ़ती हुई आत्मविश्वास सुनना अद्भुत था।

आज केन प्रभु से प्रेम करता है। वह परमेश्वर के साथ चलना सीख रहा है। उसने परमेश्वर के प्रेम को देखा है। उसने परमेश्वर में आशा पाई है। उसने परमेश्वर के बिना शर्त प्रेम का अनुभव किया है। वह अभी भी बढ़ रहा है, और हम उत्साहित हैं यह देखने के लिए कि परमेश्वर ने उसके लिए क्या रखा है।

मैं बहुत खुश हूँ कि परमेश्वर ने केन को मेरी ज़िंदगी में लाया। परमेश्वर का केन और मेरे लिए एक योजना थी। परमेश्वर ने केन को दिखाना चाहा कि वह उससे प्रेम करता है और तब भी उसके लिए वहाँ रहेगा जब जोश उसकी पीठ मोड़ दे। परमेश्वर ने यह भी चाहा कि मैं अपनी युवावस्था में एक बोझ उठाऊँ। वह जानता था कि मैं कितनी आसानी से पैसे और मौज-मस्ती से भटक जाऊँगी। वह जानता था कि मुझे उठाने के लिए एक बोझ चाहिए था, किसी आत्मा की देखभाल करने के लिए। वह चाहता था कि मैं कठोर आत्मा की खोल के नीचे एक दुखी बच्चे को देख सकूँ। वह मुझे इतना बड़ा बोझ देना चाहता था जिसे मैं अकेले वहन न कर सकूँ ताकि मैं उस पर टेकेना सीख सकूँ। और सबसे बढ़कर, वह मुझे व्यापक रूप से उसकी सेवा करने के लिए तैयार करना चाहता था।

प्रिय ईसाई भाइयों और बहनों, अपने जीवन को परमेश्वर के कार्य के लिए खोलिए। किसी दुखी आत्मा से प्रेम करने का अवसर खोजिए। किसी ऐसे व्यक्ति की खोज कीजिए जिसे एक मित्र की ज़रूरत है और उससे प्रेम कीजिए, और देखिए कि परमेश्वर आपके लिए क्या रखता है। तब तक प्रेम कीजिए जब तक कि दर्द इतना तीव्र न हो जाए कि आप न जानें क्या करें, और फिर यीशु की ओर मुड़िए, जो आपकी मदद करने के लिए वहाँ है। परमेश्वर शायद आपकी प्रथम चाल की प्रतीक्षा कर रहा हो ताकि वह आपका उपयोग कर सके। आपका जीवन आपके सामने है। आप एक आरामदायक, सुखी जीवन चुन सकते हैं, या आप खुद को खोल सकते हैं कि आहत हों और देखिए कि वर्षों के बीतने पर आपका जीवन अर्थ और उद्देश्य से भरपूर हो जाएगा। यीशु ने इस संसार के दर्द और कष्ट को खुलकर स्वीकार किया, और केवल उसी के द्वारा हमारे पास आशा है। वह हमसे अपने उदाहरण का अनुसरण करने को कह रहा है, खुद को दर्द के लिए खोलने को ताकि दूसरों के पास आशा हो सके। और जैसे वह महिमामय हुआ, वैसे ही किसी हद तक हम भी एक दिन महिमामय होंगे, और हमें उस दर्द का कभी पछतावा नहीं होगा जो हमने सहा।

It's incredible to me to see how God uses His people throughout history to bring glory to His name. He uses the weak things to confound the wise; the base things to bring to nothing the wisdom of earthly wise men. God uses physical weakness, hardship, loss, grief, toil, and pain to increase our spiritual treasures and build His Kingdom here on the earth!

This hymn became precious to my family and me several years ago as we awaited the birth of our fourth genetically challenged baby. We knew she couldn't stay with us very long. She passed away at just three days old. After researching this hymn, I was amazed to find out that the man whose story had inspired this hymn had lost eight out of his nine children.

The story of this man is a notable one. His 61 years on earth were marked by grief and loss, persecution and imprisonment. Yet, his dedication to Christ was outstanding, and his fire for God and zeal for preaching the gospel never waned until his last day.

Samuel Rutherford, son of a prosperous farmer, was born in the year 1600. His life began in the small village of Nisbet, Scotland. As we glimpse into his life, we notice the hand of God at work in Samuel’s early years. At only three years old, he was playing with his friends when he fell into the town well. His sister and friends ran to get help. When they returned, they found a very wet Samuel sitting on the grass beside the well. They asked him how he got out, and his reply was, "A bonny white man came and drew me out of the well." His family believed that God sent an angel to rescue him that day.

From what we know about Samuel Rutherford, he had two brothers and one sister. He was sent to school when he was young, and he became a very diligent scholar. He learned Latin and Greek so well that he eventually became a professor. He married Eupham Hamilton around 1624, soon after he began teaching at Edinburgh University. At this time, Samuel was yet unconverted and cared only for pursuing his academic goals.

In 1626, at the age of 26, Samuel came to a clear and saving faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. He said, "O but Christ hath a saving eye. When He first looked on me I was saved. It cost Him but a look to make hell quit to me." From that moment he was filled with a passion to preach and to speak about his Saviour. This change of life caused such a stir in the university that Rutherford ended up resigning his professorship.

In 1627, Samuel took his wife and two young children to Galloway, Scotland, where he began pastoring the small church of Anwoth. As he commenced his calling there he said, "I have received the commission from the royal and princely Master, my Lord Jesus, to preach Christ to the people." His passion was for the conversion of the people, and it is said that he seemed to be always praying, always preaching, always visiting the sick, always teaching and instructing, always writing or studying. The zeal with which he preached and his concern for the welfare of his congregation had a great effect on them. Not only them, but folks came from the surrounding towns and villages to hear his preaching. A friend once reported, "Many times I thought he would have flown out of the pulpit when he came to speak of Jesus Christ."

Samuel was not estranged from grief and sorrow. In 1631, only four short years after he began his work as a pastor, his wife passed away. His two children also became ill and left this world. In 1636, after nine years of preaching, he was banished to Aberdeen, where he was forbidden to preach the gospel. This was a very difficult time for him as he greatly missed his wife and children as well as his congregation, the Church at Anwoth. This time in his life is indeed one reason he is so well remembered, for he began writing letters back to his church people and friends. Out of the 365 letters he wrote, 220 of them were written during these 22 months of banishment.

The government eventually changed hands, which gave more liberty to the non-conformist Covenanters. Thereupon Rutherford quickly returned to his beloved flock at Anwoth. About a year later, in the fall of 1639, he again reluctantly left Anwoth but this time to fulfill an appointment to become Professor of Divinity at St Mary's College in St. Andrews. This change was difficult for him, as he again greatly missed his congregation. He writes, "My removal from my flock is so heavy to me, that it maketh my life a burden to me, I had never such a longing for death. The Lord help and hold up this sad clay."

After five months in his new position and having been alone for nearly ten years, the 40-year-old Samuel married Jean McMath. Together they had seven children. Sadly, six of them died in infancy and early childhood. Only a daughter named Agnes survived to adulthood.

Rutherford continued to be an influential leader in the non-conformist movement in Scotland for the next 20 years until 1660. With the death of Cromwell, the rule of the commonwealth came to an end, and Charles II was restored to power. Once again, the wrath of the monarchy fell on Samuel. He was summoned to appear before the judge and charged with high treason against the government for preaching the truth. He was put in prison to await execution. However, before the king could put him to death, Samuel became quite sick. He said, "I have a summons already from a superior Judge, and I behoove to answer my first summons and when your day arrives I shall be where few Kings and great folks come."

Late in the afternoon of the last day of his life in answer to the question, "What think ye now of Christ?" answered thusly, "Oh, that all my brethren in the land may know what a Master I have served, and what peace I have this day! I shall sleep in Christ, and when I awake, I shall be satisfied with His likeness. This night shall close the door, and put my anchor within the veil, and I shall go away in a sleep by five of the clock in the morning. Glory! glory to my Creator and my Redeemer forever! I Shall live and adore Him. Oh, for arms to embrace Him! Oh, for a well-tuned harp! Glory! glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land!" These words were heard by his wife, daughter and friends, and he was indeed with his Lord by five in the morning.

Nearly two centuries later, Annie Ross Cousin, a Scottish poet and hymn writer and the wife of a minister, was inspired by the life and writings of Samuel Rutherford. She summarized his life in a biographical hymn,"The Sands of Time are Sinking". This hymn was first published in 1857 in the Christian Treasury. Out of the nineteen original verses, only four are used in our hymn books. (in bold copy)

The sands of time are sinking,
The dawn of heaven breaks,
The summer morn I’ve sighed for,
The fair, sweet morn awakes:
Dark, dark hath been the midnight,
But dayspring is at hand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

2. Oh! well it is forever,
Oh! well forevermore
My nest hung in no forest
Of all this death-doomed shore!
Yea, let the vain world vanish,
As from the ship the stand,
While glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

3. There the Red Rose of Sharon
Unfolds its heart-most bloom.
And fills the air of Heaven
With ravishing perfume;
Oh, to behold its blossom,
While by its fragrance fann’d
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

4. The King there in His beauty,
Without a veil is seen:
It were a well-spent journey
Though seven deaths lay between:
The Lamb with His fair army,
Doth on Mount Zion stand;
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

5. Oh! Christ He is the fountain,
The deep sweet well of Love!
The streams on earth I’ve tasted,
More deep I’ll drink above;
There, to an ocean fullness,
His mercy doth expand,
And glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

6. E’en Anwoth was not heaven—
E’en preaching was not Christ;
And in my sea-beat prison
My Lord and I held tryst:
And aye my murkiest storm-cloud
Was by a rainbow spann’d,
Caught from the glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land.

7. But that He built a heaven
Of His surpassing love,
A little New Jerus’lem,
Like to the one above,—
“Lord, take me o’er the water,”
Had been my loud demand,
“Take me to love’s own country,
Unto Immanuel’s land.”

8. But flowers need night’s cool darkness,
The moonlight and the dew;
So Christ, from one who loved it,
His shining oft withdrew;
And then, for cause of absence,
My troubled soul I scann’d—
But glory, shadeless, shineth
In Immanuel’s land.

9. The little birds of Anwoth,
used to count them blest,—
Now, beside happier alters,
go to built my nest:
O’er these there broods no silence,
No graves around them stand,
For glory, deathless, dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

10. Fair Anwoth by the Solway,
To me thou still art dear!
E’en from the verge of Heaven
I drop for thee a tear.
Oh! if one soul from Anwoth
Meet me at God’s right hand,
My Heaven will be two Heavens,
In Immanuel’s land!

11. I’ve wrestled on towards Heaven,
‘Ganst storm, and wind, and tide;—
Now, like a weary traveler,
That leaneth on his guide,
Amid the shades of evening,
While sinks life’s ling’ring sand,
I hail the glory dawning
From Immanuel’s land.

12. Deep waters cross’d life’s pathway,
The hedge of thorns was sharp;
Now these lie all behind me,—
Oh, for a well-tuned harp!
Oh, to join Hallelujah
With yon triumphant band,
Who sing where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land!

13. With mercy and with judgment
My web of time He wove,
And aye the dews of sorrow
Were lustered with His love!
I’ll bless the hand that guided,
I’ll bless the heart that plann’d,
When throned where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

14. Soon shall the cup of glory
Wash down earth’s bitterest woes,
Soon shall the desert brier
Break into Eden’s rose:
The curse shall change to blessing–
The name on earth that’s bann’d,
Be graven on the white stone
In Immanuel’s land.

15. Oh! I am my Beloved’s,
And my Beloved’s mine!
He brings a poor vile sinner
Into His “house of wine:”
I stand upon His merit,
I know no other stand,
Not e’en where glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

16. I shall sleep sound in Jesus,
Fill’d with His likeness rise,
To live and to adore Him,
To see Him with these eyes:
‘Tween me and resurrection
But Paradise doth stand;
Then—then for glory dwelling
In Immanuel’s land!

17. The bride eyes not her garment,
But her dear Bridegroom’s face;
I will not gaze at glory,
But on my King of Grace—
Not at the crown He giveth,
But on His pierced hand:
The Lamb is all the glory
Of Immanuel’s land.

18. I have borne scorn and hatred,
I have borne wrong and shame,
Earth’s proud ones have reproach’d me,
For Christ’s thrice blessed name:
Where God His seal set fairest
They’ve stamp’d their foulest brand;
But judgment shines like noonday
In Immanuel’s land.

19. They’ve summoned me before them,
But there I may not come,—
My Lord says, “Come up hither,”
My Lord says, “Welcome home!
My King now at His white throne,
My presence doth command,
Where glory—glory dwelleth
In Immanuel’s land.

The fine complementary tune for this text was composed in the early 1800s by a French musician, Chretien D`Urhan. It is well fitted to the words of the hymn—its solemn tempo matches the solemnity of the words. The rising melodic line of the last phrase perfectly matches the anticipated joy expressed by the refrain—"And glory, glory dwelleth in Immanuel's land."

As we conclude this hymn history, let us continue to marvel at the providence of God in the lives of those who have gone before us. May we follow Christ with all our hearts and be vessels ready for the Master's use! One last quote by Samuel Rutherford to take with us. "They lose nothing who gain Christ."
