Our spiritual forefathers had much to say on the many issues facing the American Mennonite church in their time, and we can still learn from the collected writings of these church leaders and brethren. We will look first at the hermeneutics of the early American Mennonite church, endeavoring to draw examples from which we, as 21st-century Christians, can learn.

First, the correct interpretation of Scripture was a matter of great importance to these earlier Christians. They had only recently emigrated away from a largely hostile area, where they had been constantly tested to the point of death on matters of faith and now faced a different set of challenges when confronted with peace and religious freedom. We will look at how they navigated these challenges by studying several of their doctrines and practices.

The Doctrine of Nonresistance

One matter that was well interpreted and applied by many of the early Mennonite writers is the principle and doctrine of the nonresistant Christian. Although many of their Anabaptist descendants of today still hold, to varying degrees, this doctrine, it is oftentimes not done with the clarity and solemnity of their forefathers. The early American Mennonites understood nonresistance as a foundational aspect of the Christian life, as it should be, and taught extensively on the practical application and appearance of nonresistance in the life of a believer. Their primary motivation for living peaceably and without malice toward one’s fellow man was the given example of Jesus. Christ typified the acceptable response to violence and ill-will: gentleness, meekness, as befitted one who is called a Lamb.

The Emphasis of Biblical Foundations

There was also a firm focus amongst early Mennonite writers against building doctrine on the writings of men. This emphasis comes through strongly in their works, as they quote Scripture extensively. They made their point by bringing in an example of Christ or by way of an applicable Scripture verse, rather than building on the sandy soil of a man’s opinions. One of the areas in which they did so was the matter of salvation.

Importance of Practical Salvation

We can learn much from the early Mennonites about the practical working out of salvation. First, salvation is portrayed as both an inward and an outward change. The inward is affected first through the working of the Holy Spirit in the willful sinner’s life. It is an important distinction that the sinner is willful. This position was contrary to most of the greater established churches of the time. If a sinner must be willful, then it implies that all men can willfully accept salvation, an idea that is fundamental in nature, if not always verbalized, to the church of today.

In the early Mennonites’ time, predestination as taught by Calvinism seems to have necessitated this emphasis on man’s ability to choose freely, which is still true today. There is also another flavoring of the “unwillingly saved” interpretation, and that comes from the aftereffects of the charismatic movement and the effect it has had on Mennonite and Amish circles. This “unwilling salvation” is not a matter of predestination, but rather is described as almost a coercive calling by the Spirit. It has been observed in several salvation testimonies where the testifiers recalled how they were completely comfortable in their lives of sin and debauchery when suddenly they would be struck down in the manner of Saul and could not help themselves but follow after God and give their lives to Him. There are numerous pitfalls with this dramatic understanding of conversion, namely that it absolves responsibility from the one converted for his decision to convert. This leads to a lack of counting the cost of Christianity, which is a death of oneself, a death of pride, and a death of favor with man. If the believer hops headfirst into Christianity, not reckoning that he must give up all these self-pleasing traits, how will he be able to grow spiritually if he cannot let go of his former vices? While this form of conversion may be genuine at the beginning, it does not often progress beyond the milk of the Word to the meat of which a mature Christian must partake. This maturing of a Christian is emphasized in writings ranging from those of Menno Simons up to Abraham Goshalk. It is also important for the sake of the church that the believer be firmly committed and engaged in the steady growth of his faith.

The Seriousness of a Pure Church

The idea of church to the early American Mennonite seems to have been a more serious thought, less individualistic than our current state. It is the pitiable state of nominal Christianity that the church has become a social organization with room for all sin and depravity.

It behooves us to consider closely the character of the church that Christ established and to note as well the character of the true churches, unspotted by apostasy and laxness. This character is, like Christ himself, simple and yet incredibly full of meaning and spiritual vitality.

The first aspect of the church to recognize is its pure state as the bride of Christ. Here again, we should consider the character of Christ. Did He ever give Himself space for sin? Do we find Him occasionally indulging in a brief enjoyment of a “guilty pleasure”? The understanding reader will agree that Christ was pure in His entirety, and so how else should the bride be with which He is to be intimately and eternally joined? To aid our minds in answering such a question, let us consider the earthly symbol of this heavenly union: that of a man and a woman joined together for life. This earthly union is recognized even by non-Christians as something set aside purely for the two individuals involved, a relationship and a sharing of each other that is not and never to be partaken of by anyone outside of the intimate union. This paints clearly for our earth-bound minds the mind of Christ, insomuch as that marriage is a symbol of Christ and His bride. The bride and Christ are for each other and give themselves to nothing and no one other.

Now that we can see the purity of the church, let us examine its practical working out amongst fallen man. If it is to be pure, then how are we to be a part of it? Here enters the need for a clear understanding of regeneration, a doctrine held in high regard by these Mennonite forefathers. They taught that the Spirit affects the spiritual washing and cleansing that will be made apparent in a changed state of thought and action in the believer. This change is still at variance with our fallen nature, but through continued surrender and a deep humility, the Spirit will fill the believer until the nature of sin becomes the dominated instead of the dominant. It is important to realize, however, that this victory over sin is brought into effect by the believer yielding his will and allowing the Spirit complete control.

Thus, a pure church is a surrendered, Spirit-filled group of believers who recognize in true humility that their power is not in any way linked to their own merit. The absence of pride, achieved only by the constant aid of the Spirit, gives further room for purification of the willing believer. In this way, we can see the Christian life in shoe leather.

The Teachings of Practical Christianity

The practicality of the early American Mennonite’s faith was continually on display. In his book, “Pride and Humility,” John M. Brenneman maintains that the outward appearance of a person is directly related to his inward heart, a view which extends as well to the actions of the individual. It is necessary to build on the beliefs of willful salvation, regeneration, and a pure church previously examined to frame the mindset of a Mennonite’s interactions in daily living.

To these serious-minded Christians, there was no difference in importance between the religious belief expressed on Sundays and the mundane actions of the rest of the week. This is evidenced by their general abstinence from political matters and other elements of a worldly nature that would infringe upon the beliefs they held. This put them in direct opposition to many of the churches of their day, where thrived two schools of thought: either that one’s earthly duties in a political manner were carried out completely separate from one’s faith, or that the accomplishment of these civic duties were incorporated in the will of God and so permissible for the Christian to engage in freely.

To the early American Mennonite, these types of stances betrayed the very meaning of his Christianity: he was a new person, alive only in the power of Christ that flowed through him. This influenced and directed every aspect of his life, from his business dealings, which were carried out in a way so as not to take advantage of any party involved, to his dress and manner of deportment, which was to be based on humility and plainness, to his method of conversing with his fellow man, which was to show a genuine concern for the spiritual well-being and eternal destiny.

Conclusion

The sum of all these colonial Mennonite beliefs was the doctrine of how to grow into a mature, humble, repentant, but spiritually powerful servant of God. He denied the allures of the world around him in favor of an eternal reward promised upon the purity of his faith and willing renunciation of the sin in which he had formerly lived. This example, lived out by believers like us, should inspire us to further press into the Kingdom of God, working out our faith in humility and repentance.

আমাদের আধ্যাত্মিক পূর্বপুরুষরা তাদের সময়ের আমেরিকান মেনোনাইট চার্চকে ঘিরে বহু সমস্যার উপর অনেক কথা বলেছিলেন, এবং আমরা এখনও এই চার্চ নেতাদের ও ভাই-বোনদের সংকলিত রচনাগুলি থেকে শিখতে পারি। আমরা প্রথমে প্রাথমিক আমেরিকান মেনোনাইট চার্চের ব্যাখ্যাবিদ্যা (hermeneutics) দেখব, এবং উদাহরণ টেনে এমন শিক্ষা আহরণ করার চেষ্টা করব যেগুলো আমরা, কুড়ি-এক শতাব্দীর খ্রীষ্টানরা, শিখতে পারি।

প্রথমত, বাইবেলের সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা এই আগের খ্রীষ্টানদের কাছে একটি অত্যন্ত গুরুত্বপূর্ণ বিষয় ছিল। তারা সম্প্রতি এমন একটি অঞ্চল থেকে অভিবাসী হয়ে এসেছিল যেখানে বেশিরভাগই শত্রুভাবাপন্ন ছিল, যেখানে তারা বিশ্বাস নিয়ে পরীক্ষা-নিরীক্ষায় সর্বশেষ জীবনের বিনিময়ে পর্যন্ত পরীক্ষিত হয়েছে এবং এখন শান্তি ও ধর্মীয় স্বাধীনতার মুখোমুখি হয়ে অন্য ধরনের চ্যালেঞ্জ দেখেছিল। আমরা তাদের কয়েকটি মতবাদ ও অনুশীলনের অধ্যয়নের মাধ্যমে দেখতে চেষ্টা করব তারা কিভাবে এই চ্যালেঞ্জগুলোর মধ্য দিয়ে চলাফেরা করেছিল।

The Doctrine of Nonresistance

একটি বিষয় যা প্রাথমিক মেনোনাইট লেখকদের মধ্যে বহুজনই ভালভাবে ব্যাখ্যা ও প্রয়োগ করেছেন আর তা হলো অপ্রতিরোধী (nonresistant) খ্রীষ্টান নীতিমালা ও মতবাদ। যদিও আজকের অনেক অনাবাপটিস্ট উত্তরসূরি বিভিন্ন মাত্রায় এই মতবাদের প্রতি ধারণা রক্ষা করে, তা প্রায়ই তাঁদের পূর্বপুরুষদের মতো স্পষ্টতা ও গম্ভীরতার সঙ্গে করা হয় না। প্রাথমিক আমেরিকান মেনোনাইটরা অপ্রতিরোধীতাকে খ্রীষ্টীয় জীবনের একটি মৌলিক দিক হিসেবে বুঝতেন—যেমন হওয়া উচিত—এবং বিশ্বাসীর জীবনে অপ্রতিরোধীতার ব্যবহারিক প্রয়োগ ও রূপটি ব্যাপকভাবে শিখিয়েছেন। সহানুভূতিশীলভাবে শান্তিপূর্ণ ও পরের মানুষের প্রতি কোনো বিদ্বেষ ছাড়া জীবন যাপনের তাদের প্রধান প্রেরণা ছিল যীশুর প্রদত্ত উদাহরণ। খ্রীষ্ট সহিংসতা ও খারাপ ইচ্ছার উপস্থিতিতে গ্রহণযোগ্য প্রতিক্রিয়ার উদাহরণ ছিলেন: নম্রতা, বিনয়, এমন এক ব্যক্তির যোগ্যতা যাকে মেষশাবক বলা হয়।

The Emphasis of Biblical Foundations

প্রাথমিক মেনোনাইট লেখকদের মধ্যে এরাও শক্তভাবে বৈশিষ্ট্যযুক্ত ছিল যে তারা মানুষে রচিত লেখার উপর নির্ভর করে মতবাদের নির্মাণের বিরুদ্ধে স্থির মনোভাব রাখতেন। এই জোর তাদের রচনাগুলোতে স্পষ্টভাবে প্রকাশ পায়, কারণ তারা ব্যাপকভাবে বাইবেল উদ্ধৃত করেছেন। তারা একটি উপযুক্ত বাইবেলিক প্যাসেজ বা খ্রীষ্টের উদাহরণ এনে তাদের বক্তব্য প্রকাশ করতেন, বরং মানুষের মতামতের বালুকাময় মাটিতে ভিত্তি গড়তেন না। ভ্রূণভাবে এক ক্ষেত্র যেখানে তারা এভাবেই আচরণ করেছিলেন তা ছিল উদ্ধার (salvation)-এর বিষয়।

Importance of Practical Salvation

আমরা প্রাথমিক মেনোনাইটদের থেকে উদ্ধারপ্রক্রিয়ার ব্যবহারিক বিশ্লেষণ সম্পর্কে অনেক কিছু শিখতে পারি। প্রথমত, উদ্ধারকে ইঙ্গিত করা হয় যেন তা হোলো অভ্যন্তরীণ ও বাহ্যিক পরিবর্তন—দুইই। অভ্যন্তরীণ পরিবর্তন প্রথমে পবিত্র আত্মার কার্যক্রমের মাধ্যমে অভিলাষী পাপকেই প্রভাবিত করে। এটি একটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ ভেদ যে পাপী স্বেচ্ছাচারী (willful)। এই অবস্থান তখনকার অধিকাংশ প্রতিষ্ঠিত চার্চের বিপরীত ছিল। যদি পাপীকে স্বেচ্ছাচারী হতে হয়, তাহলে এর অর্থ হলো সমস্ত মানুষই স্বেচ্ছাপূর্বক রক্ষা গ্রহণ করতে পারে, একটি ধারণা যা আজকের চার্চে মৌলিকভাবে বিদ্যমান, যদিও সবসময় মৌখিকভাবে উচ্চারণ করা না-ও হতে পারে।

প্রাথমিক মেনোনাইটদের সময়ে, ক্যালভিনবাদ দ্বারা শেখানো নির্বাচন (predestination) সম্ভবত মানুষের মুক্ত ইচ্ছা গ্রহণের ওপর এই জোরকে প্রয়োজনীয় করেছিল, যা আজও সত্য। আরেকটি রূচি রয়েছে “অনিচ্ছাসন্ত্রীয়ে উদ্ধার” ব্যাখ্যার, যা চারিত্রিক আন্দোলনের পরিণতি এবং মেনোনাইট ও অ্যামিশ পরিধায় এর প্রভাব থেকে উদ্ভূত। এই “অনিচ্ছায় উদ্ধার” কোনোভাবে নির্বাচন থেকে উদ্ভূত নয়, বরং এটি এমন এক প্রায় বলপ্রয়োগী ডাকের মতো বর্ণিত হয় পবিত্র আত্মার দ্বারা। এটি বহু উদ্ধারের সাক্ষ্যপ্রদানে দেখা গেছে যেখানে সাক্ষী ব্যক্তিরা স্মরণ করে যে তারা তাদের পাপ এবং অসভ্যতার জীবন নিয়ে সম্পূর্ণ আরামে ছিল এবং হঠাৎ তারা শাউলের রূপে পতিত হয়েছিল এবং নিজেরাই থামতে পারে না; তাদের বাধ্য হয়ে ঈশ্বরের পিছনে চলে যেতে হয়েছিল এবং তাদের জীবন তেঁহাদের উদ্দেশ্যে উৎসর্গ করতে হয়েছিল। এই নাটকীয় রূপ ধারণা সম্পর্কে বহু জালতা বিদ্যমান, বিশেষত এটি রূপান্তরিত ব্যক্তির উপর তার রূপান্তর গ্রহণের দায়িত্ব থেকে অব্যাহতি দেয়। এটি খ্রিস্টীয়তায় ব্যয় গণনা না করার দিকে নিয়ে যায়—যা নিজেকে মরে ফেলা, অহংকারের মৃত্যু, এবং মানুষের অনুকম্পার মৃ্ত্যু। যদি বিশ্বাসী মাথায় কেবল ঝাঁপিয়ে পড়ে খ্রিস্টীয়তায় এসে, এই নানাবিধ আত্ম-সুখদায়ক স্বভাব ত্যাগ করতে হবে না ভেবে, সে কিভাবে আধ্যাত্মিকভাবে বৃদ্ধি পাবে যদি সে তার পূর্বের অভ্যাস ছাড়তে না পারে? যদিও এই ধরণের রূপান্তর শুরুতে সত্যিকারের হতে পারে, এটা প্রায়শই বাক্যের দুধ থেকে মাংসের দিকে অগ্রসর হয় না, যা পারিপক্ব খ্রীষ্টানকে গ্রহণ করতে হয়। মেনো সিমন্স থেকে শুরু করে অ্যব্রাহাম গোষাল্ক পর্যন্ত রচনায় একটি খ্রিষ্টানের এই পরিণতি প্রাপ্ত হওয়া জোর দিয়েছে। চার্চের কল্যাণের জন্যও এটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ যে বিশ্বাসী দৃড়ভাবে প্রতিশ্রুতিবদ্ধ ও তার বিশ্বাসের ধারাবাহিক বৃদ্ধিতে নিয়োজিত থাকুক।

The Seriousness of a Pure Church

প্রাথমিক আমেরিকান মেনোনাইটদের জন্য চার্চের ধারণা আরও গম্ভীর ছিল বলে মনে হয়—এটি আমাদের বর্তমান অবস্থার তুলনায় কমই ব্যক্তির উপর নির্ভরশীল ছিল। নামমাত্র খ্রিস্টীয়তার পীড়া হলো যে চার্চটি এখন একটি সামাজিক সংগঠনে পরিণত হয়েছে যেখানে সকল পাপ ও বিস্তারের জন্য জায়গা রয়েছে।

এটি আমাদের বুক কাঁপিয়ে দেয় যে আমরা যেই চার্চটি খ্রীষ্ট প্রতিষ্ঠা করেছিলেন তার চরিত্রকে মনোযোগ সহকারে বিবেচনা করি এবং সেই সাথে সঠিক চার্চগুলোর চরিত্রও লক্ষ করি, যেগুলি বিস্তার বা আলশলতার দ্বারা দূষিত হয়নি। এই চরিত্র খ্রীষ্টের মতোই সরল এবং তবু অত্যন্ত গভীর অর্থ ও আধ্যাত্মিক প্রাণশক্তিতে পূর্ণ।

চার্চের প্রথম দিকটি স্বীকৃত করার মতো তার বিশুদ্ধ অবস্থায় অবস্থান হলো খ্রীষ্টের কনেরূপ। এখানে আবারও, আমাদের উচিত খ্রীষ্টের চরিত্র বিবেচনা করা। তিনি কি কখনও নিজের জন্য পাপের জায়গা রেখেছিলেন? কি আমরা তাকে মাঝে মাঝে কোনো সংক্ষিপ্ত “কৃতকর্মের আনন্দ” উপভোগ করতে দেখি? বোঝাপড়া সম্পন্ন পাঠক একমত হবেন যে খ্রীষ্ট সম্পূর্ণরূপে পবিত্র ছিলেন, এবং তাহলে কনে কেমন হওয়া উচিত যার সাথে তিনি ঘনিষ্ঠভাবে এবং চিরকালের জন্য মিলিত হবেন? আমাদের মনের জবাব দেওয়ার জন্য, আসুন আমরা এই স্বর্গীয় মিলনের ভূভিত্তিক প্রতীকটিকে বিবেচনা করি: একটি পুরুষ ও একটি নারী জীবনভর একত্রিত হওয়া। এই পৃথিবীর মিলন এমনকি অবিশ্বাসীরাও এমন কিছু হিসেবে স্বীকার করে যা কেবল সেই দুই ব্যক্তির জন্য পৃথক, একটি সম্পর্ক এবং পারস্পরিক ভাগাভাগি যা কোনোরকমভাবে বা কখনোই ঐ ঘনিষ্ঠ মিলনের বাইরে অন্য কেউ অংশগ্রহণ করবে না। এটি আমাদের পৃথিবীর মস্তিষ্কে স্পষ্টভাবে খ্রীষ্টের মনকে চিত্রায়িত করে, ফেবতু তরকা যে বিবাহ খ্রীষ্ট ও তাঁর কনের প্রতীক। কনে ও খ্রীষ্ট একে অপরের জন্য এবং নিজেদেরকে অন্য কোনো কিছুর বা কারো জন্য দেয় না।

এখন আমরা চার্চের পবিত্রতা দেখতে পেয়েছি, আসুন এটি পতিত মানুষের মধ্যে কিভাবে ব্যবহারিকভাবে কাজ করে তা পরীক্ষা করি। যদি চার্চ বিশুদ্ধ হতে হয়, আমরা কিভাবে এর অংশ হব? এখানে পুনর্জন্মের (regeneration) একটি স্পষ্ট বোঝাপড়ার প্রয়োজন দেখা দেয়—একটি মতবাদ যা এই মেনোনাইট পূর্বপুরুষদের দ্বারা উচ্চ মর্যাদায় ধারণ করা হতো। তারা শেখাতেন যে আত্মা আধ্যাত্মিক ধোয়া ও পরিস্কারের কাজকে প্রভাবিত করে যা বিশ্বাসীর চিন্তা ও কর্মে পরিবর্তন হিসাবে প্রকাশ পাবে। এই পরিবর্তন আমাদের পতিত স্বভাবের সঙ্গে এখনও বৈপরীত্যে থাকে, কিন্তু ধারাবাহিক সমর্পণ ও গভীর বিনয়ের মাধ্যমে, আত্মা বিশ্বাসীকে পূর্ণ করে তুলবে যতক্ষণ না পাপের প্রকৃতি প্রাধান্য নয়, বরং পরাভূত হয়। তবে বুঝতে গুরুত্বপূর্ণ যে পাপের উপর এই জয়টি কার্যকর করা হয় যখন বিশ্বাসী তাঁর ইচ্ছে ছেড়ে দেয় এবং আত্মাকে সম্পূর্ণ নিয়ন্ত্রণের অনুমতি দেয়।

অতএব, একটি বিশুদ্ধ চার্চ হলো আত্মসমর্পিত, আত্মায় পূর্ণ বিশ্বাসীদের একটি দল, যারা সচ্চরিত্রভাবে স্বীকার করে যে তাদের শক্তি কোনোভাবেই তাদের নিজের গুণের সঙ্গে যুক্ত নয়। অহংকারের অনুপস্থিতি, যা কেবলমাত্র আত্মার ধারাবাহিক সহায়তায় অর্জিত হয়, ইচ্ছুক বিশ্বাসীর পরিশুদ্ধতার জন্য আরও জায়গা দেয়। এইভাবে আমরা খ্রীষ্টীয় জীবনকে বাস্তব জুতো-চামড়ায় দেখতে পারি।

The Teachings of Practical Christianity

প্রাথমিক আমেরিকান মেনোনাইটদের বিশ্বাসের ব্যবহারিকতা নিয়মিতভাবে প্রকাশ পেত। তাঁর বই “Pride and Humility” তে, জন এম. ব্রেনেম্যান রক্ষা করেন যে একজন ব্যক্তির বাহ্যিক চেহারা সরাসরি তাঁর অভ্যন্তরীণ হৃদয়ের সাথে সম্পর্কিত, একটি দৃষ্টিভঙ্গি যা ব্যক্তির কর্মকাণ্ডেও প্রযোজ্য। স্বেচ্ছাচারী উদ্ধার, পুনর্জন্ম, এবং পূর্বোক্ত বিশুদ্ধ চার্চের বিশ্বাসের উপর ভিত্তি করে এই মনোভাব গঠন করা প্রয়োজন যাতে একটি মেনোনাইটের দৈনন্দিন জীবনে মিথস্ক্রিয়ার মানসিকতা ফ্রেম করা যায়।

এই গুরুতর-মনের খ্রীষ্টানদের কাছে রবিবারে প্রকাশিত ধর্মীয় বিশ্বাস এবং সপ্তাহের বাকি অংশে করা সাধারণ কাজগুলোর মধ্যে কোন গুরুত্বপূর্ণ পার্থক্য ছিল না। এটি তাদের সাধারণভাবে রাজনৈতিক বিষয় ও অন্যান্য জাগতিক উপাদান থেকে বিরত থাকার মাধ্যমে প্রমাণিত, যেগুলো তাদের ধারণাগুলোর উপর হস্তক্ষেপ করতে পারত। এটি তাদের সেইকালে অনেক চার্চের সঙ্গে সরাসরি বিরোধ তৈরি করেছিল, যেখানে দুইটি মতের স্কুল বিকশিত হয়েছিল: অথবা যে একজনের পৃথিবীজ চাকুরিগুলো রাজনৈতিকভাবে সম্পূর্ণভাবে তাঁর বিশ্বাস থেকে আলাদা থাকে, অথবা যে এই নাগরিক দায়িত্বগুলোর সফলতা ঈশ্বরের ইচ্ছার অংশ এবং তাই খ্রীষ্টানদের জন্য স্বাধীনভাবে ব্যবসা করা অনুমোদনীয়।

প্রাথমিক আমেরিকান মেনোনাইটদের জন্য এই ধরনের অবস্থানগুলি তাঁর খ্রিস্টীয়তার প্রকৃত অর্থকে খণ্ডন করতো: তিনি একজন নতুন ব্যক্তি ছিলেন, যিনি কেবল খ্রীষ্টের দ্বারা প্রবাহিত শক্তিতে জীবিত ছিলেন। এটি তাঁর জীবনের প্রতিটি দিককে প্রভাবিত ও নির্দেশিত করত—তার ব্যবসায়িক লেনদেনগুলো, যা কোনো পক্ষকে আরোপ করা থেকে বিরত রেখে পরিচালিত হতো; তার পোশাক ও আচরণ, যা বিনয় ও সরলতার উপর ভিত্তি করে হওয়া উচিত; এবং তার পরের মানুষের সঙ্গে আলাপ-আলোচনা করার পদ্ধতি, যা সত্যিকারের উদ্বেগ প্রদর্শন করে তাদের আধ্যাত্মিক মঙ্গল ও চিরস্থায়ী গন্তব্য সম্পর্কে।

Conclusion

এই সব ঔপনিবেশিক মেনোনাইটধর্মমতের সারাংশ ছিল কিভাবে একজন পরিণত, নম্র, অনুতপ্ত, কিন্তু আধ্যাত্মিকভাবে শক্তিশালী ঈশ্বরের দাস হিসেবে বৃদ্ধি পেতে হয় তার মতবাদ। তিনি চারপাশের বিশ্বের আকর্ষণকে অস্বীকার করতেন এবং তাঁর বিশ্বাসের পবিত্রতা ও পূর্বে যাঁর মধ্যে তিনি বাস করতেন সেই পাপের ইচ্ছাকরণ আন্তরিকভাবে পরিত্যাগ করার বিনিময়ে একটি চিরস্থায়ী পুরস্কারের প্রত্যাশায় বসবাস করতেন। আমাদের মত বিশ্বাসীবৃন্দ দ্বারা জীবিত এই উদাহরণটি আমাদের প্রেরণা হওয়া উচিত যাতে আমরা আরও গভীরভাবে ঈশ্বরের রাজ্যে প্রবেশ করি, নম্রতা ও তাড়না দ্বারা আমাদের বিশ্বাসকে কার্যকর করে তুলি।

“Get out of my shop! I don’t need people like you around me! And never come back!” My lips quivered as I looked into the dark, angry eyes of the yelling man. I blinked back the unbidden tears, realizing that once more, I had to leave this man that I loved. All night I could sense that we were coming to this, and I had tried so hard not to let it happen. With one last attempt, I feebly yelled above the tension, “Ken, we don’t want to ...” but once more, I was rudely cut off. With slumped shoulders and downcast eyes, I turned to escape the confines of his dingy, pawn shop, his ever-crescendoing voice drowning the last hope of respite.

The lingering smell of smoke and the echo of his angry voice joined the troubled thoughts of my emotionally overwrought mind, as I slowly walked up the street. “What do you think, Josh?” I asked my faithful, quiet friend.

“I don’t know, " he responded, and we fell back into silent anguish at the outcome of our supposed Bible study, grasping for an explanation for the terrible response. What could we have done differently? Why could he not accept the truth? What lay behind those flashing eyes, and what memories are stored beneath his ever-crowning beanie?

Ken was born on a country farm in the rolling hills of Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, a splendid place for a curious and adventurous little boy to live.

When Ken was four years old, his parents separated. He had heard them fighting a lot, but he didn’t know that it was possible for Mom and Dad to separate. It crushed his heart and confused his innocent soul. He did not know how to handle the stress and change that was tossed on his peaceful life.

The terror and confusion of his mom hurriedly packing their belongings, loading him and his siblings in the car, and driving away are still riveted in his mind. It made no sense! Why couldn’t they just go home? In his musty bedroom at their little, dingy apartment, he lay staring at the moldy ceiling, wondering endlessly what had gone so wrong.

Ken soon adjusted to his new home in the city of Pottsville with only cars, people, and sidewalks instead of cows, frogs, and mud. But fate did not leave the small security his new lifestyle provided him. His mom was not able to properly care for him and his siblings, and so the children were placed in different foster homes. That was even worse than leaving Dad! The clothes he wore were the only things familiar to him. Instead of understanding and loving him, each new family brought more yelling, hatred, and beating. Terror, tears, loneliness, and pain accompanied him.

Ken thought the second foster home that he was placed in would be a safe, loving home. The dad was tall and strong and appeared to be gentle. The mom was overweight, but her friendly smile resolved his fears. But the first night, when he reached for the food, he accidentally dumped a cup of water. She screamed at him and told him that he was worthless, and she wished they had never gotten him. The dad continued eating as if he didn't hear or care. Why didn’t the strong man stop her?

That evening, Ken crawled into his big, strange bed, already crying in loneliness, when he heard the mom yell. He quickly jumped out of bed and, with trembling legs, slipped behind the door to hide. She charged up the stairs bellowing angrily, and Ken was sure that he was in trouble. To his relief, she continued down the hall. He was still too scared to leave his hiding place for fear of receiving a beating. He wiped his tears as he began to sing under his breath a song he had heard in Sunday school, “Jesus loves the little children, all the children of the world.” He stopped to think, and his crying quit. “Then why am I here? " he wondered. “Have I done something wrong? God must not love little children. That song is not true! If God loved me I would not be here!" With that conclusion, he burst into tears and lost hope in God. He woke the next morning, still hidden behind the door.

Darkness had long fallen, and my family was all peacefully sleeping in our old farmhouse. I cried myself to sleep, crying for Ken's soul, crying because I didn’t know what to do, crying because my friend, the man I longed to see at peace with God, hated me.

Ken continued to fire questions. “How can God be good and allow so much bad? How could God let children suffer?” I listened on as he continued saying the same things that I heard so many times before, giving me no chance to talk.

Again, it was time to leave, and I was so glad to do so. He kept talking as we backed out the door. Once more, my friend and I walked up the street —tired, frustrated, and wishing never to come back.

Ken was 13 years old, and his life was no better than it had been when he was first put into the foster system. His life was in turmoil. He was continually yelled at and belittled at home. Ken was tired of crying. No one cared, and there was no one with whom he could share his problem. That’s when he came up with his clever plan. His school friend was a hippie, and his parents traveled a lot. They were called Gypsies. He heard that they were headed to California. So, Ken told them about his terrible life and asked if they would give him a ride. They were glad to help.

That exciting morning, he just did his usual thing. He left for school and instead went to California. He didn’t mind leaving all his stuff behind—he really didn’t have much anyway. His foster parents didn’t even care that he left.

In California, Ken lived on the beach and worked for fishermen, and whoever else needed help. He always had enough to eat and something to do. He had his fellow beach bums, but he was still alone inside. His heart was still empty. He longed for love.

Ken lived on the beach for a year and a half and then hitchhiked to Arizona. There he found a home in a homeless shelter and got a job. He did well and soon was on his own, but his search for love took him down the wrong roads. Ken really wanted to be married to a loving wife and have a family, but the girl he married did not marry him because of love. She was hurt, and Ken’s own hurt soul was attracted to her. They got married and all was well for a few years until he found out that his wife was seeing other men. His heart was broken, and his world was thrown into turmoil. Ken wanted desperately to provide security for the children that were born to them, and so he tried his best to stay together. He did not want to put his children through the life that he experienced. But after eight rough years, they got a divorce.

Ken moved on and tried to recover from the devastation of the divorce. His search for love brought him only more sadness and pain. Since Ken was hurt and unhappy, he found satisfaction in making others happy. He spent all his money on them, and when he had nothing more to offer, they left.

Now Ken is sitting in his pawn shop, alone, hurt, sad, and hiding. He found through his sad life that no one cared. Every time that he opened himself to love, he was always hurt. Deep down inside, he truly felt that God did not care. He lost hope in God, people, and last of all, he lost hope in love itself. That is why we were still visiting the dingy, smoke-stained shop after six years of very little apparent success. God kept bringing us back. He put in us a persistent love and relentless burden for this wounded soul. That is why we spent many hours hearing the same criticisms over and over. The same problems, the same confusion.

Nearly every month, he would fluctuate between hope and despair, love and hate, new life in God, and sadness and sin. We never knew what the next visit would bring. We could be swelling with hope and filled with blessing, or torn with angry words and sickened with dread. But we kept going back, and slowly he emerged from the pit of despair, and slowly allowed himself to be wrapped in the wonderful love of God and the glorious message of His redeeming grace. It was amazing to see the change in his life and to hear his ever-growing confidence in the love of Christ.

Today Ken loves the Lord. He is learning to walk with God. He has seen the love of God. He has found hope in God. He has experienced the unconditional love of God. He is still growing, and we are excited to see what God has for him.

I’m so glad that God brought Ken into my life. God had a plan for Ken and I. God wanted to show Ken that He loved him and that He would be there for him even when Josh turned his back on Him. God also wanted me to carry a burden in my youth. He knew how easily I would be distracted with money and fun. He knew that I needed a burden to carry, a soul to care for. He wanted me to be able to see beneath the shell of a hard soul and see a hurting child within. He wanted to give me a burden too big for me to carry so that I would learn to lean on Him. And most of all, He wanted to equip me to serve Him in broader ways.

Fellow Christians, open your lives to the work of God. Find an opportunity to love a hurting soul. Search out someone who needs a friend and love them, and wait and see what God has in store for you. Love until it hurts so badly that you don’t know what to do, and then turn to Jesus, who is there to help you through. God may be waiting for you to make the first step before He will use you. Your life is before you. You can choose to live a comfortable, happy life, or you can open yourself up to be hurt and find that after years pass, your life is overflowing with meaning and purpose. Jesus opened Himself to the pain and anguish of this world, and only through that do we have hope. He is asking us to follow His example, to open ourselves to pain so that others can have hope. And as He was glorified, so will we be glorified, in some measure, someday, and we will never regret the pain that we faced.

“Keluar dari tokoku! Aku tidak membutuhkan orang sepertimu di sekitarku! Dan jangan pernah kembali!” Bibirku bergetar saat aku menatap mata gelap penuh kemarahan pria yang berteriak itu. Aku menahan air mata yang tak diundang, menyadari bahwa sekali lagi, aku harus meninggalkan pria yang kucintai ini. Sepanjang malam aku bisa merasakan bahwa kami akan sampai pada titik ini, dan aku telah berusaha keras agar itu tidak terjadi. Dengan satu upaya terakhir, aku berseru pelan di atas ketegangan, “Ken, kita tidak mau ...” tetapi sekali lagi, aku diputuskan secara kasar. Dengan bahu merosot dan mata tertunduk, aku berbalik untuk melarikan diri dari ruang sempit toko gadaiannya yang kotor, suara yang terus meninggi menenggelamkan harapan terakhir akan kelegaan.

Bau rokok yang tersisa dan gema suaranya yang marah bergabung dengan pikiran-pikiran resah dari jiwaku yang emosional, saat aku perlahan berjalan menaiki jalan. “Bagaimana menurutmu, Josh?” aku bertanya kepada temanku yang setia dan pendiam.

“Aku tidak tahu,” jawabnya, dan kami kembali tenggelam dalam kesedihan hening atas hasil dari yang kami kira studi Alkitab, meraba-raba penjelasan atas respon yang mengerikan itu. Apa yang bisa kami lakukan berbeda? Mengapa dia tidak bisa menerima kebenaran? Apa yang tersembunyi di balik mata yang berkerlip itu, dan kenangan apa yang tersimpan di bawah topi beanie yang selalu ia kenakan?

Ken dilahirkan di sebuah peternakan di perbukitan Schuylkill, Pennsylvania, tempat yang indah untuk seorang anak kecil yang ingin tahu dan suka berpetualang.

Ketika Ken berusia empat tahun, orang tuanya berpisah. Ia sering mendengar mereka berkelahi, tetapi ia tidak tahu bahwa Ayah dan Ibu bisa berpisah. Hal itu menghancurkan hatinya dan membingungkan jiwanya yang polos. Ia tidak tahu bagaimana menghadapi tekanan dan perubahan yang dilemparkan ke dalam kehidupannya yang damai.

Teror dan kebingungan saat ibunya dengan tergesa-gesa mengemas barang-barang mereka, memasukkan dia dan saudara-saudaranya ke dalam mobil, dan pergi begitu saja masih membekas dalam pikirannya. Itu tidak masuk akal! Mengapa mereka tidak bisa pulang saja? Di kamar lembabnya di apartemen kecil yang kotor itu, ia berbaring menatap langit-langit berjamur, bertanya-tanya tanpa henti apa yang membuat semuanya salah.

Ken segera menyesuaikan diri dengan rumah barunya di kota Pottsville yang hanya penuh mobil, orang, dan trotoar menggantikan sapi, kodok, dan lumpur. Tetapi nasib tidak memberinya keamanan kecil dari gaya hidup barunya itu. Ibunya tidak mampu merawat dia dan saudara-saudaranya dengan benar, sehingga anak-anak itu ditempatkan di panti asuhan yang berbeda. Itu bahkan lebih buruk daripada meninggalkan Ayah! Pakaian yang ia kenakan adalah satu-satunya hal yang akrab baginya. Alih-alih pengertian dan kasih sayang, setiap keluarga baru membawa lebih banyak teriakan, kebencian, dan pukulan. Teror, air mata, kesepian, dan rasa sakit menemani hidupnya.

Ken mengira panti asuhan kedua tempat dia ditempatkan akan menjadi rumah yang aman dan penuh kasih. Ayahnya tinggi dan kuat dan terlihat lembut. Ibunya gemuk, tetapi senyum ramahnya menghilangkan rasa takutnya. Namun malam pertama, ketika ia meraih makanan, ia tidak sengaja menumpahkan secangkir air. Sang ibu berteriak padanya dan mengatakan bahwa ia tidak berharga, dan ia berharap mereka tidak pernah mendapatkan dia. Sang ayah terus makan seolah tidak mendengar atau peduli. Mengapa pria kuat itu tidak menghentikannya?

Malam itu, Ken merayap ke tempat tidurnya yang besar dan asing, sudah menangis karena kesepian, ketika ia mendengar sang ibu berteriak. Ia meloncat dari tempat tidur dan, dengan kaki gemetar, bersembunyi di balik pintu. Ia mendengar dia naik tangga dengan berteriak marah, dan Ken yakin bahwa ia akan mendapat masalah. Dengan lega, ia mendengar dia terus turun ke koridor. Ia masih terlalu takut untuk meninggalkan tempat persembunyiannya karena takut dipukuli. Ia menghapus air matanya sambil mulai bernyanyi lirih sebuah lagu yang pernah ia dengar di sekolah Minggu, “Jesus loves the little children, all the children of the world.” Ia berhenti untuk berpikir, dan tangisnya pun berhenti. “Lalu mengapa aku di sini?” ia bertanya-tanya. “Apakah aku melakukan sesuatu yang salah? Tuhan pasti tidak mengasihi anak kecil. Lagu itu tidak benar! Kalau Tuhan mengasihiku aku tidak akan berada di sini!” Dengan kesimpulan itu, ia menangis tersedu-sedu dan kehilangan harapan pada Tuhan. Keesokan paginya ia terbangun, masih bersembunyi di balik pintu.

Kegelapan telah lama turun, dan keluargaku semuanya tidur dengan tenang di rumah peternakan tua kami. Aku menangis sampai tertidur, menangis untuk jiwa Ken, menangis karena aku tidak tahu harus berbuat apa, menangis karena temanku, pria yang ingin kucapai damai dengan Tuhan, membenciku.

Ken terus melemparkan pertanyaan-pertanyaan. “Bagaimana Tuhan bisa baik dan membiarkan begitu banyak keburukan? Bagaimana Tuhan membiarkan anak-anak menderita?” Aku mendengarkan saat ia terus mengatakan hal yang sama yang sering kudengar sebelumnya, tak memberiku kesempatan untuk berbicara.

Sekali lagi, saatnya untuk pergi, dan aku sangat senang melakukannya. Ia terus berbicara saat kami melangkah mundur keluar pintu. Sekali lagi, temanku dan aku berjalan menaiki jalan—lelah, frustrasi, dan berharap tak perlu kembali lagi.

Ken berusia 13 tahun, dan hidupnya tidak lebih baik daripada ketika ia pertama kali masuk ke dalam sistem panti asuhan. Hidupnya kacau. Ia terus-menerus diteriaki dan diremehkan di rumah. Ken lelah menangis. Tidak ada yang peduli, dan tidak ada yang dapat ia ajak berbagi masalahnya. Saat itulah ia merancang rencana cerdiknya. Teman sekolahnya seorang hippie, dan orang tuanya sering bepergian. Mereka disebut Gipsi. Ia mendengar bahwa mereka akan menuju California. Jadi, Ken menceritakan kehidupannya yang mengerikan dan meminta apakah mereka bersedia memberinya tumpangan. Mereka senang membantu.

Pagi yang menggairahkan itu, ia hanya melakukan kebiasaannya. Ia pergi ke sekolah dan malah menuju California. Ia tidak keberatan meninggalkan semua barangnya—sebenarnya ia tidak punya banyak. Orang tua asuhnya bahkan tidak peduli bahwa ia pergi.

Di California, Ken tinggal di pantai dan bekerja untuk para nelayan, dan siapa pun yang membutuhkan bantuan. Ia selalu punya cukup makanan dan sesuatu untuk dilakukan. Ia punya teman-teman senasib di pantai, tetapi ia masih merasa sendirian di dalam. Hatinya masih kosong. Ia rindu akan kasih.

Ken tinggal di pantai selama satu setengah tahun lalu berjalan-jalan ke Arizona. Di sana ia menemukan tempat di penampungan tunawisma dan mendapat pekerjaan. Ia bekerja dengan baik dan segera hidup mandiri, tetapi pencariannya akan kasih membawanya ke jalan yang salah. Ken sangat ingin menikah dengan seorang istri yang penuh kasih dan memiliki keluarga, tetapi wanita yang dinikahinya tidak menikahinya karena cinta. Dia terluka, dan jiwa Ken yang terluka tertarik padanya. Mereka menikah dan semuanya baik-baik saja beberapa tahun sampai ia mengetahui bahwa istrinya melihat pria lain. Hatinya hancur, dan dunianya kacau. Ken sangat ingin memberi keamanan bagi anak-anak yang lahir dari pernikahan itu, jadi ia berusaha sebaik mungkin untuk tetap bersama. Ia tidak ingin menyeret anak-anaknya melalui kehidupan yang pernah dialaminya. Tetapi setelah delapan tahun yang sulit, mereka bercerai.

Ken melanjutkan hidup dan mencoba pulih dari kehancuran perceraian itu. Pencariannya akan kasih hanya membawanya pada lebih banyak kesedihan dan rasa sakit. Karena Ken terluka dan tidak bahagia, ia menemukan kepuasan dalam membuat orang lain bahagia. Ia menghabiskan semua uangnya untuk mereka, dan ketika ia tak lagi punya apa-apa untuk diberikan, mereka pergi meninggalkannya.

Sekarang Ken duduk di toko gadainya, sendirian, terluka, sedih, dan bersembunyi. Ia menemukan melalui hidupnya yang menyedihkan bahwa tidak ada yang peduli. Setiap kali ia membuka diri untuk kasih, ia selalu terluka. Jauh di dalam, ia benar-benar merasa bahwa Tuhan tidak peduli. Ia kehilangan harapan pada Tuhan, pada orang, dan terakhir-tama, ia kehilangan harapan pada kasih itu sendiri. Itulah sebabnya kami masih terus mengunjungi toko kotor yang berasap itu setelah enam tahun dengan sedikit keberhasilan yang tampak. Tuhan terus membawa kami kembali. Ia menaruh dalam diri kami kasih yang gigih dan beban yang tak kenal menyerah untuk jiwa yang terluka ini. Itulah sebabnya kami menghabiskan banyak jam mendengar kritik yang sama berulang kali. Masalah yang sama, kebingungan yang sama.

Hampir setiap bulan, ia berfluktuasi antara harapan dan putus asa, kasih dan kebencian, hidup baru dalam Tuhan, dan kesedihan serta dosa. Kami tak pernah tahu apa yang akan dibawa kunjungan berikutnya. Kami bisa dipenuhi harapan dan berkat, atau tercerai-berai oleh kata-kata marah dan diliputi ketakutan. Tetapi kami terus kembali, dan perlahan ia muncul dari lubang keputusasaan, dan perlahan mengizinkan dirinya dibalut oleh kasih Tuhan yang luar biasa dan pesan mulia tentang kasih karunia-Nya yang menebus. Sungguh menakjubkan melihat perubahan dalam hidupnya dan mendengar kepercayaan dirinya yang terus bertumbuh pada kasih Kristus.

Hari ini Ken mengasihi Tuhan. Ia belajar berjalan bersama Tuhan. Ia telah melihat kasih Tuhan. Ia telah menemukan pengharapan pada Tuhan. Ia telah mengalami kasih Tuhan yang tak bersyarat. Ia masih bertumbuh, dan kami bersemangat melihat apa yang Tuhan sediakan baginya.

Aku sangat bersyukur bahwa Tuhan mempertemukan Ken dalam hidupku. Tuhan memiliki rencana bagi Ken dan aku. Tuhan ingin menunjukkan kepada Ken bahwa Dia mengasihinya dan bahwa Dia akan ada untuknya bahkan ketika Josh membelakangi-Nya. Tuhan juga ingin memberiku beban di masa mudaku. Dia tahu betapa mudahnya aku teralihkan oleh uang dan kesenangan. Dia tahu bahwa aku membutuhkan beban untuk dipikul, sebuah jiwa untuk diperhatikan. Dia ingin aku mampu melihat di balik cangkang jiwa yang keras dan melihat seorang anak yang terluka di dalamnya. Dia ingin memberi bebanku terlalu besar untuk kubawa sehingga aku belajar bersandar pada-Nya. Dan yang terutama, Dia ingin membekaliku untuk melayani Dia dalam cara-cara yang lebih luas.

Sahabat seiman, bukalah hidupmu untuk pekerjaan Tuhan. Carilah kesempatan untuk mengasihi jiwa yang terluka. Carilah seseorang yang memerlukan seorang teman dan kasihi dia, dan tunggu dan lihat apa yang Tuhan telah sediakan bagimu. Kasihilah sampai sakit begitu hebat sehingga kamu tidak tahu harus berbuat apa, lalu berbaliklah kepada Yesus, yang ada untuk menolongmu melewatinya. Mungkin Tuhan menunggumu mengambil langkah pertama sebelum Dia mau memakai kamu. Hidupmu ada di hadapanmu. Kamu bisa memilih menjalani hidup yang nyaman dan bahagia, atau kamu bisa membuka dirimu untuk terluka dan menemukan bahwa setelah bertahun-tahun berlalu, hidupmu penuh makna dan tujuan. Yesus membuka diri pada rasa sakit dan kecemasan dunia ini, dan hanya melalui itu kita memiliki pengharapan. Dia meminta kita mengikuti teladan-Nya, membuka diri pada rasa sakit agar orang lain dapat memiliki pengharapan. Dan seperti Dia dimuliakan, demikian pula kita akan dimuliakan, dalam ukuran tertentu, suatu hari nanti, dan kita tidak akan pernah menyesali rasa sakit yang kita hadapi.

The winter of 1882 unfolded in the small southern town of Tuscumbia, Alabama. A happy, normal two-year-old girl fell desperately ill with a strange fever. The fever came and went, came and went, and came again. The family doctor feared the child would die of the strain, but the child was strong and one day the fever finally left for good. The following day the mother waved a hand past her daughter's face, but the child did not blink. Subsequent efforts wrought no results and a new day dawned upon the family with a blind daughter.

As the child gained strength enough to resume play, the great dinner bell released its peal to all around, but Helen did not respond. Other noises produced similar results and the Keller family came to the stark realization that life would never be the same again. Most of us may never face the grim circumstances that Helen Keller's family did, but each of us will certainly endure hardships tailored specifically by our God.

The human mind is an amazing and intricate creation. Though many have sought to understand it, its operational ability remains incomprehensible to mankind. It is no small wonder that a portion of the keenest insight into the health of the mind is revealed in God's Word. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Fear is the ominous adversary to a sound mind. It towers over the soul and taunts the saint with its menacing derision. Fear can take a sunny meadow and turn it into a lonely wilderness. It can render a grand wedding celebration as dark as a cave, and turn a banquet fit for a king into a nauseating affair. It is the most powerful and devastating tool in the devil's employment. Despite many bold claims, none are exempt from its wielding. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) It is fear that stands to attack and quench all the prosperity of the soul. If we are to resist it in these days, we he must rise with all diligence in defiant warfare.

We do not need to look very far to behold the disarmament and weakening of man's mind. Medication for the mind ranks among the leading prescriptions consumed in America today. This is no pointed accusation at any individuals who may find themselves in need of medical assistance to control their mind. But it takes no scholar to look at obesity and consider the diet, to see rebellious teens and connect it to the infrastructure of the home, or to see men's hearts (minds) failing them and believe that fear is at the root. While some may totally master their diet, few can claim to be accomplished parents. Fewer yet are those who are not, at times, accosted by fear. Though pride and sense may keep the outward man in check, and remaining perfectly calm, the inward man, at least subconsciously, must deal with the strain. Americans love to claim the motto, "No fear!" but our medication consumption tells a different story. Paul claimed no exemption, for he was “troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

What do we fear? Loss, pain, and humility. No one likes to lose something that we have fought to obtain. No one enjoys pain. No one loves to be humiliated. Still, we do not need to read far in the Scriptures to realize that these are often the avenues that God uses to further urge His servants down the path into His likeness. There is no insurance on earth that can secure the vibrancy of youth, the love of a family, or the respect of friends. The things that supply us with earth's greatest vanguard are all vulnerable to the risks of loss. Therefore, we fear. Though we lie in bed until the dawn of the morning, we can in no wise increase our stature nor alleviate the loss that God has laid upon our lives. This anxiety only furthers our grief and adds fuel to our fears.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Herein is the keeping of our hearts and minds: prayer, peace, and thanksgiving.

Like a skillful artisan we must carefully weave these two scriptures together on the loom of life for there seems to be a direct correlation between the fruitful - power, love and sound mind, to the “rootful”- prayer, peace, and thankfulness. There will be no conquering of our fears without these things, and every society that is anemic to these ingredients will certainly be handicapped.

Prayer Begets Power

In our weakened condition we cannot apprehend prayer as we ought. It is then we must rely on those who can or perhaps the Spirit, which maketh intercession for us with groanings which cannot be uttered. Communing with the Omnipotent Head of the universe is a tremendously bold task. Many will administer prayer as merely a formal task, seeking to be perfectly reverent in it. This is not communing as with a friend, nor is it bold. It is more apt to fall under the description of fear. The remedial therapy for fear is in pouring out all our anxiety, bitterness, and complaint onto our God. The saints of yesteryear had been known to vehemently pour out their accusations and the bitterness of their soul unto God.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

All these spewed forth bold accusations and complaints against God in fervent prayer and none of them offended Him. On the contrary, God had not given them the spirit of fear but of power, and they serve as our examples. It was faithless Ahab who was told to ask of God a sign in the heavens or earth. In his pious reply he refused to "tempt" God. This lack of boldness and abundance of fear is more tempting to God than the abundance of bitterness in our complaint for “there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Peace Begets Love

We are all at rest with the things we love. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) A sparkling young child who is at peace with his father worships the man and strives to imitate him. Through the lad's tender eyes, his father's character is unflawed. His skill is unmatched. Even the brand of vehicle he drives is the best, and he emulates his every action. Even though every father knows the limitations of his son's expectations, we all bask in the seasonal loyalty. It is knowledge and fear that undermines this loyal love. An abusive father will destroy such childhood esteem and fear will be its replacement. It was through base fear that the evil servant buried his talent and did not trade with it. In his eyes his master was austere and to be feared. But God has not given us the spirit of fear but of love.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) The soul who is affected by this love cannot but imitate it. He is at great peace with his Father’s love and the eyes through which he views his Father's character can only enlist replication. However dire the circumstances we may find ourselves in, this spirit of love and peace will carry us through whatever opposition we may meet with on life's pathway. Jacob made nothing of the hard service he was to endure for Rachel; the spirit of love to God will set us above the fear of man, and all the hurt that a man can do us.

Thankfulness Begets a Sound Mind

We do not need to study happy souls long to find buried within the bedrock of each one, a foundation of gratitude. The spirit of a sound mind, or quietness of mind, is a peaceable enjoyment of life. We are oftentimes discouraged in our way when the features of our environment do not measure not up to our own fancy and imagination. A mere sober, solid, thinking mind would obviate and defuse such fruitless notions, yet we are all tempted to entertain formidable ingratitude. It takes no brainpower to expose things we disdain, for Satan is certain to magnify and outline every unsatisfactory detail we encounter. We each may think ourselves into a deep cave, but we must thank ourselves out.

Fear of losing our health, wealth, reputation, and happiness is the biggest hindrance to securing it. To focus on our pain is to invite more. To be constantly analyzing our life to see if we are being fulfilled is a sure avenue to ingratitude. The world is constantly asking, "Are we having fun yet?" The answer is, "No". To these souls, life will never be adequate, and they must wander forth seeking the bigger fulfillment that the last one did not secure. It is the fear that we are not receiving our fair allotment in life that breeds discontentment. It is discontentment that produces more fear, and the downward spiral progresses. Such was the consternation of the soul who asked Christ to speak to his brother to divide the inheritance with him. This may be logical thinking, but it is not conducive to a sound and peaceable mind. This offended soul has no root in himself and will forever be wronged in some fashion and spend his days in search of a savior to come and fix the other party. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

There is no earthly level of attainment or perfect environment that will promote a sound mind. It can only be secured through prayer, peace, and thankfulness. This may take some reprogramming of our minds to reach into the subconscious recesses, but we must soberly gird up the loins of our minds and exercise them if we ever hope to obtain “the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13)

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8

Der Winter 1882 entfaltete sich in der kleinen südlichen Stadt Tuscumbia, Alabama. Ein fröhliches, normales zweijähriges Mädchen erkrankte verzweifelt an einem seltsamen Fieber. Das Fieber kam und ging, kam und ging und kam wieder. Der Hausarzt fürchtete, das Kind könne an der Belastung sterben, doch das Kind war kräftig und eines Tages verschwand das Fieber schließlich für immer. Am folgenden Tag wedelte die Mutter mit der Hand vor dem Gesicht ihrer Tochter, aber das Kind blinzelte nicht. Weitere Versuche blieben ohne Erfolg, und ein neuer Tag dämmerte für die Familie mit einer blinden Tochter.

Als das Kind genug Kraft gewann, um wieder zu spielen, läutete die große Abendglocke mit ihrem Klang für alle in der Umgebung, doch Helen reagierte nicht. Andere Geräusche zeigten ähnliche Ergebnisse, und die Familie Keller erkannte in aller Deutlichkeit, dass das Leben niemals wieder dasselbe sein würde. Die meisten von uns werden wahrscheinlich nie den düsteren Umständen gegenüberstehen, denen Helen Kellers Familie ausgesetzt war, aber jeder von uns wird gewiss Prüfungen erleiden, die speziell von unserem Gott zugeschneidert sind.

Der menschliche Geist ist eine erstaunliche und komplexe Schöpfung. Obwohl viele versucht haben, ihn zu verstehen, bleibt seine Funktionsfähigkeit für den Menschen unbegreiflich. Es ist kein geringes Wunder, dass ein Teil der schärfsten Einsichten über die Gesundheit des Geistes in Gottes Wort offenbart wird. “For God hath not given us the spirit of fear; but of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” (2 Timothy 1:7)

Furcht ist der unheilvolle Gegner eines gesunden Geistes. Sie ragt über die Seele empor und verspottet den Heiligen mit ihrer bedrohlichen Verhöhnung. Angst kann eine sonnige Wiese in eine einsame Öde verwandeln. Sie kann eine große Hochzeitsfeier so dunkel wie eine Höhle machen und ein zum König passendes Bankett in eine übelkeitserregende Angelegenheit verwandeln. Sie ist das mächtigste und verheerendste Werkzeug im Dienst des Teufels. Trotz vieler mutiger Behauptungen ist niemand von ihrem Griff ausgenommen. “A dreadful sound is in his ears: in prosperity the destroyer shall come upon him. He believeth not that he shall return out of darkness, and he is waited for of the sword.” (Job 15:21, 22) Es ist die Furcht, die darauf steht, all den Wohlstand der Seele anzugreifen und zu ersticken. Wenn wir ihr in diesen Tagen widerstehen wollen, müssen wir mit aller Sorgfalt im trotzigen Kampf aufstehen.

Wir müssen nicht weit schauen, um die Entwaffnung und Schwächung des menschlichen Geistes zu sehen. Medikamente für den Geist gehören heute zu den führenden Verschreibungen, die in Amerika konsumiert werden. Dies ist keine gezielte Anschuldigung gegen einzelne Personen, die möglicherweise medizinische Hilfe benötigen, um ihren Geist zu kontrollieren. Aber es braucht keinen Gelehrten, um bei Übergewicht an die Ernährung zu denken, bei rebellischen Jugendlichen an die Struktur des Zuhauses zu erinnern oder bei Männern, deren Herzen (Geister) versagen, zu glauben, dass Angst die Wurzel ist. Während einige ihre Ernährung völlig im Griff haben mögen, können nur wenige von sich behaupten, hervorragende Eltern zu sein. Noch weniger sind diejenigen, die nicht zumindest zeitweise von Angst heimgesucht werden. Obwohl Stolz und Vernunft den äußeren Menschen im Zaum halten und er vollkommen ruhig bleibt, muss sich der innere Mensch, zumindest unterbewusst, mit der Belastung auseinandersetzen. Amerikaner lieben es, den Wahlspruch "No fear!" zu verkünden, doch unser Medikamentenkonsum erzählt eine andere Geschichte. Paulus beanspruchte keine Ausnahme, denn er war „troubled on every side; without were fightings, within were fears.” (2 Corinthians 7:5)

Wovor fürchten wir uns? Verlust, Schmerz und Demütigung. Niemand verliert gern etwas, wofür er gekämpft hat. Niemand genießt Schmerz. Niemand liebt Demütigung. Dennoch müssen wir nicht weit in den Schriften lesen, um zu erkennen, dass dies oft die Wege sind, die Gott benutzt, um Seine Diener weiter auf den Pfad zu drängen, damit sie Sein Ebenbild annehmen. Auf Erden gibt es keine Versicherung, die die Lebendigkeit der Jugend, die Liebe einer Familie oder den Respekt von Freunden sichern kann. Die Dinge, die uns die größte Vorhut der Erde liefern, sind alle dem Risiko des Verlustes ausgesetzt. Darum fürchten wir uns. Auch wenn wir bis zum Morgengrauen im Bett liegen, können wir in keiner Weise unsere Stellung vergrößern noch den Verlust lindern, den Gott über unser Leben gelegt hat. Diese Angst verschlimmert nur unser Leid und schürt unsere Furcht.

“Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.” (Philippians 4:6 7) Hierin liegt die Bewahrung unserer Herzen und Sinne: Gebet, Frieden und Dankbarkeit.

Wie ein geschickter Handwerker müssen wir diese beiden Schriftstellen sorgfältig auf dem Webstuhl des Lebens miteinander verweben, denn es scheint eine direkte Korrelation zwischen dem Fruchtbaren – Kraft, Liebe und ein gesunder Geist – und dem "Wurzelhaften" – Gebet, Frieden und Dankbarkeit – zu bestehen. Ohne diese Dinge wird es kein Überwinden unserer Ängste geben, und jede Gesellschaft, die diese Zutaten vermissen lässt, wird gewiss beeinträchtigt sein.

Gebet bringt Kraft hervor

In unserem geschwächten Zustand können wir das Gebet nicht so erfassen, wie wir sollten. Dann müssen wir uns auf diejenigen verlassen, die es können, oder vielleicht auf den Geist, der für uns mit unaussprechlichen Seufzern bittet. Die Gemeinschaft mit dem allmächtigen Haupt des Universums ist eine ungeheuer kühne Aufgabe. Viele verrichten das Gebet lediglich als eine formelle Pflicht und bemühen sich, darin vollkommen ehrfürchtig zu sein. Das ist nicht die Gemeinschaft wie mit einem Freund, und es ist nicht kühn. Es fällt eher unter die Beschreibung von Furcht. Die heilende Therapie gegen Furcht liegt darin, all unsere Angst, Bitterkeit und Klage vor unseren Gott auszuschütten. Die Heiligen vergangener Zeiten waren dafür bekannt, ihre Anschuldigungen und die Bitterkeit ihrer Seele heftig vor Gott auszuschütten.

“Then Job answered and said, Even to day is my complaint bitter: my stroke is heavier than my groaning. Oh that I knew where I might find him! That I might come even to his seat! I would order my cause before him, and fill my mouth with arguments. I would know the words which he would answer me, and understand what he would say unto me. Will he plead against me with his great power? No; but he would put strength in me.” (Job 23:1-6)

  • David —“I poured out my complaint before him; I shewed before him my trouble.” (Psalm 142:2)
  • Hannah —“For out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” (1 Samuel 1:16)
  • Jeremiah —“He hath filled me with bitterness, he hath made me drunken with wormwood.”
    (Lamentations 3:15)
  • Naomi —“Call me Mara: for the Almighty hath dealt very bitterly with me.” (Ruth 1:20)
  • Hezekiah —“He will cut me off with pining sickness: from day even to night wilt thou make an end of me.” (Isaiah 38:12)
  • Jesus — “My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?” (Matthew 27:46)

All diese schütteten kühne Anschuldigungen und Klagen gegen Gott in glühendem Gebet aus, und keiner von ihnen beleidigte Ihn. Im Gegenteil, Gott hatte ihnen nicht den Geist der Furcht gegeben, sondern den der Kraft, und sie dienen uns als Beispiele. Es war der unglaubwürdige Ahab, dem gesagt wurde, er solle ein Zeichen bei Gott erbitten am Himmel oder auf der Erde. In seiner frommen Antwort weigerte er sich, Gott zu "versuchen". Dieser Mangel an Kühnheit und Fülle der Furcht ist für Gott eher verlockender als die Fülle der Bitterkeit in unserem Klagen, denn „there is no fear in love; but perfect love casteth out fear: because fear hath torment. He that feareth is not made perfect in love.” (1 John 4:18)

Frieden bringt Liebe hervor

Wir sind alle mit den Dingen, die wir lieben, im Frieden. "Great peace have they which love thy law: and nothing shall offend them.” (Psalm 119:165) Ein lebhaftes Kind, das in Frieden mit seinem Vater ist, verehrt den Mann und bemüht sich, ihn nachzuahmen. Durch die zarten Augen des Jungen ist der Charakter seines Vaters makellos. Seine Fähigkeiten sind unübertroffen. Sogar die Automarke, die er fährt, ist die beste, und er imitiert jede seiner Handlungen. Obwohl jeder Vater die Begrenzungen der Erwartungen seines Sohnes kennt, schwelgen wir alle in dieser zeitweiligen Loyalität. Es sind Erkenntnis und Furcht, die diese treue Liebe untergraben. Ein misshandelnder Vater zerstört solch kindliche Achtung und Furcht wird ihr Ersatz. Aus niederer Furcht vergrub der böse Knecht sein Talent und handelte nicht damit. In seinen Augen war sein Herr streng und zu fürchten. Aber Gott hat uns nicht den Geist der Furcht, sondern den der Liebe gegeben.

“We love him, because he first loved us. If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” (1 John 4:19, 20) Die Seele, die von dieser Liebe ergriffen ist, kann nicht anders, als sie nachzuahmen. Sie ist in großem Frieden mit der Liebe ihres Vaters, und die Augen, durch die sie den Charakter ihres Vaters betrachtet, können nur Nachahmung hervorbringen. So ernst die Umstände auch sein mögen, in denen wir uns befinden, dieser Geist der Liebe und des Friedens wird uns durch jedes Hindernis tragen, dem wir auf unserem Lebensweg begegnen mögen. Jakob machte nichts aus dem harten Dienst, den er für Rachel zu ertragen hatte; der Geist der Liebe zu Gott wird uns über die Furcht vor dem Menschen erheben und über all den Schaden, den ein Mensch uns zufügen kann.

Dankbarkeit bringt einen gesunden Geist hervor

Wir müssen nicht lange glückliche Seelen studieren, um im Fundament eines jeden eine Grundlage der Dankbarkeit vergraben zu finden. Der Geist eines gesunden Geistes oder die Ruhe des Geistes ist ein friedliches Genießen des Lebens. Oftmals sind wir verängstigt auf unserem Weg, wenn die Gegebenheiten unserer Umgebung nicht unseren eigenen Vorstellungen und Phantasien entsprechen. Ein nüchterner, solider, denkender Geist würde solche fruchtlosen Vorstellungen entkräften und entschärfen, doch wir sind alle versucht, mächtige Undankbarkeit zu hegen. Es bedarf keiner großen Denkleistung, Dinge aufzudecken, die wir verachten, denn Satan wird gewiss jedes unbefriedigende Detail vergrößern und skizzieren, dem wir begegnen. Wir können uns in eine tiefe Höhle denken, aber wir müssen uns durch Dank daraus befreien.

Die Furcht, unsere Gesundheit, unser Vermögen, unseren Ruf und unser Glück zu verlieren, ist das größte Hindernis, sie zu sichern. Sich auf den Schmerz zu konzentrieren, heißt, mehr einzuladen. Sein Leben ständig zu analysieren, um zu sehen, ob man erfüllt wird, ist ein sicherer Weg zur Undankbarkeit. Die Welt fragt ständig: "Are we having fun yet?" Die Antwort ist: "No". Für solche Seelen wird das Leben niemals ausreichend sein, und sie müssen weiterziehen, um die größere Erfüllung zu suchen, die die letzte nicht sicherte. Es ist die Furcht, dass wir unseren gerechten Anteil im Leben nicht erhalten, die Unzufriedenheit hervorbringt. Unzufriedenheit erzeugt mehr Furcht, und die Abwärtsspirale schreitet voran. So war die Bestürzung der Seele, die Christus bat, zu seinem Bruder zu sprechen, damit der das Erbe mit ihm teile. Das mag logisch denken sein, aber es fördert keinen gesunden und friedvollen Geist. Diese beleidigte Seele hat keine Wurzel in sich und wird sich auf ewig in irgendeiner Weise benachteiligt fühlen und ihre Tage damit verbringen, nach einem Retter zu suchen, der kommt und die andere Partei richtet. “... neither fear ye their fear, nor be afraid. Sanctify the LORD of hosts himself; and let him be your fear, and let him be your dread.” (Isaiah 8:12, 13)

Es gibt kein irdisches Maß an Erreichung oder perfekte Umgebung, die einen gesunden Geist fördern wird. Er kann nur durch Gebet, Frieden und Dankbarkeit gesichert werden. Das mag eine Umprogrammierung unserer Gedanken erfordern, um in die unterbewussten Winkel vorzudringen, aber wir müssen nüchtern die Lenden unseres Geistes umgürten und ihn üben, wenn wir je hoffen, „the grace that is to be brought unto you at the revelation of Jesus Christ;” (1 Peter 1:13) zu erlangen.

“And the peace of God,
which passeth all understanding,
shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.
Finally, brethren, whatsoever things are true,
whatsoever things are honest, whatsoever things are just,
whatsoever things are pure, whatsoever things are lovely,
whatsoever things are of good report;
if there be any virtue, and if there be any praise,
think on these things.

— Philippians 4:7, 8

“It is so hard,” the man sitting across from me said. “We’ve been married for nearly fifty years, but I never expected anything like this.”

“What is going on?” I asked Al, sympathetically.

“It’s Lisa,” he said. “You know her memory has been slipping for a little while. Well, we went to the neurologist like you told us to, and they ordered a whole bunch of tests and a brain scan of some sort. Then, they told her she had dementia.”

“I thought that was what was going on,” I replied.

“I know you told us that,” Al said. “Well, there are times she doesn’t recognize me. She looks at me blankly like she is wondering what crazy stranger has gotten into her house.”

“That’s got to be hard,” I said.

“The only thing I’ve found that brings her back to herself is to go outside and call her on her cell phone. I tell her to come out to the garage, I’ve got something to show her. Somehow when I do that, it brings her back to the present and lets her know who I am – for a little bit, anyway.”

We moved on to talking about other things, but I could tell that Al’s heart was breaking. His wife of 48 years looked the same as ever on the outside and yet, she was a completely different person.

I’d like to explore some of the challenges in dealing with dementia.

Dementia in the Bible

Ecclesiastes 12:1-7 gives a somewhat dismal view of the aging process. “Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth, while the evil days come not, nor the years draw nigh, when thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them; While the sun, or the light, or the moon, or the stars, be not darkened, nor the clouds return after the rain: In the day when the keepers of the house shall tremble, and the strong men shall bow themselves, and the grinders cease because they are few, and those that look out of the windows be darkened, And the doors shall be shut in the streets, when the sound of the grinding is low, and he shall rise up at the voice of the bird, and all the daughters of musick shall be brought low; Also when they shall be afraid of that which is high, and fears shall be in the way, and the almond tree shall flourish, and the grasshopper shall be a burden, and desire shall fail: because man goeth to his long home, and the mourners go about the streets: Or ever the silver cord be loosed, or the golden bowl be broken, or the pitcher be broken at the fountain, or the wheel broken at the cistern. Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

In this passage, the poetic description seems to speak of loss of teeth, loss of hearing, unsteady gait, and general frailty. It is hard to say if any of these images speak of memory loss. What is certain is that the passage begins with a command: “Remember!”

This is not the only place in Scripture where humans are commanded to remember. Over and over, we are told to remember God. We are to make certain that we instruct our children about Him. “And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up” (Deuteronomy 6:7).

The time may come when we are not able to remember anymore. The most important thing – even as we think about the subject of dementia is that we remember the One who made us and follow Him with all our hearts.

What Dementia is

Dementia is any illness that causes a loss of memory, reasoning, and social functioning. Most people think mostly of the loss of memory. I suppose this is because early in the illness other people notice things like difficulty finding words and frequent repetition of stories.

Social functioning is often maintained until late in the illness. If you ask someone with mild dementia if they know today’s date, they will likely answer, “Oh, you know, I stopped paying attention to things like that when I retired.”

The most common cause of dementia is Alzheimer’s dementia – at least 70 percent of people who have progressive memory loss have Alzheimer’s dementia. Alzheimer’s seems to be related to proteins called amyloid, which get deposited in the brain and prevent nerve cells from communicating with each other.

Other causes are vascular dementia, where blockages in the blood vessels in the brain cause the death of nerve cells. Lewy Body Dementia is a sort of memory loss that is associated with Parkinson’s Disease. Approximately eighty percent of people with Parkinson’s Disease will eventually develop dementia.

Diagnosing Dementia

If family members suspect someone is developing memory loss, the best thing is to bring them to their primary care provider for an evaluation. Along with doing a physical exam, the doctor will typically do things like have the patient draw a clock and do a mini mental status exam, which asks the patient to answer a lot of simple questions and do some short-term recall of items.

Blood tests including a thyroid and Vitamin B12 level would be done. A brain scan or ultrasound of the neck arteries might be done as well.

The goal is to identify areas that can be treated and take care of those.

Eliminate Medications

Many medications increase the risk of memory issues. As people get older, trying to avoid these medications is helpful to prevent the development of dementia.

Anticholinergic medications are probably the biggest culprit that I encounter. The most common of these medications are older antihistamines like diphenhydramine (used as either a sleep aid or allergy pill) and doxylamine (used as a sleep aid). In one study, patients who took an anticholinergic medication for the equivalent of three years had a significantly higher risk of dementia than patients who took these sorts of medications for less than three months.1 Older depression medications can also fall into this category.

Anxiety medications, called benzodiazepines, have also been associated with memory issues. Studies indicate that patients who take these medications have a higher risk of developing dementia than patients who do not take them.2

Seizure medications may make thinking ability worse as well. Having a seizure disorder seems to increase the risk of dementia, but certain older medications like valproate and gabapentin seem to make it harder for older people to think clearly, and shifting to lower-risk seizure medications is in order (if possible) for older people.

There are times when someone needs to take medication, but as patients get older, it is important to think about the risks of those medications. There is a list of medications that are wisest to avoid for patients over 65 years of age, called the Beers List. Substituting similar medications with fewer side effects or using lower doses is recommended.3

Medical Treatments

The first rule when dealing with dementia is to make certain that all of the metabolic things are in as good control as possible. So, if someone has diabetes, it is best to make certain that their sugar is in as good control as possible. If someone has high blood pressure, make certain that it is well-regulated (this is particularly true if someone has vascular dementia).

There are several different classes of medications that are approved for treating dementia. One group is the cholinesterase inhibitors. These medications raise the level of a chemical called acetylcholine in the brain and peripheral nervous system. These medications are certainly not miracle drugs and at best they seem to slow the progression of memory loss and do not really restore previous brain function.

The other medication is called memantine. It works by targeting the glutamate receptor in the brain. Just as with the cholinesterase inhibitors, the effects are not huge and the end result only slows the memory loss.

Both of these medications are generic, and it is reasonable to try them and see how someone responds to them.

One last medication to mention is called lecanemab. It is an IV infusion that targets amyloid, a kind of protein that develops in the brain of people with Alzheimer’s dementia. The medication seems to work quite well at clearing amyloid from patient’s brains. This medication is very expensive ($26,500 per year)and it has been linked to an increase in strokes. In the studies, dementia symptoms were only slowed by about 30 percent compared with a placebo.

There are no other medications currently approved to treat dementia.

Non-medication Therapies

There are several things that people can do to help slow the progression of dementia. These can be helpful for people who have a strong family history of dementia and want to prevent its onset.

Cardiovascular exercise is very important. Doctors mention exercise in relation to nearly every chronic illness because it has been shown to work. In the case of dementia, people who exercise regularly have about 30 percent decreased risk of developing the disease. Regular exercise seems to slow the progression of dementia.4

Doing puzzles that require mental activity, like Sudoku or crossword puzzles seems to help slow the progression of memory loss and may also reduce the chance of developing dementia.

Lastly, it is helpful to learn something new. People who learn a new skill or focus on learning a new language help their memories quite a bit. A study compared older people who learned a new skill with people who went to social events.

The point seems to be that our brains need to be pushed to create new pathways or they will tend to break down.5

Caring For Someone with Dementia

Caring for someone with dementia is challenging in a number of ways. It is often difficult to know how much independence to allow the person. There have been many books written on this subject, but there are a few things that are worth mentioning.

It is important to avoid dangerous things. The two most dangerous things for someone with faulty memory are driving and cooking. Both of these seem commonplace, and the person may seem to be doing fine, but they can become a problem very quickly.

The danger of driving a car or a buggy is twofold. First, some people freeze at certain points, not remembering how to do a particular skill. This can be a problem, not only for them but also for others on the road.

Second, older people can start off on short journeys to a local store or restaurant and end up getting lost. I have had patients who ended up driving around for hours trying to find their way home when they got confused driving to town.

Cooking, of course, really comes down to a question of remembering to set timers and take things off the stove or out of the oven at the appropriate time.

Many times, people who have dementia do not realize how much their abilities have slipped and resist the idea that they need to give up the car keys. Maybe it simply comes down to a loss of independence, but it is hard to face the fact that you are no longer safe behind the wheel.

Try to keep things the same within the room and the home. Even small changes in room arrangement can be enough to upset the situation. Taking someone out of their home – for instance, admitting them to the hospital often makes things a lot worse. Suddenly, confusion that only seemed mild before is now extremely high.

If there is a fruit of the spirit that is key for dealing with someone with dementia, it is patience. None of us has as much patience as we need, as dementia spreads that patience awfully thin.

People with dementia often act like children on a long trip. They ask over and over when they are going home. They wonder where dead relatives are or why the children aren’t home yet. No amount of explanation helps, because only a minute or two after they ask the question, they have forgotten the answer and are asking again.

Their skills often wax and wane. One day, they can button their shirt, and the next day, that skill seems to have flown out the window. It is easy to believe that they aren’t “trying hard” and that they could do more if they would only make the effort.

Unfortunately, the fact that someone with dementia could do something yesterday doesn’t mean that they can remember how to do it today. Getting upset with them only makes these things worse as it adds anxiety to a person who already lacks the memory of how to do a skill.

As much as possible, answer the person gently even if it is the fifty-third time that you have answered the same question. Use distractions as well. If there is an activity that they can still do, such as sewing or jigsaw puzzles (even children’s puzzles with really big pieces), get them to do it. Late in the illness, letting them look at books with pretty pictures or sometimes even giving them a baby doll to hold can help settle them and distract them from their anxieties of the moment.

Get Others to Help

It is easy to become frustrated. Trying to provide all of the care needed by yourself is not a long-term solution. Dementia care is a marathon and not a sprint. Many people live for years after the diagnosis, and even though their physical body remains relatively strong, they require more and more care.

One of the blessings of having family connections and church communities is that we have people who are available to provide assistance.

Having family members or friends step in to give you some respite is key to not becoming seriously burned out or even angry with someone that you care about. It is best to take some time away periodically before you are mentally depleted. You may think you are doing fairly well, but all of us have a tendency to get weary in well doing if we never get a break.

Conclusion

I wish there were more medical solutions for dementia. Perhaps more will come later. For now, medications are quite limited.

The key is to put the fruit of the Spirit into practice. “But the fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance: against such there is no law” (Galatians 5:22-23).

Even on the most frustrating days, people who are dealing with severe memory loss need love, gentleness, and patience from their family members. It is only through the Holy Spirit’s power that we can provide the care that is needed for someone whose body is strong, but who no longer even recognizes you.
